The public `IDocumentRtService` stored-document validation path passes `isDisplayValue = false` in both dynamic-Groovy and generated Java; `true` belongs to a lower-level presentation-validation path, not to ordinary document validation. The sibling explicit `Valid`/`Invalid(field, type)` condition invokes the validator without a declaring field's bounds, with the runtime's fixed condition locale and stored-value mode.
- **Relevance short-circuits invocation, and one formal result is reused.** A non-relevant custom cell is not passed to the validator. For a relevant cell the formal pass obtains the validator result once and reuses that formal state for message emission and downstream unknown/suppression behavior; a stateful validator or remote bridge must not be observed twice for one cell in one pass.
- **No registered validator → it THROWS.** `getCustomFieldValidator` resolves the validator from the factory / global `CustomFieldTypeService`; missing → `ValidatorException("Custom field validator '<name>' missing.")`, which `validateFull` surfaces as `FaultException("Unable to invoke validation")`. So a *filled* custom-typed field on a bare model fails the **whole** validation (an empty/not-relevant cell short-circuits before reaching it). There is no "fire a formal error" and no "skip".
- **The error code is the validator's OWN key**, `ICustomFieldTypeCheckError.getErrorKey()` (project-specific, e.g. `"invalidCreditCardNumber"`) — **not** a fixed kernel code like the `StringType` length codes.
- **The validator's own message is processed by the ordinary error handler.** Every literal `$<fieldName>$` token in the returned message is replaced by that concrete field instance's localized identifier; ordinary text is preserved.
- **The bounds DO reach the model + runtime** (`md.model.api.fieldtypes.ICustomFieldType.getMinLength/getMaxLength`; codegen carries them into the validation param) — they are real model properties, just never kernel-enforced.

This is the kernel truth behind the interpreter's treatment (auto-validate each filled custom cell against the consumer-registered predefined type; unregistered → report unsupported + degrade leniently, since the native runtime cannot host the validator) — INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF26. JS/TS identical, so a Kotlin/JS consumer mirrors it.

**Amended 2026-09-22 — three of the clauses above are now RUNTIME-measured on kernel 30.8.1, not only source-read.** A probe request can register a validator (`customFieldTypes`, [KERNEL-PROBE-SPEC](KERNEL-PROBE-SPEC.md) §3), so the delegation is observable rather than inferred: (a) the host's `getErrorKey()` arrives as the artifact's message `code` with its own text and `type: VALUE_ERROR`, identically on dynamic-Groovy and static-Java; (b) **full delegation is discriminated by message COUNT** — a value over a CUSTOM field's declared `maxLength` produces exactly **one** message, the host's, where a kernel that also checked would add its own, and the **within-model control** is a `StringType` field carrying the *same* declared bound in the *same* model, which does fire the kernel's `stringZuLang`; (c) an unregistered type's raise is the whole call's, so every other rule on that document is lost with it. The `1`/`999` normalization is unchanged and remains source-read. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.KernelProbeCustomFieldTypeTest`; the raise itself by `adapter.laws.KernelProbeFaultCaptureTest`.)*

## §12 supplement — a starred VALUE-LIST quantifier's complete extent needs wildcard coverage (source + differential, 2026-07-22, SPEC-2026-07-22-09) <a id="kf55"></a>

> Fold: folded → §12.

In partial validation a starred value-list quantifier entry carries a **complete-extent** fact SEPARATE from its per-cell relevance: the extent is established only when the relevant set **wildcards** the starred level (`ALL_SEMANTIC`, or a relevant ancestor whose descent covers it) — enumerating every currently-instantiated row CONCRETELY does not. An extent-unknown entry is gated **side-specifically**, exactly the IF42 all-rows-aggregate rule applied to the value-list operators: `No` is suppressed to UNKNOWN on **either** side (`RuntimeController.keinFeldWertInWerteListeIntern` and `fuegeFeldWerteZuWerteListe` reject an extent-unknown starred fields/values entry before scanning), `NotAll` on the **values** side, while `AtLeastOne` (either side) and `NotAll` on the fields side scan the relevant cells and ignore extent (`mindestensEinFeldWertInWerteListeIntern` / fields-side `nichtAlleFeldWerteInWerteListeIntern`). Full validation is unaffected.

**Interpreter:** the fix reuses the existing `starRelevant` wildcard-extent seam (IF42) — `ValueListQuantEval` sets a `VlqOperand.extentUnknown` bit from `starRelevant(starPath)` (null in full validation → never set → the full path is byte-identical) and routes it through the same side-specific arms (since IF218 the fields-side gate for `No` sits at the operand's position in the ordered scan); per-cell relevance and formal-cell classification are unchanged. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.PartialValidationValueListDiffTest` — dynamic-Groovy vs static-Java vs interpreter, the three extent-sensitive cases plus fields-side-`NotAll`/`AtLeastOne`/non-repeatable controls — + multiplatform `interpreter … PartialValidationValueListExtentTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF42.)*

## §4/§12 supplement — an eligible empty INDEX field's declared S-value: FULL validation stages it, PARTIAL silently suppresses the cell (source + dual-strategy differential, 2026-07-23, SPEC-2026-07-23-14) <a id="kf56"></a>

> Fold: folded → §4 + §12.

An ordinary closed **Enumeration may declare one stored token as its S-value** (DM-JSON `sValue` on `EnumerationType`; `IEnumerationType.getsValue`) — a **model-owned INDEX default**, not a document value. One index-cell instance is **eligible** when the index field is *not explicitly mandatory* (the author's requiredness — the auto index requiredness doesn't count), its repeatable group has **exactly one physically instantiated row under the current parent** (per-parent scoping: sibling parents are independent), and that row's index cell is **clean-empty** — physically absent or present-empty, never an admitted explicit value (`IndexFieldDefaultValueUtils.getIndexFieldIdsEligibleForDefaultValueHandling`). What happens next splits by CALL KIND, not by the relevant set's extent (`ValidationCache.addDefaultValuesForIndexFieldsIfNecessary`, invoked from `CheckCommand.formalePruefung`'s ingestion tail):

- **FULL validation stages the S-value into its transient evaluation cache** — before the generated index mandatory/uniqueness checks and before authored rules, **without mutating the document** (`setIndexFieldToDefaultValue` → `addFeldToDatenCache`, which also feeds the index cache and flips group fill). Observables (dual-kernel-route + JVM/Node locked): no `mandatoryField`/`uniqueIndex` for the defaulted cell; a dependent authored rule reading the index **sees the staged token** (`[ServiceLevel] == "STD"` fires on the otherwise-bare row); a bare eligible row satisfies its generated checks entirely.
- **PARTIAL validation does NOT stage it** — even with the whole document wildcard-relevant. The same eligible cell is **silently marked unavailable for that call** (`markFieldAsInvalidForValidation`: the formal-invalid set + `erroneousGroups` propagation — **no message**): neither `mandatoryField` nor `uniqueIndex` is emitted, dependent authored conditions read UNKNOWN and are Kleene-suppressed, and the **containing group retains error state** (a `NoGroupFilled` over the group cannot prove absence). This prevents partial from reporting errors full validation would not.
- **Ineligible shapes get no default in either call kind**: multiple sibling rows (each empty index draws its ordinary `mandatoryField` — and NO injected `uniqueIndex` pair, the duplicate/default interaction), an admitted explicit value (evaluates normally), an explicitly mandatory index (`mandatoryField` stands), a non-Enumeration index (the S-value is not even representable), and a **formally invalid explicit value stays unavailable and never exposes the S-value** to authored evaluation. With **zero** instantiated rows nothing is staged and **no phantom row** appears (`NoGroupFilled(G*)` still fires on the genuinely empty group).

**Interpreter reconciliation (SPEC-2026-07-23-14):** the model surfaces gained the representation (modelkit `EnumSpec.sValue` + `EnumFieldBuilder.sValue(...)`, the DM-JSON key round-trips through the CLI field-spec; the interpreter model carries `FieldDef.enumSValue` → `ModelDef.indexDefaults`); a FULL call stages the eligible cells through the existing call-local computed-overlay document (never mutating the caller's document), and a PARTIAL call feeds the same eligible cells to the formal-status cache as silently **unavailable** (a message-less generated failure that suppresses the generated checks, turns dependent reads UNKNOWN, and joins the group-presence error state) — INTERPRETER-FINDINGS. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.IndexDefaultStagingDiffTest` — absent/present-empty staging, dependent-rule visibility, admitted-explicit/invalid-explicit/multi-row/mandatory controls, explicit-duplicate control, per-parent scoping, no-phantom-row, and the four partial-suppression arms — dynamic-Groovy · static-Java · interpreter, full AND `validatePart`; `interpreter.IndexDefaultStagingMultiplatformTest` — the pure engine on JVM + Node, including document-not-mutated; authoring: `modelkit.EnumSValueTest`.)*

**Two-corner supplement (IG104 probe, 2026-07-24) — the staging cache is EVAL-only, and an out-of-domain S-value is a MODEL error, both dual-strategy-confirmed:**

- **A `$field.value$` message interpolation over a STAGED index cell renders as if the cell were EMPTY** (→ the field's format default, `""` for an enum, `0` for a number) — even though the same staged token DECIDED the firing condition. Mechanism (source): the staging writes only into the transient `ValidationCache.datenCache` (which `getWertXML` / condition reads consult), while `MainValidatorController.getReplacementForParam` reads the **original caller data** — `validationCache.getDaten().getValueForDisplay(id)` — which never sees that cache; an empty display then falls to `IFormatDefinition.getDefaultValue`. So the split is between the eval cache (staged) and the caller document (`getDaten`, original). *(Locked dual-route + interpreter: `adapter.laws.StagedIndexDefaultInterpolationDiffTest`, `interpreter.StagedIndexDefaultInterpolationMultiplatformTest` (JVM+Node); interpreter reconciliation IF221.)*
- **An enum `sValue` OUTSIDE its declared value domain is a MODEL-consistency error, `MVK_S_VALUE_INVALID`** ("The s-value '…' is not contained in the list of XML-values for the enumeration"), reported by `checkConsistency` — and **BOTH kernel strategies REFUSE to generate validation code** (dynamic-Groovy throws `DocumentValidationException`; static-Java's `generateValidationCode` returns null). There is no runtime "staged-formal-check" path: an out-of-domain S-value model is simply not kernel-consistent and never runs. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.OutOfDomainEnumSValueRejectionTest` (kernel MVK stance + the interpreter loader's matching loud refusal), `interpreter.load.EnumSValueLoadTest` (JVM+Node); interpreter reconciliation IF221.)*

## §12 supplement — Partial validation (`validatePart`) — rule-gating + 3VL relevance (source + probe-confirmed 2026-06-24) <a id="kf57"></a>

> Fold: folded → §12.

`validatePart(DocumentV2, Set<DocumentMultiPointer> relevantEntities, DocumentProcessingConfig)` validates only a *part* of the document. The contract (kernel javadoc on `IDocumentRtService.validatePart`, probe-confirmed) is two mechanisms:

- **Rule-level filter skip precedes relevance and 3VL.** Every code-generation target's rule-definition template (`validation/java`, `validation/groovy`, and `validation/java_script_vk` `rulesDir/CodeGenRuleDefinition.st`) emits a method-entry return under `t.filterConditions` when the validation cache is in partial-with-3VL mode. Generated Java and Groovy confirm the emitted branch, and the BA appendix lists rules with filter conditions among the checks partial validation may skip. Therefore a rule containing any `Having` filter does not run in partial validation even when its error field and all field instances are wildcard-relevant; the same rule evaluates normally under full validation. This is the shared mechanism behind the seed-33 fuzz mismatch, not a value-specific correlation edge. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.PartialValidationFilterSkipDiffTest`, with equality and ordered-correlation controls live under full validation and absent under partial; the exact randomized reproducer remains in `PartialValidationFuzzDiffTest`.)*

- **Rule-gating by the error field.** A validation rule is **executed only if its error field is in the relevant set at the repetition levels the rule's ITERATION bound** (this includes the auto-generated formal/mandatory/unique field checks, whose error field is the field itself). So a rule whose error path is not relevant at all simply does not run — no message. **Corrected 2026-08-08:** this used to say "error-field *instance*", which is too strong. Iteration is reference-driven, so the levels compared come from the plan, not from the rule's declared group; anything below them was never chosen and is not compared, and the message reports at the default first repetition. Measured both strategies, `PartialRuleGateScopeDiffTest`.
- **Suppression via 3VL on non-relevant references.** Of the rules that *do* run, "validation errors will be suppressed if the rule references any repetition of a field/group that is not marked as relevant — **except for some cases where the kernel is sure that no possible value of that field/group repetition could have prevented the error**." That exception is exactly **Kleene three-valued logic**: a non-relevant reference is **UNKNOWN**, and `true Or Unknown = true` (still fires — no value could prevent it) while `true And Unknown = Unknown` (suppressed). Probe over a two-field rule confirmed: `And` with only the error field relevant → suppressed; the same as `Or` → fires; only the *other* field relevant (error field not) → not run.

Relevant pointers: `DocumentMultiPointer.of(fullName, repetitions)` with **`ALL_SEMANTIC` (index `0`)** as the per-level wildcard ("all repetitions"); a relevant **group** makes all its **descendants** relevant. The kernel **encourages** wildcarding every path level — a *subset* of repetitions has subtle suppression around wildcards/aggregates (`/RG*/f1` references not-filled reps too) and `NumberOfFilled…`/semantic-index/parallel-iteration.

**GLOBAL fields are auto-added to the relevant set — but by the MD-LAYER, not the core validator (source-verified 2026-06-26).** A field flagged **`global`** (DM-JSON `"global": true` in the Field body; `IField.isGlobal`) is **always relevant in partial validation**, regardless of the caller's set. The mechanism is precise: the **core** validator (`ValidationCommand`) does *not* touch global fields; the **md-runtime-service** layer — exactly the `IDocumentRtService.validatePart(DocumentV2, …, config)` boundary the oracle calls — injects them first (`LowKernelApiUtils.validatePartlyWith3ValueLogic` → `addGlobalFieldsToRelevantEntities`, which adds `metaModel.getValue("GlobalFields")` = each global field's pointer **wildcarded at all reps**, `MetaModelImpl` building them with all-zero `ALL_SEMANTIC` indices). `IField.isGlobal`'s own javadoc states the contract: *"Global fields should always be passed to a partial validation in addition to the usual relevant entities. The caller of the validation is responsible for passing the global fields."* So at the kernel's *public* runtime boundary they ARE auto-added; a rule whose error field is global therefore RUNS even when the caller's relevant set omits it. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.PartialValidationGlobalFieldDiffTest` — global vs. non-global control vs. the kernel; the loader mapping by `cli.interp.InterpreterRealModelDiffTest.loaderReadsTheGlobalFieldFlagIntoModelDef`.)*

**Interpreter treatment:** `PreparedModel` records `hasFilterConditions` once per rule and `DmInterpreter.rowOutcomes` returns before iteration, correlation planning, or condition evaluation when that flag meets a partial-validation pass. This is an O(1) hot-path branch and makes partial filtered rules cheaper, while full validation retains the existing indexed correlation path unchanged. For every non-filtered rule, the remaining behavior maps directly onto the existing 3VL engine — `DmInterpreter.validatePart` gates each emitted message by its error field's relevance and resolves non-relevant referenced instances to `Val.Unknown` (the same `invalid`-operand mechanism formal errors already use), so Kleene logic yields the kernel's exact suppression. **Starred-aggregate relevance is PER-OPERATOR (probe-confirmed 2026-06-26).** Under a subset relevant set, an aggregate over a starred reference `G*/f` is relevant per its operator:
- **all-rows aggregates** (`Sum`, `MaxValue`, `MinValue`, `NumberOfDifferentValues`) require wildcard coverage at every starred level **after the kernel has expanded relevant groups and removed identifiers encompassed by broader wildcards**. Enumerating concrete rows, even ALL of them, leaves the aggregate UNKNOWN; one wildcard does not rescue concrete siblings that survive reduction. Controlled probe (2 rows, no fillable tail): `Sum(Lines* / Price) > 1000` fires under a lone `Lines` wildcard but NOT under `{Lines[1], Lines[2]}` listed concretely. **Corrected 2026-08-06, amended 2026-08-07: `SumOfProducts` has its OWN, WEAKER gate** — it evaluates under a COMPLETE concrete enumeration (every declared repetition listed), because the kernel walks its two lists in a hand-written loop with no three-value pre-survey; under a PARTIAL enumeration the kernel is SILENT, exactly like the other four. The 2026-08-06 correction read "concrete enumeration evaluates" off a both-rows case alone and dropped the gate entirely, which made the interpreter fire where the kernel does not on 5 of 180 fuzz combinations. Both granularities are pinned kernel-side by `PartialValidationAggregateDiffTest.sumOfProductsSeparatesCompleteFromPartialRowEnumeration`.
- **`FirstFilled`** is **order-aware**: it returns the first FILLED cell's value and is UNKNOWN only when a non-relevant cell precedes that first filled cell. So it fires when the first filled row is relevant (wildcard, both-rows, or that-row-only) and is UNKNOWN when that row is non-relevant (probe: row-1-filled fires under row-1-only, suppresses under row-2-only).

**The wildcard gate consumes a reduced set of internal field identifiers, not the caller's relevant pointers independently (source-discriminated 2026-08-08).** `ValidationCommand.initialisiereRelevanteFelder` expands every relevant group to identifiers for its descendant fields. `compressRelevantFieldsForValidationCall` stores those identifiers per field name, and `ValidationCache.reduceRedundancies` removes an identifier only when a broader wildcard identifier of that name encompasses it. For the current aggregate row, `EntityIterator.certainlyNotInSameSubtree` drops identifiers that are certainly outside its bound subtree, then `existiertEbeneMitSternUndTeilvalidierungUngleich` makes the extent unknown when any remaining identifier is concrete at any starred iterator level. This distinguishes the mechanism from the tempting "any wildcard wins" reading: a field wildcard plus concrete group rows can remain mixed and suppress the aggregate, while a semantic wildcard broad enough to encompass those expanded group rows removes them and evaluates. The same discriminator reproduced with `NumberOfDifferentValues` whose error field is the operand and with `Sum` whose error field is separate; `SumOfProducts` remained on its distinct complete-enumeration path. The Java runtime source has a TypeScript sibling with the same sequence. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.PartialValidationAggregateDiffTest`, including the reduction matrix and `SumOfProducts` control; the structurally metered `perf.PartialValidationFuzzDiffTest`; interpreter reconciliation [IF262](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if262).)*

**This universal reading is the FOUR ALL-ROWS AGGREGATES' gate only — the starred VALUE-LIST extent gate is EXISTENTIAL (measured 2026-08-08).** On `{field wildcard} + {concrete group rows}` the kernel **fires** a starred `No` and is **silent** on `Sum` over the same rows, on both codegen strategies. So the value-list entry's extent is established by ONE covering identifier that wildcards every reopened level, and concrete siblings beside it do not take it away. The sharpening that keeps both readings honest: a wildcard beside a concrete identifier **for its own field** fires on *both* sides, because `reduceRedundancies` removes the encompassed sibling — the two gates differ in whether the **expanded group** identifiers reach the universal test, not in how they treat wildcards. Seven relevant-set shapes with the two operators side by side, plus the no-wildcard control where both are silent. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.PartialExtentGateShapeDiffTest`; interpreter split [IF264](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if264).)*

This is exactly the runtime `isWertAngegeben` 3VL (a non-relevant cell read is UNKNOWN; an all-rows fold with any UNKNOWN → UNKNOWN), with the reduced wildcard-vs-concrete identifier set governing whether the star's cells are check-relevant. *(Interpreter: `DmInterpreter.starRelevantOf` + the per-operator `evalFunc` gate, IF42/IF262; locked `adapter.laws.PartialValidationAggregateDiffTest` + the randomized `perf.PartialValidationFuzzDiffTest`.)*

**A duplicated INDEX cell compromises a rule only when its duplicate PARTNER is also relevant (measured 2026-08-08).** IF39's relevance-restricted duplicate cache has an observable consequence one layer out: a rule whose error field is a duplicated index cell RUNS under a partial set that omits the partner, because `uniqueIndex` never fires and the cell is therefore not compromised — and is suppressed as soon as the partner joins the set. Measured on a starred `AtLeastOne` over an index field with two rows sharing a value: relevant-{matching row}, {non-matching row}, {matching row + an unrelated group row}, and {the matching row's group} all FIRE; {non-matching row + the matching row's group} and a full wildcard are SILENT. Both codegen strategies agree on every row. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.PartialAtLeastOneScanDiffTest`, both strategies plus the interpreter. The interpreter matched only from 2026-08-08: it carried a second, relevance-blind duplicate source in `IndexColumn` that every evaluation site read — [IF266](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if266).)*

The oracle path is the modern `validatePart(DocumentV2, …, config)` (`RuntimeLaws.firedCodesPart`/`messagesPart`). Global fields are auto-relevant (IF37, above); a `CustomCondition` receives the relevant set (null for full, the subset for partial — IF38, source `MainValidatorController` → `getAllPruefungsrelevanteEntitiesExtern`; the set is the caller's *external* pointers **as passed** — wildcards preserved, groups NOT expanded — plus the auto-added globals); and uniqueness needs the duplicate **partner** relevant too (IF39 — the kernel's duplicate caches are built from the relevant fields only, `befuelleCacheMitRelevantenFeldern`). *(Locked: `adapter/…/laws/PartialValidationDiffTest` + `interpreter/commonTest/PartialValidationTest`; the rule-level `Having` skip by `PartialValidationFilterSkipDiffTest`; subset-repetition aggregates by `PartialValidationSubsetRepDiffTest` (IF35, non-directional); global fields by `PartialValidationGlobalFieldDiffTest` (IF37); custom-condition relevant-set propagation by `PartialValidationCustomConditionDiffTest` (IF38); subset uniqueness by `PartialValidationUniqueIndexDiffTest` + `PartialValidationRepetitionNotUniqueDiffTest` (IF39); per-operator starred-aggregate relevance by `PartialValidationAggregateDiffTest` (IF42, above); and a randomized `PartialValidationFuzzDiffTest` sweeps (document × relevant-subset) combinations across the whole partial surface. The interpreter matches the pinned kernel across that exercised surface.)*

## §9 supplement — `validateFull` also emits STRUCTURAL over-repetition errors — `zuGrosseZeile` / `zuGrosseKontextnummer` / `zuGrosseLfdNummer` (model-fuzz finding, 2026-06-24; non-repeatable increment 2026-07-26) <a id="kf58"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

A document instance with **more rows than a group's effective maximum** is flagged by `validateFull` with a structural VALUE error and its ordinary checks (uniqueIndex/mandatory/rules) are suppressed. Bounded repeatable groups use their declared cap; non-repeatable groups use 1. **The code depends on the first exceeded coordinate's position, not on repeatability** (corrected 2026-09-08, `SPEC-2026-09-08-01`): position 0 emits **`zuGrosseLfdNummer`** on the root row and every reported descendant; a deeper group's own coordinate emits **`zuGrosseZeile`**; a deeper ancestor coordinate emits **`zuGrosseKontextnummer`**. A field's address carries its own terminal coordinate after the containing groups. The root case wins even when its one coordinate is also the last.

`RootOverLimitPositionDiffTest` compares exact message keys on our Shipment fixture against dynamic-Groovy and static-Java. With both root and nested caps at 2, the in-capacity document is clean; root row 3 draws serial codes on the row, its direct field, a child row and field, and a grandchild row and field. Nested row 3 under root row 1 instead draws one row code and context codes below it. Violating both levels emits only serial codes, including on the materialized empty nested rows: the earliest violated coordinate absorbs the deeper violation. A second fixture with fixed-cap groups confirms root coordinate 2 uses serial codes, while a deeper fixed-group coordinate 2 uses row/context codes. These two discriminators falsify the interpreter's previous repeatability-kind selector in opposite directions. `AutoChecks.overRepetitionType` now selects by position at the shared structural-message and field-admission boundary; `RootOverLimitPositionTest` locks both discriminators on JVM and Node. This measurement uses direct document-instance construction and full validation; it makes no new claim about the computation or JSON-ingress routes.

The check is per **entity instance** (`FormalChecker.checkIndicesLessOrEqualThanMax`): walk the instance's coordinates against the per-level maxima and report the first excess. Group display pointers omit their own trailing index, while message keys retain it. The separate `FEHLER_LAUFENDE_NR_ZU_GROSS` USB/multi-form counter remains outside the single-document scope. Interpreter reconciliation: [IF27](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if27).

**Placement-boundary correction (dual-strategy document-conversion probe, 2026-07-26).** A field's terminal coordinate is not a repetition axis and must be exactly 1. A root field at terminal coordinate 2 and a nested field at terminal coordinate 3 are both refused by the Kernel's V1-to-V2 document conversion with `AssertionError("expected repetition 1 for field, but got …")`, before dynamic-Groovy or static-Java validation can run. This is distinct from a group coordinate above its effective maximum, which remains representable for formal validation. The portable transport therefore refuses the exact field-terminal class as `INVALID_FIELD_REPETITION`; this is a Kernel-matching corrective boundary, not interpreter runtime semantics. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.OverRepetitionFormalGateDiffTest.fieldTerminalCoordinateOtherThanOneIsRejectedBeforeEitherKernelStrategy`; `interpreter.DocumentTransportTest.readRefusesPositiveFieldTerminalCoordinatesAboveOneWithDedicatedDiagnostic` on JVM + Node.)*

**Coordinate-width boundary (compiled API characterization, 2026-07-26).** Every public `DocumentPointer.of` overload in Kernel 30.8.1 accepts repetition coordinates as primitive/boxed signed 32-bit integers, and `repetitionIndexes()` returns `List<Integer>`; there is no long-coordinate overload. `Int.MAX_VALUE` round-trips through the exact-pointer factory. This does not impose a repetition maximum—the formal rules above still own effective maxima—but it does establish the transport domain against which a JavaScript façade must guard: a larger JavaScript safe integer is not representable by either the Kernel pointer contract or the portable Kotlin `Int` storage and must be refused before numeric narrowing. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.OverRepetitionFormalGateDiffTest.kernelDocumentPointerCoordinateDomainIsSigned32Bit`.)*

**It is an ADDRESS-FORMAL gate that runs BEFORE scalar conversion — not a later annotation over an already scalar-checked cell (source + dual-strategy differential, SPEC-2026-07-23-13, 2026-07-23).** `CheckCommand.formalePruefung` invokes `FormalChecker.checkIndices` *before* value conversion and inserts a cell/group into the `ValidationCache` **only when the address gate succeeds**, so an over-limit coordinate never reaches scalar/custom checking and is absent from the evaluation cache. The observable consequences (each dual-kernel-route + JVM/Node locked):

- The first over-limit coordinate supplies `zuGrosseZeile`/`zuGrosseKontextnummer` **in place of** any scalar/custom cause — an over-limit descendant that is *valid*, *malformed*, *absent*, or *registered-custom* all expose over-repetition, never a format/custom result. A registered `CustomFieldType` callback the kernel would otherwise invoke on that cell is **not invoked** (proven with an instrumented validator on both kernel strategies + the interpreter). An **absent** over-limit descendant reads **unavailable**, not clean empty — a per-row rule referencing it is suppressed, not fired on empty→0.
- The ancestry walk is complete: an in-cap **inner** coordinate beneath an over-limit **outer** ancestor is still over-repetition (terminal-axis-only checking is wrong); an in-cap sibling stays ordinary.
- Because the over-limit cell/row is never in the cache, it is **outside every star aggregate / quantifier / count domain**: `Sum`, `NumberOfFilledFields`, and `NumberOfFilledGroups(G*)` range over the in-cap (declared-range) rows only — **clean and definite, never poisoned** (with rows `10.00`, `20.00` in cap and an over-limit `99.00`, `Sum` is `30.00` and the count is `2`). The immutable physical over-limit row nonetheless stays **instantiated**: on these deeper-than-root fixtures it emits `zuGrosseZeile` and remains `GroupFilled`-visible structural content for its non-repeatable ancestors. (This is distinct from the index-field mandatory/uniqueness rules `AutogeneratedRulesService` runs in the later preliminary-rule phase.)
- **…and it is the OPERAND'S extent, not one carrier's projection: the FIXED (unstarred) group operand excludes an over-limit cell on every carrier that admits one (tri-engine differential, 2026-08-31, a12-kernel-lean's `EXP-2026-08-31-02`).** The bullet above measured the STARRED carriers only. Over a nonrepeatable shell whose repeatable descendants cap at 2, all six admitted carriers answer as if the over-limit cell did not exist, at either repetition depth: `NumberOfFilledFields(Shell)` is `0` with the only filled cell at `Parcels[3]` or at `Cartons[1,3]` and `1` with it one index lower; `NumberOfValueInFields("KEEP" In Shell)` and its Boolean form behave the same; and with an in-capacity `5` beside an over-limit `7`, `Sum` is `5`, `MaxValue` is `5`, `NumberOfDifferentValues` is `1`, and (reversed) `MinValue` is `7`. The answers are **definite**, read off a candidate ladder of exact equalities rather than from a single positive rule — a rule that only fires on the positive answer cannot separate `0` from *unavailable*, since an unavailable count leaves both `> 0` and `< 1` silent (the discriminator a12-kernel-lean's checkpoint contributed).
- **The mechanism is exclusion from the domain, not toleration inside it — established on a discriminating case rather than inferred from the numbers above.** "Definitely 0" fits *removed from the extent* and equally fits *classified unavailable and not counted*, and the two differ wherever unavailability propagates. A malformed cell separates them: `Sum(Shell)` with a non-numeric cell in an **in-capacity** row is unavailable (no exact-equality candidate fires at all), while the identical cell one index **above capacity** leaves `Sum` definite at the in-capacity value. So an over-limit cell is not an excused member of the domain; it is not in the domain being classified. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.GroupOperandOverLimitExtentDiffTest` — the interpreter agrees with both kernel strategies on every row, so this shape needed no interpreter fix, which was not knowable before measuring: our own over-limit locks covered the starred carriers only.)*
- **…and the STARRED spelling answers identically, the empty in-capacity domain is a definite ZERO on EVERY aggregate carrier, and the malformed split holds on the COUNT carrier too (same differential, 2026-08-31 — the three limits the entry above stated; the empty-domain half extended from `Sum` to the whole family later the same day).** The starred/fixed equality is asserted as an equality between the two spellings **in one run**, per row, rather than as two tables compared from memory: `NumberOfFilledFields(Notes)` and `NumberOfFilledFields(Notes/Parcels*)` agree on every document, as do `Sum(Amounts)` and `Sum(Amounts/Charges*)` — including on the malformed pair. It cost a12-kernel-lean three conformance cases (`SPEC-2026-08-31-10`, their `LF124`): they had split fixed from starred precisely to claim only what our measurement covered, and the only support for the starred side was a case written from their own implementation, so a careful-looking refusal to over-claim had promoted an untested claim to a design invariant. **The empty domain closes a limit neither project held a row on**: our own ladder had avoided it by mixing values, and their reproduction carried no `== 0` member, so `Sum` read unavailable there in exactly the way a definite `0` also would. Measured `0`, on both spellings, both with no repeatable row at all and — the discriminating document — with content present in the document but entirely above capacity, which is empty only *after* the projection. So the exclusion does not make the aggregate non-evaluable. **Extended 2026-08-31 from `Sum` to the whole family — `MaxValue`, `MinValue`, `NumberOfDifferentValues`, `NumberOfFilledFields` and `NumberOfValueInFields` all read a definite `0` there too**, on both documents. That extension exists because a12-kernel-lean published an observed SPLIT (`Sum` definite, the extrema and the distinct count `UNAVAILABLE`) and retracted it within the day: their extrema ladders ran `5`/`7` and their distinct-count ladders `1`/`2`, so none could express the only value that could have been the answer, and the "split" was their instrument's silence (their `LF125`). The reading is also the *plausible* one — an extremum over an empty set is undefined in most languages — which is why it drew no scrutiny on either side, and it is measured here on our own fixture through our own three engines rather than adopted from their report. **The transferable check is per CARRIER, not per model**: they had verified rule *presence* (counting admitted rules) and still missed per-carrier *coverage*, because the two carriers they read first happened to carry their zero member. Two of our own ladders had the identical shortfall and read a value only because those documents were non-empty; `read()` now refuses a ladder that cannot express `0`. **And the count carrier splits where `Sum` splits**: a malformed cell in capacity leaves `NumberOfFilledFields` unavailable, the identical cell above capacity leaves it at `1` — measured rather than carried across from `Sum`, which is what the peer asked for after recording that its own count behaviour there was an account rather than a measurement.
- **…and it is the OPERAND'S extent on the starred FIELD list too — the spelling these carriers are actually typed for, which every row above had skipped (same differential, 2026-08-31).** All the rows above are *group* operands, fixed and starred, and "group operand" was allowed to stand for "operand". That substitution is not a near miss: the catalog types all five aggregates over a **field** list (`Sum` a `number-field-list`, the extrema a `sortable-field-list`, `NumberOfDifferentValues` a `homogeneous-field-list`, `NumberOfValueInFields` a `literal` + `field-list`), and the typed surface reaches a group only through the starred `GroupListRef` — so `Charges*/Fee` is the primary form and the group operand is the variant, making the unmeasured half the one a real author writes. Measured: `Sum` `5`, `MaxValue` `5`, `MinValue` `7`, `NumberOfDifferentValues` `1` and `NumberOfValueInFields(5 In …)` `0` with the over-limit cell excluded, each against a both-in-capacity control (`12`/`7`/`5`/`2`/`1`), and the malformed split holds identically (in capacity → unavailable; the same cell above capacity → `5`). The value count needs the **reversed** document (in capacity `7`, over limit `5`) because counting `5` over the forward one answers `1` either way — a row that cannot separate the two readings measures nothing.
- **…and the COMPUTATION arm separates the mechanism on a WELL-FORMED document, because the operand's formal error rides its own channel (tri-engine differential, 2026-08-31, a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-08-31-11`; `OverLimitOperandComputeArmDiffTest`).** Every row above is the *validation* arm, and the entry stated its limits without saying so. Under `compute` the over-limit cell's address defect appears in `formalErrorsInOperands` — `zuGrosseZeile` at the row plus `zuGrosseKontextnummer` at the operand cell — while the computation returns `cleared: false, errored: false` with a definite value (the in-capacity total, `5`, against a both-in-capacity control of `12`). So "the formal error is present in the operand and does not reach the result" is one observation on one document with no malformed cell in it, where the validation arm needs the malformed pair to say the same thing. **Three further facts, each measured against the rival that fits the other rows.** (a) **An unavailable computation is ABSENT, not zero**: a malformed cell *in* capacity yields **no outcome at all** for the target plus `zahlHatUngueltigeZeichen` in the channel, so an emitted `0` is always a real zero and can never be unavailability rendered as the identity value — which is what makes the emptied-domain zeros above readable rather than ambiguous. (b) **The channel is operand-SCOPED, not document-wide**: an over-limit row in a group no computation reads draws nothing there, measured on a row left empty so only the group walk could speak for it. (c) **Its scope reaches the operand's whole ANCESTRY, not its parent group**: with the operand two repetition levels down and the *outer* row over capacity, the channel carries three messages — `zuGrosseZeile` at the outer group and `zuGrosseKontextnummer` at both the intermediate row and the operand cell. **Those sites are pinned, not read off the code multiset**, which cannot settle them because one code lands twice; the lock asserts the full `code@pointer` list, and it makes [IG145](INTERPRETER-GAPS.md) visible in passing — both group sites lose their own row index in the house projection (`…/Items` is really row 3, `…/Splits` really row 1) while the field site keeps `Splits[1]`. Rules (b) and (c) both fit every earlier row, in which the over-limit row simply *was* the operand's parent; each needed the document that separates them. **This arm found a live interpreter defect that the validation arm's repeated green could not see** ([IF315](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if315)): our compute path filtered the group walk with a set of operand *field* paths, so `zuGrosseZeile` was unreachable under `compute` for any model.
- **An over-limit row ABSORBS every violation beneath it, and the finding set covers what the document WROTE (tri-engine differential, 2026-08-31, a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-08-30-10`).** When the violated level is below the root, the outermost violated row draws **one** `zuGrosseZeile` at its group, plus one `zuGrosseKontextnummer` per written node under it — each instantiated descendant row and each present cell. An over-limit row nested **inside** that subtree draws **no row code of its own and is named nowhere**: over `Invoices[2]`▸`Periods[2]`, a document filling `Invoices[3]/Periods[3]/Label` emits one `zuGrosseZeile@/Billing[1]/Invoices` and four node findings, and `Periods` — which exceeds its own capacity of 2 — appears only as an address, never as a violated row. The absorption is charged to nesting rather than to the fixture by the outer-only control, identical but for the inner index, which produces the same single row code. Declarations contribute nothing: the same over-limit row written `{}` emits the row code **alone**. And the suppression is confined to the violated subtree, not the document — a non-numeric cell two levels below the over-limit row exposes over-repetition instead of `zahlHatUngueltigeZeichen`, while the identical value in an in-capacity sibling row reports it normally. **The consequence a reimplementation gets wrong is that the formal channel is not monotone in the document:** fixing the outer row reveals an inner violation no message had named, so a consumer deriving the violated-group set from the message stream sees one group where two are violated, and a naive per-row check finds both.
- **…and our formatted ADDRESS is lossy exactly here, which the formatted differential cannot see (measured in the same run).** The kernel gives each instantiated descendant row its own coordinate on one path — `[1,3,1]`, `[1,3,2]`, `[1,3,3]` at `/Billing/Invoices/Periods` — while `formatPointer` indexes every segment but the last, right for a field (whose terminal coordinate is not a repetition axis, per the placement-boundary correction above) and wrong for a repeatable group node, so all three render `/Billing[1]/Invoices[3]/Periods`. So an engine attributing a group-node finding to the wrong descendant row would compare **equal** in every `adapter/laws` differential, which compares formatted addresses. The lock therefore pins the **kernel's own** addresses across both codegen strategies beside the formatted comparison; the rendering itself is [IG145](INTERPRETER-GAPS.md). *(Corrected 2026-08-31, same day: this first named the probe artifact and dmtool's addresses among the affected surfaces. They are not — both prefer A12's canonical exact form, which is faithful here (`[1,3,1]`→`…/Periods`, `[1,3,2]`→`…/Periods[2]`, `[1,3,3]`→`…/Periods[3]`) and fall back to the house form only for a pointer with no repetition indexes. The lossy projection is tool-owned and reaches the differentials and the committed corpus keys only.)* *(Locked: `adapter.laws.NestedOverLimitAbsorptionDiffTest` — four tests, all three engines agreeing on every formatted row.)*
- **The same exclusion holds in the index-keyed PARALLEL ITERATION** (the §9 outer join, validation and compute — dual-kernel-route, 2026-07-24): an over-limit row is not in the `IndexFieldCache`, so its index value is **not a join key** and a reference to it reads **UNMATCHED**, not its value. Observable in COMPUTE: a calc `Total*/Amount = [../Demand/Amount] + [../Supply/Amount]` whose `Total[Extra]` key matches only an OVER-LIMIT `Demand[Extra]` row reads that side **empty-as-0** (`Total[Extra]` = `0`), never the over-limit cell's poison — the reader computes cleanly. The exclusion covers the joined groups, the common-parent rows, and a repeatable **frame** row above a joined group (`/Plan/X(frame)/A ⋈ B`), all the same way. In VALIDATION a per-row cross-group compare over the over-limit key does not fire (its cell reads unavailable either way, so the interpreter already agreed there). *(Interpreter reconciliation IF220: the compute divergence was the interpreter's `parallelContexts` join reading the rows unfiltered, so the over-limit row joined and its cell poisoned the reader; fixed by the same [`overLimitRows`] exclusion the star domain uses, across `indexMap` / `parentRowsOf` / the frame-row expansion — no second walker.)*

Interpreter reconciliation (SPEC-2026-07-23-13): the per-cell gate order + ancestry walk already matched (the phase separators landed as agreement locks). The original **observed divergence** was that over-limit repeatable rows leaked into the interpreter's star-aggregate row domain; the parallel-iteration join was the same class. Both were fixed at the shared document-owned row-domain root. The 2026-07-26 R2.8 increment measured the non-repeatable sibling and generalized the same decision from authored `declaredReps` to one group-only effective-bound map: a declared cap for bounded repeatable groups, implicit 1 for non-repeatable groups, and no entry for unbounded repeatable groups or field terminals. That map now drives exact structural-code selection, ordinary-check suppression, and aggregate/join exclusion. A field's terminal coordinate remains outside runtime semantics because Kernel document conversion refuses it before validation; placement decoding owns that gate. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.OverRepetitionFormalGateDiffTest` — phase separators, fixed-group emission, and repeatable/fixed aggregate-exclusion siblings across dynamic-Groovy · static-Java · interpreter; `interpreter.OverRepetitionFormalGateMultiplatformTest` on JVM + Node; the parallel-iteration domain by `adapter.laws.OverLimitParallelIterationDiffTest` and `interpreter.OverLimitParallelIterationTest`.)*

## `mandatoryGroup` (`FEHLER_PFLICHTKONTEXT`) is a DEAD code in 30.8.1 — defined but never emitted; a group cannot be declared mandatory (source-verified 2026-06-26) <a id="kf59"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a dead-code inventory fact (defined, never emitted) with its re-open trigger; nothing to fold.

The runtime formal-error code **`mandatoryGroup`** (`IFormaleFehlerConstants.FEHLER_PFLICHTKONTEXT`, "auto generated rule: mandatory group") is **referenced nowhere** in the kernel `30.8.1` source except its own constant definition (Java + the TS twin) — **no code, codegen template, or generated validator emits it**. And **no DM-JSON property declares a *group* mandatory**: the md-serializer and the `a12-kernel-mm` metamodels carry mandatory/`requirednessConfig` only on **fields** (→ the `mandatoryField` rules `AutogeneratedRulesService` generates, KERNEL-FINDINGS §4), not on groups. So `mandatoryGroup` **cannot fire on any loadable DM model** — an unemitted code over an undeclarable property (a probe accordingly returned empty). The interpreter correctly never emits it; this is **parity by construction**, not a gap. *Re-open trigger:* a kernel upgrade that wires `FEHLER_PFLICHTKONTEXT` to an emission site **and** a group-mandatory declaration (re-check on the next [`KERNEL-UPGRADE`](KERNEL-UPGRADE.md)).

## `multiSelect` value uniqueness (`FEHLER_MULTI_SELECT` = `uniqueValue`) is DEAD code in 30.8.1 — generated by NEITHER strategy (source-verified 2026-06-27) <a id="kf60"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a dead-code inventory fact (generated by neither strategy) with its re-open trigger; nothing to fold.

A `usageType == "multi-select"` group (KERNEL-FINDINGS "group templates", the `MultiSelectGroupRule` consistency shape) is described as carrying an auto value-uniqueness check — "no value selected twice". In kernel `30.8.1` **that check is generated by no evaluation path**, so it never fires on any loadable model:

- **md-RUNTIME** (`AutogeneratedRulesService`, the `IDocumentRtService` autogen provider): generates only `MANDATORY_FIELD` / `UNIQUE_FIELD` (index) / `SOLITARY_FIELD` rules — there is **no multi-select method** at all. (Confirmed by differential: a 3-row multi-select group with duplicate values fires `mandatoryField` on an empty row but **nothing** for the duplicate — `adapter.laws.MultiSelectUniquenessDiffTest`.)
- **Groovy CODEGEN** (`CodeGenRuleDefinition`): has a `case UNIQUE_VALUE → "FEHLER_MULTI_SELECT"`, but that case is **provably unreachable**. `RuleInfo.getAutogenType()` returns `((IAutogeneratedRule) rule).getGenerationType()`, and the **only** `IAutogeneratedRule` implementations (`MandatoryFieldRuleImpl` / `UniqueFieldRuleImpl` / `SolitaryFieldRuleImpl`) return `MANDATORY_FIELD` / `UNIQUE_FIELD` / `SOLITARY_FIELD` — **none returns `UNIQUE_VALUE`**, and no code constructs such a rule. So the `case UNIQUE_VALUE` switch arm is dead.

**The COMPLETE `usageType: "multi-select"` handling map (full read/write trace, 2026-06-27).** Tracing every site that writes or reads the flag across the whole kernel shows it is a **model + editor + consistency marker ONLY** — no evaluator touches it:

| layer | site | what it does with `multi-select` |
|---|---|---|
| write | `GroupSerializer` | serializes `usageType` to DM-JSON |
| write | editor / `DocumentModelExpand`+`CollapseService` | sets / propagates / unsets across include expansion |
| read (consistency) | `MultiSelectGroupRule` | **the only active handler** — validates the group SHAPE at `checkConsistency` (repeatable · one enum/string field · required · not-index) → `DOCUMENT_MODEL_MULTI_SELECT_*` problems |
| read (model→runtime) | `ValidationModelConverter:194-209` | stores `usageType` in the validation-model `Group`, but only the `A12_ATTACHMENT` branch *acts* on it — multi-select is stored then **never consumed** |
| read (attachment-only) | `DecorationField/GroupModelJoiner`, `ExpandService:689` | all gated on `A12_ATTACHMENT`/`cockpit_attachment` — never multi-select |
| runtime eval (`kernel-rt`) | — | reads `usageType` **nowhere** (only the dead `FEHLER_MULTI_SELECT` constant) |
| codegen (`kernel-tool`) | — | reads `usageType` **nowhere** (only the dead `UNIQUE_VALUE_ERROR_ID`); **no `.stg` template emits it** |
| generated code | — | no `.stg`/`.groovy` references `multi-select`/`uniqueValue` |

So `usageType: "multi-select"` drives only the UI checkbox-list widget + the `checkConsistency` shape check; it reaches the validation (runtime) model via `ValidationModelConverter` but `kernel-rt` never reads it back (dead storage). For ANY document-validation evaluator (runtime or codegen-equivalent) it is a no-op beyond the shape check.

`uniqueValue` is therefore **vestigial** — the runtime-and-codegen sibling of the dead `mandatoryGroup` above. Both kernel strategies produce nothing, so the interpreter (matching BOTH per the CLAUDE.md #1 rule) correctly does **not** fire it — **parity by construction**, NOT a gap, and NOT a runtime-vs-codegen divergence (they agree: dead in both). **Corroborated from the model side (2026-06-27 sweep):** all **6** real multi-select groups in the 2025.06-ext5 workspaces are the minimal shape (`repeatability` + `usageType: "multi-select"` + one field — **no** `indexFieldName` / `unique` / extra property that could trigger a uniqueness rule), and the **`a12-kernel-mm` MM_Group metamodel** defines `multi-select` as merely a `usageType` **enum value** (beside `attachment`/`complexType`) with **no uniqueness constraint attached** (zero `uniqueValue`/`FEHLER_MULTI_SELECT` anywhere in the metamodels). Source + runtime + codegen + real models + metamodel all agree. The kernel's *consistency/editor* layer still validates the multi-select group **shape** (`MultiSelectGroupRule`) and the UI widget still prevents duplicate selection — but neither produces a `validateFull`/runtime `uniqueValue` message. *Re-open trigger:* a kernel upgrade that adds a multi-select method to `AutogeneratedRulesService` **or** an `IAutogeneratedRule` returning `UNIQUE_VALUE` (re-check on the next [`KERNEL-UPGRADE`](KERNEL-UPGRADE.md)). *(Locked: `adapter.laws.MultiSelectUniquenessDiffTest`.)*

## `IRule.getCustomRefErrorEntitiesIfFilled/IfNotFilled` (modeler-defined error-entity attribution) is UNWIRED in 30.8.1 (source-verified 2026-06-26) <a id="kf61"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an unwired kernel API slot (feature not supported in 30.8.1) with its re-open trigger; nothing to fold.

A rule can, *in the metamodel*, carry **custom-ref error entities** (`MM_Common_v2` defines a `CustomRefErrorEntities` slot with `CustomRefErrorEntityIfFilled`/`IfNotFilled`) — modeler-defined relative paths that refine **which field(s) a fired rule blames**, chosen by the referenced field's filled-state (the "nichtangabe-fehlerfelder"). But the feature is **not supported in kernel 30.8.1**: the md-model rule mapping (`kernel-md-model/.../mapping/Rule.java`) returns `List.of()` for both accessors, commented *"update implementation when customRefErrorEntities get supported in A12"* (A12K-2281 / A12K-2361); the `IRule` default and every autogenerated rule impl (Mandatory / UniqueField / SolitaryField) also return empty; and `RuleParser` short-circuits the candidate-relpath expansion whenever both are empty — i.e. **always**. So a loaded rule **never** carries custom-ref error entities, and the kernel **always** uses its default automatic error-entity attribution. The interpreter attributing a fired rule to its declared error entity is therefore **parity by construction** (the default path the kernel always takes); the modeler-defined refinement is moot until the kernel wires it. *Re-open trigger:* a kernel upgrade that lands A12K-2281/2361 (re-check on the next [`KERNEL-UPGRADE`](KERNEL-UPGRADE.md)).

**Extended 2026-09-13, measured: a STORED model cannot even carry the member, which is a shorter chain than the one above.** Adding `customRefErrorEntitiesIfFilled` to a rule's DM-JSON body makes the model **UNREADABLE** — A12's own deserializer refuses the property, so no declaration is examined and no consistency verdict is reached at all. That settles the reachability of the two codes `MVK_REF_ERROR_ENTITY_IF_FILLED_NOT_REFERENCED` and `MVK_REF_ERROR_ENTITY_IF_NOT_FILLED_NOT_REFERENCED` (`RuleParser.hasValidCustomErrorEntities`): nothing a stored model can spell reaches them, so they are not candidates for a Kernel-free checker. The accessor argument is the second, independent link and it was attacked rather than cited — every implementor in the kernel's main sources returns `List.of()` unconditionally, with no branch: the `IRule` default, `MandatoryRuleImpl`, `UniqueFieldRuleImpl`, `SolitaryFieldRuleImpl` and the md-model `mapping.Rule` (`RuleInfo` delegates to whichever of those it wraps). The law those codes carry is also not what the ledger described — it is not about error-message text but about two declared lists of relative paths, each entry of which must appear among the paths the rule's CONDITION references.

## §8 supplement — the ==/!= string-enum compatibility matrix (display-texts, probe-confirmed 2026-06-17) <a id="kf62"></a>

> Fold: folded → §8.

For `==`/`!=` between direct string/enum fields, the kernel first classifies each Enumeration by its **effective display remapping** (`IEnumerationType.hasDisplayValues`), not by whether label nodes were authored. No labels and identity-only labels (display equals stored token for every value) are effectively textless; either may compare with a plain String or another effectively textless Enumeration. A genuinely display-bearing Enumeration is incompatible with those profiles (`MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_ENUM_TO_STRING`). Two display-bearing Enumerations need not have identical declarations: disjoint and partially overlapping maps are accepted, but in every shared locale their overlap must be a partial bijection — a shared stored token cannot map to different displays and a shared display cannot denote different stored tokens (`MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_ENUM_TO_ENUM`). An identity pair still participates in that consistency test once another member makes both profiles display-bearing. Literal-domain checking and category projection remain separate. (Source `IEnumerationType.hasDisplayValues`, `FieldUtils.isEnumWithDisplayValues`, `CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkEnumVsStringType`, and `CheckEntityListenUtils.checkDisplayValues`; a category comparison is exempt.) *(Locked: `validate.laws.EnumComparabilityLawsTest`.)*

## §8 supplement — three enum-ish kinds: "extensible enum" is an IStringType quality, NOT a field type (source-verified 2026-06-17) <a id="kf63"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a type-system/model-structure classification (what is a field type vs a client-SPI quality), outside the evaluation scope.

Three distinct concepts, easy to conflate:

- **Closed `EnumerationType`** — a fixed value set; a normal DM-JSON field type (the md `EnumerationType` DTO: values/categories/errorMessage/alphabeticalSorting/sValue — *no* extensible flag).
- **Extensible (non-closed) enumeration** — **not a field type at all**: an **`IStringType` with `isExtensibleEnum() == true`** (parser `FieldUtils.isExtensibleEnum` = `type instanceof IStringType && isExtensibleEnum()`; `isLikeString` = string ∪ enum ∪ ext-enum). `isExtensibleEnum()` is a **client-SPI/runtime quality** — `IStringType` is "intended to be implemented by clients", the kernel's md `StringType` **defaults it `false`**, and there is **no DM-JSON property** for it (its open/dynamic values are served at runtime, e.g. via `DynamicEnumerationService`). So a DM-JSON field is **just a `StringType` — fully buildable and modelkit-authorable**; the "extensible" quality itself is unauthorable via DM-JSON (always `false` in a plain model) but doesn't need to be: `ValidType`/`InvalidType` accept the field **because it is-a string** (`isLikeString`), which the N7 `Valid(CustomerName, "EMail")` validExample already exercises. **NOT a modelkit gap.**
- **Dynamic / table-backed enumeration** — the genuinely **un-buildable** one (the `ValueNotConsistent` finding below): values from an external table, not DM-JSON-serializable.

(The model/editor metamodel `MM_Common` carries an "ExtensibleEnumerationType" config — maxLength/displayValues — and form-model/UI notions like `fieldConfigurationEntry`/`externalEnumeration` exist, but those are **tooling/FM layers outside rulekit's DM-JSON scope**, not runtime DM field types.) *(Corrects an earlier draft that wrongly called extensible enums "un-buildable" and cited `IEnumerationType.isExtensible` — it conflated the extensible `IStringType` quality with the dynamic/table-backed enum.)*

## §9 supplement — ordinary-iteration negative admission is level- and OPERAND-sensitive, and the host conversion is the separator (probed 2026-07-25; a12-kernel-lean SPEC-2026-07-24-02) <a id="kf64"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

**`MVK_NEG_CONDITION_IN_ITERATION` is not a fixed list of "negative" operators — admission is decided per ordinary iteration level, and for a direct Number field against an immediate literal it turns on the literal's HOST-CONVERTED integer form.** The kernel's `IterationNotValidVisitor` enumerates the relevant levels and applies connective rules (`And` needs one child that both references and is admitted at that level; `Or` needs every child to), then dispatches a per-operator/per-operand leaf test. `FeldOperationUtil` supplies the literal conversion: `Double.parseDouble` → `Math.round` → `(int)`. Measured against the real kernel (`rule check`, the accept/reject oracle) on a repeatable `Items` group:

**Group-list star correction (real-kernel accept/reject + tri-differential, 2026-07-30; a12-kernel-lean SPEC-2026-07-26-01).** At a queried ordinary-iteration level, a starred group-list operand references only the captured prefix strictly above its first star: `AtLeastOneGroupFilled(G*)` is admitted there exactly when every list operand references that level, so a fixed peer outside the prefix makes the mixed list unguarded; `NoGroupFilled(G*)` is unguarded whenever any operand references the level. A leaf outside the captured prefix contributes no reference there. The existing connective rules then compose those leaf classifications: an independent positive iterating sibling under `And` admits the negative group list, while the same sibling under `Or` does not. `StarredGroupListIterationAdmissionLawsTest` locks the five-way static matrix (star-only positive admission, mixed fixed/star positive rejection, star-only negative rejection, guarded `And` admission, and corresponding `Or` rejection); `StarredGroupListIterationScopeDiffTest` plus the JVM/Node `StarredGroupListIterationScopeTest` lock the legal runtime control, where `Regions/Checks*` binds the exact `Regions` ancestry and reports only the populated outer row. This reuses the existing first-star binding topology and adds no client-side visitor.

| condition (rule group `/Order/Items`) | admission | why |
|---|---|---|
| `[Count] == 0`, `>= 0`, `<= 0` — and `0 == [Count]`, `0 >= …`, `0 <= …` | **REJECTED** | converted literal is zero; symmetric in operand order |
| `[Count] > 0`, `< 0`, `!= 0` | admitted | strict comparison / ordinary `!=` |
| `[Count] == 5`, `>= 5`, `<= 5`, `5 == [Count]` | admitted | converted-nonzero literal |
| `[UnitWeight] == 0.40`, `== 0.49`, `0.40 == [UnitWeight]` | **REJECTED** | `Math.round` → 0 |
| `[UnitWeight] == 0.50`, `0.50 == …`, `== 0.60`, `== 1.00` | admitted | `Math.round(0.5)` → **1** |
| `[UnitWeight] == -0.50`, `== -0.40` | **REJECTED** | `Math.round(-0.5)` → **0** — half-up toward +∞ |
| `Abs([Count]) == 0` · `MinValue(Count, UnitWeight) == 0` · `MaxValue(…) == 0` · `Length(Sku) == 0` | **REJECTED** | direct field *operations* keep the zero-sensitive partition |
| `Length(Sku) > 0`, `== 3` | admitted | strict / nonzero, same partition |
| **`[Count] + 0 == 0`** | **admitted** | top-level arithmetic is an `ICompositeOperation` — no direct-operand branch |

**The ±0.5 pair is the sharpest control**: `0.50` admitted and `-0.50` rejected pins `Math.round`'s half-up-toward-+∞ semantics, ruling out HALF_EVEN (0 for both) and away-from-zero (1 for both). **The composite separator is the second**: wrapping a field in arithmetic flips static admission while leaving runtime arithmetic identical — so "flatten arithmetic to its field references" is a wrong model of this classifier.

**Scope of what is locked here (deliberately partial).** `RuleGroupIterationLawsTest` covers the direct-Number partition, both operand orders, the conversion boundary including the negative-half asymmetry, direct `Abs`/`MinValue`/`MaxValue`/`Length`, and the composite separator. **Not yet locked** from SPEC-2026-07-24-02's full matrix: `RangeAsNumber`/`FieldValueAsNumber` scope+runtime controls, temporal component extraction, the ordered two-operand `DifferenceIn{Months,Years,Days,Hours,Minutes,Seconds}` family, entity-list/aggregate partitions (`FirstFilledValue`, distinct/value count, `NumberOfValueInFields`, `SumOfProducts`), mixed-level any-literal rejection, and the filter-reference exclusion. rulekit **delegates** the visitor to the kernel (no reimplementation), so these are boundary locks, not a ported classifier.

**Correction (2026-07-25): the `(int)` narrowing is NOT unrepresentable — it is authorable on any scale-0 field, and is now locked.** This entry previously claimed the `2^32` wrap and long saturation "need a literal the scale gate (`MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES`) or the grammar rejects first". That was inference, and it is wrong: the dec-places gate compares the literal's *fractional* digits against the field's scale, so on a **scale-0** field a bare integer literal matches trivially and reaches the partition, where it is judged on its **narrowed** value.

| condition (`Count` is scale-0) | admission | why |
|---|---|---|
| `[Count] == 4294967296` (2^32) | **REJECTED** | `(int)` narrows to **0** — a literal of 4,294,967,296 classified as zero |
| `[Count] == 4294967297` (2^32+1) | admitted | narrows to 1 |
| `[Count] == 9223372036854775808` (2^63) | admitted | `Math.round` saturates at `Long.MAX_VALUE`, narrowing to −1 |
| `[Count] == 9223372036854775807` (2^63−1) | admitted | parses UP to 2^63, which **exceeds `Long.MAX_VALUE`** → `Math.round` saturates DOWN to 2^63−1, low 32 bits all set → **−1** |
| `[Count] == -9223372036854775807` (−(2^63−1)) | **REJECTED** | parses DOWN to −2^63, which **IS `Long.MIN_VALUE`** → passes through unsaturated, low 32 bits clear → **0** |
| `[Count] == -9223372036854773760` (−(2^63−2048)) | admitted | one representable step in (doubles are 2048 apart at 2^63) — residue **2048** |

**The long boundary is asymmetric, and the cause is the TWO'S-COMPLEMENT RANGE, not binary64 granularity** *(basis: the discriminating observation is the pair of intermediate values, measured — `parseDouble` returns ∓2^63 for BOTH literals while `Math.round` returns `Long.MAX_VALUE` for one and an unchanged `Long.MIN_VALUE` for the other, so a granularity explanation predicts symmetric outcomes and is refuted by the observed split)*. Neither ±(2^63−1) is representable as a double — both parse onto ∓2^63 — so **the parse step is symmetric there and decides nothing**. The split is the **saturation**, and it happens on one side only because the long range is lopsided: `Long.MAX_VALUE` is 2^63−**1** (so +2^63 overflows and saturates down, landing on all-ones low 32 bits → −1, admitted) while `Long.MIN_VALUE` is −2^63 **exactly** (so −2^63 passes through untouched, low 32 bits clear → 0, rejected). Binary64 granularity is only what gets both literals *to* ±2^63, and what makes the third row's nearest representable neighbour 2048 away.

**This is the sharpest separator against exact 64-bit integer arithmetic** — the default in a Rust/Python/BigInteger reimplementation, where −(2^63−1) mod 2^32 = 1 would ADMIT what the kernel rejects. The positive row cannot catch it (every account agrees at +(2^63−1)), and the third row is a required control: without it the pair reads as "the negative boundary always rejects", which is false. *(a12-kernel-lean SPEC-2026-07-25-03 predicted all three rows; measured against the real kernel here — locked `RuleGroupIterationLawsTest.theLongBoundaryIsAsymmetricBecauseTheTwosComplementRangeIs`. **The rows survived a corrected cause twice:** their first account, and then my own restatement of it, both blamed representability/absence-of-saturation; the measurements never changed, only the explanation — a reminder that a right table can carry a wrong mechanism.)*

**The ±1 pair straddling 2^32 is the sharpest control of the three separators**, and better than the ±0.5 pair: two literals differing by one, both astronomically far from zero, land on opposite sides of the whole partition. A widening or saturating conversion admits both, so the pair pins 32-bit truncation specifically *(locked: `RuleGroupIterationLawsTest.theThirtyTwoBitNarrowingIsObservable`)*.

## §9 supplement — the seven digit gates, named once (glossary, 2026-07-25) <a id="kf65"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a naming aid for the surrounding entries, not a kernel law of its own.

**The word "digits" covers seven distinct quantities on four axes.** They were conflated across a whole cross-project exchange, costing rounds in which each side "corrected" the other about a *different* number. Cite the name, never the bare word:

| name | value | axis | oracle |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fieldScaleCap` | **14** | field config — max declarable `maxFractionalDigits` | model check (MVK-less message) |
| `fieldScaleOrdering` | `min ≤ max` | field config | `MVK_FRACT_DIGITS_INVALID` |
| `enteredValueTotalDigits` | **15** | runtime formal check on an entered VALUE, integer+fractional, **generic on every number field** | `stelligkeitZuLang` |
| `amountIntegerCap` | **15 − scale** | runtime, **amount-trait only** | `zahlZuvieleVorkommastellen` |
| `literalFracDigits` | **≤ the field's scale** | static gate on an authored comparison literal — **suppressible** | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` |
| `literalTotalDigits` | **ungated** (19 observed) | static — a 19-digit literal passes model check | measured, `== 9223372036854775808` |
| `shortestLiftingDecimal` | **17** frac digits | IEEE-754 property, not a kernel gate — the shortest decimal in `[½−2⁻⁵⁵, ½)` | conversion chain |

Two traps the naming prevents: `enteredValueTotalDigits` (15) is **not** a literal-length gate — it bounds *entered values*, so it never explains a literal being accepted or refused; and the 55/57-character exact decimal of `½−2⁻⁵⁵` is a **notation artifact**, not a required digit count — any decimal in the interval works, and the shortest needs 17.

## §9 supplement — the host conversion's PARSE step lifts a below-half decimal onto one half, and the witness IS authorable via the suppressible dec-places gate (measured 2026-07-25; answers a12-kernel-lean SPEC-2026-07-25-02) <a id="kf66"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

**The conversion `Double.parseDouble` → `Math.round` → `(int)` has TWO rounding steps, and the first one is the surprising one.** `Math.round` does not lift a double strictly below one half (that was Java ≤ 6's `floor(x + 0.5)`, fixed by JDK-6430675 in Java 7 — on our JDK 21 pin `0.49999999999999994` converts to **0**). But **`Double.parseDouble` can lift a below-half *decimal* onto `0.5` before `Math.round` ever sees it**: binary64 round-to-nearest-**even** maps every decimal in `[½ − 2⁻⁵⁵, ½)` onto exactly `0.5`, because that interval's values are ties between `0.5` (even significand) and `0.5 − 2⁻⁵⁴` (odd). Measured through the exact chain:

| decimal literal | `parseDouble` | `→ int` |
|---|---|---|
| `0.49999999999999994` = ½ − 2⁻⁵⁴ | `0.49999999999999994` | 0 |
| `0.49999999999999998` (**17 fractional digits — the shortest lifting decimal**) | **`0.5`** | **1** |
| ½ − 2⁻⁵⁵ exactly (55 fractional digits) | **`0.5`** | **1** |
| one ulp below the interval | `0.4999999999999999` | 0 |
| −(½ − 2⁻⁵⁵) | `-0.5` | **0** |

**The lift creates a separator only on the positive side**, because `+0.5` is where `Math.round`'s boundary is inclusive; on the negative side a lifted `-0.5` still converts to 0, same as any smaller magnitude — so the ±0.5 asymmetry survives the parse step rather than being softened by it.

**Reaching it needs 17 fractional digits, which ordinarily exceeds what a field can be compared against — but that gate is SUPPRESSIBLE, so the witness is authorable.** Three links, all locked: (1) the shortest lifting decimal needs **17** fractional digits (at ≤16 the interval holds no decimal strictly below ½ — the ceiling lands on `0.5` itself); (2) a Number field's `maxFractionalDigits` **caps at 14** — the kernel rejects 15 at model check with a plain, MVK-less message naming neither the property nor the cap ("Only values smaller than or equal to 14 are allowed"). **modelkit now refuses it fail-fast** in `FieldTypeSpec.NumberSpec`, so the cap is unauthorable through *every* construction path (builder, CLI `field add/modify`, schema import, editor) and the corrective error names the property. Refusing `minFractionalDigits > 14` alongside it cannot over-reject, because the kernel independently requires `min ≤ max` (`MVK_FRACT_DIGITS_INVALID` — measured, not inferred: min 9 against max 5 is refused), so a min above 14 would force an illegal max *(`modelkit.FieldConfigTest.aNumberScaleAboveTheKernelCapIsRejectedFailFast`; the kernel side stays locked by `aNumberFieldScaleCapsAtFourteenInTheKernel`, which patches the emitted scale so a future kernel change to the cap can't leave our client-side constant silently stale)*; (3) the `==`/`!=` scale gate rejects 17-against-14 as `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` — an instance of the asymmetric rule already stated in the §5 supplement (only a *capable smaller*-scale side may be padded, so a scale-17 literal against a scale-14 field cannot reconcile, while the shorter `0.5` reconciles and reaches the classifier normally) *(`aComparisonLiteralMayCarryAtMostTheFieldsScale`)* — **but `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` is the kernel's ONE suppressible warning** (`@SuppressWarning(...)`, the CLI's `allowDifferingDecimals`; GRAMMAR-LEDGER `preamble` row, `DirectiveLawsTest`), so link (3) is defeatable by a first-class directive.

With the gate suppressed against a scale-14 field, two 17-digit literals differing only in their final digit straddle the entire partition — both strictly below one half:

| condition (scale-14 field, gate suppressed) | admission | why |
|---|---|---|
| `[W] == 0.49999999999999998` | admitted | inside `[½ − 2⁻⁵⁵, ½)` → parses onto `0.5` → converts to **1** |
| `[W] == 0.49999999999999990` | **REJECTED** | just below the interval → converts to **0** |

**So the separator is a real language property, not a host-only detail** *(locked: `RuleGroupIterationLawsTest.theParseStepLiftIsAuthorableWithTheGateSuppressed`; `.theZeroSensitivePartitionStillHoldsAtTheMaximumScale` is the control that the partition runs at scale 14 at all)*. A reimplementer that models the classifier with exact decimals diverges on a legal model.

**Correction of this entry's own first version (same day).** It originally claimed the witness was "unauthorable on every kernel-legal model, by exactly three decimal places", and was filed `> Fold: not-foldable` on that basis. The three links were each measured, but the proof was never tested for a *defeater* — and the defeater was a documented directive already exposed in our own CLI and schema. Measuring every link of a chain does not establish the chain; it has to be attacked.

**Two traps this closed, both from reading a message instead of measuring.** The `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` text says the two digit counts "are different", which reads as an equality requirement — it is **at most**: a *shorter* literal is admitted and reaches the partition normally (`[W] == 0.5` on a scale-14 field is accepted; `== 0.4` is rejected as converted-zero). And `FeldOperationUtil.getZahlKonstanteWert` returns **−1 as its "not a number constant" sentinel**, which collides with the value some legal literals convert to — not just the saturating 2^63 but **plain `-1`**, and every literal whose rounded long has its low 32 bits set (`4294967295`, `8589934591`, …). All **12 invocations across 5 caller classes** were read (2026-07-25), grouped here into the 6 distinct call contexts (`IterationNotValidVisitor` contributes two separate methods):

| call site | how it uses the result | collision risk |
|---|---|---|
| `mandatoryinformation.EvaluatorVisitor.visit(IComparisonCondition)` | tests `z != -1` / `z == -1` **as** the is-a-constant test | **conflates** — a colliding literal is read as "not a constant" and the visit bails |
| `parser.CheckerFuerUsbEinschraenkung.deriveMaxAnzahlUsb` | guarded by `isZahlKonstante` before the call | none — safe by construction |
| `IterationNotValidVisitor` (`checkIfVergleichMitNull`, `checkIfVergleichMitKleiner`) | tests `z == 0` / `z > 0` | benign — −1 simply fails the test, as any other non-matching constant would |
| `CollectorFuerGlobalePflichtmengenInfo`, `CollectorFuerPflichtVordruckInfo` | test `z > 0` | benign, same reason |

So the conflation is real but confined to **one** caller in the **mandatory-information** subsystem, which this project does not model at all (no reference anywhere in `:adapter`/`:interpreter`/`:cli`/`:rulekit`) — and every colliding literal makes the comparison itself degenerate (`AnzahlAngegebeneFelder >= -1` is trivially true; the large ones are unsatisfiable), so no meaningful mandatory-set derivation is at stake. Recorded as a characterized kernel-internal hazard with its locus named; **not** a hypothesis and **not** an open item. *(Whether it manifests in mandatory-information OUTPUT is unprobed — we drive no such surface — but the source classification above is complete.)*

## §11 supplement — the parallel-iteration computation route replaces the read-time index gate with post-loop marking, whose blast radius depends on WHICH index group is malformed (differential, 2026-07-25; answers a12-kernel-lean EXP-2026-07-25-03) <a id="kf67"></a>

> Fold: pending — the route split needs a deliberate edit to the §11 computation prose.

**A computation reached through a parallel-iteration operand has no read-time semantic-index gate. Instead the iteration-values lookup returns empty (so the loop body never runs) and `CalculationCache.markFieldsUsingInvalidIndexGroupsAsIncorrectlyCalculated` marks affected instances afterwards — and it marks by TRUNCATED coordinates, so an off-path malformed key clears clean sibling rows while an on-path one does not.** `CodeGenCalculatedField.getParallelIterationGroupsCode()` passes **both** the index group on the computed field's own path and the off-path groups the operands iterate; marking then keys on each existing field instance's indices **truncated to `numSharedLevels` = `commonAncestorLevel(computedField, indexGroupParent) + 1`**. So the blast radius is the shared prefix, not the malformed row:

| malformed index key lives in | shared prefix reaches | sibling parent row's computed target |
|---|---|---|
| the **off-path** iterated index group (`/Order/Refs`) | only `/Order` — above the sibling level | **CLEARED** — a clean sibling does *not* survive |
| the computed field's **own on-path** index group (`/Order/Lines/Slots`) | `/Order/Lines` — below the sibling level | **survives** with its value |

Observed on a two-sibling-row document: with all keys distinct both targets compute (100 / 200); duplicating a key in the off-path group clears **both**, including the sibling whose own slot key still matches a clean row; duplicating a key inside one line's own `Slots` clears only that line's instances and leaves the sibling at 200. **Both kernel strategies agree on all three, so this is kernel truth, not a strategy split.** The kernel's own comment concedes the off-path case marks "more field instances as invalid than strictly necessary … we don't think we need to get too clever."

**Authoring preconditions (and why no corpus reaches this route):** the iterated group's index field must have the **same name** as the index field on the computed field's path, else the model is rejected with `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX` ("iteration is specified, but the index field on the error field path has another name; therefore wildcard has to be specified or another error field must be defined"). The operand must also be a bracketed **non-starred** reference (`[../../Refs/Amount]`) — a starred `Refs*` is a *wildcard*, not an iteration, and takes the ordinary route; `Sum(...)` over a single such reference is rejected `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN`.

**The two loci are NOT separately reachable — one model must carry both (a12-kernel-lean's marker derivation, 2026-07-25; their reading, our fixture is the evidence it is right).** The bean's level is `-1` unless **two independent facts hold**: **(A)** a `PARALLEL_ITERATION` marker exists in the computation's own operand trees, and **(B)** the computed field has an index-field-bearing group on its own ancestry (`getIndexFieldLevel`, `-1` if none). Neither implies the other. The marker itself is stamped in two passes (`ParserService`), and **pass two — the only producer of ON-PATH markers — runs only if pass one stamped an OFF-PATH one.** So an on-path index group can never be parallel-iterated unless an off-path iterated group exists in the same computation: both loci are present together or neither is. **Consequence for any experiment here: use ONE document containing both and move the malformed key**, never two structurally different documents, which would compare shapes rather than loci. That is why the three cases below are comparable at all.
