**Two further cells, measured in the same grid, each removing a constant of the older sets.** With the written field FIXED and uncontained, an unstarred per-row read reaches the containment gate from a rule as it does from a computation — and it does so whether the extent it crosses DECLARES an index field or not, where the same read with the written field CONTAINED splits into `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` and `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NO_INDEX`. The wildcard classes are therefore not pre-emptions of this gate; they are what answers when this gate has nothing to say. And a condition that never REACHES its uncontained error field still draws the containment class, not `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` — every containment row in the estate had carried a reaching reference, so that precedence had never been put to the kernel.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.ErrorTargetContainmentLawsTest` — the 2×2, the read-source grid with its star-aggregate and reach-only controls, and the referenced-ness precedence; kernel 30.8.1, 2026-09-15. Reproduced by the portable checker's `CheckFamily.ERROR_TARGET_CONTAINMENT`, whose mirror carries the same rows.)*


*(Locked: `validate.laws.ComputationDeclaringGroupLawsTest` — the tables above, the index control, the rule arm's derived error paths, and the stored `computedFieldRelPath` each accepted placement writes; kernel 30.8.1, 2026-08-29. The accept tables cannot self-certify — without a kernel backend `RuleValidator` degrades to `STRUCTURAL_ONLY` and every row would read admitted — so the refusal tables are the class's positive control.)*

## §9/§11 supplement: an AGGREGATE derives no iteration, so a fixed-target computation is constrained on neither side — and the extent's INDEX declaration picks which gate answers an unstarred read (kernel, 2026-08-29) <a id="kf213"></a>

> Fold: pending — the companion of [KF212](#kf212); fold both into §9's iteration-scope account in one pass, since the gate and its absence are one clause.

[KF212](#kf212) says when `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP` fires. This says what is left when it cannot: **a computation that derives no iteration is constrained on neither side** — its declaring group is free of the computed field, and its operands are free of the declaring group and of each other. Measured on a two-root parts catalogue, five declaring-group relations per row:

| the operation reads… | into a FIXED target, at all five placements |
|---|---|
| nothing (bare constant) | admitted |
| `Sum(/Catalogue/Lots*/Quantity)` and `FirstFilledValue(/Catalogue/Lots*/Quantity, /Catalogue/Batches*/Quantity)` — two star aggregates | admitted, **cell for cell the constant's**, both |
| `FirstFilledValue(Pricing/BasePrice, Terms/TermMarker)` — two sources in two groups, neither the declaring one | admitted |

The five placements are the target's own fixed group, the root ancestor, an unrelated fixed sibling, **the starred source's own repeatable group**, and an unrelated repeatable group. That fourth one is the discriminator: an account of the code as *"a repeatable group appears in the operand path"* forbids it most clearly, and it is admitted. **A star aggregate is not a per-row operand** — it reads no row, so it derives no iteration, and the row-for-row match with the constant is what shows the admissions are containment's absence rather than the star's doing. **Two members, not one:** `FirstFilledValue` is the operator a12-kernel-lean's clause actually names, and this repository treats sibling-star `FirstFilledValue` as its own specially-behaving route elsewhere (§11), so generalizing from `Sum` alone would have been a denominator of one — added 2026-08-30 after review.

**Containment is PATH containment, with no root-relative component.** A model may declare more than one root group and stay kernel-valid, which is the widest separation available: a fixed target is admitted from a group in the *other* root, and a star over the other root's repeatable extent is admitted from home. The same bare constant into a *repeatable* target refuses `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP` from that other root exactly as it does from a non-containing sibling inside its own root — with the target's own ancestor admitted in the same table as the control. Crossing a root boundary is not itself a refusal; failing containment is.

**Which gate answers an UNSTARRED read of a repeatable field depends on TWO variables, not one, and the second is easy to miss.** From the repeatable group it reads, the read reaches the placement gate (`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP`) — for an index-keyed extent and a plain one alike. From a *fixed* declaring group it never reaches placement, but which gate pre-empts it is the **read extent's own index declaration**: a non-index-keyed extent draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`, an index-keyed one draws `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NO_INDEX`. The two groups in the fixture differ in nothing else, so the declaration alone moves the code. a12-kernel-lean reported the unqualified form (`SPEC-2026-08-29-03`, "`MVK_NO_WILDCARD` only from a nonrepeatable declaring group"); it holds for a plain extent and not for a keyed one, and this repository's own [KF212](#kf212) table had already recorded the keyed code without the two being put side by side.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.NonIteratingComputationFreedomLawsTest` — the three fixed-target tables with the constant as their control, the two-root separator with its ancestor control, and the index-controlled wildcard table; kernel 30.8.1, 2026-08-29. The all-admitted tables cannot self-certify — without a kernel backend `RuleValidator` degrades to `STRUCTURAL_ONLY` — so the refusal rows of the last two tests are the class's positive control. The self-reference row is deliberately NOT that control: it is `Computation.Builder`'s own pre-check and never reaches the kernel, which is why it is asserted as a thrown `PrecheckException` and its kernel basis is cited to the MVK-LEDGER row rather than claimed here.)*

## §13 supplement: the rule-message `$#…$` GROUP position resolves the same words differently from the NAME position — an absolute path that must CONTAIN the rule, behind two separately reported gates (kernel, 2026-08-29) <a id="kf214"></a>

> Fold: pending — the group half of the parameter surface [KF198](#kf198) opened; fold both into §13's interpolation account in one pass.

[KF198](#kf198) measured the parameter **name** position exhaustively and recorded, as a measured absence, that `RootGroup`/`LfdNr` is *not reachable* there (`INVALID_ENTITY`) while `RuleGroup` is recognised and refused (`INVALID_PARAMETER`). That absence is **position-scoped, and the `$#…$` group position is where those words live**: both shorthands are admitted there. Reported as `SPEC-2026-08-29-04` by a12-kernel-lean and measured here on an insurance policy with a second declared root; the rule sits at the repeatable `/Policy/Cover/Sections`.

**The admitted set is the rule's own group plus its ancestors — everywhere except the root locus.** `$#/Policy/Cover/Sections$`, `$#/Policy/Cover$`, `$#/Policy$`, `$#RuleGroup$` and `$#RootGroup$` are all admitted from a rule three levels down.

> **Corrected 2026-09-05: "at any depth" was over-general, and the exception is the `RuleGroup` WORD rather than the position.** A rule sitting directly in a declared root group refuses `$#RuleGroup$` on its own code, `RULEGROUP_IMMEDIATELY_BELOW_ROOT` — "The parameter '#RuleGroup' is not allowed in rules which are ordered right below the rootgroup" — while `$#RootGroup$` and the absolute `$#/Order$` name that *same* group from that *same* rule and are admitted. So containment still decides which groups are referable; one spelling is additionally barred at one locus. Every fixture behind the original clause put the rule three levels down, which is the constant no row inside that set could expose: the model had no root-level field to hang a rule on, so the locus was never varied. The control is within-model — the same shallow model, the rule moved one level down, `$#RuleGroup$` admitted. Prompted by a12-kernel-lean, whose `spec/11-messages-and-custom.md` carried this for the COMPUTATION carrier and flagged the validation crossing as unmeasured; they measured the crossing and told us, and the row above is our own measurement of it on our own carrier. Locked by `validate.laws.RuleMessageGroupParameterLawsTest.theRuleGroupShorthandIsRefusedAtTheROOTLocusWhileTheSameGroupIsNameableTwoOtherWays`. Everything else a declared root contains is `INVALID_GROUP` on one code — a **descendant** of the rule's group, a **sibling**, a branch sharing only the root, a group under the **other** declared root, that root itself, and a **relative** spelling of a real ancestor (`$#Cover$`). So the position takes an absolute path, and containment decides.

**Containment here runs OPPOSITE to the computation declaring-group gate.** There the written field must lie *at or below* the declaring group ([KF212](#kf212)); here the *named* group must *contain* the rule's group. `RuleGroup` and `RootGroup` are keyword shorthands for the two endpoints of that same chain.

**An absolute argument resolves in two gates the kernel reports apart.** An undeclared first segment draws `INVALID_ROOT_GROUP` whatever follows it — `$#/Nope$` and `$#/Nope/Sections$` alike — and `$#/policy$` shows the root match is **case-sensitive**. Only *under* a declared root does containment decide and report `INVALID_GROUP`, which the non-containing `$#/Policy/Admin$` control establishes in the same table.

**The terminal match is on the RAW argument, so quoting removes a word's terminal reading rather than merely being stripped ahead of it.** `$#/'Policy'/'Cover'$` reaches the same group as its bare spelling (the quote is transparent for a *segment*), but `$#'RootGroup'$` and `$#'RuleGroup'$` draw `INVALID_GROUP` — looked up as group names of that spelling. Malformed spellings never reach either resolution gate: an unbalanced quote and an empty quoted segment are `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR`, a trailing separator `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`, a doubled one `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`.

**`RootGroup` is the rule's OWN chain root, not a model-wide one — and only the second root can show it.** A model may declare two roots and stay kernel-valid. From a rule under the second, `$#RootGroup$` is admitted while `$#/Policy$` (the first-declared root) draws `INVALID_GROUP`. Admission alone cannot separate "the chain's root" from "admitted unconditionally", since the chain root always contains the rule, so the refusal row is the one carrying the claim.

**Two retired terminals are RECOGNISED here and refused on the modern route:** `$#Zeile$` and `$#Usb$` draw `PARAM_INVALID_IN_NEW_WORLD`, distinct from `INVALID_GROUP` — the kernel parses them and rejects them, rather than failing to find a group of that name. `$#Vordruckzeile$`, `$#Vordruckname$`, `$#index(1)$` and `$#'Zeile'$` draw plain `INVALID_GROUP`, so they are not terminals in this position at all.

**The confound that eats this whole measurement.** A negative condition in an iterating rule is refused `MVK_NEG_CONDITION_IN_ITERATION` *before* the error-text checker runs, so every row — controls included — reports the condition's verdict and the table measures nothing about the message. a12-kernel-lean lost a first attempt to exactly this. `KernelLaws.messageVerdict` runs a plain-text control per row for that reason, which turns it into a caught mistake.

Consumer-visible consequence: `Dsl.repetitionIndex(GroupRef)` emits `$#<absolutePath>$` from a model-bound ref, so the relative-spelling refusal is unreachable through the typed helper, and the containment demand is now on its javadoc and in the `rule add` schema's message description. The helper has no spelling for the two shorthands; that is deliberate — the absolute path is strictly more explicit and nothing is blocked by their absence.

**Both shorthands are BILINGUAL here, and each language admits only its own spelling** (added 2026-09-05). `$#RuleGroup$` and `$#RootGroup$` are admitted on an `en_US`-condition model and draw `INVALID_GROUP` on a `de_DE` one; `$#RegelKontext$` and `$#LfdNr$` are admitted on the German model and draw `INVALID_GROUP` on the English one — the position looks the other language's word up as a group NAME. Measured in both directions on one model pair, which is what separates "this position recognises the terminal" from "this position recognises the English words". That completes [KF198](#kf198)'s five-terminal table: the rule-group pair is `INVALID_PARAMETER` in the name position and admitted here, and the root-group pair is unreachable there and admitted here, so the name-position absence recorded as position-scoped is now measured on the position that owns it.

**EXISTENCE is not part of the law, measured 2026-09-15 against a source read that said otherwise.** An absolute path under a DECLARED root that resolves to nothing — `$#/Policy/NoSuchGroup$` — draws `INVALID_GROUP`, the same class a declared non-containing group draws, and so does a path naming a FIELD rather than a group. A read of `CheckIdNameImpl.checkAndCreateFullName` predicts `INVALID_ENTITY` there, its absolute arm answering that for an unresolvable candidate; in this position `resolveAndStoreEntity`'s group branch is what answers instead. The chain the source suggests therefore collapses onto one class, which is what lets a checker test CONTAINMENT alone here without first asking whether the named group is there — the portable checker does exactly that (`CheckFamily.MESSAGE_GROUP_PARAMETER`, reporting all four of this position's classes from 2026-09-15).

**Extended 2026-09-15 — a gate BEHIND containment: the condition must ride the named group without a wildcard.** `$#RuleGroup$` from a rule in a repeatable group whose condition reads that group's field through a star ALONE draws `ITER_PARAM_WITH_STARREFERENCE`, while the same parameter beside a per-row read is admitted and the parameter-free control on the starred condition is admitted too — so the class is the parameter's. **The law belongs to the POSITION, not to the shorthand** its kernel comment names: the same group spelled `$#/Order/Lines$` draws the same class on the same condition. And **a star BELOW the named group leaves it ridden per row**: `$#RootGroup$` on that starred condition is admitted, as is an ancestor named from an inner rule that reads its own field per row beside a starred read of the outer group's. Two further gates sit behind this one and are NOT measured — a group that is a PARALLEL ITERATION, or a parameter carrying a semantic index, then hands the decision to a kernel visitor over the parsed condition (`INVALID_USE_OF_ITERATION_PARAM` / `INVALID_USE_OF_SEMANTIC_INDEX`).

**Corrected 2026-09-05 — this entry's scope line said the RENDER half "stays open"; it is measured**, on this estate rather than only by the peer's `SG10`: [KF245](#kf245) carries what the position renders, on all three engines, including the repeatable-root and nested-ancestor arms this fixture's topology cannot reach.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.RuleMessageGroupParameterLawsTest` — the admitted set, the containment refusals, the two ordered gates with their case control, the quoting separator, the four lexical classes, the retired terminals with their non-terminal controls, and the two-root separator; kernel 30.8.1, 2026-08-29. `validate.laws.RuleMessageParameterLanguageLawsTest` — the bilingual admission of both shorthands in this position, both directions, kernel 30.8.1, 2026-09-05. Each row rides `KernelLaws.messageVerdict`'s plain-message control, so a row can only report on the message.); `validate.laws.MessageGroupParameterIterationLawsTest` — the wildcard gate on both spellings of one group, with the per-row control, the parameter-free control on the starred condition, the root shorthand, and the star-below-the-group row.)*

## §1 supplement: declaring a group and NAMING one are separate questions, and emptiness is judged over the SUBTREE (kernel, 2026-08-29) <a id="kf215"></a>

> Fold: pending — folds into §1's group/path account beside the group-list root classes ([KF185](#kf185)).

A group carrying no fields is **legal to declare**, and the model stays kernel-valid — for a subgroup, for a repeatable group, and for an entirely unpopulated ROOT, all three in one model. Every operand that then names one is refused, on codes of their own rather than on the unknown-group class: `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` for a group, `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` for a root. Reported as `SPEC-2026-08-29-05` by a12-kernel-lean and measured here on a retail store model with a second, unpopulated root.

**The gate is over the SUBTREE, not the direct children** — the row the finding rests on, because without it "empty" and "childless" are the same claim. A group with no direct field but a field in a descendant subgroup is admitted everywhere an empty one is refused. The table below exercises a **fixed** shell on three carriers and a **repeatable** one on the row-count carrier, which is the shape each carrier admits; "both repetition shapes" is the union of the table, not a claim that either shell was tried on all four:

| carrier | empty | shell (no direct field, one populated descendant) | populated — control |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GroupFilled(G)` | `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` | **admitted** | admitted |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(G*)` | `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` | **admitted** | admitted |
| `AllGroupsFilled(G, …)` | `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` | **admitted** | — |
| `GroupsNotCollectivelyFilled(G, …)` | `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` | **admitted** | — |

**Extended 2026-09-13 — the law is not the group-operand position's.** The same empty group draws the same class in a FIELD-list operator (`AtLeastOneFieldFilled(G)`) and in an INDEX position (`CurrentRepetition(G*)`), and in the second it PRE-EMPTS: the populated control there is refused for its wildcard (`MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`) while the empty one is refused for its emptiness. That is what lets a checker reading condition TEXT state this class for any reference resolving to an empty group — which operand position a name sits in is the one thing such a checker cannot recover.

**The trap that eats the control rows.** The empty-group refusal reports *ahead of* `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`, so a table whose conditions do not reference the error field reads correctly on every refusing row and reports the wrong code on every admitted one — measured here on the first attempt, which is why each condition carries a `FieldFilled(<error field>) And` conjunct.

Consumer-visible consequence: this is the ordinary state of a model **mid-edit** — `group add` then `field add` — so refusing the declaration would make the obvious authoring order impossible. `dmtool` declares it, `model check` reports the model valid, and the refusal arrives only when a rule names the group; the group survives that refusal in the model. That separation is what the CLI lock asserts end to end.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.EMPTY_GROUP_OPERAND`), on the DECLARATION that names the group rather than on the group.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.EmptyGroupOperandLawsTest` — the four-carrier table with its shell and populated controls, and the root class beside a populated-root control; `cli … EmptyGroupDeclarationCliTest` — declare, `model check` valid, name-and-refuse, over the CLI. Kernel 30.8.1, 2026-08-29.)*

## §8 supplement: an Enumeration category pairs POSITIONALLY with its values, and the fractional-digit cap is reported with no MVK code at all (kernel, 2026-08-29) <a id="kf216"></a>

> Fold: pending — folds into §8's Enumeration account beside the category-suffix rendering ([KF198](#kf198)).

Both facts are the measured basis for a `modelkit` constructor refusal, taken because a12-kernel-lean's dmtool feedback of 2026-08-29 observed — correctly — that a client-side refusal makes the kernel's own gate unobservable through the structured verbs. **The observation route it asked for already exists:** `model check` runs `checkConsistency` over a model file with no field-spec preflight in the way, so hand-writing the refused shape into DM-JSON and checking it reaches the kernel gate and returns its verdict in the standard envelope, `source: KERNEL`, `verification: KERNEL_CONFIRMED`. Every row below was taken that way.

**A category's `values` array pairs with the enum's BY POSITION, so equal cardinality is the kernel's whole rule** — not a proxy for set membership, which is the account every misaligned row is equally consistent with. The discriminator is same-length **disjoint** tokens, and they are admitted:

| category tokens over enum values `[BASIC, PLUS]` | verdict |
|---|---|
| `[STANDARD, HIGH]` — control | admitted |
| `[X, Y]` — same length, **disjoint** | **admitted** |
| `[HIGH, STANDARD]` — same length, reordered | admitted |
| `[STANDARD]` — one short | `MVK_MISSING_CATEGORY_VALUE` |
| `[STANDARD, HIGH, TOP]` — one too many | `MVK_MISSING_INTERNAL_VALUE` |
| `[STANDARD, HIGH, TOP, MAX]` — two too many | `MVK_MISSING_INTERNAL_VALUE` ×2 *(added 2026-09-13)* |
| `[]` | `MVK_MISSING_CATEGORY_VALUE`, once per unclassified value |

So `FieldTypeSpec.EnumSpec`'s cardinality check is **exactly** the kernel's rule rather than a conservative one, and its single message collapses a pair of per-element kernel diagnostics — under-reporting, never over-rejecting.

**Amended 2026-09-13 — the multiplicity was measured in ONE direction only.** The per-element count was taken on the shortfall side (`[]` → one diagnostic per unclassified value) and reused on the surplus side, which had a single row and so could not distinguish "one per surplus token" from "one per misaligned category". Two surplus tokens draw two diagnostics, so the reuse was right — but it was a transfer until the row was run, and it needed no new branch, which is why nothing prompted the question.

**Amended 2026-09-13 — an EMPTY `values` never reaches the pairing.** An `EnumerationType` whose `values` is `[]` makes the model **NOT BUILDABLE**, with categories and without them alike, so a checker that pairs an empty left side against declared tokens reports codes A12 does not raise on that model. This repository's portable checker did exactly that (two `MVK_MISSING_INTERNAL_VALUE`) until the row was measured. **Not reported by the checker**, deliberately: a dynamic enumeration takes its values from a rule (`Regel_t.dynamicEnumerationRule`), so whether that shape makes an empty list legal is unmeasured, and widening a refusal on two rows that share a constant is the direction a client-side check may never take. *Re-open trigger:* a measurement of an empty `values` on a field carrying a dynamic-enumeration rule.

**The fractional-digit cap is a real kernel gate reported with NO code.** `maxFractionalDigits: 15` and `minFractionalDigits: 15` each draw one diagnostic reading *"Field with path '/Store/Scale14': Only values smaller than or equal to 14 are allowed."* — no `MVK_*` class, no property name, and **one** diagnostic even when both keys breach. Stated precisely, and the precision is [KF75](#kf75)'s lesson rather than pedantry: the kernel's MESSAGE carries no class key, so there is nothing for `Diagnostic.kernelClass` to lift — every code we report is our extraction from the message's terminal bracket, so "no code" is always a statement about the message and never about a field the kernel declined to fill. The quoted text above is what makes that checkable here. That code-lessness is the reason `modelkit` refuses it correctively rather than delegating, which the code comment already said and can now cite.

**Amended 2026-09-13 — the MEMBER NAMES, and the reader's answer to a near-miss.** Every row above was authored through the kit, so it settles the law and says nothing about which STORED members carry it — the question a checker reading DM-JSON has to answer, and one it may not settle by reading the Java field ([KF308](#kf308), corrected). Put to the kernel as stored JSON, an Enumeration spells its values `values: [{"value": …}]` and its categories `categories: [{"name": …, "values": [ … ]}]`. **Each of those four names written NEARLY right makes the model UNREADABLE rather than being ignored:** A12's reader refuses a member it does not know and names the six it accepts (`values`, `annotations`, `categories`, `sValue`, `errorMessage`, `alphabeticalSorting`). The prediction was the opposite — an over-permissive reader dropping the member silently, which would have let a consumer keyed on a wrong name read as clean on every model. Two further rows: a second category is judged independently of the first, and a body with no `categories` at all is admitted.

Consumer-visible consequence: both refusals now ride the `rejected` envelope with `RK_INVALID_VALUE` and `source: PRECHECK`, on all four spec verbs (`field add`/`modify`, `typedef add`/`modify`), and the cap message no longer attributes a local refusal to the kernel that never saw it. *(Locked: `validate.laws.EnumCategoryAlignmentLawsTest` — the positional table, built by editing the aligned model's own JSON since the kits refuse to construct the misaligned shape, with the per-element multiplicity asserted and a three-value row showing the pairing runs left-to-right; `validate.laws.RuleGroupIterationLawsTest.theScaleCapIsReportedWithoutAnyMvkClassOnEitherKey` — the cap's code-lessness on both keys, which this entry rests on and nothing pinned until 2026-08-30; `cli … SpecValueRefusalEnvelopeTest` — the envelope, the code, the `PRECHECK` source, and the de-attributed wording across the four spec verbs and the scaffolding verb; `validate.laws.EnumCategoryWireShapeLawsTest` — the stored member names and the four near-miss rows.)*

## §1 supplement: a nested-descendant group is not only an ADMITTED group-count operand, it COUNTS — over the whole subtree, on both arms (kernel runtime + static, 2026-08-30) <a id="kf217"></a>

> Fold: pending — folds into §1's group-fill account beside [KF119](#kf119)'s repeatability split and [KF215](#kf215)'s subtree gate.

a12-kernel-lean reported the static half as `SPEC-2026-08-30-01`: in the plain multi-group `NumberOfFilledGroups`, a fixed group whose only field lies in a **descendant subgroup** is an admitted operand, at first position, at second position, and in a three-group list. Reproduced here and extended past that entry's stated limits — a field **three levels down** is admitted too, and so is a group whose only content is a **repeatable descendant**; a shell that is ITSELF repeatable follows the operator's ordinary wildcard rule instead, `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` unstarred and admitted starred — with three controls in the same table proving the carrier still refuses: the empty group draws `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY`, a single fixed group `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDGN`, and a group under a repeatable extent `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` (locked in `validate.laws.EmptyGroupOperandLawsTest`).

**The half that entry could not settle, and the reason it matters: admission is not contribution.** A legal operand may still contribute nothing, so "admitted" leaves both counting accounts alive — whole subtree, or direct children only. The discriminator is one document where they predict different numbers: a flat group filled *and* the shell's descendant filled. Whole-subtree predicts 2; direct-children predicts 1, because under that account a shell has no direct field and can never be filled.

| document | count | whole-subtree | direct-children |
|---|---|---|---|
| flat filled + shell's descendant filled | **2** | 2 ✓ | 1 ✗ |
| flat filled, descendant emptied — control | **1** | 1 ✓ | 1 ✓ |

**Measured: 2. The count reads content over the whole subtree**, so the fill notion is [KF119](#kf119)'s non-repeatable "a filled descendant field", at any depth, and not a direct-child scan. The control is what makes the pair discriminating — a count stuck at 1 would satisfy the direct-children prediction for the wrong reason.

**Both arms agree.** The computation arm's stored value and the validation arm's comparison against it are separately specified, and the plain multi-group count is the stricter of the two on erroneous operands ([KF120](#kf120)), so their agreement on the nested shape is measured rather than carried over. Locked in `adapter.laws.NestedGroupFillCountLawsTest` (kernel oracle: `RuntimeLaws.compute` and `RuntimeLaws.fires`).

**"Content" has TWO constituents, and the second is not a cell at all** *(a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-30-03`, reproduced here 2026-08-30)*. A shell whose only content is a **repeatable descendant** counts when that descendant holds **one instantiated but EMPTY row** — no filled cell anywhere in its subtree. Control: with no row instantiated the same shell is not counted, so it is the row that moved it.

| document | counted |
|---|---|
| `Contact` filled, `Coverage/Riders` = one empty instantiated row | **2** |
| `Contact` filled, `Coverage/Riders` = no rows — control | **1** |

This does **not** replace the subtree rule above: the rows at the top of this entry carry no repeatable group anywhere, so a filled descendant *cell* moves the count on its own.

**The disjunction itself is measured, in the one shape that can separate the constituents.** Neither project's original probe established it, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: a shape with no repeatable descendant cannot exercise the row constituent, and *inside* a repeatable descendant a cell cannot exist without a row, so each side measured one constituent live exactly where the other could not fire. A group owning **both** a nonrepeatable `Notes/Text` and a repeatable `Items` separates them against one operand in one model:

| document | counted |
|---|---|
| the nonrepeatable cell filled, **no row instantiated** | **2** |
| one instantiated empty row, **no cell filled anywhere** | **2** |
| neither — the control | **1** |

Either constituent alone suffices and neither is necessary. The control is what makes the pair mean anything: without it, "counts either way" is indistinguishable from "counts unconditionally".

**Repetition DEPTH does not bound the row constituent, and the half-instantiated shape says which rule that is** *(a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-30-08` acceptance condition, measured here 2026-08-30 on our own fixture, plus the row their stated limit could not reach)*. Every row above has the repeatable descendant exactly ONE level below the operand, which cannot separate a **containment** rule — any instantiated row anywhere beneath the operand — from a **leaf-row** rule about the innermost repeatable. A shell whose only content is a repeatable `Pallets` containing a repeatable `Cartons` separates them:

| document | counted |
|---|---|
| one `Cartons` leaf row instantiated, its cells empty | **2** |
| the same, one cell filled | **2** |
| **half-instantiated — a `Pallets` row with NO `Cartons` row beneath it** | **2** |
| no row at either level — the control | **1** |

**Containment.** The half-instantiated row is the discriminator: a leaf-row rule predicts 1 there, since no row of the innermost repeatable exists. Measured 2, so an instantiated row is content wherever it sits beneath the operand, and the rule is neither an axis count nor a statement about the deepest level. The peer had marked that row as their implementation's own reading and unmeasured on either estate; it is measured now. Locked in `adapter.laws.DeepRepeatableRowConstituentLawsTest`, which also asserts the static admission gate on the two-level shell, since running an engine and getting a number is not an `MVK_*` verdict.

Together they are exactly [KF119](#kf119)'s non-repeatable fill notion — "a filled descendant field, **or** an instantiated repeatable descendant row" — now confirmed for the unstarred multi-group count carrier rather than only for `GroupFilled`. The peer reached it from the starred form's structural rule; the reconciliation is that both operand shapes share one notion of repeatable content, so a checker needs one predicate with two sufficient constituents, not a cell scan with a special case.

**And on the computation arm, formally invalid content IS content for the fill predicate** *(a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-30-02`, measured here 2026-08-30)*. This is a distinct question from the arm divergence below, though the two coincide in outcome: that one asks what an erroneous operand does to each arm, this one asks whether malformed content counts as content at all. Same shell holding **only** a malformed value → **2**; the same shell holding nothing → **1**. So the count's compute-arm notion of content is *not* the admitted-value cache [KF120](#kf120) describes for `GroupFilled`, where invalid-only is FALSE — a third way this carrier's "content" is wider than a cell-admission scan.

**The two arms DIVERGE on a formally invalid operand** — which scopes [KF120](#kf120)'s "any erroneous group makes the count unavailable" to the validation arm, where its locks live. On the identical document: the **computation** arm stores the value and counts the group (2, at both depths); the **validation** arm is suppressed, and it is suppression rather than a different number, since neither `== 2` nor `== 1` fires. Static admission is untouched by this — it is a runtime split, so a `computation add --dry-run` or `model check` verdict is not affected.

**Authoring trap the rule arm carries:** a condition that is *only* the count draws `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`, because the operand names groups while the error field sits outside all of them — the same conjunct device [KF215](#kf215)'s table needs.

## §9 supplement: the group count is an ADDITIVE fold whose per-operand contribution depends on the operand FORM (kernel runtime, 2026-08-30) <a id="kf218"></a>

> Fold: pending — folds into §9 beside [KF217](#kf217)'s content account and the starred form's structural tally.

a12-kernel-lean reported (`SPEC-2026-08-30-04`) that a starred operand contributes a **row count** rather than a presence bit, and read it as the two operand forms having *separate result domains*, so that the operator "cannot be folded by one presence question per operand". **The first half is already ours and locked; the second half overshoots, and their own mixed column refutes it.**

**Not new here:** the starred single-group tally — every instantiated row counts, empty ones included — is the catalog's stated meaning and is locked tri-differentially in `adapter.laws.NumberOfFilledGroupsStarDiffTest` (`emptyInstantiatedRowStillCounts`, `soleEmptyAndAbsent`), which pins 0 rows → 0, one empty row → 1, and filled+empty+filled → 3. **That lock drives `validateFull` and asserts a comparison firing, so it is the VALIDATION arm** *(scoped 2026-08-30 on a12-kernel-lean's provenance note — without the qualifier it reads as pre-existing compute-arm coverage, which it is not)*; the compute-arm confirmation is this entry's own fixture.

**New here: the MIXED form's arithmetic.** The sweep behind that gap, stated so it can be re-run: `git grep -o 'numberOfFilledGroups(' e228345a9~1 -- adapter/src/test` returns **21 occurrences**, one of which is a javadoc mention, so **20 call sites — all 20 read**. Ten pass a single operand and ten pass a pair — nine of those pairs all-fixed, the tenth the round-trip case named below; **no site executes a list mixing a STARRED operand with a fixed one**, which is why the arithmetic below was unmeasured. *Corrected 2026-08-30, same day: this sentence first said "all 24 … either a single starred operand or an all-fixed pair". The 24 was HEAD's occurrence count — it counted the javadoc and the three sites this entry's own commits added, including the mixed one it claims does not exist — and "all-fixed pair" overstated the residue: `FilledCountReadTest.roundTripsNumberOfFilledGroupsOverMixedRepeatableAndFixedGroups` does mix a repeatable `Items` with a fixed `ShippingAddress`, but **unstarred**, and it round-trips the rendering without executing it. That third operand form — an unstarred repeatable group inside a multi-group list — needs no new probe: it is the `"the shell itself REPEATABLE, unstarred"` row of [KF217](#kf217)'s table, **`MVK_NO_WILDCARD`**, locked in `validate.laws.EmptyGroupOperandLawsTest`. So the round-trip test renders a condition `checkConsistency` refuses, which a read-path test does not assert against and would not notice.* Measured on a fixed `Contact` beside a starred `Coverage/Riders*`, one model, one operand list:

| `Contact` | rows instantiated (all empty) | counted |
|---|---|---|
| filled | 3 | **4** |
| empty | 3 | **3** |
| filled | 0 | **1** |
| empty | 0 | **0** — control |

**The discriminator is the first row.** A presence bit for the starred operand caps the total at 2 whatever the fixed operand does; 4 is only reachable if that operand contributes a cardinality. So the operator **is** a per-operand fold — `Σ contribution(operand)` over one result domain (ℕ) — with an *indicator* contribution for a fixed operand and a *cardinality* contribution for a starred one. What cannot be done is fold it with **one presence question** for every operand; what can be done is fold it, which is the part the "separate result domains" reading denies. The distinction matters for a checker: one traversal with a form-dependent contribution suffices, no per-form result type is needed.

**And the fold sums over OPERAND POSITIONS, not over distinct groups** *(measured here 2026-08-30, the runtime half of a shape a12-kernel-lean had pinned statically)*. The 20-site sweep above found no list with two starred operands at all, so both rows below are new coverage:

| operand list | document | counted |
|---|---|---|
| `(Coverage/Riders*, Bundle/Items*)` | 3 rider rows, 2 item rows | **5** |
| same | 3 rider rows, no item rows | **3** |
| same | no rows — control | **0** |
| `(Coverage/Riders*, Coverage/Riders*)` — the SAME group twice | 3 rider rows | **6** |
| same | no rows — control | **0** |

**The duplicate row is the discriminator for this entry's own phrasing**: a fold over distinct groups predicts 3, `Σ contribution(operand)` predicts 6. Measured 6, so "per operand" is literal — a repeated operand contributes once per position. The lock pins the rendered spelling beside the numbers (`NumberOfFilledGroups(/Catalogue/Coverage/Riders*, /Catalogue/Coverage/Riders*)`), because a silent dedupe in our own builder would produce 3 and read as a kernel fact; that assertion failed on its first form and was corrected to what the renderer actually emits. **The REASON we first published for that admission was borrowed and is false — corrected 2026-08-31.** The sentence *"duplicate checking skips wildcarded operands"* came from a peer's message, went into our catalog gotcha and this entry as the mechanism, and a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-08-31-06` then refuted it from their own `spec/02`. Measured here on our own carrier, the boundary is **identity, not the star**:

| condition | verdict |
|---|---|
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Store/ShellRows*, /Store/ShellRows*)` — the same group twice | `ADMITTED` |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Store/RowShell, /Store/RowShell/Rows*)` — a member strictly CONTAINING another | **`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2`** |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Store/RowShell, /Store/FilledRows*)` — the same pair made disjoint, the control | `ADMITTED` |

So containment *is* checked and the star does **not** exempt it; what is tolerated is the identical operand. The number (6, not 3) was ours and executed and stands — only the explanation was wrong, which is exactly the split the inbound-channel rule in [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) names: a measurement of ours carrying a mechanism of theirs. The catalog gotcha now states the measured double-count and its admission and no longer offers a reason; the refusal lives here, because the catalog's own guard requires an executed claim probe behind any author-facing refusal and its probe fixtures carry no containing pair. Locked in `validate.laws.EmptyGroupOperandLawsTest`.

**Static admission of the duplicate is ours too**, not carried on report: `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Store/ShellRows*, /Store/ShellRows*)` is `ADMITTED`, a row added to [KF217](#kf217)'s table in `validate.laws.EmptyGroupOperandLawsTest`, which matters because the catalog line below asserts static admission and would otherwise rest on someone else's oracle. All three shapes a peer had reported as pinned are now measured **here** instead — `(ShellRows*, ShellRows*)`, `(ShellRows*, FilledRows*)` and `(Filled, ShellRows*, FilledRows*)` are each `ADMITTED`, matching the recorded rule that duplicate checking skips wildcarded operands. *Corrected 2026-08-30: this sentence first cited a12-kernel-lean as having pinned those rows `KERNEL_CONFIRMED`, on their message. They retracted it — the rows came from a window they could not certify clean, and they had explicitly declined to cite them — so a citation of ours briefly rested on evidence its own author disowned. The channel rule's inbound mirror, now in [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md).* Runtime acceptance would not have closed this either way: the kernel building an engine for the duplicate model and computing 6 is not an `MVK_*` authoring verdict, which is why the static rows are measured separately. Locked in `adapter.laws.NestedGroupFillCountLawsTest.aRepeatedStarredOperandIsCountedTWICEAndTwoDistinctStarredOperandsAdd`.

**Authoring consequence, and it is why this rides the catalog too:** naming a starred group twice is statically admitted and silently doubles its rows, so the spelling closest to "count these rows once" is the one that cannot warn you.

Locked in `adapter.laws.NestedGroupFillCountLawsTest.theMixedFormAddsAFixedPresenceBitToTheStarredRowCardinality`.

**Related, and answering one of that entry's stated non-measurements from the other arm:** an **over-limit** row is instantiated and `GroupFilled`-visible yet excluded from the starred count — `NumberOfFilledGroups(Coverages*)` over rows 1,2,3 with 3 beyond the declared range counts **2**, locked in `adapter.laws.OverRepetitionFormalGateDiffTest.numberOfFilledGroupsExcludesOverLimitRow`. **And a computation writing INTO an over-limit row has its target CLEARED — measured on the indexed-parallel carrier, where it was open on both estates** *(a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-31-08`, whose `limit` row left this carrier unclaimed; measured here 2026-08-31)*. Their reason for not inheriting it was specific: a parallel computation's index column has no entry at an over-limit row, so that row might be outside its execution domain rather than merely capacity-excluded. **The premise turns out not to be load-bearing.** `Lines` declared max 2, joined to `Picks` by `LineRef`, target `Fulfilled = [Picks/PickedQty For LineRef]`:

| document | `Lines[1]` | `Lines[2]` | `Lines[3]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| two lines — at capacity | `10` | `20` | — |
| three lines, line 3 carrying a **resolvable** join (`L3` → a pick of 30) and a seeded `999` | `10` | `20` | **cleared, no value** |
| two lines, line 2's join **unresolvable** (`L9`, no partner), seeded `999` | `10` | **`0`** | — |

The over-limit row is cleared *although* its join would have yielded 30, so the clearing follows the capacity exclusion and not the index domain. **The third row is what makes `cleared` mean anything:** an in-capacity row whose join cannot resolve does not clear — it computes the kind's empty value `0` and overwrites the seed. So the carrier distinguishes "no value to compute" (a number) from "this row is not mine to write" (cleared, no value), and without that row a cleared line 3 would be equally consistent with an unresolved join. In-capacity siblings are asserted unchanged across the two documents. Locked in `adapter.laws.OverLimitIndexedParallelTargetLawsTest`.

That lock is on the **rule** arm. **The compute arm agrees, measured here 2026-08-30 rather than inherited** — `Riders` declared max 5, at four, five, six and seven instantiated rows the starred count reads 4, 5, 5, 5 and a starred `Sum` over the same rows reads 4, 5, 5, 5, so the surplus rows contribute to neither quantity. The four-row row is the control: without it "5 everywhere" is equally consistent with the quantity being pinned at capacity regardless of content. Locked in `adapter.laws.NestedGroupFillCountLawsTest.theCOMPUTEArmExcludesAnOverLimitRowFromBothTheCountAndTheSum`.

**Why this was measured rather than assumed, and it is the transferable part.** The exclusion had been stated arm-scoped precisely because these two arms diverge on this same operator for a formally invalid operand ([KF120](#kf120)), so agreement elsewhere proves nothing about it. a12-kernel-lean measured the compute arm independently on that flag (checkpoint `src-starred-group-count-computation`, row `over-limit`) and reports it caught a live defect in their own work: they had implemented the exclusion by reusing an in-capacity extent whose evidence was rule-arm only, a reuse that needed no new branch and so raised no question. **Reuse across an arm, carrier, phase, depth, or topology boundary is a claim, not an inheritance** — the general form is now a row in this project's oracle table. Three instances here inside one week, two of them silent: [KF120](#kf120)'s count sentence read as unscoped, `NumberOfFilledGroupsStarDiffTest`'s `validateFull` lock read as compute-arm coverage, and this one, which was flagged instead.

## §9 supplement: a computation's self-validation polarity asks whether growth can still REACH the stored value (kernel runtime, 2026-08-30) <a id="kf219"></a>

> Fold: pending — folds into §9 beside [KF218](#kf218)'s fold structure; the polarity channel itself is §"error typing".

*Corrected 2026-08-30, before this entry had been read by anyone but its author: it first claimed the flip **follows the starred operand**, on rows that were all taken BELOW a repeatable group's declared capacity, where that account fits every row and is still false. a12-kernel-lean built the at-capacity discriminator and refuted it; the original rows stand as measured and are kept below.*

A computation's implicit self-validation message — raised when the stored target value does not match the computed one — carries `OMISSION_ERROR` when **filling more could still reconcile the two**, and `VALUE_ERROR` otherwise. Two conditions, both necessary: the quantity must have headroom, **and** growth must move it *toward* the stored value. A starred operand is only the ordinary instance of having headroom.

*Corrected twice, both times because a peer built the document our own rows could not distinguish. First reading, "the flip follows the starred operand": every row was taken below capacity, where it fits and is false. Second reading, "the quantity could still grow": every row either project held had the computed value BELOW its seed, so headroom and direction moved together and no row separated them. The rows themselves were right each time; the mechanism written on top of them was not, which is the failure the oracle table's mechanism row names.*

**Each conjunct has its own discriminator, and neither alone suffices.**

*Direction is necessary* — headroom without it is not enough. `Riders` is below capacity at three of five rows, every cell filled, so the count can still grow; the only variable is the stored seed:

| document | stored seed | computed | message type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 of 5 rows, cells filled | **1** | 3 — *above* the seed | **`VALUE_ERROR`** |
| the same document | 9 | 3 — below the seed, the control | `OMISSION_ERROR` |

Growing moves the count further from 1, so no amount of filling reconciles them and the kernel says so. A pure headroom account predicts `OMISSION_ERROR` on both rows. *(Raised by a12-kernel-lean, who held only below-seed rows and could not reach this document; measured here.)*

*Headroom is necessary* — direction without it is not enough either. `Riders` declared max 5, so filling it exhausts the growth channel a row count depends on:

| document | starred count | starred `Sum` over the same group |
|---|---|---|
| 4 of 5 rows, every cell filled | `OMISSION_ERROR` | `OMISSION_ERROR` |
| **5 of 5 rows, every cell filled** | **`VALUE_ERROR`** | **`VALUE_ERROR`** |
| **5 of 5 rows, every cell EMPTY** | **`VALUE_ERROR`** | **`OMISSION_ERROR`** |

**The third row is the one that settles it**: one document, one starred group, two operators disagreeing. No account in terms of the *operand's form* can split them — both read `Riders*`. The count cannot grow because capacity is exhausted; the sum still can because a row's cells are empty. **Two growth channels — add a row, fill a cell — tracked per quantity.**

**The original rows, still valid and still useful**, showing the operand-form half below capacity (one row instantiated, so both channels open):

| computation | its operands | message type |
|---|---|---|
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(Contact, Warranty)` | filled | `VALUE_ERROR` |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(Riders*)` | same document | `OMISSION_ERROR` |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(Contact, Warranty)` | emptied — control | `OMISSION_ERROR` |

They are consistent with the corrected rule: a fixed pair with every operand filled has no headroom, a starred group below capacity has some.

**What this does to the field-count reading**, and it is the interesting part: `adapter.laws.FilledCountLawsTest`'s rule — unfilled operands remaining ⇒ `OMISSION_ERROR`, every operand filled ⇒ `VALUE_ERROR` — is **not** a prior that happened to fit here. It is the same rule, and the sentence added on top of it, *"a starred operand can never reach all-filled"*, is the false part: it can, by exhausting capacity. Both projects had the mechanism right and the boundary wrong, because both measured only below capacity.

Locked in `adapter.laws.NestedGroupFillCountLawsTest` — `thePolarityIsDIRECTIONALAndNotMerelyWhetherTheQuantityCanStillMove` (the direction rows), `polarityTracksTheQuantitysOwnHeadroomAndNotTheStar` (the capacity rows) and `aStarredOperandFlipsTheComputationSelfValidationPolarity` (the below-capacity rows, retained as the operand-form half).

**The same message's `fillToFix` channel is the whole `referenced` set or empty — never a proper subset**, so it is not a list of what is unfilled. a12-kernel-lean measured that across 30 message observations; reproduced here on a shape neither side had used for it, the computation's implicit self-validation, and on our kernel oracle. **The trap is a document with nothing empty in it:** four of five rows instantiated with *every* cell filled types `OMISSION_ERROR` on row headroom alone, and the channel is still non-empty and still equal to `referenced`. A consumer that filters it to unfilled cells therefore renders an empty hint for the one message whose purpose is saying what to fill.

**And `referenced` itself is derived from the AUTHORED OPERAND, not from what evaluation read** *(a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-30-07`, measured here 2026-08-30)*. The discriminator is a starred operand in a document holding **no instantiated row**, and the strong form settles it without argument — the set is **byte-identical** with zero rows and with four filled rows:

| document | `referenced` for `NumberOfFilledGroups(Riders*)` |
|---|---|
| no row instantiated | `/Catalogue[1]/TallyStar`, `/Catalogue[1]/Coverage[1]/Riders[0]/RiderName`, `/Catalogue[1]/Coverage[1]/Riders[0]/RiderAmount` |
| four rows, every cell filled | *identical* |

A set built from cells evaluation reached would be empty in the first document and would enumerate eight pointers in the second. It does neither. **The consequence is the same trap as `fillToFix`'s:** a checker that builds the inventory from cells it managed to read under-reports on exactly the documents where the message matters.

**Instrument limit, and it is load-bearing for anyone comparing this channel with another project's.** Every pointer in our `referenced` / `fillToFix` / `errorField` readings is rendered by **our own** `formatPointer(fullName, repetitionIndexes)` — slash-led, one segment at a time, no elision of index one, printing whatever integer the pointer object holds. The kernel's own string rendering never reaches us. So this estate **cannot** observe a difference between two kernel-side address spellings: we normalise every pointer to one form before reading it, and an absence of dialect variation here is a property of our formatter, not a measurement of the kernel. What *is* kernel data rather than our formatting is the **integer**, taken from `repetitionIndexes()` — which is why the `0` below is a real observation and the surrounding punctuation is not. *(Written 2026-08-31 after a12-kernel-lean reported two address dialects in one list; agreeing would have been a false confirmation.)*

Three facts fall out of the same rows. The starred axis carries coordinate **0** — not a row index, since no row 0 exists and four instantiated rows do not move it, so it reads as the *unbound* wildcard axis; this is the kernel pointer's own `repetitionIndexes()`, not a parse of a rendered string. The extent follows **each operand's own reach**: the group-count operand names its group's whole subtree (both row fields), while a `Sum` over one flattened field names `/Catalogue[1]/TallySum`, `/Catalogue[1]/Coverage[1]/Riders[0]/RiderAmount` — that field alone. And every message also names its **computed target**. Locked in `…NestedGroupFillCountLawsTest.theReferencedSetFollowsTheAuthoredOperandAndIsUnchangedByWhetherAnyRowExists`.

Our interpreter is not exposed to either trap: `messageReferences` walks the condition's `Cond` tree rather than the evaluation's reads, and `DmInterpreter` sets `fillToFix` to `referenced` for an OMISSION and to empty otherwise, unconditionally, so it cannot emit a proper subset — an identity differentially locked against the kernel's `getRefOmissionErrorResponsiblePointers` in `RichMessageDiffTest`, which this adds the all-filled row to. Locked in `…NestedGroupFillCountLawsTest.anOmissionsFillToFixIsTheWholeReferencedSetEvenWhenEveryCellItNamesIsFilled`.

**a12-kernel-lean's wildcard-free witness is now reproduced here too**, in the same at-capacity document: the wildcard-free `NumberOfFilledGroups(Contact, Warranty)` sits at `VALUE_ERROR` beside the starred `Sum`'s `OMISSION_ERROR`. Worth stating precisely, because it is the **weaker** of the two splits for refuting an operand-form account — a fixed-versus-starred pair is exactly what such an account predicts. The refutation is the starred-count-versus-starred-**Sum** row, where operand form is held constant and the two still differ. The wildcard-free row is carried because that witness had rested on one project.

## The mandatory-information collectors read a numeric literal through a SENTINEL that a 32-bit narrowing can collide with (kernel SOURCE READ — hypothesis, not measured, 2026-08-30) <a id="kf220"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a rule-set analysis TOOL-API internal, outside KERNEL-SEMANTICS's runtime-evaluation scope. **This entry is a source read.** No row here has been executed; nothing in our estate calls the interface, so we hold no observation of the derived output. It is written down because it is a trap for the first consumer of a surface our survey now marks verified, and because the enumeration below corrects the shape it was reported to us in.

`FeldOperationUtil.getZahlKonstanteWert(IOperation)` returns `(int) Math.round(Double.parseDouble(value))` for a numeric constant and **`-1` for "not a numeric constant"** — one value carrying both meanings, after a rounding *and* a 32-bit narrowing. So `-1`, `4294967295`, `8589934591` and any decimal rounding onto `-1` all produce the sentinel.

**The enumeration, so the next reader does not re-derive it.** `grep -rn 'getZahlKonstanteWert' <kernel>/kernel-tool/kernel-core-service/src/main/java/com/mgmtp/a12/kernel/core/service/internal/mandatoryinformation` → **6 call sites in 3 files, all 6 read**:

| file | sites | guard | what the sentinel is confused with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EvaluatorVisitor` | 83, 103 | `z != -1` / `z == -1` | only the sentinel |
| `CollectorFuerGlobalePflichtmengenInfo` | 101, 109 | `z > 0` | the sentinel **and** every genuine constant ≤ 0 |
| `CollectorFuerPflichtVordruckInfo` | 222, 230 | `z > 0`, assigned into a `double z` | as above — and the widening happens *after* the narrowing, so it does not undo it |

*(a12-kernel-lean reported this as "the three visitors bail on `z == -1`". Only the first file does. The other two use `z > 0`, a weaker predicate that also swallows legitimate non-positive constants, so the corrective for a consumer differs per file.)*

**Why most of it is probably unobservable, and where it might not be.** Every literal that collides is either negative — where `NumberOfFilledFields(…) >= -1` is vacuously true and "nothing mandatory" is the *correct* answer — or ≥ `4294967295`, which under the `<=`/`<` directions the `z > 0` sites test is equally vacuous. In those five sites the bug's answer and the right answer coincide, which is why no consumer would have noticed. The exception is `EvaluatorVisitor`'s `AnzahlFelder >= z` arm: there a colliding literal is **unsatisfiable-but-strong**, so a semantics-respecting collector and a narrowing-bugged one need not agree.

**What would settle it** — and it is a design, not a run we have made: three rules over one two-field list, `>= 2` (satisfiable baseline), `>= 3` (**the control** — unsatisfiable, `z` valid) and `>= 4294967295` (unsatisfiable, `z` narrows to `-1`), comparing `getMandatory()` across them. The control is the load-bearing row: if `>= 3` already yields nothing, the shape cannot discriminate and the collision is unobservable here too. Blocked on a capability rather than on cost — the query takes kernel `IRule` objects and `KernelAdapter` deliberately lets no kernel type escape ([`ARCHITECTURE`](ARCHITECTURE.md) N8), so routing it means giving the adapter a typed mandatory-information capability first.

## §2 supplement — a repeatable group's `repeatability` domain is `> 0`, and the LOAD gate tolerates everything the MVK gate refuses (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-08-31) <a id="kf221"></a>

> Fold: pending — it belongs beside the structural model-shape rows in §2, which have no folded home yet.

A group's `repeatability` is admitted for any integer **greater than zero**, and refused below that by the MVK gate with `MVK_MAX_VALUES_INVALID`. The refusal is emitted **per element** — once for the group, once for each field beneath it — followed by one message naming the domain, and that last message has two distinct wordings: a zero or `null` draws *"Only values greater than 0 are allowed."* while a negative draws *"Only values without a sign are allowed."*

| value | deserialize + expand | `checkConsistency` |
|---|---|---|
| `2`, `3` | loads | **admitted** |
| **`1`** | loads | **admitted** |
| `"2"` (the number as text) | loads | **admitted** |
| key absent | loads | **admitted** — absence means non-repeatable |
| `0` | loads | `MVK_MAX_VALUES_INVALID` + *greater than 0* |
| `null` | loads | `MVK_MAX_VALUES_INVALID` + *greater than 0* |
| `-1` | loads | `MVK_MAX_VALUES_INVALID` + *without a sign* |
| `-2147483648` (the signed 32-bit floor) | loads | `MVK_MAX_VALUES_INVALID` + *without a sign* |
| `-2147483649` (one below it) | **refused** | — |
| `true` | **refused** | — |

**The two gates are the finding, not a detail of the method.** Every rejected value above **loads cleanly**: deserialize + expand accept `null`, `0` and `-1` without complaint, and only the consistency check refuses them. So a table taken at the reader — which is what `WorkspaceIncludeStructureKernelTest` measures for the neighbouring MOUNT carrier, where the kernel really is tolerant — cannot speak for this question at all. This was measured the wrong way round first: a load-gate-only run reported every value admitted and was one sentence from being published as a contradiction of a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-08-31-07`, which had it right. Naming which gate a verdict comes from is what separated a correction from an error.

**Their clause is right on `null` and `0` and one step too strong on the rest.** It states the domain as "a finite integer of **at least two**"; `1` is admitted at both gates, so the measured domain is `> 0`. A repeatability of `1` is simply a non-repeatable group spelled explicitly, which is why it is legal and why nothing downstream needs it.

**That `1` means non-repeatable is now MEASURED and not merely read off the domain (added 2026-08-31).** The clause above asserted it; the discriminator is a star. A group carrying `"repeatability": 1` — which is exactly what this project writes for every non-repeatable group, root groups included — is refused a wildcard with `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` and the kernel's own wording *"Since 'Plain' is not repeatable, it is not allowed to specify an asterisk"*, while the same rule over a `repeatability: 3` sibling is `valid`. So the kernel reads `1` as not repeatable, agreeing with our encoding; the admitted-integer domain (`> 0`) and the set of values that make a group a repetition LIST (`≥ 2`) are two different questions, and conflating them is what makes our builders look stale. *(a12-kernel-lean read the `≥2` help text as a lag behind this entry's `> 0` on 2026-08-31; it is not one.)*

**Our own builders are deliberately stricter, and now that is documented rather than merely true — and since 2026-08-31 the reason travels with the refusal**, in `GroupAddCommand`/`GroupModifyCommand`'s `--repeatable` help and `GroupBuilder.repeatable`'s javadoc, because a bound stated without its reason is indistinguishable from a stale one to every reader who meets it there rather than here. `DocumentModelDraft.GroupBuilder.repeatable` and `ModelDocument.addRepeatableGroup` both refuse below `2`, so they refuse `1` where the kernel admits it. That is an intentional API narrowing — `repeatable(1)` asks for a repeatable group that cannot repeat, i.e. a no-op the caller almost certainly did not mean, and the plain group builder already expresses it — but until this measurement the refusal had **no test and no kernel basis anywhere in the repository**, which is exactly the shape the standing client-side-refusal rule calls a defect waiting to be found. The narrowing stays; what changes is that its basis is measured and its one-step breadth is stated.

**Extended 2026-09-16 with the two boundary cells, and the reason they were worth taking is the CHECKER rather than A12.** The floor is symmetric with the ceiling: `-2147483648` still draws the class, and one below it is refused by the reader exactly as one above `2147483647` is. The portable checker's `GROUP_REPETITION_COUNT` family had implemented only the upper half, so a stored `"repeatability":0` was reported by A12 and **silent** there — a route by which a model A12 rejects returned no finding at all. Fixed the same day with both boundaries; the checker's mirror is `consistency.GroupRepetitionCountTest`, and the false-pass class this belonged to is [the coverage residue](archived/PORTABLE-CONSISTENCY-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md#coverage-residue).

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.GroupRepeatabilityDomainLawsTest` — both gates in one call, the refusal text pinned verbatim including the per-element repetition and both domain wordings.)*

## §6 supplement — a bare constant's admission and its store are both decided by the target's declared FORMAT STRING, and the declared kind reaches neither (kernel `checkConsistency` + `compute`, 2026-08-31) <a id="kf222"></a>

> Fold: pending — newly recorded constant-assignment fact; folds into §6 (dates and time) on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-08-31-02`, `-03` and `-04` on our own fixtures, independently built in a different domain, with a two-field group and a different Base Year value. Every cell they predicted reproduced on the first run.

**Admission is a family gate keyed on the format string.** A TIME field declared `HH:mm:ss` admits `"12:30:00"` and refuses `"05.03.2024"`; a **DATE** field declared `HH:mm:ss` does exactly the same, and a TIME field declared `yyyy-MM-dd` inverts both. Each kind appears on both sides of both outcomes, so the kind is excluded as the cause rather than left unvaried. A family mismatch draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`; a String constant into a STRING field is the live control that keeps the refusals from reading as a dead gate.

**The cross-kind cells STORE, so the format governs the runtime too.** A DATE-kind field declared `HH:mm:ss` stores `12:30:00`; a TIME-kind field declared `yyyy-MM-dd` stores `2024-03-05`. A peer keying its renderer on the kind stays green on the admission table and writes the wrong text here.

**The store drops the components the format omits, silently.** One `"05.03.2024"` stores `05.03.2024` into `dd.MM.yyyy`, `2024-03-05` into `yyyy-MM-dd`, and `2024` into `yyyy` — nothing cleared, nothing errored, no message. A component-omitting target discards day and month with no signal at all, which is the most likely authoring mistake in this family.

**A declared Base Year is an authoring gate and contributes nothing to the stored text.** With `baseYear` 2019 declared, one `"05.03.2024"` stores `03` for `MM`, `03-05` for `MM-dd`, `2024-03` for `yyyy-MM`, `2024` for `yyyy` and `2024-03-05` for `dd.MM.yyyy`. 2019 appears in no cell, so an admitted constant is not evidence that the Base Year's year survived into the value.

**Our typed builder now models this gate rather than the kind, and its agreement is locked over the WHOLE admitted vocabulary** (fixed 2026-09-05, was `DG43`). `Computation.Builder` used to require `operation.kind() == computedField.kind()`, refusing both cross-kind cells the kernel admits and stores. It now compares the operation's temporal family against the family of the target's **declared format** — supplied by `BoundModel.computation` from `ModelIndex.temporalFormat`, so no public type had to grow a component. Two things make it a model rather than a loosened predicate: kind equality is no longer a pass on a temporal pair either (a DATE-kind field declared `HH:mm:ss` refuses a date value, and the builder now refuses it too, with a message naming the format rather than the kind), and the agreement is asserted cell for cell against the kernel over all **twelve** admitted format strings × three constant families, not over the two crossings the fix was written for.

**The classification is read off the format's components, and the datetime row is why that needed measuring.** `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` *contains* the clock pattern, so a "has clock components" reading classifies it as clock-accepting; measured, it refuses a bare clock constant and takes only the datetime spelling. Presence of **both** component sets is what makes a format datetime. Quoted literal sections are erased before the components are read, since the `'T'` separator is otherwise a component letter. `DATE_RANGE` is deliberately outside the gate — its declaration is a `(format, separator)` pair and nothing here measures assigning across it, so it keeps plain kind equality.

**The DATETIME carrier stores by its format too, and it was measured rather than inherited** (added 2026-09-05). The twelve-format admission sweep runs on a DATE-declared target, so `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` was covered *there* — but every STORE row was a date-only or clock-only format, leaving the carrier whose format holds both component sets unmeasured on the half that decides what a reimplementer writes. Both cross directions now measure: a **DATE**-declared field declared `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` stores `2024-03-05T12:30:00`, and a **DATETIME**-declared field declared `yyyy-MM-dd` stores `2024-03-05` and declared `HH:mm:ss` stores `12:30:00` — each following its format, never its kind, with the aligned rows as controls. Asked by a12-kernel-lean, who explicitly refused to inherit the DATE/TIME result onto DATETIME and narrowed their own certificate instead; the crossing did not follow from the rows we held, and saying so is what got it run.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.ConstantTargetFormatLawsTest` — the 2×2×2 family gate with its String control, both cross-kind stores, the DATETIME carrier's four store rows, the component-omitting stores, the Base Year admission table across DATE and DATE_FRAGMENT, the complete twelve-format × three-family map with our own builder's verdicts beside the kernel's in the same table, and the four-cell crossing table that keeps the fix from reading as "temporal targets no longer check anything".)*

## §6 supplement — the omitted-year date and the DATETIME literal are both WITNESSED, and the Base Year is required exactly where constant and target disagree about the year (kernel `checkConsistency` + `compute`, 2026-08-31) <a id="kf223"></a>

> Fold: pending — newly recorded temporal-literal vocabulary; folds into §6 (dates and time) on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

**Corrects a12-kernel-lean's two "no witness found" records** (`SPEC-2026-08-31-02`'s `omitted-year` row, `-03`'s `inventory` row), and sharpens `-04`'s Base Year account from one quadrant to the whole grid.

**A refusal code names the check that refused, never the input that reached it** — the reading a12-kernel-lean withdrew in `-03`, and it was drafted here too before a control refuted it. An unclassifiable `"HELLO"` draws the *same* code as a well-formed literal of the wrong family on every target measured, so a code shared with that control carries no information about classification. The only evidence a spelling classified is that it was **admitted**.

**The omitted-year date literal exists: `"05.03."` and `"13.07."` are admitted; `"05.03"` and `"03.2024"` are not.** The trailing dot is load-bearing. It holds in both carriers — assigned as a constant to a computation target, and compared against a field, which is the carrier this project's own `DateLiteral` javadoc has always claimed and never measured.

**A Base Year is required exactly when the constant and the target disagree about carrying a YEAR, in either direction.** Two constants × seven declared formats × Base Year present or absent, no cell omitted: a complete constant needs one for `MM` and `MM-dd` only; a yearless constant needs one for all five year-bearing formats and none for the two yearless ones. The year-leading targets are what make this specific rather than "any component disagreement" — `yyyy` differs from a complete constant in two components of three and needs no Base Year, while `MM-dd` differs in one and does. a12-kernel-lean's clause covers the first row; the second reverses it.

**The DATETIME literal is the German date, `T`, and the clock: `"05.03.2024T12:30:00"`.** Against a DATETIME target declared `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` it is the only one of four spellings admitted — the ISO form the target's own declared format uses is refused — and it stores as `2024-03-05T12:30:00`. So the literal's spelling is a lexer convention owing nothing to the format the value is rendered into, the same two-rule composition [KF222](#kf222) records for dates.

**The DATERANGE literal stays unwitnessed over six spellings**, and that is an absence over those six rather than a claim of unauthorability: `05.03.2024-31.03.2024`, `05.03.2024 - 31.03.2024`, `05.03.2024/31.03.2024`, `05.03.2024..31.03.2024`, `2024-03-05-2024-03-31`, `05.03.2024T31.03.2024`. All six share the negative control's code. A plain date literal on the same target draws a *different* code, which is the only reason to believe this gate discriminates its operand at all.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.TemporalConstantLiteralWitnessLawsTest` — both carriers, the complete 28-cell Base Year grid computed from the year-agreement rule, the DATETIME witness with its store, and every probed spelling listed in its assertion so the denominator is the finding.)*

## §3 supplement — a formally erroneous field contributes NEITHER TRUE NOR FALSE to a quantifier over its list, so only what needed it is undecided; full validation behaves exactly as partial does (kernel `validateFull` + `validatePart`, 2026-08-31) <a id="kf224"></a>

> Fold: pending — newly recorded formal-error fact; folds into §3 (formal errors and the "unknown" state) on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Answers a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-08-31-05`, which is source-grounded from the kernel's business documentation with no measurement of their own — they cannot reach `validatePart` on their accepted probe route, and we can, so the entry is settleable here. **One half confirms and one half is contradicted.**

**Confirmed: the rule is not a partial-validation artefact.** Four documents through `validateFull` and through `validatePart` with the whole group relevant agree cell for cell, both malformed ones included.

**Contradicted: "dropped from the LIST rather than counted on either side" is not what happens, and it is not equivalent to "neither filled nor empty" as their consequence states.** Over a three-member list with one erroneous member and two filled, `AllFieldsFilled` does **not** fire — dropping predicts that it would, counting the member filled predicts `count == 3`, counting it empty predicts the negation and `count == 2`, and none of the three occurs. The erroneous member is in the list and settles nothing.

**Corrected 2026-08-31, same day, and the correction is worth more than the entry.** This first read "a formally erroneous field SUPPRESSES every quantifier over its list", measured on four rules over one malformed document — `AllFieldsFilled`, its negation, and the count at two values. **a12-kernel-lean re-derived the result independently and reported the row that refutes that wording: `AtLeastOneFieldFilled` fires on the very same document.** Every rule in the original set needed the erroneous member's state to reach a verdict, so the account fitted every row and was still false; nothing in the set sat on the other side of that axis. This is the set-level confound the oracle rules name, in a set of RULES rather than of documents or fixtures — a shape the rule's existing instances had not covered.

The measured law is symmetric, and needs both malformed documents to state:

| the three-member list holds | `ALL` | `NOT_ALL` | `AT_LEAST_ONE` | `NO_FIELD` | `count == 3` | `count == 2` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| three valid — control | fires | — | fires | — | fires | — |
| one empty, two valid — control | — | fires | fires | — | — | fires |
| **one erroneous, two valid** | — | — | **fires** | — | — | — |
| **one erroneous, two empty** | — | **fires** | — | — | — | — |

So a quantifier is decided exactly when the members whose state is KNOWN already settle it: a known TRUE settles the existential, a known FALSE settles the negation, and only a verdict that would need the erroneous member's own state is left undecided. Consistent with [KF120](#kf120)'s group carrier ("leaving erroneous groups in neither bucket") and with `QuantifierMalformedDiffTest`, which holds the row where `AtLeastOneFieldFilled` does NOT fire because no known member is filled — the fourth row above, reached one rule at a time as a kernel↔interpreter differential.

What no row here can see is the clause's own subject: whether the kernel's internal *relevant set* excludes the field. The observable behaviour is only inconsistent with it being dropped from the **quantifier's operand list**.

Measured on two converters (a malformed NUMBER, an out-of-calendar DATE) so the result belongs to the class rather than to one converter, with a liveness control reading a field OUTSIDE every quantified list — the first version read the list's own first member, which the fourth document leaves empty, so the control would have gone silent exactly where it was needed.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.ErroneousFieldRelevanceLawsTest` — six quantifier rules × four documents × two converters, plus the full/partial equality.)*

## §4 supplement — the mandatory-information derivation reads rule CONDITION SHAPE, and its two channels spell paths differently (kernel `getMandatoryInformationFromRules`, 2026-08-31) <a id="kf225"></a>

> Fold: pending — newly recorded model-level derivation; folds into §4 (the "required" property) on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

`IRuleCollectionMetaInformation.getMandatoryInformationFromRules` derives three name sets from a rule collection with no document in play — the kernel's own answer to "which fields does this model require?", and the first MODEL-level observation this project can make. Reached through `KernelAdapter.mandatoryInformation`, which keeps the kernel types inside and returns plain `Set<String>`.

**It reads condition SHAPE, not referenced fields.** On a five-rule claim model, a field named by two rules in ordinary comparisons (`[Amount] > 1000`) appears in no set, while `FieldNotFilled` and `GroupNotFilled` conditions do. A starred negative quantifier reaches nothing, matching the kernel's own note that it does not hold for every repetition.

**Two shape facts that were predicted wrong before being measured, and both bite a consumer joining these names to model paths.** `GroupNotFilled(/Claim/Adjuster)` on a NESTED group yields the enclosing **root** group, not the group named. And the two channels spell paths differently: the field sets carry a leading slash (`/Claim/PolicyNumber`), `mandatoryRootGroups` does not (`Claim`).

**What the `GroupFilled ∧ FieldNotFilled` shape does is measured but not explained.** The kernel's documentation offers it for "mandatory regarding its root group"; it puts the field in **both** field sets, which is also consistent with that documentation's other note that a mandatory field is mandatory regarding its root group too. This model does not separate those readings, so no mechanism is claimed.

**A COUNT shape names no field at all, and reaches the root group only in the `<` direction.** One rule per model so an empty set can be attributed, over a two-field `NumberOfFilledFields`:

| the model's single rule | `mandatory` | `mandatoryForRootGroup` | `mandatoryRootGroups` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NumberOfFilledFields(PolicyNumber, Amount) < 2` | — | — | `Claim` |
| `NumberOfFilledFields(PolicyNumber, Amount) >= 2` | — | — | — |
| `FieldNotFilled(PolicyNumber)` — presence control | `/Claim/PolicyNumber` | `/Claim/PolicyNumber` | `Claim` |

The pair varies direction and nothing else: both comparisons are satisfiable and non-trivial over two fields, where `< 3` against `>= 3` would have moved satisfiability too and given an empty result two explanations. The presence control is what makes the count row readable — it reaches the root group as well, so the root group is not a count-shape peculiarity, and the count row's content is the two **empty field sets** beside a root group the kernel still reports: it knows the group cannot be left alone and cannot name which field settles it. a12-kernel-lean reported both facts from their own run of this capability; they are recorded here as our rows because they were re-measured here, on our fixtures, and the presence control corrected the prediction that only a count shape would move the root-group set.

Built for a12-kernel-lean's `EXP-2026-08-30-01`, whose question — whether a rule literal that narrows to the kernel's absent-value sentinel silently drops a rule from this derivation ([KF220](#kf220)) — needs exactly this observation and cannot be reached by `validateFull` or `compute`. The derivation itself is not the answer to that question; it is the instrument.
