**The parameter terminal bundle follows the owning DECLARATION, not the rule kind.** Reported as a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-06` for admission; measured here on the render side, which they explicitly did not claim. A computation at a repeatable `/Invoice/Lines` whose message reads `row=[$#RuleGroup$] qty=[$Qty.value$]`, over a document whose second row disagrees with the computed value, renders `row=[2] qty=[3]` on both kernel strategies. The group shorthand resolves against the generated rule exactly as it would in a hand-written one.

**The field parameter rides along as the discriminating control.** Without it, an engine that rendered no text at all for this carrier and an engine that rendered text but dropped the group token produce the same visible symptom — an empty or half-empty message — and only the field position separates them. It earned that role immediately: this interpreter rendered the message as the **empty string**, because its loader never read a computation's `errorMessage` ([IF324](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if324)), and the control is what showed the defect was one layer below the group parameter rather than in it.

*(Locked: [`adapter.laws.ComputationMessageDiffTest`](../adapter/src/test/kotlin/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/adapter/laws/ComputationMessageDiffTest.kt) — Groovy-dynamic, generated Java and the interpreter, on a computation authored through the typed `EditSession`/`Computation.Builder` surface rather than injected as JSON, so the row also witnesses that our own authoring path carries the message through.)*

## §6 supplement — a YEARLESS stored day is bounded by its month's length in the DECLARED Base Year (`validateFull`, both strategies, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf247"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §6's incomplete-format account beside [KF239](#kf239)'s admission gate; folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-12` on an independently authored carrier, measured here rather than cited: their rows are their observation, and this repository now holds its own. A `MM-dd` DATE cell holding `02-29` is `datumFormatFalsch` under a declared Base Year of **2023**, admitted under **2024**, and admitted when **no** Base Year is declared at all. So the year the model anchors to is what bounds the day, not February's greatest possible length.

**The undeclared configuration is the separator, and it is why the rule is about the anchor's leapness rather than about declaring a Base Year.** A base-year-free model behaves exactly like the leap case — because the anchor it falls back to is itself a leap year — so a reading of "declaring a Base Year tightens the bound" is refuted by the row that declares none. **The century pair separates it from a `year % 4` test**, which agrees on 2023/2024 and gets 1900 wrong: 1900 is refused and 2000 admitted, so the bound is the full Gregorian rule. February is the only month whose two candidate bounds differ, so one witness settles it; `02-28` and an ordinary March day cross under all five configurations, and `02-30` is refused even under a leap anchor, which is what keeps "admitted" from meaning "unchecked".

**This estate already implemented it, and the interesting part is that our LOCK stated the fact too broadly.** All three of our paths — the two `AutoChecks` check paths and `Document`'s store/read — pass `model.baseYear ?: 2000` into `completeFragmentToIso`, which bounds the day with `daysInMonth(y, mo)` against that anchor, so every row above was already correct and is now measured. But `interpreter … TemporalDeclaredFormatFormalTest`'s grid pins `MM-dd` + `02-29` as **admitted** with no base year in its `ModelDef` at all, so that row holds *because* the fallback anchor happens to be leap and nothing in the test said so. Every row in that grid shares the one configuration — the "one CONSTANT across every row you hold" confound, with the fixture supplying the constant. The row is not wrong; it was unconditional where the fact is conditional, and the axis it was missing is the one a12-kernel-lean's entry supplies.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.YearlessDayBoundBaseYearDiffTest` — five Base Year configurations over one document and one declaration, tri-engine, with the model bytes asserted to actually carry (and in the undeclared row, to lack) the base year, plus the crossing controls and the leap-anchor `02-30` refusal.)*

## §6 supplement — the COMPARISON-admission gate partitions temporal operands by declared FORMAT, on both kinds (kernel `checkConsistency` + tri-engine runtime, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf248"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends [KF211](#kf211)'s classifier rule to the comparison gate; folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-13`. [KF211](#kf211) established that a temporal field's declared format, never its kind, selects its formal check and its value decoder, on the complete 8-format × 3-kind grid. The operand family at the **comparison** gate follows the same rule: a clock-declared DATE compares with a clock and draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` against a date, while a date-declared TIME does the reverse.

**Why this was not already covered, which is the methodological point.** `adapter.laws.TemporalDeclaredFormatGateDiffTest` does measure the comparison gate — but on one arm (a date-declared TIME against a date-declared DATE) plus the ordinary clock-versus-date refusal as its control, and its model declares no clock-formatted DATE at all. The mirror was therefore *inherited* from the classifier rule rather than measured, and a classifier and an admission gate are different gates: that is a scope transfer, the reuse needing no new branch and so prompting no question. Measuring it took one model.

**The grid is a within-model 2×2 and every kind appears on both sides of both outcomes**, which is what rules out "DATE is the permissive kind" or "TIME is" and leaves the format; one direction alone would not have. Both admitted cross-kind arms were also RUN on all three engines, firing on equal operands and silent on unequal ones — an admission verdict cannot see a silent suppression, which is precisely the shape of the defect [IF314](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if314) fixed in this area.

**Our own surfaces already honour it, and one of them is the reason the typed API can express these conditions at all.** `BoundModel.requireTemporalShape` admits a handle when the declared format's shape matches, not only when the kind does, so `m.time(<clock-declared DATE>)` yields a time handle; without that the two admitted rows would be unauthorable through the typed surface and would read as "not a thing" rather than as admitted — the type-level-erasure failure mode. **Extended 2026-09-05 to the DATE_TIME family, which had been an explicit gap on BOTH sides.** a12-kernel-lean's entry limited itself to the DATE/TIME pair under equality and recorded the DateTime family's cross-kind comparison as untested; so did this entry, and so did four rounds of the exchange around it — each side declining to inherit the other's basis across a family boundary, correctly, since KF211's 12 × 3 grid reaches a DATE_TIME *declaration* only for the CLASSIFIER. Measured now on the same 2×2 shape one family over: a **stamp-declared DATE** compares with a stamp and draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` against a date, a **date-declared DATE_TIME** does the reverse, the two ordinary fields refuse each other, and both admitted arms fire tri-engine on equal operands and are silent on unequal ones. So the rule is the declared format's across all three date-bearing kinds, with each kind on both sides of both outcomes in every family.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.CrossKindTemporalComparisonGateDiffTest` — the 2×2 admission table plus the ordinary-pair refusal and both same-family controls, the model bytes asserted to carry the contradicting declarations, and the two admitted arms run tri-engine on firing and non-firing documents.)*

## §9 supplement — an extremum's operand-family refusal names the class its FIRST operand fixed (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf249"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §9's aggregate operand-admission account; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-11` on an independently authored carrier. The same two operands draw **`MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE`** behind a temporal leader and **`MVK_NOT_SORTABLE`** behind a numeric one, so the reported code names the class the first operand fixed rather than the offender's — and an author who reorders the list to "fix" it merely changes which code they get.

**Enumerated across the family rather than sampled, because the two spellings are different operators.** `MinValue`/`MaxValue` take a bare field list and `Min`/`Max` take bracketed value expressions; all four behave identically here, and the homogeneous controls (two dates, two numbers) are admitted in both forms, which is what keeps the refusals attributable to the family mix rather than to operand count.

**We already held the mechanism on a different operator, which is exactly why this needed measuring.** The catalog documents this first-operand rule on `NumberOfDifferentValues`, with its own worked pair — but a mechanism proved on one operator is not proved on another, the reuse needs no new branch, and so nothing prompts the question. `MaxValue`'s constraint named `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` alone and `Min`'s said only "kinds cannot be mixed", so our own self-describing surface could not have told an author what `MaxValue(<date>, <number>)` would return. That gap is closed in the same change: all four entries now carry a `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` corrective whose reject probe is CI-executed to that exact code and whose advertised repair is CI-executed as accepted.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.ExtremaOperandFamilyRefusalLawsTest` — both leaders × both spellings × all four operators, with the family-homogeneous controls; plus the four catalog correctives, executed on both polarities by `CatalogExamplesAreKernelValidTest` and `CatalogKernelClaimEvidenceTest`.)*

## §6 supplement — the extractor gate and the opt-in pre-1900 policy on a CLOCK-DECLARED DATE, the carrier our read-gate table lacked (kernel `checkConsistency` + tri-engine, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf250"></a>

> Fold: pending — completes [KF211](#kf211)'s read-gate account on its missing carrier; folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Takes the row a12-kernel-lean handed over from their `SPEC-2026-09-05-14` — so neither estate measured it twice — and settles, on the same model, a policy question they raised about six sites of theirs.

**The extractor pair, mirrored.** On a **DATE field declared `HH:mm:ss`**, `HoursFromTime` is **admitted** and `YearFromDate` is refused `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`; the admitted arm runs tri-engine, firing on `10:30:00` and silent on `11:30:00`. [KF211](#kf211)'s pair is the same two extractors with both axes flipped — admitted `YearFromDate`, refused `HoursFromTime`, on a TIME declared `yyyy-MM-dd`. Together the two carriers show the extractor gate keying on the declared format from **both** sides, which neither alone establishes.

**The opt-in pre-1900 guard is a model-ADMISSION question, and the answer is neither of the two an obvious 2×2 offers.** A DATE field declared `HH:mm:ss` carrying the check is refused outright — `MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID`, *"For date fields without a year, no 'additional check' may be specified"* — while the identical check on a year-bearing DATE declaration is admitted and duly reports `datumFalsch` at `1899-12-31` and nothing at `1900-01-01`. So the guard is not admitted-and-inert on a clock declaration; it is **not declarable there at all**, and the kernel's own message keys on the declared format's components rather than on the kind. **Consumer consequence, which is why a12-kernel-lean asked:** a policy that admits the opt-in check for the DATE *kind* is over-permissive on exactly this declaration, and one that refuses it for the TIME and DATE_TIME kinds is right — but right by schema, not by kind-reasoning (below).

**The other half of that 2×2 names no model, so it is a SCHEMA fact.** `youngerThan1900Check` is a property of the **`DateType` declaration object**: the kernel's `TimeType` and `DateTimeType` carry `format` and annotations and nothing else (kernel SOURCE at 30.8.1, the primary oracle for a signature question). "A TIME field declared `yyyy-MM-dd` with the guard set" is therefore unrepresentable rather than refused. The one link source reading leaves open — whether the DM-JSON path would carry the key in anyway, making it declarable-but-inert — is attacked and closed: injecting it makes the kernel's own **deserializer** reject the model, naming `TimeType` and the property in its reference chain, one layer earlier than any consistency gate. So the shape never reaches a gate that could be inert.

**Our own builder will construct the refused model.** `dateField(…).format("HH:mm:ss").rejectBefore1900()` produces DM-JSON the kernel rejects at codegen; the diagnostic arrives from `checkConsistency` rather than from the builder. That is delegation under-reporting, which is safe rather than wrong. *Corrected 2026-09-05: this first deferred the disposition to the owner via a `DEV-API-GAPS` row. The class that row asked for was then enumerated — see [KF251](#kf251) — and the answer is that no client-side refusal is added, because the record a refusal would guard is also built on the READ path; the two codes carry a curated corrective instead.*

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.ClockDeclaredDateGateDiffTest` — the extractor pair with an ordinary-clock counterpart, the admitted arm run tri-engine on firing and non-firing documents, the admission refusal asserted as exactly one message with its code, the year-bearing control on both sides of the 1900 boundary, the model bytes asserted to carry the declarations each row needs, and the deserializer attack on the schema claim.)*

## §6 supplement — the two DateType CONFIG gates read the declared format differently, and the refusal echoes the format in German pattern letters (kernel `checkConsistency`, complete over the derived vocabulary, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf251"></a>

> Fold: pending — completes [KF250](#kf250)'s single measured pair into the class it belonged to; folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

[KF250](#kf250) measured **one** conflicting pair — a `HH:mm:ss`-declared DATE carrying the opt-in pre-1900 check — and left the class open. `DateType` carries exactly two config axes that can disagree with its declared format, so the class is finite: both are put to the kernel here against every format in the derived [temporal vocabulary](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md), which is what makes the boundaries below component claims rather than one-spelling coincidences.

| config axis | the gate | admitted formats |
|---|---|---|
| `youngerThan1900Check` (`rejectBefore1900()`) | the declared format carries a **YEAR** | `yyyy`, `yyyy-MM`, `yyyyMM`, `yyyy-MM-dd`, `dd.MM.yyyy`, `yyyyMMdd`, `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` |
| a partial `datePrecision` (`DAY_`/`MONTH_`/`YEAR_OPTIONAL`) | the format is a **complete date and nothing further** | `yyyy-MM-dd`, `dd.MM.yyyy`, `yyyyMMdd` |

**The two gates disagree in both directions, which is why one pair could not have settled either.** `yyyy-MM` takes the guard and refuses the precision, so a refusal keyed on "the format is incomplete" over-rejects a model the kernel admits. And the instant format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` takes the guard and **refuses the precision too, despite carrying all three date components** — so a refusal keyed on "the three components are present" would admit a model the kernel rejects. That cell was predicted ADMITTED here and measured refused; it is reachable rather than hypothetical, because the instant spelling is a legal DATE declaration ([KF206](#kf206) — the format gate reads the string, not the kind). The verdict does not move with *which* component a partial precision makes optional, and `FULL` — the default, never emitted — carries no format requirement at all, which is the control separating "a partial precision needs a complete format" from "declaring a precision at all needs one".

**A format that fails both gates draws both codes**, not the first: `MM-dd` + guard + partial precision reports `MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID` and `MVK_OPTIONAL_DATE_TYPE_INVALID` together.

**The precision refusal echoes the offending format in GERMAN pattern letters, in every locale.** An `en_US` model declaring `yyyy-MM` is told *"A partial known date is not permitted for the format: `'JJJJ-MM'`"* — `y→J`, `d→T` (`MM-dd` → `'MM-TT'`, `MMdd` → `'MMTT'`, `HH:mm:ss` unchanged). A `de_DE` model produces the identical spelling, which is the discriminator: this is a fixed letter substitution, **not** a localization, so no reader ever sees the format they must actually declare. An author who copies the spelling out of the diagnostic writes a format the kernel refuses outright.

**Disposition — the corrective, not a client-side refusal.** Both codes are orphans of the operator catalog-join (no operator's `invalidExample` documents a field-declaration conflict), so each now carries a curated `fix`/`explain` in `StructuralKernelFix`, naming the formats that *would* be accepted and warning off the German spelling. A client-side refusal was measured, considered and declined: `FieldTypeSpecReader` builds `DateSpec` on the **read** path, so a constructor check would make an inconsistent-but-present kernel model unreadable rather than merely unauthorable, and a builder-only check would cover `DateFieldBuilder` while missing the CLI's own authoring path. Delegation already reports both conflicts correctly; what was missing was the corrective, which is the enricher's lane. **Amended 2026-09-13:** that disposition is about the rulekit's Java authoring/read path and still stands there. The portable checker reads STORED JSON and has no such read path, so it now reproduces both codes (`consistency`'s `TEMPORAL_CONFIG` family), asked only over the formats A12 is measured to admit — an unrecognised format leaves it silent, since the admitted set is a probe's result rather than a closed one ([KF313](#kf313)). The member names it reads are measured in [KF314](#kf314), not taken from the Java fields.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalDeclarationConfigAdmissionLawsTest` — both grids over the complete admitted vocabulary, the bare-declaration and `FULL` positive controls, the both-axes conflict, the two refusal messages pinned verbatim, the German-letter substitution across two locales and four formats, and the enrichment asserted through `KernelDiagnostics.enriched` — the exact call `model check` makes. The class is a registered completeness claimant of `TemporalFormatVocabularyGuardTest`, so a short axis fails the build rather than narrowing the basis silently.)*

## §6 supplement — the DATEFRAGMENT kind admits the SAME formats as the other date-bearing kinds, measured rather than inherited (kernel `checkConsistency` over the derived candidate universe, 2026-09-05; count corrected 2026-09-13) <a id="kf252"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends [KF206](#kf206)'s kind-independence onto the one date-bearing kind its grid never covered; folds into §6 with it.

[KF206](#kf206) established that the temporal format gate reads the string and not the kind, over **DATE / TIME / DATE_TIME**. `DateFragmentType` was outside that grid — it declares its format under its own key (`formatOfFragment`) — and every surface in this estate named the same four members for it (`MM`, `yyyy`, `yyyy-MM`, `MM-dd`), including [KF81](#kf81)'s own bullet. Measured over the [derived candidate universe](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md): **all twelve admitted formats are admitted on a fragment field too**, `yyyy-MM-dd`, `dd.MM.yyyy`, `yyyyMMdd`, `HH:mm:ss` and the ISO instant included.

**Why it needed measuring instead of extending.** A fragment is *by definition* a date that is not a full calendar date, so a narrower set was the plausible reading, and extending KF206 to it would have been a scope transfer onto an unmeasured carrier — the failure the four-member lists in three published schema descriptions and the diagnostic enricher actually exhibited. The domain now regenerates from the kernel as its own section of the derived artifact, beside the DATERANGE pair table, so no consumer assembles it from the members it happened to use.

**The limit, stated because a reader will otherwise carry the result further than the measurement.** This is an **admission** result only. The fragment RUNTIME completion recorded in §6 ("date-fragment runtime completion" — missing month/day to `01`, missing year from the Base Year) was measured on the four conventional formats; what a fragment declared `yyyyMMdd` — a *complete* date wearing the fragment kind — does at runtime is unmeasured on either engine, and the interpreter's `DatePrecision.FRAGMENT` path has never seen that combination. *Settled 2026-09-05, same day: measured across all three routes — comparison against a full date, paired comparison between two fragments of one declaration, and the formal check that runs with no rule reading the value — the two engines agree everywhere, because a clock-declared fragment is handled as a clock value rather than through the fragment completion ([IF327](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if327)).*

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalFormatVocabularyGuardTest` — the fragment probe is a third derived domain with its own discrimination floor, and the artifact comparison fails the build if the kernel and the committed set disagree.)*

## §9 supplement — `NumberOfDifferentValues` counts temporal operands by DECODED date, so two spellings of one date count once (adapter differential, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf253"></a>

> Fold: pending — the runtime half of [KF193](#kf193)'s temporal aggregate gate; folds into §9 beside [KF226](#kf226) on the next canonical pass.

[KF193](#kf193) measured `NumberOfDifferentValues`'s *admission* gate: date-like operands must share a declared component SET, not a format string, so `yyyy-MM-dd` beside `dd.MM.yyyy` is admitted. That admission is what makes this question askable at all — the two operands can hold **different stored texts denoting one date**, and there a textual identity and a chronological one give different counts. Measured on both engines: the count is **chronological**.

| operands | stored values | distinct count |
|---|---|---|
| `yyyy-MM-dd`, `dd.MM.yyyy` | `2024-03-05`, `05.03.2024` — one date, two spellings | **1** |
| `yyyy-MM-dd`, `dd.MM.yyyy` | `2024-03-05`, `06.03.2024` — different dates | 2 |
| `yyyy-MM-dd`, `yyyy-MM-dd` | `2024-03-05`, `2024-03-05` | 1 |
| `yyyy-MM-dd`, `yyyy-MM-dd` | `2024-03-05`, `2024-03-06` | 2 |

**The first row alone does not establish it, and that is the whole design of the table.** A count of 1 is equally consistent with a decoded comparison and with an engine that cannot evaluate a cross-spelling pair and folds it to one value — the two are indistinguishable from a single cell. The second row holds the spelling difference fixed and varies only whether the dates agree; the collapse reading cannot produce its 2. The same-spelling pair is the third leg, showing a count of 1 is reachable through the path nobody disputes, so neither arm is a constant.

**Read against its neighbour or the result inverts.** `FieldValuesNotUnique` refuses this pair outright at authoring under its own code, so it never reaches a runtime identity question — do not carry either operator's answer to the other ([KF226](#kf226) records the same warning on the classification gate). No Base Year is declared in the measured model: every declaration carries its own year, so supplementation is not a second variable here.

**Asked by a12-kernel-lean's `SG22`**, whose `route-state` recorded the question as having no constructible witness — "under a mandatory single format the decoded and stored accounts agree on every currently constructible input". The premise is what fails: the format is not mandatory-single for *this* operator, which is exactly the fact their proposed format-equality gate would have erased. They have withdrawn the recommendation.

**The DATETIME sibling question — instant identity or label identity — is not observable at this operator, and the assumption their `SPEC-2026-09-07-08` leaves open is already measured here** *(2026-09-07)*. Every operand is cell-sourced, so no value reaching the fold retains an instant a label did not produce; our own fold has no instant to retain at all, since a DATE_TIME cell canonicalizes to its offset-free ISO **label** text and the distinct key is that text. Their entry names one gap in its own basis: whether a **stored spring-forward gap label** is refused, calibrated only on the literal carrier. It is refused, and the two oracles behind that are not equally strong, so keep them apart: a stored `2024-03-31T02:30:00` under a declared `Europe/Berlin` zone draws `datumFormatFalsch` and suppresses the referencing rule on **both kernel strategies and the interpreter** (`adapter.laws.DstTimeZoneDiffTest.gapWallTimeIsAFormalError`), while the generalization to **every era** rests on a `SimpleDateFormat` non-lenient probe of the parser the kernel uses — one layer below the kernel, and stated as probed in the §6 DST rows rather than kernel-confirmed. The first row is what answers their assumption; on it, the label-identity account survives the one shape that could have parted it from the instant account.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.DistinctCountTemporalIdentityDiffTest` — every cell asserts kernel and interpreter equal before its value is pinned, so an engine divergence fails ahead of the pin; the cross-spelling pair's admission is asserted rather than assumed, since a refused pair would make the counts measurements of a model that does not exist.)*

## §6 supplement — the temporal format gate is CASE-SENSITIVE, and "lowercase" was never the rule (kernel `checkConsistency` over a new case axis, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf254"></a>

> Fold: pending — closes the case axis [KF206](#kf206)'s string-gate result left unprobed; folds into §6 with it.

Eleven published schema descriptions and the diagnostic enricher all said a date/time format must be **"a LOWERCASE Java pattern"**. Read literally that licenses `yyyy-mm-dd`, which the kernel refuses. Measured over a new case axis — both the all-lowercase and all-uppercase spelling of every candidate, universe 135 → 375: **no case variant of any admitted format is accepted**, and the admitted set stays exactly twelve.

| spelling | verdict |
|---|---|
| `yyyy-mm-dd`, `yyyymmdd`, `dd.mm.yyyy`, `hh:mm:ss` | REFUSED |
| `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYYMMDD` | REFUSED |
| the admitted vocabulary as published | ADMITTED |

**"Lowercase" was reaching for a real fact and named the wrong one.** The surfaces carry a true adjacent claim — the A12 editor's UPPERCASE labels (`YYYY-MM-DD`) are display labels, not format values — and "lowercase" was shorthand for *not those*. But the actual rule is that Java pattern letters are case-**significant**: `MM` is months where `mm` is minutes, so `yyyy-mm-dd` is a **different pattern**, not a miscased one. A reader who applied the description's own rule produced a string the description's own list does not contain.

**The mechanism is the one this file keeps recording: a description asserted a rule no candidate exercised.** The generator varies components and separators — the axis [KF196](#kf196) proved discriminating — at fixed case throughout, so both case claims were unfalsifiable by construction. That is the same defect as the short allowlists [KF252](#kf252) corrected, one layer up: there the *set* was wrong, here the *rule for forming a member* was, and neither was reachable by the probe that was supposed to cover the surface. Adding the axis was the fix; rewording alone would have left the next case claim equally unchecked.

**Found by a12-kernel-lean, 2026-09-05**, who read the schema before the diagnostic, wrote the lowercase spelling and lost a round to it — the failure mode the description uniquely causes, since `field add`'s own rejection text was correct and lists all twelve. Their report is what prompted the axis; the verdicts above are measured here.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalFormatVocabularyGuardTest` — the case axis is generated from every candidate rather than from named members, so a future admitted format is case-probed without anyone remembering to add it.)*

## §11 supplement — the operand-scope law transfers to the RULE carrier unchanged, sibling index rows included (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf255"></a>

> Fold: pending — completes [KF226](#kf226)-era carrier discipline on the §11 scope law; folds into §11 beside the computation rows.

`ComputationOperandScopeLawsTest` established on the **computation** carrier that an operand is admitted by whether the target's repetition scope **binds** every repeatable level it crosses — not by scope equality, and not by cross-group-ness. Whether a **rule** decides the same way was an explicitly unmeasured transfer. Measured now: **it does, on every row, including the three that make the law interesting.**

| operand, relative to the error field | rule carrier | computation carrier |
|---|---|---|
| form-level into a one-level / two-level target | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| one level up into a two-level target | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| own level — control | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| one level BELOW the target | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| repeatable into a form-level target | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| sibling repeatable, index field SAME name | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| sibling repeatable, index field ANOTHER name | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX` | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX` |
| sibling repeatable, NO index field | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |

**A clean transfer is a result, not a non-result, and it had to be run rather than assumed.** This estate has measured the opposite outcome three times in a week on one operator family ([KF120](#kf120), [KF218](#kf218), [KF242](#kf242)) — the reuse needs no new branch, so nothing prompts the question and a silent assumption that happens to hold produces no signal at all. The row that would have been most expensive to get wrong is the sibling triple, where siblinghood alone predicts one verdict and the kernel gives three.

**The two carriers are NOT symmetric, which is what made the transfer non-obvious.** A rule's condition must reference its error field (`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`), so every rule row carries **two** operands where the computation rows carried one, and the error-field read is itself a scope participant. A computation can pair a bare constant with a repeating target; a rule cannot. The scope verdict is nevertheless identical, so the binding relation is decided by the operand and the target locus alone and does not count operands.

**Vacuity is excluded by the sibling table rather than by a separate control**: one helper returns three distinct outcomes over three groups differing only in their index declaration, so it is demonstrably reading the kernel and not defaulting.

**Prompted by a12-kernel-lean's `SG5`**, which reframed its own row around this boundary rather than assuming it after their cross-group probe turned out to be the no-index-field case. The result closes the transfer for both estates; the carrier boundary is now measured rather than flagged.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.RuleOperandScopeLawsTest` — the computation law's fixture verbatim, so the carrier is the only variable; each table pinned as measured.)*

## §9 supplement — a FILTERED star is an admitted operand at every entity-list carrier, and the temporal gate reads through the filter (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf256"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends [KF193](#kf193)'s temporal gate and [KF125](#kf125)'s slot laws onto the filtered operand shape; folds into §9.

Nothing in this estate had crossed `Having` with the extremum operators — six law files use `.having(…)` and none reached `MaxValue`/`MinValue` or `latestOf`/`earliestOf`. Measured now, on our own fixture: **a filtered star is admitted wherever a plain star is**, and the temporal component-set gate still runs on it.

| operand shape | verdict |
|---|---|
| temporal extremum, plain star — control | ADMITTED |
| temporal extremum, FILTERED star | ADMITTED |
| numeric extremum, plain star — control | ADMITTED |
| numeric extremum, FILTERED star | ADMITTED |
| `NumberOfDifferentValues` / `FieldValuesNotUnique`, filtered star (each with its plain-star control) | ADMITTED |
| filtered star **beside a differing component set**, both in the operand list | `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` |
| filtered star beside the same set spelled differently | ADMITTED |

**Our pre-checks were silent here, not deliberate.** `ListAggregate` and `DateListAggregate` inspect an operand's KIND and never its filter, so a filtered star built through `FieldListRef.having(…)` passed straight through. That is the correct behaviour — but "delegated on purpose" and "nobody looked" are indistinguishable from inside the code, and only a run separates them. This is the read-path half of the client-refusal rule arriving as its mirror image: the risk was never a wrong refusal, it was an untested absence of one.

**The refusal row is what stops the admissions being worthless.** Six ADMITTED cells are equally well explained by "a filtered operand is not gate-checked at all" — a worse outcome than a refusal, since it would mean the filter smuggles an operand past the temporal gate. The differing-set row shows the gate still fires through the filter.

**A first draft measured the wrong gate, and its own control caught it.** Putting the second date on the **comparison** rather than in the operand list made every row ADMITTED — correctly, because an aggregate compared to a date is a *direct* comparison and takes §6's coarse gate (year presence, date/no-date class), while the exact component-set gate reads the aggregate's own operand list. Published as-is it would have claimed "the filter exempts the operand from the gate". The plain-star control failed by being ADMITTED where it had no business being: a control earns its place by failing when the row's **design** is wrong, not only when the kernel surprises you.

**Prompted by a12-kernel-lean**, whose own decline of this shape rested on a *real* neighbouring divergence — the DATERANGE-endpoint carrier genuinely refuses starred operands under `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`. A known-real boundary predicted the wrong side of itself, which is a stronger argument for measuring than an unsupported guess would have been.

**Extended 2026-09-07 — the FAMILY gate reads through the filter too, and the two filtered forms DO NOT AGREE.** The rows above measure the component-set gate; the family gate is a different one, so it is measured rather than transferred. On a starred **field** the filter is transparent: a filtered STRING, BOOLEAN or CONFIRM leader draws `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` and a filtered DATE leader `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE`, each **equal to its plain twin**, with a sortable NUMBER leader admitted filtered and plain alike. On a **group** the filtered operand is refused `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` outright, where its plain twin reaches the kind gate and reports `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` instead. So no single rule serves both filtered forms: reading the field half onto the group admits what the kernel refuses, and the group half onto the field refuses what it admits, and both are silent on models that filter nothing.

The group claim rests on its own control: a filtered starred **field** inside that same subgroup, carrying the identical filter, is **admitted** — which excludes the filter's spelling, the operand's depth and the filter's scope, and leaves group-ness as the only difference. **No mechanism is proposed for it.** `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` is the code the carriers that refuse groups outright report, which invites reading the filtered operand as routed somewhere a group is not a legal shape at all; nothing measured here isolates that, so it stays a hypothesis. Held fixed across the whole grid: the operator, the arity, the comparand, the locale, the filter condition, the operand order, the group and the error field.

A filtered group operand is **unrepresentable in our typed surface** — `GroupListRef` carries no filter at all — which is a claim about our own types, discharged by reading the record rather than by the kernel's refusal happening to agree; the rows use raw DSL for that reason. Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-07-01`.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.FilteredStarExtremumOperandLawsTest` — every filtered row carries its plain-star control, and the numeric extremum sits beside the temporal one so a refusal would separate a filtered-star ban from a temporal-carrier one; the family-gate grid twins four leader kinds filtered against plain, and the group rows carry the filtered-field control.)*

## §11 supplement — a wrong-kind CONSTANT assignment reports an ordered ladder over the (constant, target) PAIR (kernel `checkConsistency` via raw `DraftComputation`, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf257"></a>

> Fold: pending — a §11 authoring-tier diagnostic law; folds into §11 beside the computation kind rows.

Which class the kernel reports for a wrong-kind constant assignment is **not** a function of the target kind, and not of the constant either. It is an ordered ladder over the pair, measured here on one model carrying a target of every kind:

| rung | condition | class |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | target is BOOLEAN | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YESNO`, for **any** constant |
| 1 | target is CONFIRM | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YES`, for **any** constant |
| 2 | constant is TEMPORAL, any remaining target | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` — String and Number included |
| 3 | otherwise the target decides | temporal → `..._TO_DATE`; String/Enum → `..._TO_ENUM_OR_STRING`; NUMBER → `..._TO_ENUM_OR_STRING` for a string constant but **`MVK_INCONSISTENT_TYPES_COMPARED`** for a Boolean one |

**Two cells are pair-dependent and the rest are target-keyed, which is exactly what makes a careless sample dangerous.** A batch that holds the constant fixed and varies the target produces a clean target-keyed table *whether or not the target is the key* — the assumption is not merely unverified there, it is unfalsifiable by that batch. Both exceptions are locked against same-target controls carrying a different constant, so the pair-dependence is visible rather than inferred: rung 2's temporal column, and the Boolean-into-NUMBER cell where one target yields two classes.

**BOOLEAN and CONFIRM do not share a class.** They sit at the same rung and report different codes, so a checker collapsing the two flag kinds is wrong on one of them.

**A "temporal literal" is not a separate syntax — it is a string literal whose CONTENT parses as a date.** The kernel lexer admits one spelling (`StringLiteral : '"' ( '""' | ~["] )* '"'`, cited in our own `DslRenderer`), so `"05.03.2024"` is temporal and `"pending"` is not, by content alone. Single quotes are not a literal and draw `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` — which is how a mis-spelled probe row silently leaves the grid instead of failing: a first draft here spelled the string constant `'pending'` and four cells reported a parse error that looked like data. A bare `05.03.2024` lexes as a Number, pinned by its own row.

**None of this is authorable through our typed surface** — `Computation.Builder`'s kind/format gate refuses every cell first, with a kind-mismatch message that names no code. That is correct behaviour and not a defect: the kernel refuses all of them too, so the pre-check is delegation-equivalent, merely earlier. It does mean the kernel's own class was unmeasured here, reachable only through the raw `DraftComputation` seam that `ConfirmComputationSourceKindLawsTest` established for the same reason.

**The ladder is the kernel's COMPARISON vocabulary, not an assignment table — corrected the same day.** The identical class fires on a plain rule condition with no computation and no assignment anywhere (`[Handler] == "05.03.2024"` on a String field), with the non-date literal at that exact site admitted as the control; The `Having` filter is the third carrier and is measured here too — a12-kernel-lean reported it first, and it is re-derived on our fixture because our shipped corrective names it, so it may not rest on their run. **Hypothesis, not a finding:** that assignment reaches this gate through its generated equality rule, which would explain why the codes are named `..._COMPARE_TO_...` at all. Both estates reached that account independently and neither holds a witness for it — concurrence tests whether two parties reason alike from the same input, never whether the account is right. The discriminator nobody has built: a case separating a generated equality rule from a classifier that both routes simply call. It matters beyond taxonomy: the first version of our corrective was written from the assignment carrier alone and spoke of a "target" — a word with no referent in a filter or a plain comparison. That is the same comparison-versus-assignment split that had left the ledger rows incomplete, repeated one level out, inside the fix for it.

**Consequence taken:** `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` now carries a `StructuralKernelFix` corrective telling the author to check the LITERAL before the field, since the code fires against fields with nothing temporal about them and on every carrier. Three MVK-ledger rows classified `erased` were extended in place — they described the *comparison* surface, and assignment is a second, live firing site on it.

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean (`LF153` / `SPEC-2026-09-06-03`)**, whose own account rests on 80 kernel-gated children in one batch; re-derived here on our fixture rather than cited, because our diagnostic surface is what carries the corrective. Their method note is the transferable part: *name the key you think the answer is a function of, and vary it* — if the honest answer is "left, right, or the pair", cross them.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.LiteralComparisonDiagnosticLadderLawsTest` — each rung with its same-target controls, plus the bare-dotted-literal fixture control. Open here as there: a CUSTOM target, the one rung the ladder does not claim.)*

## §9 supplement — the exact-duplicate gate reads a reference's FORM, so a starred operand may repeat where a direct one may not (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf258"></a>

> Fold: pending — sharpens the duplicate-slot rows in §9; folds beside [KF125](#kf125).

`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` rejects an *exact* reference repeated in one operand list — and "exact" is load-bearing. A **wildcarded (starred) occurrence is a repetition-wide scan rather than an exact reference**, so two of them are two independent reads and repeat legally:

| operand list | verdict |
|---|---|
| `AtLeastOneFieldValueIncludedInValueList(Code, Code In …)` | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` |
| `AtLeastOneFieldValueIncludedInValueList(Items*/Sku, Items*/Sku In …)` | ADMITTED |
| `NumberOfValueInFields(0 In Total, Total)` | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` |
| `NumberOfValueInFields(0 In Items*/Count, Items*/Count)` | ADMITTED |
| two *distinct* direct references, either carrier — liveness control | ADMITTED |

**Our catalog said this on seven operators and contradicted it on two.** `Sum`, `MaxValue`, `MinValue`, `NumberOfDifferentValues`, `NumberOfFilledFields`, `NumberOfFilledGroups` and `FirstFilledValue` all spell out the star exemption. The value-list family said only "no exact reference may repeat" and `NumberOfValueInFields` said "a field may not be listed more than once" — both of which, read as written, forbid a form the kernel admits. That is an **internal contradiction in one shipped artifact**, which is what makes it a defect rather than a difference of emphasis: an author reading one entry gets a rule the neighbouring entry denies. Both corrected.

**The liveness control is what makes the admissions mean anything.** Without a distinct-reference row on each carrier, "the starred repeat is admitted" and "this operator never reaches the duplicate gate at all" are the same observation; the direct-duplicate row then shows the gate is armed in the same model.

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean on four carriers** (value list, `NumberOfDifferentValues`, `FieldValuesNotUnique`, `Sum`). Measured here on the two whose *wording* was wrong, since our published text is what carried the defect — the other two already said the right thing. Their same-day corroboration from the other direction is **their report and not re-derived here**: at the DateRange overlap operators a keyed reference repeated under the *same* key refuses and under a *different* key is admitted, which would make the exact identity the (field, key) pair.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.StarredOperandRepeatExemptionLawsTest` — both carriers, each with its direct-duplicate row and its distinct-reference liveness control.)*

## §6 supplement — a temporal field may declare NO format, and the kernel resolves its KIND's default; a BLANK format string is refused (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf259"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §6's declaration tier beside [KF206](#kf206); folds on the next canonical pass.

**Absent and empty are two different declarations.** An empty type payload — `"DateType": {}`, `"TimeType": {}`, `"DateTimeType": {}` — is kernel-valid, and the field then behaves as if it had declared its kind's default spelling. A present-but-blank `"format": ""` is refused, not by a consistency rule but by the kernel's own type converter (`DateTypeImpl`'s `notBlank` precondition), which throws inside `checkConsistency` before any structured problem exists.

**Three gates pin the resolved default, and no one of them alone would.** Each answers a different question about what "the default" is:

| gate | row | reading |
|---|---|---|
| format STRING (`FieldValuesNotUnique`) | format-less DATE beside `yyyy-MM-dd` ADMITTED; beside `dd.MM.yyyy` refused, exactly like the declared ISO/German control | the resolved value is a *string* equal to the default spelling, not an exemption from a gate it has no string for |
| component SET (`NumberOfDifferentValues`) | format-less DATE beside format-less TIME and beside format-less DATETIME both `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE`; beside `dd.MM.yyyy` ADMITTED | the three kinds resolve three *different* defaults, which a shared one could not produce |
| extractor | `YearFromDate` admitted on the format-less DATE and DATETIME, refused on the format-less TIME; `HoursFromTime` the mirror | which components the resolved default carries |

**Our own writer cannot emit either shape, and that is the reason the caveat existed.** `DocumentModelDraft` substitutes the kind default for a null format, so both variants above are built by editing the emitted DM-JSON.

**The CLI authoring path substitutes too, which makes a read-back a PROJECTION rather than a measurement.** `dmtool field add` with an empty temporal payload writes `"format": "yyyy-MM-dd"` into the stored model, so `dmtool field read` then returns a resolved-looking literal that is our own substitution echoed back, byte-identical to a declared field's. Anyone trying to answer "what literal does the kernel resolve?" by adding a format-less field and reading it back gets a confident answer to a different question — the value never left our writer. That is why the three gates above bound the default indirectly instead: they are the only instruments here that ask the kernel. **The exact resolved literal remains unread on our side** (a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-06-02` asks for it; the honest answer is that our loader cannot witness it). The blank-string variant additionally exposed a **reporting** defect on our side: the kernel's throw escaped `ModelLoader.loadAndCheck` and reached the caller as `RK_INTERNAL_ERROR` — "this is a dmtool defect, not an invalid input" — which asserts the opposite of the truth. It is the whole-model sibling of the leak `RuleValidator.checkDraft` already closes for an injected draft, and it is fixed at the tier that owns it: the wrapper sits on `checkConsistency` alone and never on the deserialize/resolve/expand step above it. **That narrowness is load-bearing** — a malformed DM-JSON and a reference our own resolver could not resolve belong to earlier tiers that report themselves, and folding either into this channel would publish a KERNEL gate receipt for a gate that never ran. A first, broader attempt did exactly that and eight CLI contract tests said so.

**The class has a second member, and it is what confirms the mechanism rather than the symptom.** A DUPLICATE rule name in one group is caught by the same deserialize/convert tier and threw the same bare `IllegalArgumentException` out of `BoundModel.ofJson` — a case nobody reported, predicted from the locus and found already pinned by `validate.laws.RuleSlotLawsTest`, which asserted the leak. Both now arrive as a `ModelConsistencyException` carrying the kernel's own reason, so the fix sits at the shared root rather than on the reported path.

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-06-02`**, whose rows could bound the default's equality class but not exhibit it; the extractor column is added here, and their side's note that this project "refuses an empty format string outright" is true of *their* flat model, not of this one.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalDeclarationWithoutFormatLawsTest` — the three gates, plus the blank-string row asserting the rejection arrives as a `ModelConsistencyException` carrying the kernel's own reason.)*

## §6 supplement — a partially known Date splits the FIVE field-list operators along the identity they COMPARE (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06; fifth carrier added 2026-09-07) <a id="kf260"></a>

> Fold: pending — new precision axis on §6's operand gates; folds beside [KF193](#kf193).

A `DateType` may declare `datePrecision` `DAY_OPTIONAL` / `MONTH_OPTIONAL` / `YEAR_OPTIONAL`, and **precision is independent of the declared component set** — a `yyyy-MM-dd` declaration exposing all three components may still be partially known, so an operand gate reading components alone cannot see it.

| operator | verdict on all three precisions | why |
|---|---|---|
| `MinValue` / `MaxValue` / `NumberOfDifferentValues` | `MVK_PARTIAL_DATE_NOT_ALLOWED` | they compare a **decoded date**, which a partial has not |
| `FieldValuesNotUnique` | ADMITTED | it compares the **exact stored text**, which a partial has |
| `FirstFilledValue` | ADMITTED | it **selects** a value rather than comparing one, so no decode is required |
| `ValueAsDate` | the inverse gate — REQUIRES a partial, refuses a fully known source `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE_FOR_OP` | so the distinction is enforced in both directions |

This is static corroboration of the identity split that [KF173](#kf173)/[KF253](#kf253) establish at runtime, arriving from an independent direction. The full-precision control is admitted at all five carriers on the same fixture, and the only variable across the refused rows is `datePrecision`.

**Corrected 2026-09-07: the denominator was four because four had been run.** `FirstFilledValue` is a field-list operator of the same family and was never asked; it admits all three precisions, so the split is three-against-two rather than three-against-one. The tell was structural rather than a doubt about the rows: [KF272](#kf272) had just had to add `FirstFilledValue` as a fifth carrier at the neighbouring component-set gate, where it turned out to read a *third* thing — so an adjacent entry naming it as a distinct case is the cue to ask whether this entry's set was a set or a sample.

**A group operand's expansion is NOT leader-keyed here**, which is the row a12-kernel-lean asked for and the one a "the leader fixes the class" reading gets wrong: a group declaring a FULL-precision date first and a month-optional one second is still refused at all three decoding carriers, with the all-full sibling group admitted as the control. So this gate reads the whole expansion — unlike the kind gate, where the leading declaration does decide ([KF263](#kf263)).

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-06-05`.** Their entry records that a partial precision is "not authorable through `field add`"; it is, on this tool — the spec key is `date.precision` and the DM-JSON key it writes is `datePrecision`.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.PartialDatePrecisionOperandLawsTest`.)*

## §6 supplement — a declared Base Year reaches the temporal EXTRACTOR gate, and the admitted extractor then decides nothing (kernel `checkConsistency` + differential, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf261"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends the Base-Year supplementation rule to a third gate; folds beside [KF193](#kf193).

Our record had the Base Year supplementing the year at the **comparison** gate and the **aggregate** gate. It reaches the **extractor** gate too: `YearFromDate` on a pure `HH:mm:ss` field is refused `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` with no Base Year and **ADMITTED** with one. So the year part's gate is *component present OR a Base Year supplies one*, not *component present*. The control is within-model — the same draft built twice, differing in one builder call — and the ordinary-DATE extractor row is admitted on both, so the gate is visibly armed either way.

**Admission is not a value.** At runtime that admitted extractor decides nothing: neither `== 2024` (the declared base year) nor `== 2023` fires on a filled clock cell, on both kernel strategies and in the interpreter, while the same rule shape over an ordinary DATE field fires on the same document. Asking one comparand could not separate "the Base Year supplies the year" from "the operand yields nothing"; asking two does.

**The declared FORMAT decides the operand family, and the KIND is not read** — [KF211](#kf211)'s rule reaching the completed-period difference: `DifferenceInYears` takes a TIME-declared `yyyy-MM-dd` field beside an ordinary DATE and refuses a pure clock field, `HoursFromTime` the mirror on the same declaration.

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-05-14`** (narrowed by them to these two rows after finding the wider claim already in [KF211](#kf211)); their limit is static admission, and the runtime row is added here.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalExtractorBaseYearGateLawsTest` + `adapter.laws.BaseYearExtractorAdmissionDiffTest`.)*

## §6 supplement — the distinct count and the extrema fold a COMPONENT-OMITTING temporal operand at its declared precision (differential, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf262"></a>

> Fold: pending — the runtime half of the component-set gate; folds beside [KF253](#kf253).

[KF253](#kf253) measured the fold on complete-date spellings; the admission side already proved a `yyyy-MM` or a yearless `MM` list legal, so these rows were constructible and simply never run. **The comparison is the decoded value at the list's SHARED declared component set**, not at full calendar precision: a `yyyy-MM` pair folds `2024-03` with `2024-03` as one value and separates it from `2024-04`, and a yearless `MM` pair does the same — and *orders* — with **no Base Year declared**.

**The reversed document is the separator.** Every pair is swapped and no ordering rule fires at all, which no constant-true reading can produce; the ascending row alone would be consistent with an extremum that ignores its operands.

**Supplementation is by the DECLARED Base Year, not by the sibling operand's year.** Under `baseYear 2024`, a yearless `03` beside `2023-03` counts as **two** values and the extremum puts the 2023 operand first. A sibling-supplied year would make the two equal and count one, so that row is what separates the accounts; `03` beside `2024-03` counting one is consistent with both.

**Extended 2026-09-07 — the 2×2's missing cell: a UNIFORMLY yearless list on a model that DECLARES a Base Year.** The rows above take the no-Base-Year arm and the supplementation rows take a mixed-precision list, so "a declared Base Year neither enables nor disturbs a list that needs no supplementation" was the one corner neither covered, and a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-07-02` lists it as unmeasured on both sides. It orders: `MM` `03` before `04` under `baseYear 2024`, the reversed document firing nothing, and an equal-valued document firing — on **dynamic Groovy and the interpreter**, which is this file's engine pair throughout (it builds one model per rule, so a generated-Java engine per rule would be codegen per row; the claim is two engines, not three). The two models differ in exactly the `baseYear` builder call, though this grid varies only the document, so the flag is constant *within* it and the cross-arm comparison is against the rows above.

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-06-08`** (the distinct count) **and `SPEC-2026-09-06-10`** (the extrema); measured here on our own fixture, kernel and interpreter agreeing on every row.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.ComponentOmittingTemporalFoldDiffTest`.)*

## §9 supplement — the extrema admit two sortable classes, NUMBER and the temporal COMPONENT SET, and a group expansion supplies the leading kind (kernel `checkConsistency`, complete over the declared-kind axis, 2026-09-06; corrected 2026-09-07) <a id="kf263"></a>

> Fold: pending — completes the declared-kind axis [KF249](#kf249) opened; folds beside [KF226](#kf226).

**Corrected 2026-09-07: the first version of this entry recorded the leader set as {NUMBER, DATE} and every later slot as NUMBER-only. Both clauses were wrong, and the confound was the COMPARAND.** Each refusal cell was measured against a bare `== 0`, which is a NUMBER literal: a temporal extremum compared against it is refused `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` by the comparison gate before the operand gate is ever reached, so TIME, DATETIME and DATE_FRAGMENT read as unable to lead when they had simply not been asked. The three kinds were also never measured — the "complete over the declared-kind axis" claim was inherited from a12-kernel-lean's report rather than derived here. Re-measured with the comparand matched to each leader's class.

[KF249](#kf249) measured the position law on the NUMBER/DATE pair. The complete axis, at both extrema, is two sortable classes: **NUMBER, and each temporal COMPONENT SET**. Every operand must share the leader's class, so the leader and follower positions are the same gate seen twice rather than two different ones:

| leader | NUMBER | same temporal components | other temporal components | ENUM / BOOLEAN / CONFIRM / DATE_RANGE / CUSTOM / STRING |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NUMBER | ACCEPT | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` |
| DATE / TIME / DATETIME / DATE_FRAGMENT | `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` | ACCEPT | `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` | `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` |
| ENUM / BOOLEAN / CONFIRM / DATE_RANGE / CUSTOM / STRING | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` |

**The declared KIND is not the axis; the component set is — and `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` is misnamed.** The within-model 2×2 separates them, and the cell that settles it is the one a kind-based reading cannot explain:

| | same component set | different component set |
|---|---|---|
| **same declared kind** | ACCEPT — DATE `yyyy-MM-dd` with DATE `dd.MM.yyyy`, two different format STRINGS | `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` — DATE_FRAGMENT `yyyy-MM` with DATE_FRAGMENT `yyyy` |
| **different declared kind** | **ACCEPT** — DATE `yyyy-MM-dd` with DATE_FRAGMENT `yyyy-MM-dd`, and TIME `HH:mm:ss` with DATE_FRAGMENT `HH:mm:ss` | `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` — DATE with TIME |

So the code reports an incompatible component set, never an unequal format string: two format strings over the same components are accepted, and one kind under two component sets is refused. This is the same mechanism as the format-not-kind law at the runtime parser ([KF211](#kf211), [KF250](#kf250)) — one more carrier for it, on the static side.

**The four temporal classes are mutually exclusive because their component sets are.** TIME and DATETIME are declarable only at full second precision (`HH:mm` and `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` are both refused at `field add`), so DATE_FRAGMENT is the only kind that can be pointed at another kind's component set — which is what makes the "different kind, same components" cell authorable at all.

**A NUMBER leader does not distinguish; a temporal leader does.** A NUMBER leader reports `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` flatly against every other class, while a temporal leader splits its refusals in two, naming a non-temporal follower `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` and a temporal one of different components `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE`. The refusal of a non-sortable leader is comparand-independent, measured under both a NUMBER comparand and a self-referencing one — the control for the confound above. **A starred single-field operand takes the same verdict and the same code as the plain field of that kind**, in both positions, so the gate reads the declaration and not the operand form.

**CUSTOM is the cell that separates the extrema's kind domain from the distinct count's, and the only kind that does.** It is refused at both extrema in either position — `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` when it leads or follows a NUMBER, `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` after a temporal leader — yet admitted by `NumberOfDifferentValues` and `FieldValuesNotUnique`, where DATE_RANGE is refused by all four — and under two different codes, `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_CMP_DATE_ALLOWED` at the distinct count against the `CMP`-less `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_DATE_ALLOWED` at the uniqueness neighbour. So the two gates hold genuinely different sets, and a consumer deriving either from the other is wrong in exactly that cell.

**A GROUP operand's expansion supplies the leading kind at both families, and the discriminator is a REORDER.** Three groups carry the same three kinds in three declaration orders; the reported class tracks the first declared member, which a "a group expansion is simply not a sortable/homogeneous list" reading cannot produce:

| expansion, first declared member | `MinValue` | `NumberOfDifferentValues` |
|---|---|---|
| ENUM, then NUMBER, then DATE | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` | `MVK_STRING_ENUM_AND_NON_STRING_ENUM` |
| NUMBER, then ENUM, then DATE | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` | `MVK_NUMBER_AND_NON_NUMBER` |
| DATE, then NUMBER | `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` | `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` |
| all NUMBER — liveness control | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-06-06`**, whose acceptance condition left the group question open on their side; the reorder rows answer it.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.ExtremumOperandKindGridLawsTest`.)*

> Fold: pending — the column [KF187](#kf187) does not carry; folds beside it.

Five non-scalar forms are refused `MVK_INVALID_PARAMETER_FOR_DATE_RANGE_COMPARISON` in the scalar position: a plain star, a `Having`-filtered star, a fixed homogeneous group, a homogeneous starred group, and a star above a nonrepeatable terminal. **Five enumerated samples, not a proved universal** — the heading's "every non-scalar form" is a summary of these rows and nothing wider; a form outside the five is untested here. **The refusal belongs to the SLOT, not to the operand form, and the `In`-slot pair is what proves it**: each of the five is measured again in the list slot on the same fixture and admitted there. That pairing is load-bearing rather than decorative — [KF187](#kf187) records this operator ACCEPTING a starred group in the `In` slot, so a scalar-slot refusal read alone would contradict a measured row.

**[KF187](#kf187) has no scalar-slot column.** Its two columns are the unstarred and starred GROUP shapes and its `AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps` row is explicitly scoped "group in the `In` slot", so this is the missing column rather than a filled-in cell. (a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-06-01` describes that `—` as a scalar-slot cell; it is not one.) **That `—` is itself now filled**, 2026-09-07: this entry's own fixture puts a NON-repeatable homogeneous group in the `In` slot and the kernel admits it, so the cell was measured here while being cited as unmeasured there — the back-fill closes it.

**A kind gate reports ahead of the slot gate, in EITHER slot.** A group whose expansion mixes kinds draws `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` in the scalar slot *and* in the list slot, so that gate is not slot-specific; a homogeneous group reaches the slot gate in one and is admitted in the other. Measuring with a mixed group alone cannot distinguish "this slot refuses a group" from "this operand offends the kind gate first".

## §11 supplement — under EQUALITY a wrong-kind comparison's class is INVARIANT under carrier, wrapping operator, operand order, and comparand form (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06; scope corrected 2026-09-07) <a id="kf265"></a>

> Fold: pending — the invariance half of [KF257](#kf257)'s ladder; folds beside it.

**Corrected 2026-09-07: every cell below writes `==`, and the heading did not say so.** The comparison OPERATOR is the axis this grid holds fixed, and it is the one that actually moves the class — ordering reports `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` where equality reports these kind-specific classes ([KF270](#kf270)). Nothing measured here is wrong; the scope was unstated, which is the more expensive defect, because a12-kernel-lean read the table as the whole grid and our answer to them — that their code "appears in no cell of ours" — was true only of the column we had. The `==` sat inside two helper methods, so it was a constant across all twenty cells and appeared nowhere in the published table: a set cannot show you the variable none of its rows vary.

[KF257](#kf257) measures *which* class a wrong-kind comparison reports. This measures that, **under equality**, the class does not move, and adds the three declared kinds that ladder's fixture does not carry:

| field kind | vs a numeric literal | vs a String literal |
|---|---|---|
| STRING | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_ENUM_OR_STRING` | ADMITTED |
| ENUM | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_ENUM_OR_STRING` | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUM_COMPARISON` |
| BOOLEAN | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YESNO` | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YESNO` |
| CONFIRM | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YES` | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YES` |
| DATE_RANGE | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE_RANGE` | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE_RANGE` |
| DATE / TIME / DATETIME | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` |
| CUSTOM | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_ENUM_OR_STRING` | ADMITTED |
| NUMBER | ADMITTED | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_ENUM_OR_STRING` |

**The carrier column is the one that settles "whose class is it".** A `Having` filter leaf and a plain per-row rule condition over the **same field** report the identical class in every cell, so the refusal belongs to the comparison and a filter is not a site with classes of its own. The wrapping operator (`Sum`, `MinValue`, `NumberOfDifferentValues`, `AtLeastOneFieldFilled`), the literal's side, and whether the comparand is a literal or a cross-kind FIELD leave it alone too.

**This contradicts an inbound row and the contradiction is not resolved here.** a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-06-04` reports String, Boolean, Confirm, Enumeration and DATE_RANGE all collapsing to `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` against a numeric literal, with only the temporal families separating out. Six distinct classes are measured here and that code appears in no cell. Three variables were moved looking for the difference and the grid is invariant under all three, so the divergence is not explained from this side — their fixture is not ours to run, and the question goes back rather than a mechanism being invented for it. The unbracketed leaf spelling was checked and is not the difference: it is a uniform `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` grammar refusal on every kind.

## §11 supplement — a wrong-kind comparison meets TWO gates, and the COMPARISON OPERATOR selects which one answers (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf270"></a>

> Fold: pending — the axis [KF265](#kf265) held fixed; folds beside it.

**Ordering (`< <= > >=`) runs an ORDERABILITY gate over BOTH operands first.** Whichever side fails it, the refusal is `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON`, and neither the other side nor the literal's family changes that. Operands that survive it — and equality's operands, which never meet it — then reach the kind-match gate, whose refusals are the kind-specific `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_*` classes of [KF265](#kf265). Orderable: NUMBER, DATE, TIME, DATETIME. Not: STRING, ENUM, BOOLEAN, CONFIRM, DATE_RANGE, CUSTOM.

| comparison | verdict |
|---|---|
| `[Confirm] > 0`, `[Boolean] > 0`, `[DateRange] > 0`, `[String] > 0`, `[Enum] > 0`, `[Custom] > 0` | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` |
| the same six under `== 0` | the kind's own `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_*` ([KF265](#kf265)) |
| `[Date] > 0`, `[Time] > 0`, `[DateTime] > 0` — orderable, kind mismatch | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` |
| `[Date] > "pending"` — orderable left, non-orderable right | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` |
| `[Number] > [Confirm]`, `[Confirm] > [Number]`, `0 > [Confirm]` | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` |
| `[Number] > 0` | ADMITTED |

**The discriminator is a field compared with ITSELF**, which no rival account survives: `[Boolean] > [Boolean]` is refused and `[Boolean] == [Boolean]` is ADMITTED. Identical operands, identical kinds, identical carrier and order — the operator is the only variable and the verdict moves with it. Two rivals die on the rows above: *"ordering always reports the orderability class"* (a DATE ordered against a numeric literal does not), and *"the LEFT operand decides"* (an orderable NUMBER left of a CONFIRM still reports it, as does a bare literal on the left).

**CONFIRM is the one kind whose self-equality is refused, for an unrelated reason: its comparand domain is the `True` constant ALONE.** It refuses every field on the right, including another CONFIRM — where BOOLEAN, which renders alike, admits one. *(Corrected 2026-09-14: under EQUALITY. This grid holds the operator at `==`, and `!=` admits a confirm partner — [KF383](#kf383) separates the two axes.)* So `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YES` names a concept and not a token; `Yes` is not DSL text (`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`). This was found by the self-comparison cell failing on one of six kinds, having been *predicted* rather than read — recorded because a mechanism-derived expectation is what the cell exists to catch.

**This resolves the `SPEC-2026-09-06-04` divergence, and neither estate was wrong.** a12-kernel-lean measured ordering with a numeric literal against equality with a String literal — two variables moving together — and read the split as the literal's family; we measured both literal families under equality alone and reported their code unreachable. Their retained ops (`882148ce…`) showed bracketed leaves, refuting the leaf-spelling hypothesis, and their own quarantined hypothesis — that the operator is the axis — is the one confirmed here. **They queued the discharging cell; it was free on our fixture and is answered above**, so the run is theirs to skip.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.WrongKindComparisonOperatorGateLawsTest`.)*

## §9 supplement — a `Having` filter reference the star does not reopen is a CONSTANT, so the filter is all-or-nothing (differential, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf266"></a>

> Fold: pending — the selection half of the filter rules in §9; folds beside [KF237](#kf237).

A reference naming a repeatable level the star does **not** reopen resolves to the same row in the candidate and captured environments, so it cannot vary across candidates: the filter keeps every candidate or none. What differs between the two carriers is only how far that constancy reaches — **per host row** for an unstarred ancestor on the operand's path, **per document** for a nonrepeatable leaf.

Three host rows gating `1, 0, 1` compute `30, 0, 50` under the above-level filter and `30, 70, 50` under the nonrepeatable-leaf one. **The middle host row carries the argument**: the same candidates answer `0` to one filter and `70` to the other in one run, which refutes a per-candidate re-read and an ignored reference at the same time — neither row alone does.

**An emptied domain is the aggregate's zero, not a clear.** Falsifying the single root cell moves every leaf-filtered target to `0` with nothing cleared, which is [KF234](#kf234)'s empty-as-zero rule reaching a filter that selects nothing at all rather than one whose rows are individually dropped.

**Both arms, both spellings.** The `[$…]`-marked filter computes the identical per-host-row values, and a validation rule over the same filter fires on exactly the gated-off host row — so all-or-nothing selection is not a computation-only effect, and the marker does not change selection at a level the star did not reopen. That marked row is what a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-06-07` records as unmeasured on either side.

Both filters carry an in-scope conjunct deliberately: without one the scope gate refuses the filter outright ([KF244](#kf244)), so the conjunct is what makes the two carriers comparable rather than one legal and one unwritable, and it is true of every instantiated row.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.ConstantFilterReferenceSelectionDiffTest`.)*

[KF205](#kf205) records the key's classes and [KF1](#kf1) the decimal-format by-product; neither states which construct owns the gate. **The parameterless row is the whole argument**: with a NUMBER index field designated and the key spelled `"k1"`, the condition is refused `MVK_INDEX_VALUE_INVALID` with **no message parameter at all**, and designating a STRING index field admits the identical condition text. A refusal that survives deleting every parameter cannot be the parameter's.

The two models are the same draft built twice, differing only in which direct child is designated the index field, and a numeric key is admitted under the NUMBER designation so the gate is visibly armed rather than absent. `MVK_INDEX_VALUE_INVALID` and `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID` are therefore two gates at two layers, and only the second is about the parameter: reporting the parameter class here sends an author to rewrite a message that is already correct.
