## §13 supplement — the group-declaration alphabet answers to TWO gates, and the kernel's own sentence states only the first (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf268"></a>

> Fold: pending — new declaration-tier rule; folds beside [KF214](#kf214).

The path validator's message reads *"A group name may only contain letters, numbers or underscores. Group names must begin with a letter or an underscore"* — and a leading underscore is then refused by a **second** gate, `NAME_STARTS_WITH_UNDERSCORE_AND_WRONG_PATTERN`, which reserves that prefix: *"The name of a group may only begin with an underscore if it is '__meta' or starts with '__attachment_meta'."* `__meta`, `__attachment_meta` and `__attachment_meta_photo` are admitted; `_Slots`, `__other` and `_1` are not. **A consumer implementing the quoted sentence admits names the kernel refuses, and the sentence is the kernel's own** — the narrow-prior-art trap in its purest form.

Two further edges, both measured: **"letters" is Unicode** (`Slöts` is admitted, so an `[A-Za-z]` validator refuses legal models from the other direction), and the message's 60-character limit is real — 60 is admitted, 61 refused.

**The alphabet gate and the LENGTH gate report differently, which one sentence hides.** A digit-initial, hyphenated, spaced or colon-bearing name draws `MVK_PATH_INVALID`; the 61-character name is refused with **no keyed notification at all**. So a consumer keying on `MVK_PATH_INVALID` to mean "malformed name" silently misses the length case. Both refusals additionally carry the path validator's sentence re-reported **without** a key, once per element beneath the offending path — the coded notification is one member of a set whose size is a property of the model's shape, not of the gate.

**In the message `$#…$` group position, quoting moves the refusal a layer earlier — for three characters out of four.** A hyphen, a space and a digit-initial spelling inside a QUOTED segment draw `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` where the identical characters BARE reach the group lookup and draw `INVALID_GROUP`. **A colon does not**: quoted, it also reaches the lookup. So the rule is not "an illegal character inside a quoted segment is a lexer error" — the lexer's alphabet and the declaration's alphabet are different sets. The control is an undeclared but well-formed name, which draws `INVALID_GROUP` in both spellings, so the two codes are two layers rather than two messages for one refusal.

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-05-05`**, whose delta states the underscore-initial form as legal (quoting the kernel's own prose) and the lexer rule without the colon exception; both are corrected here.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.GroupNameAlphabetLawsTest`.)* **Amended 2026-09-13:** both gates are the GROUP carrier's and neither transfers — a FIELD name answers to a different alphabet and a different code set, measured in [KF315](#kf315).

## §5 supplement — the power's derived scale needs a scale-0 BASE, and one waiver admits every unknown-scale operation into a known-scale target (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-06) <a id="kf269"></a>

> Fold: pending — the discriminator behind [KF43](#kf43)'s power clause; folds beside it.

[KF43](#kf43) states the derivation and [KF45](#kf45) the exponent gate. **The discriminating case is a scale-2 base against a scale-2 literal**, because "power derives the BASE's scale for a literal exponent" and "power derives scale 0 only from a scale-0 base, else unknown" agree everywhere else. `[Rate](scale 2) ^ 2 == 100.00` is **refused** `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES`, so the base's-scale reading is wrong; the multiplication row beside it is the armed control, deriving a known scale 4 and admitting the same scale-2 literal. A negative literal exponent is refused too, so "nonnegative" in KF43's clause is load-bearing.

**The exponent gate and the derived scale are two different gates.** An exponent of KNOWN scale greater than 0 — a fractional literal, a decimal-scale field — is refused `MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP`, and so is an UNKNOWN-scale expression such as a bare division. A known scale-0 non-literal exponent (a field, or a scale-0 aggregate) passes that gate and then makes the derived scale unknown, which ordering admits and equality refuses. So an aggregate exponent being legal is a statement about its *known* scale, not evidence that the operator restricts no operand shape.

**One waiver serves every unknown-scale operator.** `errorCodesToSuppress: ["MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES"]` admits a non-literal exponent, a scale-0 aggregate exponent and a bare division alike into the same scale-0 target that refuses all three without it — one property apart. That widens [KF181](#kf181), where the same key re-exposed `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` underneath: with no self-reference there is nothing underneath and the suppression simply admits.

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-05-10`**, whose clause states the derived scale as the base's and the operand shapes as unrestricted; both halves are refuted above, while its 2×2 (ordering admits a field exponent, equality refuses it) and its waiver row are confirmed. Their note that our operator catalog carries no `Power` entry is correct — `^` lives inside the `Arithmetic` entry.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.PowerDerivedScaleWaiverLawsTest`.)*

## §6 supplement — `KF211`'s declared-format rule reaches BOTH temporal CONSTRUCTOR gates AND the entity-list EXTREMA, and our read path was keyed on the kind at SEVEN sites, found in three rounds (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf271"></a>

> Fold: pending — the third, fourth and fifth instances of [KF211](#kf211)'s rule, at gates that entry's own scope note excludes; folds into §6 together with it.

[KF211](#kf211) closed with a prediction: *"rendering, computation targets, and aggregate extrema on such a declaration are untouched here … expect a third if rendering or a computation target is probed on it."* a12-kernel-lean probed two constructor gates and reported both, and the prediction holds at each. **The aggregate extrema — the third gate that note named — were then measured here and obey the same rule**, so all three of its excluded gates are now closed the same way.

**The `DateRange(start, finish)` endpoint reads the declared format; the kind takes no part.** A TIME-declared and a DATE_TIME-declared field each carrying `yyyy-MM-dd` are admitted in the start position, in the finish position, and in both at once. The DATE_TIME refusal our own catalog and laws file had recorded is its **stamp format** refusing, not its kind — a DATE declared `HH:mm:ss` is refused on the same code, which is the diagonal that separates the two readings.

**The `Date(day, month, year)` complete-Year position is the same rule, and both of its conjuncts are measured necessary.** A DATE, a TIME and a DATE_TIME field each declared exactly `yyyy` are admitted at Year. The format is necessary — the same three kinds declared `yyyy-MM-dd`, and a DATE declared `HH:mm:ss`, are each refused `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` there. The position is necessary — a `yyyy` field is refused at Day and at Month. So neither "any temporal field is admitted at Year" nor "a `yyyy` field is admitted anywhere" survives.

**Carrier note: their Year rows ran through `computation add --dry-run` and ours are rule conditions**, so this is a second carrier for that half rather than a re-run of theirs. The endpoint half sits on the carrier they used.

**Our own defect was larger than the prose they flagged, and its worse half was the READ path.** They named the `constraints` string of our `DateRange` catalog entry, which was kind-keyed. One layer down, `DateRangeConstruction`'s constructor refused any endpoint whose `kind()` was not DATE or DATE_FRAGMENT — a client-side refusal broader than its measured basis, in a record whose javadoc called both of its refusals measured. Because it is a record constructor it also fires on the way **in**, so the sweep for siblings looked for kind-keyed classifiers in `ConditionConverter`. **Three rounds were needed and the class holds SEVEN**, which is the part worth carrying and is recorded under the table. The rows below are the kernel-admitted CONDITIONS that came back unreadable — several share one site, so read them as symptoms, not as the enumeration:

| read site | the kernel-admitted condition it could not read | what it reported |
|---|---|---|
| `dateRangeEndpoint` | `DateRange(<TIME yyyy-MM-dd>, <DATE>)`, and the DATE_TIME twin | `DateRange on a TIME field …` |
| the direct-comparison dispatch | `[<TIME yyyy-MM-dd>] == [<DATE>]` — [KF211](#kf211)'s own read-gate row | `time operand FieldIdOperationImpl` |
| the same, DATE_TIME arm | `[<DATE_TIME yyyy-MM-dd>] == [<DATE>]` | `date-time/date equality operator EQ` |
| the same, the clock-declared DATE mirror | `[<DATE HH:mm:ss>] == [<TIME>]` | `converter error (IllegalArgumentException)` — reported as a bug in us, not as a degrade |
| `temporalExtremumKind` — **missed by the first sweep** | `MaxValue(<TIME yyyy-MM-dd>, <DATE yyyy-MM-dd>) == [<DATE>]`, and its DATE_TIME twin | `MaxValue takes number fields …` (the numeric arm) |
| `temporalOperandKind` — **missed by the first two** | `[<DATE_TIME stamp>] == [<DATE declared as a stamp>]` — the same pair the LEFT-operand row already read | `date-time/date equality operator EQ` |

The root is one notion the read path lacked: **which temporal classifier a DECLARATION selects**, as opposed to which kind it declares. It now exists once, as `FieldInfo.temporalClass()`. **The complete enumeration, stated so the next reader does not have to re-derive it** — every `ConditionConverter` site that classifies a field for a temporal decision, and the two that legitimately do not:

| site | what it decides | reads |
|---|---|---|
| `fieldValueComparison` | which operand family a `[field] op other` comparison's LEFT side is | `temporalClass()` |
| `temporalOperandKind` | the same for its RIGHT side, which is a different function — the reason a left-only test row leaves it unconstrained | `temporalClass()` |
| `convertTimeOperand` · `convertDateTimeOperand` | whether a field read is a legal TIME / DATE_TIME operand at all | `temporalClass()` |
| `isDateTimeValue` | whether an `AddDays` operand and a comparison partner are instants | `temporalClass()` |
| `dateRangeEndpoint` | whether a field is an admitted `DateRange` endpoint | `temporalClass()` |
| `temporalExtremumKind` | which family an entity-list extremum's operands share | `temporalClass()` ∘ `DateListAggregate.temporalClassOf` (which collapses DATE_FRAGMENT into the DATE class) |
| `homogeneousKind` · `convertValueList` | the value-list carrier's operand kind | **`kind()`, and correctly** — no temporal kind is an admitted value-list operand, so the question never arises (`validate.laws.ValueListLawsTest.everyTemporalKindIsExcludedToo`, all four kinds, added because the BOOLEAN row already there measures one kind and this is a claim about a family) |
 *(The kernel-free `interpreter-bridge` had the same defect at its own two temporal dispatches — the comparison operand family and the extremum's routing kind — and now resolves both through one `Mapping.temporalClass`; its `DateRange` endpoint already delegated. `dateRangeEndpoint`'s row was measured on our reader, not on the bridge.)* The clock-declared DATE row is the sharpest of the read failures: it did not degrade politely, it surfaced a legal model as a converter defect — and it was reachable only because the authoring side had already been widened, so the two directions had drifted apart inside one release.

**Why three rounds, which is the transferable part.** `temporalExtremumKind` had been moved off kind EQUALITY onto a kind-keyed CLASS the day before ([KF193](#kf193)), so it read as a site already fixed. And the rows that move was measured on could not have caught it: every one of them carried its own kind's DEFAULT format, so kind class and declared class agreed across the whole set — the constant-across-every-row confound, sitting inside a fix for the very rule it violates. The falsifier costs one field: a TIME field declared `yyyy-MM-dd`. Its authoring twin in `DateListAggregate` refused the same lists, so `MaxValue(<TIME yyyy-MM-dd>, <DATE>)` was unauthorable *and* unreadable; both now keep only the ROUTING check (is this operand date-like at all), the one temporal question a `ValueKind` can answer.

**And the third round is the sharper lesson, because the second round's fix was correct and its enumeration still was not.** Sites six and seven surfaced only when a mutant was planted at the two operand functions and SURVIVED: every row measured the cross-declared field on the LEFT of a comparison, and the right operand is resolved by a different function. Adding the mirrored rows immediately exposed `temporalOperandKind` as well. So the enumeration was never wrong about the sites it named — it was wrong about the *positions* it exercised, which no reading of the code surfaces and one mutant does. A sibling sweep is not finished when every site you found is fixed; it is finished when a mutant at each one dies. **That sweep was then run: `kind()` planted back at each of the seven sites, one control class per mutant, all seven killed** — and it cost an eighth row, because `isDateTimeValue` types an `AddDays` rather than a field read and survived every comparison row in the file.

**`temporalClass()` is for DISPATCH, never for refusal**, and the distinction is load-bearing rather than stylistic. `BoundModel.date` still admits a kind-matching field whose declared format disagrees, because refusing one would be a client-side refusal with no measured basis; what the new notion decides is only *which typed handle* a declaration becomes. `DateRangeConstruction` keeps a kind check for exactly the kinds it measured refused (NUMBER, STRING, DATE_RANGE) and hands the format conjunct to the kernel, since a record holding only a `FieldRef` cannot see a declaration.

**The aggregate gate's own rows.** `MaxValue`, `MinValue` and `NumberOfDifferentValues` admit a date-declared TIME or DATE_TIME field beside a plain DATE, and admit the two carriers together; the same TIME field carrying `HH:mm:ss`, and the same DATE_TIME field carrying its stamp default, are refused `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` beside that DATE. So the component set the gate compares is the DECLARATION's, and the within-model control is the same kind on the other side of the axis.

**Unmeasured here.** The runtime *value* a cross-kind endpoint contributes to the constructed range, and whether a component-omitting cross-kind endpoint completes asymmetrically the way a same-kind one does (a12-kernel-lean's own limit line on the endpoint, and ours). The `FirstFilledValue` family's `requireKind` gates are a different checker arm and are not covered here. The aggregate half's runtime IS measured — see the lock line.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalConstructorDeclaredFormatGateLawsTest` — the six endpoint admissions with their three no-date-component refusals, the three Year admissions with their six necessity rows, and the typed-surface mirror that builds every admitted endpoint while still refusing the three measured kinds. The aggregate half is `validate.laws.TemporalAggregateComponentSetLawsTest.theAggregateGateReadsTheDECLARATIONsTemporalClassAndNotTheKinds` — four admissions with two same-kind controls — plus its typed-surface mirror. `adapter.CrossKindTemporalOperandReadTest` locks the read half at all three construct families (fourteen rows), each read from a `BoundModel.ofJson` bind, whose gate that file's own positive control exercises rather than assumes; `bridge.CrossKindTemporalTranslationTest` locks the kernel-free translation half as a render round trip. `adapter.laws.CrossKindTemporalExtremumDiffTest` carries the aggregate's RUNTIME half — dynamic Groovy, generated Java and the interpreter agree on what a cross-kind extremum computes, in both the fires and the does-not-fire direction — which an accept/reject oracle cannot settle and which mattered because making the shape authorable put it in front of the interpreter for the first time. The new `Date.complete-date-at-year` catalog claim probe re-measures two of the Year rows on a second fixture.)*

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-07-07` (the endpoint) and `SPEC-2026-09-07-06` (the Year position).** Neither entry proposes a mechanism beyond `KF211`'s, and neither asks us to re-derive it; what they add is the two gates, and what we add back is that our client refused both and our reader could not read either.

## §6/§9 supplement — the equal-set pair denominator is SEVEN across three families, the admitting gate ignores component ORDER, and `FirstFilledValue` is the fifth carrier (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf272"></a>

> Fold: pending — completes [KF193](#kf193)'s denominator and adds the carrier that entry excluded; folds into §6 with it.

[KF193](#kf193) said two equal-set, different-spelling pairs exist. That is the only kind of row separating the component-SET gate from the format-STRING one, so the number is a denominator — and it had been read off the pairs that work happened to use. Derived from the twelve admitted formats ([TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md)) there are **seven, across three families**: three spellings of {MONTH, DAY} (`MM-dd`, `MMdd`, `ddMM`), three of {YEAR, MONTH, DAY} (`yyyy-MM-dd`, `dd.MM.yyyy`, `yyyyMMdd`), and two of {YEAR, MONTH} (`yyyy-MM`, `yyyyMM`).

**All seven split the five carriers identically**, each against a same-format control at the same carrier, in one model:

| carrier | every equal-set pair |
|---|---|
| `MinValue`, `MaxValue`, `NumberOfDifferentValues` | **ADMITTED** |
| `FieldValuesNotUnique` | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_DATE_ALLOWED` |
| `FirstFilledValue` | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` |

**`FirstFilledValue` is the row [KF193](#kf193) explicitly left out** — it routes through `checkAllFieldsMatchingOperationType` and that entry declined to cover it. It reads the format string, with its own third code, so the five carriers are two-and-three rather than two-and-two.

**The admitting gate ignores component ORDER, not merely spelling — the new family is what makes that measurable.** `MM-dd` reads month-first and `ddMM` day-first ([KF211](#kf211)'s separator-free grid measures that by validity), so the two decode the same four digits to different dates; `MinValue` and `MaxValue` take the pair anyway. So the admitting gate is the **unordered component set** and nothing else, which is a stronger statement than "reads the component set" and the one an importer needs: it decides whether two order-opposed spellings may share one operand list. `FirstFilledValue` refuses that same pair.

**The differing-set rows are still refused** `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` at the admitting carriers, including across the new family boundary ({MONTH, DAY} beside a complete date) — without them every admission above is equally consistent with those carriers having no temporal gate at all.

**What keeps the denominator from drifting back.** The pair list is computed from the families the sweep declares, and `TemporalFormatVocabularyGuardTest` re-derives the same list from the vocabulary the kernel actually admits and fails when the two disagree. The count lives beside the derivation rather than beside the sweep, which is precisely the arrangement whose absence produced "two exist".

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalEqualSetPairDenominatorLawsTest` — the 7 × 5 grid with 15 same-format controls, three differing-set refusals, and the order-opposed pair called out on its own; `validate.laws.TemporalFormatVocabularyGuardTest.theEqualSetPairDenominatorMatchesTheAdmittedVocabulary` derives the denominator from the kernel.)*

**Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-07-04`.** Their carrier split is one our operator catalog already carried correctly and in both directions (`FieldValuesNotUnique`'s third gotcha names the three operators it disagrees with; `NumberOfDifferentValues`' first says not to carry its gate the other way), so the split itself is confirmation. What is ours to fix is the denominator, and the seven above are derived here rather than taken from their count.

## §2/§9 supplement — `FirstFilledValue`'s filled predicate is PRESENCE, and an all-empty selection into a SEEDED target CLEARS it (tri-engine differential, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf273"></a>

> Fold: pending — the filled predicate itself, which §2's empty-value account never states; folds beside [KF20](#kf20).

Every row this estate held about `FirstFilledValue` was about which *operand* is scanned or what an *empty* selection yields. None asked what **filled** means for a kind whose value can be falsy — and only BOOLEAN can pose that question.

**It is presence, never truth.** `FirstFilledValue(Rows*/Approved)` over two rows holding `false` then `true` computes **`false`**. Two rows separate the accounts: an **absent** first row falls through and yields `true`, so the scan is not "always take the first operand"; and the trivial `true`-then-`false` control yields `true`, so the grid is not constant. All three engines agree — dynamic Groovy, generated Java, and the interpreter, whose `firstFilledOperand` consults `EvalContext.filled` (a `value != null` test) and so agreed at the mechanism rather than by a coincidence of cases.

**A CONTRARY measurement to a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-07-03`, on the axis their own limit line names.** That entry's delta says an all-empty selection "mints no outcome at all, leaving the target neither written nor cleared", while its `limit` row records "whether a *seeded* target is cleared rather than left untouched" as unmeasured — and an unseeded target cannot tell the two apart. Ours is seeded: `FirstFilledValueAdditionalKindDiffTest` seeds the BOOLEAN target with `false` and the kernel reports **CLEARED**, on both strategies, with CUSTOM and DATE_FRAGMENT beside it; `FirstFilledValueKindDiffTest` carries the same seeded row for DATE, STRING, ENUM, TIME, DATE_TIME and DATE_RANGE, against the NUMBER control that computes the fillable `0` ([KF20](#kf20)). So the kernel does mint an outcome, and an implementation that leaves a seeded target alone keeps a stale value the kernel would have removed.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.FirstFilledValueAdditionalKindDiffTest.aFalseBooleanIsFilledAndAnAbsentOneFallsThrough` for the predicate; `.allEmptySelectionsClearEveryAdditionalKind` and `adapter.laws.FirstFilledValueKindDiffTest` for the seeded clear.)*

## §1 supplement — a TYPEDEF-typed field is its base kind at every gate, which is what makes an expansion exclusion sound (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf274"></a>

> Fold: pending — a declaration-layer rule the canonical prose assumes rather than states; folds into §1.

Nothing here had put a typedef field to an admission gate. Our CLI reports a typedef field's **resolved underlying** kind, so the read surface behaves as if resolution had happened — but that is our classification, not the kernel's gates, and every consumer that works on an expanded model is resting on the kernel agreeing.

It does, at all three gates measured, and **each reports a different class**:

| gate | NUMBER-based typedef | STRING-based typedef | plain-base control |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sum`'s numeric operand | **ADMITTED** | `MVK_NO_NUMBER` | same, both sides |
| `NumberOfDifferentValues`' homogeneity | (beside a String) `MVK_STRING_ENUM_AND_NON_STRING_ENUM` beside a Number | **ADMITTED** beside a String | same, both sides |
| an ordering comparison against a numeric literal | **ADMITTED** | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` | same, both sides |

**The spread is the separator, not any single row.** A typedef treated as an opaque kind of its own would refuse uniformly; one silently admitted everywhere would pass no control. Three distinct codes, each keyed to the base kind and each matching its plain-field control, kill both.

**The ordering row independently reproduces the orderability gate** [KF270](#kf270) measures: STRING is not orderable, so an ordering comparison reports `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` before any kind match — recorded here as corroboration on a second carrier, with that entry keeping the claim.

**Why it is worth stating rather than assuming.** The rule is what makes a scope exclusion sound: a surface that puts include/expansion out of scope — as any consumer of an already-expanded model implicitly does — is relying on expansion losing no observable distinction. Reported by a12-kernel-lean as `SPEC-2026-09-07-05`, whose point is exactly that consequence.

**Unmeasured:** a typedef over a config-bearing base kind (DATE, ENUM), where a declared format or domain might not survive resolution; a typedef imported from a separate type-def model rather than declared inline; and the computation arm.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.TypedefBaseKindGateLawsTest` — twelve rows, each gate with its plain-base control.)*

## §13 supplement — `$index(…).value$` is a live message-parameter terminal whose SUFFIX is mandatory (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf275"></a>

> Fold: pending — a fifth parameter form [KF198](#kf198) did not reach; folds into §13 with it.

[KF198](#kf198) enumerated the rule-message parameter surface — a field, its value suffix, its category suffix, the `BaseYear` terminal, and the semantic-index key — and never reached `index(…)`, which pins a message to the **firing row's** declared index-field value. This estate held no claim about it in either direction; a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-07-09` corrects a no-witness clause of *theirs*, and the rows below are ours.

**It is admitted, and one character decides it.** On a rule whose error field sits inside a repeatable group declaring `indexField ClaimNo`, `$index(ClaimNo).value$` is **admitted** while `$index(ClaimNo)$` is refused `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_PARAMETER`. *(Hypothesis, not measured here: a12-kernel-lean's source read has the grammar accepting the suffix as optional and the checker enforcing it, so the class is reported instead of a parse error. That is their reading of the grammar, cited as theirs; nothing in our rows distinguishes it from a checker-only rule.)* That pair is why the terminal reads as dead: the natural first attempt omits the suffix and draws a class that sounds like it is about the argument.

**The argument is the SHORT name of an index field on the error entity's path.** Four wrong arguments draw one class, `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD`: a non-index field of the same group, a field outside it, a name no field carries, and — the row that shows what the match is against — **the index field spelled as a path**. Moving the error field to the root refuses the identical parameter under the same class, with its own parameter-free control admitted, so the refusal is the parameter's and not the rule's.

**Three spellings fail in the PARSER, not the checker**, all `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`: a capitalised `Index(`, a capitalised `.Value`, and the German `.Wert` under `en_US`. **And the category alternative is live**, gated on the index field being an Enumeration: `$index(ClaimNo)->Band$` over a String index field draws `FIELD_NO_ENUM` rather than a parse error.

**Consumer consequence.** An Explain or Translate consumer treating this terminal as having no admitting spelling silently drops a legal parameter, and one attributing the parameter class to the argument's shape rather than to the missing suffix gives advice that cannot repair it.

**Unmeasured:** what an admitted `index(…).value` **renders**, the German arm, the Enumeration index field that would admit the category form, a composed index (whose own `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_COMPOSED_INDEX` class the peer's source read names and no row here reaches), and the computation carrier.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.RuleMessageIndexTerminalLawsTest` — the admission and the suffix pair, the four-argument sweep, the three spelling rows, the category alternative, and the root-error-field row, each parameter-free control admitted alongside.)*

## §3/§6 supplement — the unsigned-number sign class, and the pre-1900 check on its two other declaration carriers (kernel `validateFull` + `checkConsistency`, tri-engine, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf276"></a>

> Fold: pending — the sign half corrects [KF37](#kf37)'s ladder in place and folds into §3; the temporal half extends [KF251](#kf251) onto the two carriers its grid never covered and folds into §6 with it.

Three declaration knobs the kernel honours were unauthorable here until this change, so an external consumer was hand-patching them into raw DM JSON: `NumberType.positivesOnly`, `DateFragmentType.youngerThan1900Check` and `DateRangeType.youngerThan1900Check`. Making them authorable turned up four facts, each with a within-model control.

**`positivesOnly` is the runtime's `hatVorzeichen`, and it is the ONLY input to it.** `TypeConverter` sets `hasSign(!positivesOnly)`; a non-negative `minValue` does not make a field unsigned at runtime (that pairing belongs to the kernel's static date-construction gate, `CheckBaseDateConstructionImpl`). A minus on an unsigned field is **`zahlMitVorzeichen`** — the code [KF37](#kf37) row 5 spelled `zahlEnthaeltVorzeichen`, which is the Java CONSTANT name and occurs nowhere in the 30.8.1 checkout. *(Corrected 2026-09-07 in KF37 itself; reported by a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-07-13` and re-derived from `IFormaleFehlerConstants` here before the row was changed.)*

**KF37's ladder positions 4/5/10 are not a precedence chain — two of the three orderings are unobservable.** The kernel conjoins `nullErlaubt && hatVorzeichen` before the signed-zero class, so it is DISJOINT from both its listed neighbours. One model, four fields differing only in the two builder calls:

| declaration | `-0` / `-0.00` |
|---|---|
| signed, zero allowed | `zahlNullEnthaeltVorzeichen` |
| unsigned, zero allowed | `zahlMitVorzeichen` |
| signed, zero **forbidden** | `zahlIstNull` |
| unsigned, zero forbidden | `zahlMitVorzeichen` |
| unsigned, zero forbidden, **`trait:"amount"`** | `zahlIstNull` |

The money row is a nested exception the kernel spells out inside the unsigned arm, and `-5.00` on that same declaration reporting `zahlMitVorzeichen` is the control that keeps it about the zero magnitude rather than about the trait. The disjointness also moves a neighbouring ordering: `-0.0` on a scale-0 field is the signed-zero class where zero is allowed and **`zahlHatDezimalTrenner`** where it is not, so KF37's "signed-zero beats the separator check" holds only on a zero-permitting declaration. Observably ahead of the sign class: `zahlMitPlus`, `zahlHatUngueltigeZeichen`, `stelligkeitZuLang`. Observably behind it: the separator, leading-zero, zero-not-allowed, length and range classes. `positivesOnly` beside a NEGATIVE `minValue` is kernel-VALID at model check, and the value refusal still fires — measured, because refusing that pairing client-side would have looked obviously right.

**The pre-1900 check's year co-requirement holds on DATEFRAGMENT and NOT on DATERANGE.** [KF251](#kf251) measured the gate on `DateType` over the complete admitted vocabulary: `MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID` unless the declared format carries a year. Re-run on the other two carriers, same denominators:

| carrier | axis | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `DateFragmentType` | the twelve admitted formats | identical to `DateType` — the five year-free spellings refused, the seven year-bearing admitted |
| `DateRangeType` | all eight admitted `(format, separator)` pairs | **every pair admitted**, the four year-free ones included |

So a checker enforcing the year co-requirement uniformly across the temporal kinds refuses four legal range declarations. Fragment agreement is measured rather than inherited, though the kernel's `TypeConverter.convertDateFragment` explains it: a fragment declaration becomes a `DateTypeImpl` carrying the flag.

**On a year-free range the check reads the base-year completion — except for the pure `MM` pair, which reaches neither date-position check.** Two models differing in exactly the `baseYear` builder call: `dd.MM|-` and `MM-dd|/` fire `datumBereichDatumFalsch` under base year 1899 and are silent under 1901, with the plain twin silent in all four cells. `MM|/` and `MM|''` fire under neither, and under a base year of **1500** the plain twin is silent too — so the always-on 1583-10-16 floor is skipped as well, while the reversed value `09/06` still reports `datumBereichNichtGueltig`. That last row is the liveness control: two dates ARE produced and ordered, so this is not "no date exists". *(Mechanism, source-read and not measured: `DateUtil.completeDateAndFormat` appends the base year only when `formatContainsOnlyDayMonth(format)` — day AND month present, year absent — so a pure `MM` endpoint gets no year and parses at a year-less pattern's default. No formal row can distinguish that default from an exemption, because any year above 1900 satisfies both thresholds.)* The interpreter carries the rule as `rangePositionCheckYear`, applied to both position checks; its `parseRangeToIso` still completes every missing year with the base year, because the interval and wrap rules it feeds are measured that way.

**The two sign classes are unreachable through A12's own Document-JSON ingress**, which is why a12-kernel-lean's 278 `validateFull` observations found neither: `-0.0`, `-0`, `-0e5` and `"-0.00"` all canonicalise to a sign-free zero with no code, and `"+5"` to `5`. `"-5"` keeps its sign, so the predicate is (a leading plus) or (a minus on a zero magnitude), not "the sign is dropped". Our own oracles reach both classes because they set cell values directly through `IDocumentFactory.createFieldInstance(path, reps, value)`, where `ValidationData.getValue` returns the string unchanged — two entry points, both correct.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.NumberUnsignedFormalDiffTest` — the sign grid, the zero 2×2 with its money row and magnitude control, and the ladder neighbours, all tri-engine; `adapter.laws.TemporalAdditionalCheckCarrierDiffTest` — the fragment and range runtime rows with their plain twins, the base-year 2×2, and the pure-`MM` exemption with its liveness control; `validate.laws.TemporalAdditionalCheckCarrierLawsTest` — both admission grids over their complete denominators, a registered completeness claimant of `TemporalFormatVocabularyGuardTest`; `adapter.laws.A12JsonIngressKernelTest` — the ingress sign rows; `cli.field.SignAndPre1900AuthoringVerbTest` — the authoring round-trips and the delegated co-requirement refusal with its range control.)*

## §8/§12 supplement — `checkConsistency` has no route to the dynamic-enumeration derivation's twelve `MVK_DYNENUM_*` classes, and the restriction pair sits behind a third facade method (kernel facade, measured, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf277"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — reachability of kernel DIAGNOSTIC classes through the facade's derivation methods, an authoring/observability fact outside KERNEL-SEMANTICS's runtime-evaluation scope.

**Two kernel derivations over a rule collection report problems no other route of ours can reach, and they are behind DIFFERENT methods.** a12-kernel-lean reported this as one ~14-class gap behind `mandatoryInformation()`'s discarding reporter; measured, it is two gaps behind two other methods, and the reported one has nothing to give.

| derivation | facade method | its classes | reachable from `checkConsistency`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| dynamic enumerations | `getDynamicEnumerationStringValues` | the twelve `DynEnumErrorType` classes | no — see the caller enumeration below |
| rule-driven model changes | `getChangesAsSpecifiedByRules` | `MVK_MAX_GROUP_RESTRICTION_TO_ONE`, and its H-model-only sibling `MVK_MAX_LFDNR_RESTRICTION_TO_ONE` | no — `CheckerFuerKontextEinschraenkung` / `CheckerFuerLfdNrEinschraenkung` are called only there |
| mandatory information | `getMandatoryInformationFromRules` | the rule PARSER's, via `MVKParserProblemManager.transferProblems` | n/a — **empty on all THIRTEEN consistency-clean models probed** (each carrying one or two spliced rules), because a condition that parsed for the gate parses here too |

So flipping the reported call's reporter surfaces nothing: the restriction checkers are not on its path, and its own channel is the one the original comment correctly called impossible. *(Our `MVK-LEDGER` had a matching error in the opposite direction, corrected the same day.)*

**The caller enumeration, run here rather than carried — and it corrects the report's count while confirming its point.** `git grep` over the 30.8.1 checkout's tracked `*.java`/`*.kt`, delombok excluded, finds `DynamicEnumerationService` CONSTRUCTED at **two** sites, not one: `RuleCollectionMetaInformation:214` inside the collection method, and `ServiceFactory:107` — `getDynamicEnumerationService(IServiceConfiguration)`, which has **no in-kernel caller at all** and returns the public `IDynamicEnumerationService`, whose single method is a PER-RULE `checkDynamicEnumerationRule(ICondition, IRule, IProblemReporter)`. `checkDynamicEnumerationRule` itself is called only from inside the service. **The load-bearing fact is therefore not the count but the placement:** neither construction site sits on a `DocumentModelConsistencyRule`, so `checkConsistency`'s registered rules cannot reach the checker. Our `dynamicEnumerationDiagnostics(rule)` stays on the collection call for one rule anyway, because `checkAndExtractDynEnumInfo` runs the form check AND the extraction and so reports a superset of the facade's per-rule check.

**The dyn-enum diagnostics are NOT defects — the derivation reports one per rule that is not a dynamic enumeration IN FORM,** which is nearly every ordinary rule. Two ordinary rules draw two; the count is per rule, not per model. Each way of being malformed draws its own class, which is what makes the channel informative rather than a boolean:

| condition, error field `/Order/ProductCode` unless noted | class |
|---|---|
| `FieldFilled(/Order/ProductCode) And [/Order/ProductCode] != "PREMIUM"` — the canonical form | none; `valuesByField` carries `[PREMIUM]` |
| `FieldFilled(/Order/ProductCode)` — an ordinary presence rule | `MVK_DYNENUM_INVALID_GATE` |
| `FieldFilled(…) And FieldFilled(…)` — an ordinary conjunction | `MVK_DYNENUM_INVALID_CALCOP` |
| the canonical form with `==` | `MVK_DYNENUM_INVALID_CALCOP_OP` |
| a gate naming a field other than the rule's error field | `MVK_ERROR_WRONG_DYNENUM_FIELD` |
| error field `/Order/UnitPrice` (`maxFractionalDigits: 2`) | `MVK_DYNENUM_INVALID_TYPE` |
| `… != [/Order/CustomerName]` — a field on the right, no safe guard | `MVK_DYNENUM_INVALID_FIELD_REFERENCE` |

**The canonical row is the load-bearing control, not a courtesy.** "One problem per non-dyn-enum rule" and "the derivation errors on everything" predict the same output on any suite of ordinary rules — the instrument confound — so a grid of malformed rows alone cannot separate them. A rule the derivation ACCEPTS, with its constants extracted, is what does. The field-type check also runs before the form check: a rule whose error entity is a GROUP draws `MVK_DYNENUM_INVALID_TYPE`, not the `_GATE` its bare-comparison condition would suggest.

**Attribution is the kernel's own and usually absent.** The collection-wide call leaves the rule unnamed, because the kernel's problem carries a rule only where its message does; `KernelAdapter.dynamicEnumerationDiagnostics(ruleFullName)` asks about one rule and stamps the answer, which is the only shape in which the answer is attributable.

**Both spellings of "restrict to one" reach the restriction class, with a live negative control.** A rule whose condition is a BARE `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Order/Items*)` comparison against a number constant: `> 1` and `>= 2` both fire (the checker decrements the `>=` literal), and `> 2` — a legal narrowing to 2 — reports nothing. The error entity must be the GROUP, because the checker visits only a top-level comparison while the consistency gate separately requires the error entity to appear in the condition.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.RuleCollectionDerivationDiagnosticLawsTest` — the canonical control, the six-class discriminator grid, the per-rule scaling, the attribution split, both restriction spellings with their control, and the class-family disjointness; `adapter.laws.KernelProbeDynamicEnumerationsTest` — the same derivation through the probe's `dynamicEnumerations` observation, its schema conformance, absence when unobserved, and byte-determinism. Surfaced as `KernelAdapter.dynamicEnumerations()` / `dynamicEnumerationDiagnostics(rule)` / `ruleDrivenModelChangeProblems()`; the probe capability is [KERNEL-PROBE-SPEC](KERNEL-PROBE-SPEC.md) "The `dynamicEnumerations` block".)*

## §9 supplement — the entity-list arity gate is a DISJUNCTION whose group arm ignores the group's field count, and the entity-valued value list does not share it (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf278"></a>

> Fold: pending — sharpens §9's entity-list operand rule; folds with the operand-arity paragraph.

**`MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN` reads "There must be more than one field or at least one group defined", and it means it.** One repetition-list selector or one group selector satisfies the gate alone; one plain field does not. Five of our catalog entries name this gate and **two stated it without the group arm** (`Sum`, `FieldValuesNotUnique`) — measured on each of the two rather than widened from a sibling, because reuse across a carrier boundary is a claim.

| operand list | verdict |
|---|---|
| a sole plain field | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN` |
| two plain fields — the arity control | admitted |
| a sole repetition-list selector (`Items*/Sku`) | admitted |
| a sole plain group owning **two** same-kind fields | admitted |
| a sole plain group owning exactly **one** field | admitted |
| a sole starred **heterogeneous** group | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED`, **not** the arity class |

**The last two rows are the ones that carry information.** The heterogeneous group reached the KIND gate, which is proof it had already passed arity — so an implementation reading that refusal as "one group is too few" mis-states both gates. And **a group's own field count is not part of the rule** — an axis neither estate's clause named. "A group counts" and "a group whose expansion yields several fields counts" predict the same verdict on any fixture whose groups all own the same number of fields, so the pair is the discriminator: `/Order/BillingAddress` (one String) beside `/Order/ShippingAddress` (two), both admitted.

**The entity-valued value list is a different family with a different arity: ONE field on each side is admitted.** Its own two gates still fire on the same fixture, so those admissions are gates passed rather than gates never reached — the same reference on both sides draws `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`, a crossed base kind `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED`. Carrying the entity-list rule across refuses a legal `(A In B)`.

Reported as a prose correction by a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-07-11`; every row above is re-derived on our own fixtures, since a peer's measurement is their report and not a pin. *(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.EntityListSoleOperandArityLawsTest` — the five-row arity table with its control, the attribution split as a "this code and not that one" refusal, the value-list trio, and the two-carrier sweep on an authored all-numeric group. Catalog: the group arm added to `Sum` and `FieldValuesNotUnique`, the field-count clause to `FirstFilledValue`, the single-slot admission to `AtLeastOneFieldValueIncludedInValueList`.)*

## §13 supplement — three message-surface gates a uniform reading gets wrong, and the two form-line parameters fault at runtime (`checkConsistency` + `validateFull`, tri-engine, 2026-09-07) <a id="kf279"></a>

> Fold: pending — the three admission gates sharpen §13's parameter paragraph; the runtime fault is a kernel defect and folds nowhere.

Three gates, each measured against a within-model twin differing in one variable. Every row below is re-derived on our own fixtures after a12-kernel-lean reported them as `SPEC-2026-09-07-12`, since a peer's measurement is their report and not a pin.

**The template's character repertoire is the BMP, not printable ASCII.** Greek, Cyrillic, CJK and `U+FFFD` are all admitted in message text; a supplementary-plane code point is refused. The refusal carries **no class at all** and is identified only by its text — `The field contains one or several unsupported signs.`, which is the RUNTIME formal charset class's wording (`ZeichenNichtImZeichensatz`) and not the checker's own `WRONG_ENCODING`. So a consumer keying on a code loses it entirely. The model declares no `supportedCharacters`, so this is the empty-list ⇒ BMP rule reaching the template rather than an authored restriction.

**`<field>.Vordruckzeile` and `<field>.Vordruckname` SKIP the field-membership gate.** One condition, one unreferenced field, three suffixes: the plain form draws `INVALID_FIELD` while both form-line suffixes are ADMITTED. The kernel's own `checkVordruckzeile`/`checkVordruckname` call only `checkValidFieldName`, never the membership check the plain form goes through — so a checker enforcing membership uniformly across name-position forms refuses two admitted ones. **Extended 2026-09-15: skipping membership is not skipping every gate.** The same suffix on a GROUP draws `INVALID_FIELD_IN_PARAMETER`, both spellings, against the admitted field twin on the one condition — `checkValidFieldName` is the only check these two forms do make, and it asks whether the parameter resolved to a field. An address that resolves to nothing is a third shape and has no verdict to record: the kernel reaches it through `getEntityRef`, which raises past every typed channel ([KF259]).

**The `.value` suffix has a second gate on the referenced field's DECLARATION.** A STRING declared `noValueValidation` refuses the suffix with `INVALID_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION`, its ordinary twin admits it, and the plain form on the same field is admitted — so the gate reads the declaration, not the parameter's shape. **Corrected 2026-09-15: the two gates are ORDERED, not independent.** On a value-validation-free field the condition reads through a star alone, A12 answers `PARAM_VALUE_WITH_STARREFERENCE` — the reference gate wins, and neither class says so on its own, so a checker reproducing the pair had to measure which. Membership pre-empts both: the same suffix on a field the condition never reads is `INVALID_FIELD`.

**And the bypass makes a kernel RUNTIME FAULT reachable.** On the admitted model above, both kernel strategies return the rule's message text as `An error occurred while evaluation the data check: Index 1 out of bounds for length 1`; the plain `$Reference$` parameter in the same message renders on every engine, so the fault is attributable to the form-line positions. The interpreter leaves the token verbatim — a characterized divergence we deliberately do not close, because there is no kernel behaviour to match ([IG150](INTERPRETER-GAPS.md)). This is the runtime case a12-kernel-lean's source-derived prediction (nothing raises `NO_VORDRUCKZEILE`, so an unguarded form-line path throws) did not have: a different carrier from the static `$RuleGroup.Vordruckzeile$` internal error they already held, and it throws.

Not measured here, and therefore still their report alone: the parameter BODY's printable-ASCII bound and its `ÄÜÖäüöß` admissions, the gate ORDER between the charset check and `$` parity, and the remaining four gates of their entry (the `$#RootGroup$` parallel-iteration refusal, the group position's semantic-index key, the index terminal's cross-declaration consistency family, and the `STR`-initial dotted-name-part rule).

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleMessageAdmissionGateLawsTest` — the six-row repertoire table, the three-suffix membership table, and the value-suffix declaration trio, each with its control; `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageValueSuffixGateOrderLawsTest` — the six-cell gate-order grid on a repeatable retail shape, carrying both controls and the membership pre-emption; `adapter.laws.RuleMessageFormLineParameterDiffTest` — the runtime fault on both kernel strategies with the interpreter's divergence and a within-message control.)*

## §13 supplement — the `index(…)` message terminal cross-checks the RULE'S OWN CONDITION, admits `->Category` on an Enumeration index field, and one of its ten classes is structurally unreachable (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-08) <a id="kf280"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends [KF275](#kf275)'s terminal with three more axes; folds with it into §13.

[KF275](#kf275) measured this terminal's admitting spelling, its argument axis, and its case sensitivity. a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-07-10` read the checker and reported ten refusal classes where our entry carried three. Three of their added axes are measured here, each with a parameter-free control on the same rule so no refusal belongs to the route.

**`->Category` is ADMITTED once the index field is an Enumeration, and the category NAME is gated.** KF275 could only show the alternative was live (`FIELD_NO_ENUM` on a String index field). With an ENUM index field carrying a declared category: `$index(Tier)->Band$` admitted, `$index(Tier)->Nope$` refused `INVALID_CATEGORY`, `$index(Tier).value$` admitted. So an Explain consumer must resolve a category mapping at this terminal, not only a stored value.

**The parameter is cross-checked against the rule's own CONDITION** — the axis a checker reading the model alone cannot see. One model, one parameter, three conditions:

| the condition's reference to the index field | verdict |
|---|---|
| plain (`FieldFilled(Claims/Tier)`) | admitted |
| STARRED (`AtLeastOneFieldFilled(Claims*/Tier)`) | `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_REP_ITER` |
| `For`-keyed (`[Claims/Tier For "BASIC"]` as a presence handle) | `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_REP_ITER` |

Each refused row's own parameter-free message is admitted, so the condition is legal and the refusal is the parameter's. From a ROOT error field the starred shape draws `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` instead — the error-entity-path gate fires first, consistent with KF275's root row.

**`INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_NONREP_ENUM` is reachable, but not every non-repeatable index parameter is refused.** The kernel admits the declaration. On our Shipment/Approval fixture, an Enumeration index with one value and that value as its S-value admits both `$index(Status).value$` and `$index(Status)->Category$`. Removing the S-value, adding a second value, or doing both refuses either suffix with `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_NONREP_ENUM`; all four declarations admit the parameter-free message. `NonRepeatingIndexMessageLawsTest` locks the 12-row grid (`SPEC-2026-09-08-03`, 2026-09-08). The Enumeration-type conjunct and the distinction between nonempty and member S-values are not independently separated by this grid; runtime rendering and German messages remain outside this measurement. **Corrected 2026-09-08:** the draft builder and `ModelDocument.setIndexField` now admit the declaration, and `RuleMessageIndexTerminalLawsTest` authors both repeatability arms through the typed builder ([API-FINDINGS finding 143](API-FINDINGS.md)). The sort-field control remains distinct: a sort field on a non-repeatable group draws `MVK_INVALID_SORTINFO`.

**`INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_COMPOSED_INDEX` is UNREACHABLE from any A12 document model** — not, as their entry reads it, an authoring limitation of `dmtool group modify --index-field`. Its trigger is `getIndexFieldNames().size() > 1`, and every link was attacked in the 30.8.1 checkout (tracked sources, `/build/` and delombok excluded): `md-model`'s `Group` declares `indexFieldNames` **final** and writes it in one place — its constructor, from a single nullable `String`; the name occurs exactly three times in the whole `kernel-md` tree (the `final` declaration plus the two writes in that constructor), with no setter or adder; that constructor has one caller, `ValidationModelConverter.createGroupFromGroupType`, which derives the name from `IGroup.getIndexField()`, an `Optional` of ONE reference. So the DM-model surface has no plural spelling to serialize and taking exactly one name is correct. *Recall limit: a source enumeration over the A12 path — another `IEC` implementation may populate several (which is consistent with the class existing), and a reflective writer would escape the search.*

**Amended 2026-09-15 — three more of the terminal's gates, measured because a checker reproducing this one had to walk them in order.** The non-repeatable arm reads the DECLARATION the parameter named, not the condition: dropping the condition's reference to the two-value Enumeration index field changes nothing, the same `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_NONREP_ENUM` comes back, and the model whose index field declares one value carrying its own `sValue` admits the parameter. The repeatability gate PRE-EMPTS the missing-suffix one — a starred reference with no suffix draws `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_REP_ITER`, not `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_PARAMETER` — which is the order a reproduction needs, since each class had only been measured where the other could not fire. And `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_REP` is REACHABLE, on the MIXED shape: a repeatable group off the error entity's path declaring an index field of the same SHORT NAME, referenced by the condition, while the error entity's own index field is admitted. Where that own index field is NOT admitted, its own class answers instead, so the two refusals sit on one list and only one of them speaks.

Still unmeasured: what an admitted `index(…)` of either suffix RENDERS, the German suffix on a German-condition model, the computation carrier, the three cross-field consistency classes, and what ORDERS the list when several of its members offend.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleMessageIndexTerminalLawsTest` — the Enumeration/category table, the condition cross-check table with its per-row controls, the non-repeatable pair, and the composed-index enumeration as a typed-surface assertion; `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageIndexTerminalRepeatabilityLawsTest` — the gate-order grid, the declaration-versus-condition pair with its admitted twin, and the mixed shape on both sides of the error entity's own gate, each with a parameter-free control.)*

## §12 supplement — the H-model form constructs DO reach their checker in an A12 model and are refused there by name, so `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP_CONSTR` is reachable on both carriers while the two codes behind it are not (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf282"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the canonical reference states what A12 means, and which legacy checker sites an A12 model cannot reach is inventory for the portable checker rather than a rule of the language.

**Corrected 2026-09-12, same day, on the discriminating case the first version lacked.** That version reported all three constructs refused with `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` and concluded the parser excludes them. Every row was measured on a model whose `conditionLanguage` is `en_US` — `DocumentModelDraft` stamps that unconditionally — and these constructs exist only in the GERMAN terminal bundle (`LexerTerminals_de`; `LexerTerminals_en` carries no `VordruckAngegeben` at all, [KF283](#kf283)). Under `en_US` the spellings are ordinary names, so the parser rejects them before any checker runs and "excluded by the parser" is indistinguishable from "reached the checker and was refused there". One condition held constant across all three rows carried the entire conclusion.

The same three conditions on the SAME model with only `conditionLanguage` flipped to `de_DE`:

| condition | `de_DE` model | `en_US` model | the code neither reaches |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VordruckAngegeben(Order/*)` | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP_CONSTR` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` | `MVK_CONDITION_WITH_WILDCARD` |
| `MindestensEinVordruckAngegeben(Order)` | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP_CONSTR` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` | `MVK_CONDITION_WITHOUT_REPEATABLE_ROOTGROUP` |
| `AnzahlAngegebenerVordrucke(Order) > 0` | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP_CONSTR` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` | — |
| the same count operation in a COMPUTATION | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP_CONSTR` | absent | — |

**So `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP_CONSTR` is an A12-facing rejection an A12 model does reach, on both the rule and the computation carrier** — its message names the construct and says it "is only allowed to be used in H models". **`MVK_CONDITION_WITH_WILDCARD` and `MVK_CONDITION_WITHOUT_REPEATABLE_ROOTGROUP` stay unreachable**, now for a source-verified reason rather than an unexplained one: the grammar attaches `checkFormularBedingungName` to `formularBedingungName` and `checkFormularBedingung` to the enclosing `formularBedingung`, so the inner action's `if (fullParser.isA12Model()) throw MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP_CONSTR` (`CheckFormularBedingungImpl.checkFormularBedingungName`) runs first. Inner-action pre-emption — the mechanism the first version recorded as refuted — is what actually happens; it only looked refuted because the keyword never became a keyword.

**The parser layer is nevertheless real, which is the control that keeps this from proving too much.** `ZeilenLueckenlos(Code)` in the same German model is refused with `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`: `einfacheBedingung` predicate-gates `zeilenBedingung` on `isHModel()` and deliberately leaves `formularBedingung` un-predicated, so the two layers are separable and the German rows above are the checker's verdicts rather than the parser's. The flip is controlled in both directions too — the German model accepts `FeldAngegeben(Code)` and refuses `FieldFilled(Code)` at the parser.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.HModelFormConditionReachabilityLawsTest`, six arms. Consumed by the portable checker's A1 legacy-exclusion inventory, [PORTABLE-CONSISTENCY-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN](archived/PORTABLE-CONSISTENCY-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md) §3.)*

## §12 supplement — a model's `conditionLanguage` selects the KEYWORD VOCABULARY, and the two vocabularies are not translations of one set: 112 English terminals against 125 German, so 13 constructs exist only in German (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf283"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — this is how the Kernel's lexer is configured, not a rule of the validation language; the canonical reference describes the language a model writes, not which spellings a given model admits.

`content.modelConfig.conditionLanguage.code` is not a presentation choice. The lexer's `ID` rule carries `{this.getMultiLanguageHandler().setTypeInLexer(this);}`, and that method looks the matched text up in **one** language's terminal map: a hit sets the keyword's token type, and a miss sets `getDefaultTokenType()`, which `ConditionMultiLanguageHandler` defines as `NameOhnePunktSTRAmAnfang` — an ordinary entity name. There is no fallback to the other language, and `SUPPORTED_CONDITION_LANGUAGES` is exactly `{en_US, de_DE}`.

*Corrected 2026-09-12: this first added "with anything else silently becoming German", read off `AbstractMultiLanguageHandler`'s constructor, which does substitute `Locale.GERMANY` for an unsupported locale. It does not manifest. A model declaring `fr_FR` is refused before any lexing — "Die im ValidierungsModus übergebene Sprache fr_FR wird nicht unterstützt", uncoded — under BOTH languages' spellings, so no model reaches that substitution. A source-read fallback stated as behaviour, which is the class the oracle table warns about; `ModelConfigCoercionLawsTest` now measures it.*

Two consequences follow, and both are load-bearing for any tool that reads condition text:

- **A keyword of one language is an ordinary field name in the other.** `And` is a terminal for `en_US` and a plain name for `de_DE`; `Und` is the reverse (measured). A tool holding the union of the two vocabularies reads such a field as an operator and drops the reference silently — no diagnostic, because nothing failed.
- **The vocabularies are nested, not parallel.** Counting the `ListResourceBundle` entries of `LexerTerminals_{en,de}` at kernel 30.8.1: **112 English spellings against 125 German**, every English terminal has a German twin, and the 13 extra German ones are exactly the H-model constructs (`VordruckAngegeben`, `ZeilenLueckenlos`, `AnzahlAngegebeneUsb`, …). So those spellings are legal field names in an English model and reserved words in a German one — which is what made the first version of [KF282](#kf282) wrong.

The renderer's side of the same map is `AbstractMultiLanguageHandler.hasToBeQuoted(str)`, which is literally `isATerminal(str)` for the model's language. So the set a checker must treat as keywords and the set A12 quotes when a field name collides are one set, per language — and `KeywordReverseParityTest.rendererQuotesEveryLiveLexerTerminalThatCanBeAnEntityName` already exercises that direction.

*(Locked: `consistency.ConditionKeywordProjectionTest` pins the portable checker's shipped keyword table to these bundles in both directions, per language; `rulekit.validate.laws.HModelFormConditionReachabilityLawsTest` locks the behavioural consequence on the Kernel itself, and `rulekit.validate.laws.ModelConfigCoercionLawsTest` the unsupported-code refusal. The count is re-derived by the projection test, not restated anywhere.)*

## §10 supplement — an unresolvable reference has THREE different answers, and the two carriers resolve from different origins (`ModelLoader.loadAndCheck`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf284"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — §10 states how a path is written and what it names; which rejection each carrier issues, and which one pre-empts the rest, is checker inventory rather than a rule of the language.

One model carries every row: a root group `Order` with a field `Code` and a subgroup `Lines` holding `Amount` and `Sku`, and a rule declared in `/Order/Lines`. Only the reference moves.

**The origin differs by carrier, and the two spellings are one level apart.** A rule's `errorEntityRelPath` climbs from the rule ELEMENT — `../Amount` from `/Order/Lines/ProbeRule` reaches its sibling field — while a reference inside the CONDITION climbs from the rule's GROUP: `../Code` reaches `/Order/Code`, and `../Lines/Code` (the element-relative reading of the same intent) is rejected. A resolver written once for both is wrong on exactly one of them for every model that has a subgroup.

**And the floor is the root GROUP, not the model root, with a code of its own.** From `/Order/Lines`, `../../Code` is `MVK_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS`; from a rule in `/Order`, one step already is. The boundary is measured on both sides at depth 1, so "two steps are too many" and "the root group is the floor" are separated rather than merely consistent.

| the reference that does not resolve | what A12 reports |
|---|---|
| an entity in a condition | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| an entity in a condition, at ROOT-GROUP level (`/Nope`) | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP` — the Kernel branches on `EntityUtils.isRootGroup`, exactly one path separator |
| an entity in a condition, climbing out of the root group | `MVK_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS` |
| a rule's `errorEntityRelPath` naming nothing | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING` **and** `MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD`, together |
| a rule's `errorEntityRelPath` climbing PAST the root | **no code at all** — `ElementPathUtils.absPath` raises while the model is deserialized |
| a computation's `computedFieldRelPath` | **no code at all** — the Kernel cannot build the model |
| an ABSOLUTE `errorEntityRelPath` (`/Order/Code`), however well it names a real field | **no code at all** — "illegal relPath" during conversion, so the member is strictly relative and the model does not build *(added 2026-09-12)* |

**Corrected 2026-09-12, hours later, by a cold review that ran the climb one step further than this entry had.** The `errorEntityRelPath` row read "whether missing or above the root", from a probe whose deepest case reached the root rather than passing it. Climbing PAST the root is a different outcome: the model does not load at all (`IndexOutOfBoundsException` in `ElementPathUtils.absPath`, through `EntityReferenceResolverVisitor.visitRule`), so it joins the computed field's class rather than the error field's. The falsifier was already in this repository — `ErrorFieldRelativePathLawsTest` records that row as uncoded — and the entry was written without reconciling against the lock beside it.

**Two more rows belong to the same question and are measured on the same fixture.** Whitespace between path tokens changes nothing, in either direction ([KF76](#kf76) states the lexer fact; `ConditionReferencePathLawsTest` now measures it on the reference path specifically). And `..` may carry a TURNING-POINT LABEL naming the ancestor it lands on: `..Order/Code` from a rule in `/Order/Lines` is admitted, while `..Lines/Code` — the label naming the rule's own group rather than the ancestor — is `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`, so A12 checks the label rather than ignoring it.

**The climb holds unchanged when the operand is a GROUP (measured 2026-09-12).** Every row above resolves a FIELD, so the rule was a claim about the group carrier until it was run there: `GroupFilled(../Lines)` and `GroupFilled(/Order/Lines)` are admitted from a rule in `/Order/Lines`, `GroupFilled(/Nope)` draws the root-group code, and the row worth having is `GroupFilled(Lines)` — which READS as naming the rule's own group and does not, because the climb starts at the declaring group and the candidate is `/Order/Lines/Lines` (`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`). A checker that special-cased a bare group name to the declaring group would admit a model A12 rejects.

**The last row is the one that changes what a report may claim.** `ModelLoader.loadAndCheck` on that model raises "the kernel could not build this model: The computed field \"/Order/Lines/Nope\" was not found." and reports nothing else — not the other rule's real `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`, not the missing error texts the same model has. So a model with an unresolvable computed field never receives a consistency verdict at all, and any list of findings for it is the reader's own reading rather than A12's. Searched for a key behind that message across our sources and the kernel checkout: there is none, so a portable report has to own a code for it or say nothing.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ConditionReferencePathLawsTest` for the path rows on the Kernel, each asserting the rival code does NOT co-fire; `rulekit.validate.laws.ErrorFieldRelativePathLawsTest` for the declared-target rows; the portable checker's mapping is `consistency.ConditionBindingTest` and `consistency.ReferenceDiagnosticTest`.)*

## §9 supplement — two `SumOfProducts` operands cannot be made to differ at their outermost index in an A12 model: five asymmetries, five different gates ahead of the comparison (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf285"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — §9 states how iteration binds; which checker a legal model can and cannot reach is inventory for the portable checker rather than a rule of the language.

`CheckEntityListenUtils.checkAllFieldsSameL` compares `EntityRef.getLfdNr()` — `indices.get(0)`, the OUTERMOST level's index — across a `SumOfProducts`' two operands and raises `MVK_INVALID_PARAMS_FOR_OP` when they differ. It is called **ungated** from `CheckFeldListenOpImpl`, so a package-path reading calls the code live; the setter enumeration points the other way (all nine `setLfdNr(` sites are `hdv`) and settles nothing, because `indices[0]` is also written by the general index path and by `CheckSemanticIndexImpl`.

So the question is reachability, and it was attacked rather than measured once. One model — a root group holding an indexed repeatable `Lines` with a repeatable `Sub` inside it, both operand fields in `Sub` — with only the operand spelling varied:

| the asymmetry | what refuses it |
|---|---|
| both operands carry the same semantic index | **admitted** (the baseline) |
| both carry one, with different index VALUES | **admitted** — the value never reaches `indices`, only the `SEMANTIC_INDEX` marker does |
| only one operand carries a semantic index | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| neither does, so the outer level is unmarked | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| the outer level starred instead | `MVK_WILDCARD_ONLY_AT_LOWEST_LEVEL_ALLOWED` |
| one operand marks the outer iteration with `$` | `MVK_INVALID_OUTER_ITERATION` — `$` is filter-only |
| one operand carries a `Having` filter beside its index | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| the two operands spell one path differently, absolute against relative | **admitted** — spelling is not structure |

**The mechanism the rows agree on**: `checkAllEntitiesInSameGroup` forces both operands into the same group, so they share a path and therefore an index-level structure and an index group; `CheckSemanticIndexImpl` then marks the SAME slot for both, or the model is refused for the level being unmarked. Every route to marking one operand alone meets a different gate first, which is why no single measurement establishes this and the set of attacks is the evidence.

**Recall limit, stated rather than implied.** Five asymmetries were attacked on one topology, on BOTH carriers (a computation's operation and a rule's comparison, which enter through different grammar entry rules and agree). An authorable shape not in that set — a third repeatable level, or a group with several index fields, where `getIndexGroup`'s choice could differ per operand — would reopen it. The H-model raiser `CheckEntityListenUtilsHModel.checkAllFieldsZIteration` is a separate, already-legacy site.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.SumOfProductsOperandIndexLawsTest`.)*

## §12 supplement — a DocumentModel's reader descends only as far as `content`, and never consults `header.modelType`, so "no groups" is a normal model rather than a malformed one (`ModelLoader.loadSelfContained`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf286"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — §12 describes the validation model's semantics; how little of the envelope has to be present for A12 to read one at all is ingress inventory, and it exists to bound a client-side refusal.

One model authored by `DocumentModelDraft`, with exactly one member removed or replaced per row:

| the source | A12 |
|---|---|
| the ordinary model (control) | read |
| `content.modelRoot.rootGroups` set to `[]` | read |
| `content.modelRoot.rootGroups` removed | read |
| `content.modelRoot` removed | read |
| `content` removed, or replaced by a string or an array | **NOT read** — the deserializer raises |
| `header.modelType` set to `selection` | read |
| `header.modelType` removed | read |

**The empty root is not a degenerate case, it is an artifact kind.** `DocumentModelDraft.typeDefModel` emits exactly `"rootGroups": []` with `modelType: "document"`, and such a library is kernel-valid standalone (`TypeDefModelImportTest`). So a consumer treating "declares no elements" as unreadable rejects a legal A12 artifact — which is why the portable checker states it as a coverage gap and refuses only the missing-`content` row.

**`header.modelType` is routing metadata, not a discriminator the reader applies.** A12 knows four values — `document`, `additive-document` (`CombinationModelService`), `combination`, `selection` (`SelectionModelService`) — and `UnexpandedModelResolverImpl` switches on it to pick the owning service. The DocumentModel deserializer does not, so a foreign type reads as a document carrying whatever content it has. A checker keying on it would be refusing on its own authority with no Kernel basis behind it.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ModelRootReadabilityLawsTest`; the portable checker's one refusal is `consistency.AdmissionPhaseTest` and its gap `consistency.ConsistencyCheckTest`.)*

## §10 supplement — a bare short name in an INCLUDED model is bound by that model's own `fieldRefByShortNameAllowed`, before the including model's flag can see it (`ModelLoader.loadAndCheck`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf287"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — §10 states what a path names; which of two models' configuration decides a name's binding, and when, is assembly inventory the portable checker needs and the language does not state.

[KF3](#kf3) records the mechanism — "a flag-enabled unique cross-group short name is bound in the included model so an including-model collision cannot retarget it". This measures WHICH flag enables it and what happens when it does not.

A provider `address` declares `Zip` one group below its root and a rule in its root group whose condition is the bare `FieldFilled(Zip)`; a host mounts it at `/Order/ShipTo`. Three binary axes, eight cells, one verdict each:

| host declares `Zip` too | host flag | provider flag | A12 |
|---|---|---|---|
| no | on | on | accepted |
| no | on | off | accepted |
| no | off | on | accepted |
| no | off | off | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| yes | on | on | **accepted** |
| yes | on | off | **`MVK_FIELDNAME_NOT_UNIQUE`** |
| yes | off | on | accepted |
| yes | off | off | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |

**Either flag suffices, by a different route, and only the collision tells the routes apart.** The grid is exactly: the reference resolves when EITHER flag is on, and when only the host's is on a name the host also declares makes it ambiguous. The provider's flag binds the name inside the provider before integration, so it emerges naming an absolute host path (`FieldFilled(Zip)` → `FieldFilled(/Order/ShipTo/Inner/Zip)`, visible in the expanded DM-JSON, and left bare when that flag is off); the host's flag resolves whatever is still bare afterwards, over the whole EXPANDED tree. The separating pair is the two collision rows one flag apart — every other cell is explained by both accounts.

**Consequence for a checker: the short-name fallback has two different denominators in one model.** A reference authored in a provider whose flag is on searches **that MOUNT INSTANCE's expanded subtree**; every other reference searches the whole expanded tree under the entry model's flag. A single denominator is wrong in one direction or the other, and the direction it is wrong in is invisible without a name that both models declare.

**Corrected 2026-09-12, hours later, by a cold review that built the two shapes this entry's own fixture could not.** The sentence above read "searches that provider alone", and the portable checker took the noun literally — keying the denominator on the AUTHORING MODEL. That is wrong in both directions and in the fatal one: a provider is fully expanded before it is bound ([KF3](#kf3)), so a field its own nested include contributed is inside its index and an author-keyed filter drops it; and one provider mounted at two points is two separate indexes, so an author-keyed filter finds both copies and reports `MVK_FIELDNAME_NOT_UNIQUE` for a model the Kernel accepts. Both re-measured through `ModelLoader.loadAndCheck`. The original eight-cell grid stands; it simply has one mount and no nesting, so nothing in it could separate "the provider" from "this mount of it". The entry also carried a wrong cell count ("six of the eight cells agree between the two accounts"), removed above in favour of the rule the grid actually states.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.IncludedShortNameBindingLawsTest`, which asserts the whole grid at once; the portable checker's reproduction is `consistency.WorkspaceMountTest`.)*

## §12 supplement — an include is refused at EXPANSION unless the provider declares every locale of the entry model, so a mounted declaration never answers to a narrower locale set (`expand`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf288"></a>

> Fold: pending — an include/expansion admission law; fold into §12's include account beside [KF3](#kf3), whose placement rules it gates.

The message-coverage law ([§13](#kf158)) is stated over "the declared locales", which is unambiguous only while a model is self-contained. A mount puts two headers in play, and a checker analysing the expanded tree has to pick one: judge a provider's rule against the provider's own header, or against the entry model's. Picking the provider's would accept a model A12 rejects — the direction no consumer can detect, since the Kernel is never asked about a declaration the checker passed.

**A12 answers one layer earlier, and that removes the choice.** A provider whose header declares fewer locales than the entry model cannot be mounted at all: `IDocumentModelService.expand` raises `DocumentModelExpansionException` — *"Cannot expand include because included model [=pricelist] does not support all locales of the base model"* — before any declaration is read. So every model that expands already covers the entry's locales, and the mounted rule answers to that set.

| provider declares | entry declares | expansion | the mounted rule is judged against |
|---|---|---|---|
| `en_US` | `en_US`, `de_DE` | **refused** | — nothing is read |
| `en_US`, `de_DE` | `en_US`, `de_DE` | expands | the entry's two locales — a rule carrying only `en_US` draws `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_FOR_LANGUAGE_MISSING` |
| `en_US`, `de_DE`, `fr_FR` | `en_US`, `de_DE` | expands | the entry's two — so the demand is COVERAGE, not equality |

The third row is what bounds it: without it "the provider must match the entry" and "the provider must cover the entry" are the same observation on every other row, and a checker built on the first would suspend a mount A12 expands in full.

**Consequence for the portable checker.** It suspends such a mount by name rather than mounting a tree A12 never builds — deliberately UNDER-reporting, since A12's own answer is a refusal to load and the checker owns no code for that beyond `CK_MODEL_NOT_BUILDABLE`, which the mount path cannot yet carry. Same disposition as an `includeLevel` spelling A12's enum refuses, for the same reason.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.IncludedDeclarationLocaleScopeLawsTest` — all four rows, on the Kernel's own `expand`; the checker's suspension is `consistency.WorkspaceMountTest`.)*

## §10 supplement — `fieldRefByShortNameAllowed` is read by Jackson's `boolean` POJO binding, which accepts `"True"` where `JsonNode.asBoolean` does not — and refuses any other string outright (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf289"></a>

> Fold: pending — a model-config admission fact that gates the §10 short-name tier; fold beside [KF287](#kf287), which measures what the flag does once it is on.

[KF287](#kf287) measures what the flag DOES. This measures how A12 decides it is set, because six readers in this repository each decide it differently and four of them are wrong in the dangerous direction. The verdict is read through the model-wide lookup itself — a bare unique name that resolves only when the tier runs — so nothing in the chain is our own reading of the member.

| authored spelling | A12 |
|---|---|
| `true` · `"true"` · `"True"` · `"TRUE"` · any non-zero INTEGER (`1`, `2`, `-1`) | **ON** |
| `false` · `"false"` · `"False"` · `0` · `null` · absent · `""` | OFF |
| any other string (`"yes"`, and `"1"` — a numeric STRING is not a number) | **the model does not deserialize** — `Cannot deserialize value of type 'boolean' from String "yes": only "true"/"True"/"TRUE" or "false"/"False"/"FALSE" recognized` |
| any FRACTIONAL number (`0.5`, `1.5`), an OBJECT, an ARRAY | **the model does not deserialize** |
