| an integer wider than any machine type (26 digits) | **ON** — so a reader must decide on the LITERAL, not on a conversion that overflows |

**A12 states its own rule in that rejection**, and it is Jackson's standard `boolean` POJO binding on `DocumentModelConfig`, reached through the normal `DocumentModel` → `content` → `modelConfig` chain. `JsonNode.asBoolean` is a DIFFERENT Jackson path with a different rule: it accepts only the lowercase `"true"` and answers false for `"True"`. So every reader here built on `asBoolean` reads a capitalized spelling as OFF where A12 reads it as ON, which turns a reference A12 resolves into `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` — a refusal the Kernel never issues, and therefore invisible. The sites were `core.ModelReader:470`, `modelkit.ModelDocument:258`, the interpreter's `load.ModelLoader:80` and the bridge's `InterpreterConditionReadBack:115`; the interpreter's `workspace.IncludeAssembly` was stricter still and refused every string spelling, including the three A12 accepts. All six now read through the shared rule (see the sweep below).

**The empty string is not an unrecognized spelling.** `""` reads as OFF rather than refusing, because Jackson's empty-string coercion supplies the type's default before the recognized-values check runs. It is the row that keeps "any other string refuses" from being stated one notch too wide.

**The fractional row is the second divergence, and the sharper one.** `0.5` and `1.5` refuse the model outright, where `asBoolean` truncates to an int: our readers answer OFF for `0.5` and **ON for `1.5`**, inventing two different verdicts about a model A12 will not load — one of them affirmative. The integral rows are the control that separates this from "numbers are refused": `1`, `2` and `-1` all read ON, which is the same answer `asBoolean` gives, so the numeric arm diverges on the FRACTION and not on the type.

**This is NOT the rule the mount exclusions follow, and assuming one rule for both is how those readers were wrong.** `excludeRules` and `excludeComputations` reach A12 through `ElementDeserializer`'s `JsonNode.booleanValue()`, which is false for every non-Boolean and never refuses ([KF3](#kf3)); this member reaches a `boolean` field through the POJO binding, which coerces three string spellings and refuses the rest. Two members, two Jackson paths, three different answers for `"True"`.

**All six readers were swept to this table on 2026-09-12, and the shared rule lives once per ESTATE rather than once.** Three implementations are forced by boundaries that exist for other reasons: `dm.core`'s `ConfigFlag.ofJsonText` serves `core.ModelReader`, `modelkit.ModelDocument` and `interpreter-bridge`; `:interpreter` and `:consistency` each carry their own, because both are Kernel-free Kotlin Multiplatform modules that may not depend on the kits (the interpreter purity lint and the checker's H1). The Java one takes the value's JSON TEXT rather than a `JsonNode` because dmkits-core publishes no third-party type on a public signature — which turns out to be what the rule needs anyway, since the wide-integer row cannot survive a conversion. Each estate's copy is locked against this same table (`core.ConfigFlagTest`, `interpreter.ConfigFlagTest`, `consistency.ConfigFlagTest`), so a divergence between them fails a test rather than drifting.

**The sweep stops at this member, deliberately.** `ModelLoader`'s `asBoolean` has four other callers — `Field.global`, `NumberType.positivesOnly` and two typed properties — and whether each reaches A12 through the POJO path or through a custom deserializer's `booleanValue()` is a per-member fact that has NOT been measured. Applying this table to them would be exactly the scope transfer the exclusions row above records going wrong. What would settle it: the same probe on each member, or a source read of the binding each one lands on.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ShortNameFlagSpellingLawsTest` — the whole table in one assertion.)*

## §13 supplement — a message slot has THREE verdicts, and a locale is matched as a PARSED locale rather than as text (`ModelLoader` + `checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf290"></a>

> Fold: pending — the raw-shape half of [KF158](#kf158)'s message-locale law; fold both into §13 in one pass.

[KF158](#kf158) measures the message law through `ModelWriter`, which emits one canonical spelling of everything. Stored DM-JSON does not, and a checker reading it meets shapes the writer cannot author. Measured on the shared subscription fixture with the header's `locales` and the rule's `errorMessage` substituted raw:

**Three verdicts, and the third is the one a reader must not fold away.** `ModelInputException` is A12's READER refusing the bytes — no rule is examined and no consistency verdict exists; `ModelConsistencyException` carrying an `MVK_*` code is its verdict on a model it did read. A reader that reports the first as an `MVK_*` finding presents its own opinion as A12's about a model A12 never judged.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| header `en-US` · message `en_US` (and the reverse) | **ADMITTED** — both spellings parse to one locale |
| header `en_us` | **UNREADABLE** — `Invalid locale format: en_us` |
| `header.locales` as bare strings (`["en_US","de_DE"]`) | ADMITTED, and the per-locale demand applies in full |
| message entry with no `locale`, or no `text` | **UNREADABLE** — `Missing locale for localized text` |
| message entry whose `locale` or `text` is a NUMBER | **UNREADABLE** |
| `errorMessage` as an OBJECT | **ADMITTED** — the reader iterates the node's elements, which for an object are its values |
| `errorMessage` as a string or number | `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` — it yields no entries |
| two entries for one locale, the LATER one blank | `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` |
| two entries for one locale, the EARLIER one blank | ADMITTED |
| a whitespace-only `text` | `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` |

**The locale rows are the dangerous ones, and a string comparison cannot get them right.** A12 parses both sides through `LocaleUtils.toLocale` and compares the parsed values, so `en-US` and `en_US` are one locale and a reader comparing text reports `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_FOR_LANGUAGE_MISSING` for a model A12 admits. The `en_us` row is what keeps the correction from being "normalize case": A12's parser REFUSES that spelling rather than accepting it leniently, so a normalizing reader would analyse a model that does not load.

**The last entry for a locale wins, and blank means blank rather than empty.** The two duplicate rows differ only in which of the pair is blank and they disagree, which is what establishes the ordering; a reader keeping the first usable entry reports nothing where A12 rejects. `StringUtils.isBlank` is the test, so whitespace-only counts as absent — every earlier measurement of this law used the empty string alone.

**The object row is what keeps the unreadable class from being stated one notch too wide.** It was predicted unreadable by a source read and is admitted: the container's shape is free, and it is the ENTRY's own members that must be strings.

**Every mechanism above is source-located, not inferred from its row** — `kernel-md/kernel-md-serializer/src/main/java/com/mgmtp/a12/kernel/md/serializer/model/internal/service/serialization/LocalizedTextMapDeserializer.java:60-94`. `deserialize` does `for (JsonNode entry : parser.readValueAsTree())`, which is Jackson's node iterator: an ARRAY yields its elements, an OBJECT its values, and a scalar yields nothing — the three container rows in one line. Each entry's `locale` and `text` must be present and `JsonNodeType.STRING` or the reader raises (`"Missing locale for localized text"`, `"Unexpected node type for localized text"`), the code goes through **`LocaleUtils.toLocale`** — Apache Commons Lang, which is why `en_123` and `en_US_POSIX` are admitted while `en_us` is not — and the result is `builder.add(locale, text)` into a MAP, which is why the last entry for a locale wins. The measurements came first; this read tells us the rows are the mechanism rather than a coincidence of the fixtures.

**Which SPELLINGS the parser takes, measured as a set rather than inferred.** Admitted: `en_US`, `en-US`, `en`, `eng`, `fr_CA`, `en_US_POSIX`, `en_123`. Refused (UNREADABLE): `en_us`, `EN_US`, `EN`, `e`, `en_U`, `en_USA`, `klingon`. The shape is therefore *lowercase 2–3-letter language, optional uppercase 2-letter country or 3-digit area, free-form variant beyond that* — and a reader must mirror the REFUSALS as refusals, because normalizing `en_us` would analyse a model that does not load.

**The two sides were varied INDEPENDENTLY, which the first table above cannot do.** Every row of that table carries the same code in the header and the message, so each of its refusals is attributable to the header alone and establishes nothing about a message's own `locale` — leaving a reader free to parse one side and compare the other as text. Holding the header at `en_US` and varying only the message: `en_us`, `EN_US`, `en_U` and `klingon` are all **UNREADABLE** there too.

**The EMPTY code reads on both sides, and the two sides then differ.** It is the "any locale" value, so the parser takes it; in the HEADER the model is then refused by the kernel's own build with **no `MVK_` code at all** (a third tier, distinct from both UNREADABLE and a verdict), while in a MESSAGE it simply covers no declared language and the declaration is left message-less (`MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING`).

**A model must declare at least one locale — `MVK_SUPP_LANGUAGES_MISSING` — and it then collects NO message at all.** With `header.locales` empty, every rule draws `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` however many texts it carries, because collection is keyed by declared locale. The two codes arrive together on any model with a rule, so the attributing row is the base fixture, which declares no rule: it draws `MVK_SUPP_LANGUAGES_MISSING` alone. This is the row that refuted the natural prediction — "with no declared locale, one message is enough" — and it is the reason a portable checker reports the header defect model-level rather than once per declaration.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageSlotRawShapeLawsTest` — one assertion per table.)*

## §13 supplement — an ABSENT `severity` is accepted, an explicit JSON `null` refuses the reader, and `errorCode` coerces a scalar (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf291"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — authoring/model-structure slot laws on the rule element, outside the evaluation scope.

The rule's other two declaration slots, measured for the first time because both are `pre-checked` in the [MVK ledger](MVK-LEDGER.md): `Rule.Builder.build` refuses them, so what A12 itself does had never been asked — and a checker reading stored DM-JSON meets every shape the builder cannot produce.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| `errorCode` absent · `""` · whitespace-only | `MVK_ERROR_CODE_MISSING` |
| `errorCode` as a NUMBER (`7`) | **ADMITTED** — Jackson coerces the scalar, so the code is `"7"` |
| `severity` `"ERROR"` · `"WARNING"` · `"INFO"` | ADMITTED |
| **`severity` ABSENT** | **ADMITTED** |
| `severity` `""` · `"error"` · `"Error"` · `"FATAL"` | **UNREADABLE** — a strict enum binding |
| `severity` whitespace-only · a NUMBER (`7`) · a JSON CONTAINER | **UNREADABLE** *(added 2026-09-12)* — none of `errorCode`'s leniencies carry across: no coercion, and blank is not absence |
| an explicit `null` on `errorCode`, `severity`, `errorCondition` or `errorEntityRelPath` | **UNREADABLE** |

**The two slots share a carrier and almost no behaviour, which is the transferable half.** `errorCode` coerces a scalar, reads blank as missing, and draws an `MVK_*` verdict; `severity` is an ENUM binding, so it coerces nothing, treats blank as a refusal rather than a default, matches case-SENSITIVELY, and every present shape outside its three constants is the READER's refusal. A checker sharing one predicate across the two would be wrong on five of those rows. *(The portable checker reports the severity tier as `CK_MODEL_NOT_BUILDABLE` — the model never loads — and reports nothing for an absent member; added 2026-09-12.)*

**`MVK_SEVERITY_MISSING` fires for none of these shapes, so the builder's refusal is broader than any measured basis.** An absent `severity` is simply accepted. That makes `Rule.Builder`'s "severity is required" an over-rejection candidate of exactly the class the [2026-07-25 audit](MVK-LEDGER.md) hunts — a refusal invisible because the Kernel is never asked. **What this does not establish:** what an absent `severity` DEFAULTS to is not measured here, and neither is what shape does fire `MVK_SEVERITY_MISSING`; the code exists in the metamodel and some other input must reach it.

**An explicit `null` is not an absent member, and that is the pair a reader collapses.** `errorCode: null` refuses A12's reader where `errorCode` absent draws a verdict — two tiers for what most readers treat as one shape. The mechanism row is the third test: `errorCondition` and `errorEntityRelPath` are refused by a `null` too, so the refusal follows the NULL rather than a null-hostile accessor on one member. Four members is the whole basis; a member outside them is unmeasured.

**The empty string means different things in different slots, which is why each is measured rather than inferred.** It is a *default* for `fieldRefByShortNameAllowed` ([KF289](#kf289)), *no message* for an `errorMessage` text ([KF290](#kf290)), *missing* for `errorCode`, and an outright reader REFUSAL for `severity`. One shape, four answers, decided by the member's binding.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleCodeAndSeverityLawsTest` — one assertion per table.)*

## §11 supplement — a computation's alternative list: one may be unguarded, SEVERAL each owe a precondition, and a common one does not substitute (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf292"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an authoring/model-structure law on the computation element, outside the evaluation scope.

The structure of a stored `computationAlternatives`, measured because `Computation.Builder` requires at least one alternative with a non-blank operation, so every degenerate shape below is one only stored DM-JSON carries — and the portable checker must reach "every alternative" to claim the family at all.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| one alternative, unguarded | ADMITTED |
| the member ABSENT, or an EMPTY list | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` **and** `MVK_CONDITION_MISSING` |
| an alternative with no `operation`, or a blank/whitespace/explicit-`null` one | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` alone |
| an alternative that is not an object, **or the member as an OBJECT, a scalar, or an explicit `null`** | **UNREADABLE** |
| two alternatives, both guarded | ADMITTED |
| two alternatives, ANY of them unguarded — first, last, or both | `MVK_ERROR_EMPTY_PRECONDITION` |
| two alternatives, one precondition present but BLANK or whitespace | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| two alternatives, one precondition an explicit `null` | `MVK_ERROR_EMPTY_PRECONDITION` |

**Corrected 2026-09-12: the second code is an observation, not the consequence it was written as.** "With no alternative there is no precondition slot either, so both gates fire" fitted every row and was never tested — all of them were measured with no `commonPrecondition`. Declaring one leaves the pair exactly as it is, so a condition slot on the model does not remove `MVK_CONDITION_MISSING`. Why it fires is not established here; that it fires beside `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`, and only when there is no alternative at all, is.

**A12 raises ONE notification for the unguarded case, however many alternatives lack a guard.** The code table cannot see that — comma-joined codes are de-duplicated — so it was measured on the notification stream. The message names the declaration and carries no alternative index, which is why the checker reports one finding per computation rather than one per alternative.

**The precondition law is the one a reader gets wrong, and it needed three rows to locate.** A single unguarded alternative is accepted, which makes "an alternative may be unguarded" look settled; add a second and the pair is refused. The two accounts that fit that one observation — *the last is the fallback and owes nothing* versus *each of several owes a guard* — differ on every real model, and the rows separate them: unguarding the FIRST, the LAST, or BOTH all draw the same code, so the demand is per-alternative once there is more than one.

**"Empty precondition" names the ABSENT member only — blank is a different defect in a different family.** Three slot families now agree that a blank string counts as absent (`errorCode`, [KF291](#kf291); a message `text`, [KF290](#kf290)), and the fourth does not: a precondition that is present goes to the condition parser whatever it spells, so `""` and `"   "` draw `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` rather than this code. A checker that carried the blank-is-absent law across would name the wrong defect, in the family that cannot fix it.

**An explicit `null` splits BY BINDING SITE, and the split is inside this one member.** On a rule's own members a `null` refuses the reader outright ([KF291](#kf291)); here `computationAlternatives: null` does the same — but one level down, inside an alternative, `operation: null` draws `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` and `precondition: null` draws `MVK_ERROR_EMPTY_PRECONDITION`, both verdicts and both identical to the omitted member. So the list and the scalars it holds answer differently, and the prediction that carried the rule-member law down was refuted on the list while holding for neither scalar. A checker inferring any of the three from another gets one wrong.

**The demand is size-INDEPENDENT, which every row of the original set left untested** by having exactly two alternatives. With THREE, an unguarded middle one draws the code and three guarded ones are admitted.

**And a `commonPrecondition` does not pay that debt.** Every row above declares none, so "one alternative may be unguarded" and "an unguarded alternative is fine while nothing else guards the computation" are the same observation there — the constant that no control inside the set can catch. Declaring one separates them: the single unguarded alternative stays accepted and the unguarded pair stays refused. The common guard is a different slot, not a substitute.

**The two list-shaped members have DIFFERENT readers, which is why each is measured.** `errorMessage` as an OBJECT is admitted — its reader iterates the node's elements, and an object's elements are its values ([KF290](#kf290)) — while `computationAlternatives` as an object makes the model unreadable. Inferring one from the other would have produced a checker that analyses a model A12 refuses to load.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationAlternativeSlotLawsTest` — one assertion per table.)*

## §13 supplement — a rule's `errorCondition` and `errorEntityRelPath`: a BLANK one is judged, an ABSENT one is not judged at all (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf293"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an authoring/model-structure law on the rule element, outside the evaluation scope.

The two members a stored rule cannot work without, measured because `Rule.Builder.build` requires both — so every shape below is one only stored DM-JSON carries.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| `errorCondition` present, blank or whitespace | `MVK_CONDITION_MISSING` **and** `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` |
| `errorCondition` ABSENT | **NOT BUILDABLE** — a rejection carrying no `MVK_*` code at all |
| `errorEntityRelPath` present, blank or whitespace | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING` **and** `MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD` |
| `errorEntityRelPath` ABSENT | **UNREADABLE** |
| either member an explicit `null` | **UNREADABLE** ([KF291](#kf291)) |

**The inversion is the finding: the shape a reader calls "missing" is the one A12 says nothing about.** Three sibling slots read a blank string as absent — `errorCode` ([KF291](#kf291)) and a message `text` ([KF290](#kf290)) — which makes "missing" look like one shape with one code. Here the two shapes sit in different TIERS. A blank member is A12's verdict about the rule; an omitted one stops A12 before any verdict exists, at two different depths: the condition's absence fails the model BUILD from inside `checkConsistency`, while the target's absence refuses the READER one tier earlier still. A checker reporting `MVK_CONDITION_MISSING` for an omitted `errorCondition` would present its own reading as A12's about a model A12 never judged.

**Both blank rows draw a PAIR of codes, and one pair is a naming trap.** `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING` and `MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD` are two distinct codes from two enums that fire together on the same shape; quoting either alone under-reports what A12 said, and the two are easy to read as one typo. A one-code assertion would have seen neither the second gate on the condition (`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`) nor the second here.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleConditionAndTargetSlotLawsTest` — one assertion per member.)*

## §13 supplement — how far an element NAME must be unique: one group's children, across kinds, case-sensitively (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf294"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure law on the element envelope, outside the evaluation scope.

[KF132](#kf132) records that two same-named sibling elements in one group are refused by a throw from inside `checkConsistency`, so the `MVK_NAME_RULES_DUPLICATE` metamodel rule never gets to report. That one observation fits several accounts that differ on models an author writes by accident, so each boundary was measured.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| two rules of one name in one group | **NOT BUILDABLE** — a rejection carrying no `MVK_*` code |
| a rule named after a sibling FIELD | **NOT BUILDABLE** |
| a rule named after a sibling GROUP | **NOT BUILDABLE** |
| the same name in two DIFFERENT groups | ADMITTED |
| a rule named after a field in another group | ADMITTED |
| two names in one group differing only in letter case | ADMITTED |

**The demand spans KINDS, and a "rule names must be unique" reading passes two of the three refusals.** The collision is among a group's children whatever each child is — the Kernel's own wording is "two child elements with the same name" — so a rule may not take the name of a sibling field or a sibling subgroup. This is the row a checker that only indexes executables cannot see at all.

**Every row of the original set added a RULE, so "two children of one name" and "a rule taking a name" were one observation.** Measured without a rule anywhere in the collision: two FIELDS of one name, and a FIELD named after a sibling group, are refused the same way; a field added to a different group is admitted. The carrier does not matter, which is what lets a checker key on the path alone.

**Extended 2026-09-13 to the two kinds no row above carried.** A GROUP taking a sibling group's or a sibling field's name, and a COMPUTATION taking a sibling group's or a sibling field's name, are all **NOT BUILDABLE**; a group and a computation of fresh names are both ADMITTED, so the refusal is the collision and not the added declaration. `Computation` had appeared in no row at all, which left the kind-agnostic reading resting on four of its cells while a checker keyed on the path alone applied it to every kind — and a pairing A12 in fact admitted would have made that checker refuse a legal model.

**And it is case-SENSITIVE, where the `vk_vk` prefix law on the same member is case-INSENSITIVE** ([KF160](#kf160)). Two laws reading one slot with opposite case rules is exactly the pair that gets unified by accident, so `Probe` beside `probe` in one group is admitted and must draw nothing.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ElementNameUniquenessLawsTest` — three grids, each with its own control.)*

## §10 supplement — a group's `indexFieldName` and `sortFields[].name`: resolved from the group, judged by what they land on (`checkConsistency`, measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf295"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure reference law on the group element, outside the evaluation scope.

The two relative field references A12 declares on a GROUP. No lock covered either, and the portable checker named both in every report as members it did not resolve.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| the member ABSENT | ADMITTED — an index is optional |
| a bare name of one of the group's own FIELDS, plainly typed | ADMITTED |
| blank, whitespace, or any bare name that is not one of them | **NOT BUILDABLE** |
| a bare name of a child GROUP | **NOT BUILDABLE** |
| a spelling that RESOLVES to a field outside the group — `../Label`, or `Items/Sku` read one level up | `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` / `MVK_INVALID_SORT_FIELD` |
| a spelling that resolves to nothing — `Items/Sku` read from inside `Items` | **NOT BUILDABLE** |
| an ABSOLUTE path, on EITHER member | **raised untyped** — `ElementPathUtils.splitRelPath`, "illegal relPath" |
| a `..` climbing past the root | **NOT BUILDABLE** — it can reach no field, the model root holding groups |
| a direct-child field declared `noValueValidation` | `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION` / `MVK_SORT_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION` |
| a `sortFields` entry with no `name` | **UNREADABLE** |
| a `sortFields` entry whose `name` is a NUMBER | **NOT BUILDABLE** — coerced to the name `"5"`, which resolves to nothing |

**TWO gates, and the second reads a NAME rather than a position.** A12 resolves the spelling positionally from the group; one that does not land on a field stops the model from being BUILT. One that does land keeps only that field's SHORT NAME, and the group must then carry a field of that name — otherwise the member's own code.

**Corrected 2026-09-12, before the first consumer shipped:** this entry first said "resolves positionally, then judges what it landed on", with the `Items/Sku` pair cited as its discriminator. That pair refutes *"`..` is the special ingredient"* and nothing more — both accounts predict it identically. The case that separates them is a short name living at TWO levels, which no fixture here had: with `/Order/Sku` present, `../Sku` written in `/Order/Items` lands OUTSIDE the group and A12 **admits** the model, because `/Order/Items` carries a `Sku` of its own. A checker judging the landing rejects a model the Kernel takes. The rows above are unchanged; the mechanism they were read as supporting was not one of them.

| the separating row | A12 |
|---|---|
| `../Sku` from `/Order/Items`, with `/Order/Sku` declared | ADMITTED |
| the same, as a `sortFields` name | ADMITTED |
| `../Sku` from `/Order/Items`, with NO `/Order/Sku` | **NOT BUILDABLE** — it lands on nothing, so it never reaches the second gate |
| `../Label` from `/Order/Items`, with `/Order/Sku` declared | `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` — the NAME decides, not the duplication |

**And passing both gates is still not sufficient: the landed field's own TYPE is gated.** A `noValueValidation` string draws `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION`, and as a sort field `MVK_SORT_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION`, even as a direct child of its group. Every admitted row above names a plain value-validating string, so "a field of this group" and "a field A12 will accept as a key" were one predicate across the whole set. *(Amended 2026-09-12: this said the table-enum gate beside it, `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_NO_TABLE_ENUM`, was unmeasured. It is now measured and DEAD for A12 input — the shape it rejects cannot be read at all — and the whole type gate, including the index/sort asymmetry in its source, is enumerated in [KF296](#kf296).)*

**An ABSENT member is legal and a BLANK one is fatal**, which inverts the blank-counts-as-absent law three sibling slots follow ([KF290](#kf290), [KF291](#kf291)) and does so in the harshest direction available.

**The check runs on every group, not only a repeatable one.** An unresolvable index on a non-repeatable group is refused just the same, so "the index is only checked where it is used" is false — and that row is the one that keeps the others from being read that way.

**The two members do NOT share a code.** `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` is named for the index and `MVK_INVALID_SORT_FIELD` for the sort; the outside-the-group row was measured on each rather than transferred from the other.

**The absolute spelling is a third member of [KF259](#kf259)'s class** — the Kernel rejects an invalid input by raising past every typed channel, so a caller that does not catch it publishes an internal-defect envelope for what is really a rejection. `KernelLaws.verdictOf` now has a fourth tier (`RAISED (untyped)`) so a row landing there is visible as a finding rather than blowing up a table.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupIndexAndSortReferenceLawsTest` — one assertion per member.)*

## §10 supplement — the ordering members' TYPE gate: a pair of live codes, and one that no stored A12 model can reach (`checkConsistency`, measured + source-verified, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf296"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure law on the group element, outside the evaluation scope.

[KF295](#kf295) established that a group's `indexFieldName` / `sortFields[].name` must resolve to one of the group's own fields, and noted that the landed field's own TYPE is gated beyond that. This entry enumerates that gate, because "the type is gated too" turned out to name three source branches of which only two can fire.

**`NoMetaModelChecks.checkIndexField` runs three gates and returns at the first that fires**, so a type verdict is only ever reached by a reference that already resolved — the two verdicts are exclusive, never cumulative:

| # | gate | code |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `EntityUtils.getEntityInGroup` finds nothing, or finds a non-field | `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` |
| 2 | `FieldUtils.isNoValueValidation(indexField)` | `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION` |
| 3 | `FieldUtils.isTableEnum(indexField.getType())` | `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_NO_TABLE_ENUM` — **unreachable, see below** |

`checkSortField` carries gates 1 and 2 only, with **no table-enumeration gate at all**. That asymmetry is real in source and turns out not to matter, because gate 3 cannot fire either.

**The predicate reads the flag only after deciding the type IS a string.** `isNoValueValidation(f)` is `isString(f) && ((IStringType) f.getType()).isNoValueValidation()`, so the same flag carried by any other type is not this law — which is why a checker keying on the flag alone, rather than on a `StringType` body carrying it, would be wider than its basis.

**Gate 3 is dead for A12 input, and the four links were attacked separately rather than inferred from one another:**

| link | what settles it |
|---|---|
| the stored shape | **measured**: a `tableName` inside an `EnumerationType` body makes the reader refuse the model outright (UNREADABLE), on both members. `md.model.a12internal.fieldtypes.EnumerationType` declares `values`, `categories`, `errorMessage`, `alphabeticalSorting` and `sValue` — no table member exists to bind |
| the construction path | `TypeConverter.convertEnumeration` returns `new EnumerationTypeImpl(errorMessages, values, categoryValues, xmlValues, sValue)`; the constructor takes no table argument, so no caller could supply one |
| the accessor | `EnumerationTypeImpl.getTableName()` returns `Optional.empty()` unconditionally — no branch, no field behind it |
| the denominator | 23 files import `core.tool.a12internal.api.ado.IEnumerationType`; exactly **one** implements it, that same class. `CodeGenEnumerationTypeImpl` extends `CodeGenFeldTypBasis` and DELEGATES to an enumeration rather than implementing the interface, and `EnumerationTypeWrapper` implements the identically-named `md.model.api.fieldtypes.IEnumerationType` — a different interface in a different layer, which never reaches `FieldUtils` |

**The last link is the one worth carrying forward: two interfaces named `IEnumerationType` live in different layers, and only one of them is the one the check reads.** A search for the name returns both, and the wrapper is the more plausible-looking answer — it is the a12internal one, it is a real binding of the stored model, and it is wrong. This is the layer collision DOC-DISCIPLINE's golden rule warns about, met in the wild: a basis that just says "IEnumerationType" is ambiguous, and picking the wrong one here would have produced a confident claim that the gate is live.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupOrderingFieldTypeLawsTest` — the live pair on both members, and the reader's refusal of the table reference. The checker's own family is `CheckFamily.GROUP_ORDERING_FIELD_TYPE`.)*

## §11 supplement — a computation's `roundingMode` and its alternatives' `toleranceRangeOp` are ONE gate, and the mode is never wrong by itself (`checkConsistency`, measured + source-verified, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf297"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure law on the computation element, outside the evaluation scope.

Two stored members that look independent and are the two conjuncts of one kernel gate. Both are plain `String` in the stored model and both are bound to a closed set one layer down, so neither is refused while the source is READ and either can stop the model being BUILT afterwards.

**The admitted spellings are A12's INTERNAL values, matched exactly.** `roundingMode` takes `Exact`, `RoundUp`, `RoundDown` (`IBaseCalculationService.RoundingMode`, whose `getByInternalValue` compares with `equals` and ends in `orElseThrow`); `toleranceRangeOp` takes `DiffersWithToleranceRange1`, `2`, `5` and `10` (`md.model.a12internal.Computation.TR1`…`TR10`, switched in `ComputationAlternativesJoiner.determineLocalizedToleranceRangeOp`, whose `default ->` throws). Neither a constant NAME (`ROUND_UP`, `TR1`) nor a different letter case is a spelling of anything, and a number is coerced to the String member and then fails the set exactly as an unknown word does.

**The gate is `cmpOp == NE && roundingMode != EXACT`** (`core.calc.internal.util.NormalisierteBerechnungsFormHelper:326`), and an alternative's band is what chooses that `cmpOp`: absent gives `!=`, a band gives the tolerance operator. So `MVK_ERROR_WRONG_ROUNDING_MODE` is a judgement about a PAIR — its message says so outright ("When using exact calculation comparisons only the rounding mode 'exact' is allowed", `kernel-core-calc` `error_messages_en.properties:23`) — and the same `RoundUp` that is refused against a strict comparison is ADMITTED against a tolerance band. A client that refused the mode on sight would reject a model A12 accepts.

**The gate is owed by EVERY alternative, not by the computation.** The mode is declared once and each alternative carries its own band, so one unbanded alternative among banded ones refuses the whole computation — measured in either position on a two-alternative carrier, because a single-alternative model cannot tell "the computation's comparison" from "each alternative's comparison".

**An explicit `null` is ABSENCE on both members, which inverts the law the neighbouring rule slots follow.** A rule's `errorCode`, `severity`, `errorCondition` and `errorEntityRelPath` are each refused by A12's READER when spelled `null` ([KF291](#kf291)); these two are read through `Optional.ofNullable` accessors and simply take their default — an absent mode is `Exact` and an absent band is the strict comparison. Only a JSON container refuses the reader here.

**The tier is NOT [KF259](#kf259)'s untyped raise, and the layer that decides that is ours.** Both throws escape every typed kernel channel exactly as the source reads, and `adapter.KernelModelPreparation.notifications()` catches them around `checkConsistency` and re-raises a codeless consistency exception — KF259's fix doing its job. Worth stating because a source read of the kernel alone predicts `RAISED (untyped)` and is wrong about where the value lands: the composition, not the read, settles the tier.

**Consequence for the MVK ledger.** `MVK_ERROR_WRONG_ROUNDING_MODE` was bucketed `erased` on the reason "kernel-generated, unreachable from rulekit". The bucket survives — no `roundingMode` exists anywhere in the Java authoring surface, so the typed API genuinely cannot express it — but the reason was a mechanism claim and it is wrong: the mode is an AUTHORED member of the stored model, and the comparison the kernel generates is generated *from* the authored band. This is the failure mode [KF182](#kf182) named, an unrepresentability argument identifying the wrong shape, and it is the second row of the `erased` bucket to fall to the systematic pass the ledger says is still owed.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationRoundingModeLawsTest` — the two spelling tables, the 2×2 pair grid, and the two-alternative carrier. The checker's own family is `CheckFamily.COMPUTATION_ROUNDING`.)*

## §11 supplement — `errorCodesToSuppress` is rendered into a ONE-argument pragma, so the list is single-valued (`checkConsistency`, measured + source-verified, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf298"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure law on the computation element, outside the evaluation scope.

A computation's `errorCodesToSuppress` is declared `List<String>` and is not a set A12 inspects: `ComputationAlternativesJoiner.createPreamble` builds `String.format("@SuppressWarning(%s)\n", String.join(",", errorCodesToSuppress))` and prefixes the generated rule condition with it, so the member is TEXT that A12's own condition parser then reads back. Every row below follows from that rendering and from nothing else, which is why reading the member as a collection gets it wrong.

**A second entry is a PARSE error whatever it spells.** The pragma takes one code, so two entries render `@SuppressWarning(a,b)` and draw `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`. The discriminating control carries the SUPPORTED code **twice** and fails identically to one supported plus one bogus — so validity explains nothing and the comma is the defect. A blank entry renders `@SuppressWarning()` and a numeric entry `@SuppressWarning(7)`, both the same failure. A plural-looking member is therefore single-valued in practice, and a checker treating it as a set would admit lists A12 refuses.

**Only `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` is suppressible**, and any other spelling draws `MVK_INVALID_SUPPRESSED_WARNING` with the offending code echoed in the message — so a reader lifting every `MVK_*` token from that message sees two, the second being the verdict ([MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) recorded the echo on 2026-07-30).

**This CLEARS a client-side refusal rather than finding one, which was not the expected direction.** `Computation.Builder.errorCodesToSuppress` throws for any code outside that single-member allowlist, and a client-side refusal may never be broader than its measured basis. A12 refuses the same set, so the allowlist is audited and stands.

**The two routes to this pragma are different carriers and only one was previously measured.** [DirectiveLawsTest](../src/test/java/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/rulekit/validate/laws/DirectiveLawsTest.java) locks the INLINE form written into a rule's condition text; this entry measures the STRUCTURED member on a computation, which A12 renders into the same directive. A ledger note saying rulekit never authors the directive is true of the inline text and not of the member.

**An explicit `null` refuses the READER**, where the rounding pair beside it takes `null` as absence ([KF297](#kf297)): this member is bound `@NonNull List<String>` rather than through an `Optional` accessor, so the tier is a property of the binding and not of DM-JSON. A bare string and an object are refused too; a numeric ELEMENT is coerced into the list and then fails in the pragma.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationSuppressionLawsTest`. The checker's own family is `CheckFamily.SUPPRESSED_WARNINGS`.)*

## §13 supplement — an `ONLY` variant filter removes a declaration from `checkConsistency` entirely, so a BROKEN rule or computation is reported clean (measured 2×2 on both carriers + source-verified, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf299"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure law on the rule element, outside the evaluation scope.

**A rule carrying `variantFilter.filterType = ONLY` is not checked at all.** The same rule with a deliberately unresolvable condition is refused with `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` when it carries no filter, and ADMITTED when it carries `ONLY`. A12 reports no finding, no warning and no code: the model comes back clean.

**The filter TYPE alone decides; the named variants are irrelevant.** Measured as a within-model 2×2 over `{ONLY, ALL_EXCEPT} × {"premium", ""}`, one broken rule, one variable per cell:

| filter | is the broken rule caught? |
|---|---|
| `ONLY ["premium"]` | **no** — ADMITTED |
| `ONLY [""]` | **no** — ADMITTED, though `""` names the default variant itself |
| `ALL_EXCEPT ["premium"]` | yes — `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| `ALL_EXCEPT [""]` | yes — `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |

**Two rival accounts were killed by that grid, and both had survived an earlier version of it.** "A filter merely being present suppresses" dies on the `ALL_EXCEPT` row; "the declaration must belong to the DEFAULT variant" dies on `ONLY [""]`, which names the default variant and is still unchecked. Only the filter type survives. The controls that make the cells readable are a sound rule (admitted either way — liveness) and the same broken rule unfiltered (refused — the break is detectable).

**The source says the same thing and says it to a logger.** `consistency.rules.CodeGenerationRule.checkModel` generates validation code for the default variant, and where `extractUsedVariants(model)` is non-empty it calls `LOG.warn("The given document model {} contains variants. A complete check was done only for the default variant (empty string). Therefore, the check may not be complete.")`. It never calls the problem reporter, and a grep for an `MVK_*` variant code returns nothing — so the incompleteness is real, known upstream, and structurally invisible to every API consumer.

**What this costs us, stated plainly: a clean `checkConsistency` verdict on a model with `ONLY`-filtered declarations is not a clean bill of health**, and that is inherited by everything built on it — `model check`, the F4 oracle, and any report this project publishes. It is not a defect we can fix by checking harder: A12 *accepts* such a model, so reporting an ERROR for the excluded declaration would reject what A12 accepts, which is the one direction a checker must never take. The portable checker's answer is therefore a COVERAGE GAP naming the declaration, which is the honest statement — no verdict about it exists on either side — and the structural counterpart of the Kernel's log line.

**Shape rows, measured on the same carrier.** An unknown `filterType` and a non-object member are UNREADABLE; a missing `filterType` is NOT BUILDABLE (the member is `@NonNull` with no default, so it fails at construction rather than at read); an explicit `null`, an empty `variants` list and a missing `variants` member are all ADMITTED — so `IVariantFilter.getVariants`'s "never null or empty" javadoc is a contract on the accessor, not a law the reader enforces.

**Extended 2026-09-12: the COMPUTATION carrier behaves identically, measured rather than inherited.** The account above is stated at the model level and names no declaration kind, which is precisely why it was not allowed to transfer on its own — the same 2×2 and the same two controls were re-run with a computation whose `operation` names a field that exists nowhere, and every cell matches the rule carrier: `ONLY` (either variant spelling) ADMITTED, `ALL_EXCEPT` (either) `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`, the unfiltered broken computation refused so the ADMITTED rows are not vacuous. The shape rows match too. So the filter type alone decides on both carriers, and the checker's coverage gap covers both. *(The cell count is deliberately not written here: `ComputationVariantFilterLawsTest` is the denominator and grew from 16 cells to 18 on 2026-09-12 while a prose count beside it said sixteen.)*

**Extended 2026-09-13: group PLACEMENT was moving with the carrier, and it does not matter.** The two carrier grids compared a rule at `/Subscription` with a computation at `/Subscription/Billing` — forced by the fixture, since the computed field lives under `Billing` — so declaration kind and group placement changed together and every cell agreeing was consistent with a placement dependence nobody had excluded. Re-running the grid's four discriminating cells with a RULE at the computation's own group gives the same four verdicts as the rule at the root group: sound ADMITTED, broken unfiltered `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`, broken under `ONLY` ADMITTED, broken under `ALL_EXCEPT premium` still `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`. The carrier comparison is therefore within one group, and placement is not a variable in this law.

**Extended 2026-09-12: WHICH KINDS of break the filter hides — it hides every verdict, and the exception is the one a checker must be built around.** The rows above all break the same thing, a condition naming a missing entity, so they establish that `ONLY` suppresses *something* and say nothing about *how much*. Seven breaks were therefore run on one rule, each unfiltered (proving it is detectable) and under `ONLY`:

| break | unfiltered | under `ONLY` |
|---|---|---|
| condition names no entity | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` | **ADMITTED** |
| condition cannot be parsed (`FieldFilled(Tier`) | `MVK_EXPECTED_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND` | **ADMITTED** |
| condition ends early (`FieldFilled(Tier) And`) | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` | **ADMITTED** |
| condition cannot be tokenized | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` | **ADMITTED** |
| error target names no field | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING`,`MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD` | **ADMITTED** |
| no error message at all | `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` | **ADMITTED** |
| **empty error code** | `MVK_ERROR_CODE_MISSING` | **REFUSED, codeless** — a verdict carrying no `MVK_*` code ([re-tiered 2026-09-15](#kf420); it read as NOT BUILDABLE while the harness collapsed the two codeless tiers) |
| `errorCode` is JSON `null` | UNREADABLE | UNREADABLE |
| message locale the reader refuses | UNREADABLE | UNREADABLE |

**Three predictions were wrong here, all in the same direction**: the declaration's own slots — its error code, its messages, its target — were expected to stay judged, on the theory that a consistency rule reading them never consults variants. They do not. So there is no surviving subset of a filtered declaration that a checker could go on judging, and suppressing one family rather than the whole declaration would still over-reject.

**The line the last three rows draw is what the checker is built on: a filter suppresses what A12 would SAY ABOUT a declaration, and cannot rescue a model that fails to BUILD.** An empty `errorCode` still refuses the model under `ONLY` — and refuses it *without* the code it carries unfiltered, so reproducing `MVK_ERROR_CODE_MISSING` there would be wrong twice over. The two UNREADABLE rows generalize it: A12's reader runs a tier before any variant logic, so a shape it refuses is refused whatever the filter says. Hence the portable checker suppresses every finding on a filtered declaration *except* the ones saying the model does not load.

**`variantFilter` also rides FIELD elements** (`serializer.FieldSerializer` writes it), a carrier outside this checker's rules-and-computations subject matter and not measured here.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleVariantFilterLawsTest` and `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationVariantFilterLawsTest`.)*

## §13 supplement — a condition that does not parse draws one of FOUR phase-specific codes, and `MVK_CONDITION` is none of them (measured, 2026-09-12) <a id="kf300"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a parse-surface law, outside the evaluation scope.

**What `checkConsistency` returns for a stored `errorCondition` that is present, non-blank, and malformed.** Every one of eight predictions for this grid said `MVK_CONDITION`, and all seven malformed rows were wrong. The codes track the ANTLR pipeline phase that failed:

| condition text | code |
|---|---|
| `FieldFilled("Tier)` — unclosed string literal | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `@@@` — stray punctuation | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `NotAnOperator(Tier)` — unknown name used as a call | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `FeldAngegeben(Tier)` — a German keyword in an English model | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `Tier` — a bare field reference as the whole condition | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier` — unclosed argument list | `MVK_EXPECTED_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier) And` — trailing infix operator | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` |

**Where the wrong prediction came from, because it is a reusable trap.** [MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md)'s `MVK_CONDITION` row says "for raw-DSL inputs the kernel's parse error is the intended contract" — a statement about *rulekit's authoring surface*, which reads as an answer about what the Kernel REPORTS. It is the narrow-prior-art shape: the record answers confidently and on-topic, and answers a different question. The neighbouring laws class is the same shape one layer down — `RuleConditionAndTargetSlotLawsTest` measures the slot's PRESENCE (absent, empty, whitespace → `MVK_CONDITION_MISSING`), so a grep for condition laws returns it and reads as coverage while the syntax axis is untouched.

**The three rows that decide FAMILY OWNERSHIP, and they all land on the parse side.** An unknown name, a foreign-language keyword, and a bare field reference are each `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` rather than a reference diagnostic — so an unresolvable name never reaches the reference check at all. A checker that reported one of them as an unresolvable reference would name the wrong defect, and one that reported it from both families would report it twice.

**These six codes live in a RESOURCE BUNDLE the ledger was blind to** — `kernel-core-parser`'s `internal/vk_parser_common_error_messages/error_messages_en.properties`, not `ParserErrorTypesEnum` (176 constants, none of them these). *(Corrected 2026-09-12: this read "not in any enum". They ARE in one — `CommonParserErrorTypesEnum`, same jar, one package over from the enum that was searched, declaring exactly these six. The sentence was an enumeration over a single enum published as an enumeration over all of them, which is the completeness failure this findings file names in its own oracle table. Both artifacts are now read by `MvkLedgerTest`, so the section is checked twice and they must agree.)* `MvkLedgerTest` therefore reported the ledger complete while all six were missing, because its denominator was three enums plus the metamodel. The bundle ships inside the kernel jar, so it is now a fifth source read from the test classpath, and the six codes have ledger rows; the two that no authored input has been found to reach are classified **unmeasured** rather than by analogy.

**Extended 2026-09-12 — the delimiter grid, which decides what a checker can report WITHOUT a grammar.** Only the shape that runs out of input draws `MVK_EXPECTED_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND`; every other imbalance draws `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`, because the parser meets a token that is wrong where it stands before the input ends.

| condition text | code |
|---|---|
| `FieldFilled(Tier` — everything still open at end of input | `MVK_EXPECTED_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier))` — an extra closing parenthesis | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `FieldFilled([Tier)` — an unclosed value bracket | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier]` — a bracket closing a parenthesis | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier)]` — a stray closing bracket | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |

The consequence is a negative result worth as much as a positive one: **the distinction is positional, not arithmetic**, so counting delimiters detects an imbalance but cannot pick which of the two codes A12 gives — it would be wrong on three of these five. A planned checker increment that would have reported delimiter balance without a grammar was withdrawn on this grid.

**Extended 2026-09-12 — the trailing-operator grid, and the RETRACTION it forced.** Measured first: a condition ending on `And`, `Or`, a comparison, arithmetic, or a comma all draw `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`, while `FieldFilled([Tier ->` and `FieldFilled([Tier For` draw `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`. That was read as the operator catalog's `OPERATOR`/`PATH_OP` split tracking A12's parse behaviour, so a checker could pick the code from the kind column while looking at nothing before the last token. **It is false in both directions, and one character shows it:**

| condition text | code | the retracted account predicted |
|---|---|---|
| `FieldFilled([Tier For` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` | ✓ — the only row it was built on |
| `FieldFilled(Tier For` — one bracket fewer | **`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`** | ✗ |
| `[Tier For` / `[Tier ->` | **`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`** | ✗ |
| `FieldFilled(Tier And` | **`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`** | ✗ |
| `FieldFilled([Tier) And` | **`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`** | ✗ |
| `RepetitionNotUnique(Addons*/Name @From` | **`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`** | ✗ — a `PATH_OP` |
| `NumberOfFilledFields(Addons*/Name Having` | **`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`** | ✗ — a `PATH_OP` |

**The variable is an unclosed delimiter earlier in the text, not the keyword's kind** — a fact about what comes BEFORE the last token, which is exactly what the account denied could matter. It was built on a single table member (`For`; `->` is punctuation and not a keyword at all) and generalized to a three-member kind whose other two members behave the opposite way. Textbook scope transfer: the reuse needed no new branch, so nothing prompted the question.

**What survives is a negative result, and it is the useful half**: which parse code a truncated condition draws depends on the parser's state, so no last-token rule can pick it — the same conclusion the delimiter grid above reached from the other side. The portable checker's completeness family therefore reports only where the text is delimiter-balanced at the trailing operator, which is a boundary drawn around the measured rows and explicitly not a mechanism; everywhere else it is silent, which under-reports and is the safe direction. Before the narrowing it answered `FieldFilled(Tier And` with `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`, where A12 says `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`.

**Extended 2026-09-12 — the FULL trailing-token set, because a client-side refusal may not be broader than its measured basis.** The checker refuses on eleven symbolic operators and on the catalog's whole `OPERATOR` kind, where two symbols and two keywords had rows. Measured on a single balanced base (`[Tier] <token>`), one variable per row:

| trailing token | code |
|---|---|
| `==` `!=` `<=` `>=` `<` `>` `+` `*` `^` `-` `/` — all eleven | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` |
| `And` `AND` `and` `Or` `OR` `or` | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` |
| `PatternMatched`, `DiffersWithToleranceRange1` | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` |
| `In` `IN` `in` `To` `TO` `to` | **`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`** |

Three things fall out. **The `OPERATOR` kind does generalize** — the two catalog operators beyond `And`/`Or` behave alike, so keying on the kind column is safe after all, which the `PATH_OP` half was not. **`*` is fine** despite also being the repetition marker, and `-`/`/` are `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` too — the tokenizer files them as punctuation because each is also a path shape, which had silently excluded them from a family whose own documentation claimed every arithmetic symbol. **`In` and `To` are not in this class in any spelling**, so the checker's silence about them — a side effect of the generated table filing them as uncataloged — is the right answer rather than a lucky one.

*(The first attempt at this grid used `[Tier] > 1 <token>` and returned `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` on six rows: the base text was itself a type error, so the grid moved two variables. Recorded because it is the same control failure this file warns about, caught only by the codes being implausible.)*

**Still unreported, and disclosed on every report rather than left silent:** the case variants `AND`/`and`/`ODER` ARE `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` and the checker misses them, because the generated keyword table carries one canonical spelling per operator and files the kernel's other terminals as uncataloged. That is a shape problem in the table, not a judgement about the text, and it under-reports — the safe direction.

**Extended 2026-09-12 — an unterminated string literal is not ONE class, and the row that locked it was confounded.** The lock's Java literal was `verdict("FieldFilled(\\\"Tier)")`, i.e. a BACKSLASH and a quote, while the table beside it printed `FieldFilled("Tier)`. Both draw the same code — a backslash alone does too, and that now has its own row — so the confound was invisible; the lock now carries the text the table prints. More substantially, which error A12 reports depends on where the PARSER is:

| condition text | code |
|---|---|
| `[Tier] == "abc` — unterminated at the end of balanced text | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled("abc` — unterminated at the end, inside an unclosed call | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `[Billing/InvoiceEmail] == "abc" And FieldFilled("x` — after an earlier COMPLETE literal | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled("x) And [Tier] == "abc"` — the literal swallows the call's closer | **`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`** |

The last row's first literal runs to the next quote, eating the `)` the grammar was waiting for, so the parser fails before the lexer does. **No grammar-free rule separates it from the third row** — quote counts are odd in both, both carry an earlier complete literal, both leave a delimiter open — so the portable checker keeps reporting the lexical failure there and carries a gap saying the code is wrong for that shape. That is deliberately the opposite treatment from the completeness family above, where a measured boundary existed and the family was narrowed to it; here inventing one would be a fourth mechanism on this layer in one day.

**Extended 2026-09-13 — the OTHER quoting form, which had no row at all.** A `'…'` name is A12's escape for a field whose name spells a keyword (`NameOhnePunktMitQuotes: '\'' STR (STR|DIGIT)* '\''`). Three shapes fail that terminal and all three draw the same code, so nothing finer needs distinguishing:

| condition text | code |
|---|---|
| `FieldFilled('Tier` — unclosed at the end | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled('Tier) And FieldFilled(Tier)` — unclosed with structure after it | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled('')` — CLOSED but empty | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled('1City')` — CLOSED but digit-leading | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled('Tier')` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `FieldFilled('And') Or FieldFilled(Tier)` — the escape doing its job | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` — a SEMANTIC code, so `'And'` reached entity resolution instead of being read as the connective |
| `FieldFilled(Tier)) And 'x` — a parse error EARLIER than the bad quote | **`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`** |

The last row generalizes the string-literal result above rather than repeating it: the lexer does not get the first word, so an unpaired quote of EITHER form loses to a parse error that sits earlier. The checker therefore carries one gap covering both terminals. The two closed-but-illegal rows matter because a checker has to decide whether to flag them, and a flag it invented would be an unmeasured refusal — measured, they are refused, and the terminal's `STR` fragment (`a-z A-Z _ Ä Ü Ö ä ü ö ß :`) is reproduced exactly by the checker's tokenizer, so it cannot over-reject a name A12 takes.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleConditionSyntaxLawsTest` (the grids above, with a valid-condition liveness control, and `whetherTheLastTokenAloneCanDecideTheCode` carrying the refutation with two positive controls showing the truncated texts are truncations of text that parses) and `MvkLedgerTest.ledgerCoversTheParserMessageBundleExactly` (the source that was missing, with an empty-denominator control so a bundle that resolved but carried nothing could not pass vacuously).

## §1 supplement — one bracket level joins ANY number of parts, and the `And`/`Or` mixing refusal is a parser ACTION scoped to a bracket PAIR, not a depth (measured + source-verified, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf301"></a>

> Fold: pending — the arity half belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §1's existing explicit-parentheses law, which states the mixing half already.

**Why this was measured before a condition parser was written.** [GRAMMAR-LEDGER](GRAMMAR-LEDGER.md)'s `bedingung` row said "max three parts per bracket level", taken from the production's shape. A parser written from that inventory would have rejected a four-part chain A12 admits, which is the one direction a checker must never take.

**The arity claim is false.** All eight rows are admitted, including four parts joined by `And` and four joined by `Or`:

| condition | verdict |
|---|---|
| one part — the liveness control | ADMITTED |
| two, three, FOUR parts joined by `And` | ADMITTED |
| two, three, FOUR parts joined by `Or` | ADMITTED |
| four parts split across two bracket levels | ADMITTED |

**Where the wrong reading came from.** The production is `teilBedingung (l1=logOp teilBedingung (l2=logOp teilBedingung {this.checkBedingung(_localctx);})*)?` — the inner group is STARRED, so the parts are unbounded, and the two labels exist so the parser's semantic ACTION can compare connectives, not to bound their number. Reading a label as a cardinality is the trap: the grammar shape carries the check's operands, not the language's arity.

**The mixing half is real, has its own code, and is NOT "both spellings appear in the text".** An unparenthesised mix draws `MVK_BRACKET_MISSING` — A12 refuses to guess a precedence rather than applying one silently, which is the better of the two possible answers: had it ACCEPTED the mix it would also have had a precedence, and a checker that guessed differently would build a different tree for text both accept, a divergence no accept/reject test can see. Five rows carrying BOTH spellings at different levels are admitted (`(A And B) Or C`, `A And (B Or C)`, both sides grouped, a grouped `Or` inside an `And` chain, two levels deep), so a check that looked for both spellings anywhere would reject five conditions A12 accepts.

**A level is a bracket PAIR, not a depth — the row that separates the obvious implementation from the correct one.** Two sibling calls one parenthesis deep, one filter carrying `And` and the other `Or`, joined at the outer level by `Or`, are ADMITTED; the same pair with the OUTER level mixed still draws `MVK_BRACKET_MISSING`, so the check is live on that text rather than switched off by the filters. A checker keyed on a depth COUNTER would record "depth 1 has seen both spellings" and over-reject. A call's parentheses likewise open their own level: `And` inside a `Having` filter with `Or` outside it is ADMITTED.

**The mechanism, source-verified and consistent with every row above.** `CheckBedingungImpl.check` compares `ctx.l1` with `ctx.l2` and throws `MVK_BRACKET_MISSING` when exactly one of them is `Und`; `l1` binds once outside the loop while `l2` rebinds per iteration, so every connective after the first is compared against the first. The check therefore runs per `bedingung` CONTEXT, and exactly three productions open one — the entry rule, `geklammerteBedingung: '(' bedingung ')'`, and the entity filter's `'Mit' filterCond=bedingung`. That is why both a grouping pair and a filter reset the comparison, and why two sibling pairs do not see each other. *(The equivalent-detection caveat: comparing every connective against the first and comparing adjacent pairs both fire at the first switch, so these rows do not discriminate between them; what is source-verified is the operand pair the kernel actually compares, not a behaviour a grid could separate.)*

**What this buys the portable checker.** A same-level `And`/`Or` mix is reportable from tokens alone — a bracket-pair stack is something the tokenizer already supports — and it is the first condition-syntax rule measured here that is NOT defeated by parser state, unlike the delimiter and trailing-token grids of [KF300](#kf300), which both ended in negative results. The discriminating cases those two grids do not cover are the five level-separated admissions and the sibling-pair row: each rejects a plausible cheap implementation (both-spellings-anywhere, depth-counter) that neither earlier grid touches.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleConditionCompositionLawsTest` (four grids: arity with a one-part liveness control, mixing with the five level-separated admissions, a call's parentheses with a filter-parses control, and the sibling-pair row with a mixed-outer-level control). The portable side is `consistency`'s `ConnectiveAgreementTest`, which reproduces the admissions as well as the refusals and pins the four connective spellings against the generated keyword table.

## §1 supplement — A12 admits five infix arithmetic symbols in a condition, and `^` refuses a FIELD exponent semantically rather than syntactically (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf302"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §1's expression law, which names arithmetic without enumerating the symbols.

**Why this was measured: a mutation check found a parser widening nothing in the estate reached.** The portable checker's parser admits `+ - * / ^` between two operands. Removing `/` from that set left every test green — the generated catalog corpus carries `+`, `-` and `*` and no population carries a division or an exponent, so two of the five rested on [GRAMMAR-LEDGER](GRAMMAR-LEDGER.md)'s `operation` row rather than on a measurement. Widening is the safe direction for a checker, but an unmeasured widening is a guess, and a guess nothing exercises cannot be told from dead code.

| condition, on two NUMBER fields of one group | verdict |
|---|---|
| `[BaseFee] > 1` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `[BaseFee] + [EffectiveFee] > 1` | ADMITTED |
| `[BaseFee] - [EffectiveFee] > 1` | ADMITTED |
| `[BaseFee] * [EffectiveFee] > 1` | ADMITTED |
| `[BaseFee] / [EffectiveFee] > 1` | ADMITTED |
| `[BaseFee] ^ [EffectiveFee] > 1` | `MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP` |
| `[BaseFee] ^ 2 > 1` | ADMITTED |
| `[BaseFee] % [EffectiveFee] > 1` — the liveness control | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |

**The `^` pair is the row that matters, and one row alone would have been read backwards.** `MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP` is a SEMANTIC code, so the field-exponent text PARSED and was then refused for what its exponent is; taken alone it reads as "A12 rejects `^`" and would have argued for narrowing the parser. The literal row separates the two readings and settles it the other way: `^` is admitted, and only a non-literal exponent is not. A checker's parser therefore must accept both, because a parse-phase family that refused the field form would name the wrong defect for a text A12's own parser accepts.

**`%` is not an operator at any layer.** It fails in the LEXER, not the grammar, which is what makes it the grid's liveness control: it shows the probe can still produce a rejection, without which seven admissions cannot be told from a probe that admits everything.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ConditionArithmeticSymbolLawsTest` (one grid, one symbol apart on one carrier, with both a no-arithmetic control and the `%` liveness control). The portable side is `consistency`'s `ConditionShapeTest`, whose division and exponentiation rows are the controls that were missing when the mutants survived.

## §13 supplement — a rule's `guiPatterns` and `variantErrorMessages` are stored but never judged, and their two binding laws differ on exactly one row (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf303"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §13, which covers message interpolation and says nothing about the variant-specific map.

**These were the last two stored `Rule` members the portable checker did not read**, and both look from the outside like constrained vocabularies a checker ought to police. `Rule.guiPatterns` even documents its own closed vocabulary — "At the moment only following patterns are possible: key=`dynamicEnumeration`, value=`true`|`false`". **A12 enforces none of it.**

| stored shape | `guiPatterns` | `variantErrorMessages` |
|---|---|---|
| absent — the control | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| an empty map | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| a well-formed entry | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| a key outside the documented vocabulary | ADMITTED | ADMITTED (any variant name, the default's `""` included) |
| a value outside the documented vocabulary | ADMITTED | — |
| a scalar where the value type is richer | ADMITTED (boolean) | ADMITTED (string, number) |
| **a null VALUE** | **ADMITTED** | **RAISED (untyped)** |
| an object value | UNREADABLE | UNREADABLE |
| a list value | UNREADABLE | ADMITTED when its entries are well formed |
| an entry missing `locale`, or missing `text` | — | UNREADABLE |
| the member as an explicit null | UNREADABLE | UNREADABLE |
| the member as a list | UNREADABLE | UNREADABLE |

**The null-value row is why measuring one member would have shipped the other's law wrong.** The shapes are identical and the tiers are not even adjacent: `Map<String, String>` takes a null value, while `Map<String, ILocalizedTextMap>` is `@NonNull`-bound on its value and raises past every typed Kernel channel. A checker sharing one predicate between two members that look this alike is wrong on that row whichever direction it picks — the same trap the rounding pair set, one record earlier, and the reason the D denominator schedules members by topic rather than one at a time.

**`guiPatterns` has exactly one reader in the Kernel and it is the serializer.** *Searched:* `grep -rn 'getGuiPatterns' ../a12-kernel --include='*.java' | grep -v delombok` — six matches (`RuleSerializer` ×2, the delegating `RuleWrapper` ×2, the `Rule` javadoc, the `IRule` declaration), all six read. The dynamic-enumeration machinery that the documented key names does NOT consult it: `CodeGenMetaRulesBuilder` and `NoMetaModelChecks.checkDynamicEnumerations` both take their information from `data.getParams().getDynamicEnumerationInformation()`, a codegen parameter. The grid is what settles it, because who calls an accessor is a reachability claim and a source read alone does not settle those here.

**So the useful result is a NON-finding.** Translating that javadoc into a refusal is the obvious move and would reject models A12 admits, in the one direction a checker must never take. What remains checkable is only whether the reader can BIND the member, which is this checker's own `CK_MODEL_NOT_BUILDABLE` tier: an unloadable model that draws a clean report reads as a verdict.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleVariantPresentationLawsTest` (both grids, each with an absent control and the vocabulary rows that would be refused by a javadoc-faithful checker). The portable side is `consistency`'s `PresentationMembersTest` and `CheckFamily.RULE_PRESENTATION_MEMBERS`.

## §13 supplement — a JSON container in a string-bound member makes the model UNREADABLE, on every carrier (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf304"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §13, which describes what these members hold and not what happens when the stored shape is wrong.

**An object or an array where A12 declares a string refuses A12's reader outright — `UNREADABLE`, never a diagnostic.** Measured on all three carriers that own such a member: a rule's `errorCondition` and `errorEntityRelPath`, a computation alternative's `operation` and `precondition`, and a group's `indexFieldName`. Four container shapes each — `{}`, an object with content, `[]`, an array holding a string — and the answer is the same twenty times over. The mirror shape settles the array-typed member the same way: a group's `sortFields` holding an object, a string or a number is equally unreadable, so the binding is strict in both directions rather than merely intolerant of containers.

**Why measuring it mattered even though the answer is uniform.** The portable checker had carried a standing coverage gap on this whole class — "each is unmeasured, and under-reporting is the only safe direction" — and uniformity was not the safe guess: the sibling presentation members ([KF303](#kf303)) show one element's two adjacent maps landing in *different* tiers on the identical shape, and `variantErrorMessages` coerces a bare scalar into a slot typed for an array while refusing an object into that same slot. A checker generalising from either of those would have been wrong here. The result is that this class needs no per-member reading at all: one shape test serves every string-bound member, and the finding it produces is `CK_MODEL_NOT_BUILDABLE` rather than any `MVK_*`, because A12 never reaches the tier that issues codes.

**One control was dead on the first run, and it is the reason the grid keeps one per carrier.** The computation grid's control used a bare field name as the `operation`, which A12 answers with `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` — so that carrier's rows were briefly verdicts about a model already broken before the substitution. A literal (`42.00`) restores it. The rule and group grids predicted correctly on the first run; only the carrier whose control was dead looked like a finding.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.StringSlotContainerLawsTest` (three grids, one per carrier, each with a live control).

## §13 supplement — a FIELD's `ONLY` variant filter DELETES the field, where a rule's merely suppresses the rule (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf305"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §13, whose variant material covers the rule carrier only.

**`variantFilter` has exactly three carriers and the third behaves nothing like the other two.** *Searched:* `grep -rln variantFilter ../a12-kernel/kernel-md/kernel-md-serializer --include='*Serializer.java'` — three files (`FieldSerializer`, `RuleSerializer`, `ComputationSerializer`), all three read; there is no group carrier. On a rule or computation, `ONLY` makes A12 say nothing about that declaration ([KF299](#kf299)) — a suppression, so silence is the faithful response. On a FIELD it is not a suppression at all: `ValidationModelConverter` keeps a field only while `VariantFiltering.fieldIsAcceptedByFilter` accepts it, so a rejected field is **absent from the validation model**, and every declaration that names it is then naming something that does not exist.

**The discriminating row, with its control.** A rule targeting `/Subscription/AutoRenew` whose condition also mentions `Tier` is ADMITTED with `Tier` unfiltered, ADMITTED with `Tier` under `ALL_EXCEPT`, and draws **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** with `Tier` under `ONLY`. The `ALL_EXCEPT` row is the control that rules out the reference itself: same model, same mention, one filter type apart. A first attempt at this row was confounded — the probe rule *targeted* the filtered field as well as mentioning it, which answers with the error-target pair (`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING` beside `MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD`) and cannot separate the two roles. Both rows are kept, because together they show the answer follows the naming ROLE rather than the filter.

**The filter TYPE alone decides here too, and that was measured rather than inherited.** A checker keying on the type is claiming the `variants` list never matters, which is KF299's result on a *different* carrier. All three lists that could plausibly rescue the field — naming the default variant by empty string, an empty list, and no `variants` member at all — leave it deleted. The mechanism is visible in `filterAcceptsVariant`, which computes `variantMatchesFilter` under a `variant != null` guard, so at the default variant it is false for every list: `ALL_EXCEPT` returns its negation and accepts, `ONLY` returns it and rejects.

**The two unbindable shapes split by tier, as on the rule carrier.** An unknown `filterType` spelling is UNREADABLE — the reader refuses while binding the string — while an ABSENT `filterType` is NOT BUILDABLE, failing one step later as A12 constructs the model. Neither carries an `MVK_*`.

**Consequence for a portable checker:** resolving a reference against every declared field, filtered or not, UNDER-reports here — A12 rejects models it admits. That is the safe direction, so this is a capability gap rather than a defect; closing it means treating an `ONLY`-filtered field as undeclared during resolution, after which the existing role→code mapping already yields A12's own codes on both paths.

**The BINDING tier is uniform across carriers, and that is measured on each rather than inferred from one (added 2026-09-13).** An unknown `filterType`, a `filterType` that is JSON null, an object or a number, and a `variantFilter` that is not an object at all are UNREADABLE on a field exactly as on a rule; an absent member and an explicit `null` are ADMITTED on both, the member being reached through an `Optional` accessor. This is worth stating because the member's SEMANTIC law is carrier-specific — a rule's `ONLY` suppresses, a field's deletes — so uniformity anywhere else about `variantFilter` is a claim needing its own rows, and the field carrier's five binding rows are those rows.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldVariantFilterLawsTest` (two grids, each with an unfiltered and an `ALL_EXCEPT` control).

## §13 supplement — a connective's THREE lexer cases are judged alike, and a fourth case is a NAME (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf306"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §13, whose connective material assumes the canonical spelling throughout.

**A12's terminal bundle carries three spellings of each connective and treats them identically.** `And`, `AND` and `and` all join a condition (ADMITTED); all three refuse a mix with `Or` in any of ITS three cases (`MVK_BRACKET_MISSING`); and a text ending on any of them is unfinished (`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`). German is the same for `Und`/`UND`/`und` and `Oder`/`ODER`/`oder`. Which spellings exist was already settled by `ConditionKeywordProjectionTest`, which measures the generated table against the Kernel's bundle in both directions; what this adds is that A12 then JUDGES them alike, which no row had asked.

**The fourth case is the finding, and it lands on a different code on every grid.** `aNd` is not a terminal, so A12 reads it as an ordinary entity name: joining two conditions with it draws `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`, mixing with it draws `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`, and ending on it draws `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` rather than the incompleteness — because a trailing name leaves a COMPLETE condition followed by a stray token, not an unfinished one. A checker folding case would report an incompleteness where A12 reports a parse error, which is a wrong verdict rather than a safe silence.
