**So the portable rule is "any case the TABLE carries", never "case-insensitively".** The checker intersects a case-insensitive match with the generated terminal set, and the promotion reaches the connectives and nothing else — an enumeration, not a hope: of the spellings sharing a case-insensitive form, only `and`/`or` and `und`/`oder` have a member the operator catalog classifies, while `in` and `to` (`in`/`zu`) are uncataloged in all three cases.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ConnectiveCaseLawsTest` (three grids, each with a canonical control and the fourth-case row).

## §10 supplement — the `noValueValidation` flag is COERCED, so a JSON boolean is not what A12 requires (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf307"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §10, whose ordering-key material names the flag without saying how it binds.

**A12 binds this flag through a coercion, and the complete admitted set is narrow rather than lenient.** `true` and the string `"true"` SET it; `false`, the string `"false"` and the number `0` clear it; the numbers `1` and `2` set it, so any non-zero number does; an explicit `null` leaves it unset. A string that is neither boolean literal — `"yes"` — is **not** coerced to false: it refuses A12's reader outright, which is a different tier again. A checker reading the member as a strict JSON boolean therefore admits an ordering key A12 refuses, and that is what this repository's did for the numeric spellings until this row.

**The neighbouring TYPE shapes are settled at the same time, and two of them are unreadable rather than admitted.** An empty `fieldType` object carries no `type` discriminator, so the reader refuses. A `NumberType` carrying `noValueValidation` likewise refuses — the member is not declared on that binding at all, which raises the source reading of `isNoValueValidation()` being a `FormatDefinitionString` method into a measured fact: **there is no "same flag, other type" model for a checker to judge**, because such a model does not load. A plain `NumberType` as an ordering key is ADMITTED, so it is the flag that is refused and never the non-string type.

**Every coerced row trips a SECOND law with it.** `noValueValidation` without `lineBreaksPermitted` draws `MVK_STRING_TYPE_NO_VAL_AND_NO_LINE_BREAK` beside the ordering gate's own code, which is why those rows carry a pair. The existing single-code control sets both members, so it does not show this and could not have.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupOrderingFieldTypeLawsTest.theShapesAroundTheRefusedTypeAreAdmitted`; the portable side is `consistency`'s `GroupOrderingFieldTypeTest`.

## §10 supplement — the `fieldType` vocabulary is thirteen names, and only FIVE tolerate a missing body (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf308"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §10, which describes field types by what they mean and never by what makes one bind.

**The admitted set is derivable, which is what makes refusing an unknown spelling safe.** `FieldtypeDeserializer.deriveFieldtype` is a single `switch` over the `type` discriminator whose `default` raises, so the vocabulary is exactly `StringType`, `NumberType`, `DateType`, `DateTimeType`, `DateRangeType`, `DateFragmentType`, `EnumerationType`, `TimeType`, `TypeDefType`, `CustomFieldType`, `ConfirmType`, `BooleanType`, `UnspecifiedType` — thirteen, by construction rather than by survey. The `switch` is on the raw string, so it is case-SENSITIVE: `stringtype` falls to the raising default like any name the kernel does not declare.

**Five cases guard a missing body and eight dereference it behind a comment that says they need not.** `StringType`, `NumberType`, `ConfirmType`, `BooleanType` and `UnspecifiedType` read `if (typeNode == null) …builder().build()`; the other eight carry `// typeNode is never null` and read the node directly. A comment is not a guard, and the measurement confirms it: `{"type":"DateType"}` with no `DateType` body makes the source UNREADABLE, while `{"type":"StringType"}` binds — which the repository's own fixtures already relied on without anyone having measured the other half. The two grids are paired row for row against a `{}`-body control, so the only variable is whether the body member is written.

**THREE tiers, and the reading the deserializer alone suggests is wrong.** An absent `fieldType` member and an empty `fieldType` object both leave the field with no type, so "they are the same null" predicts one verdict — and they part: the empty object is UNREADABLE and the absent member is NOT BUILDABLE. What separates them is that `Field.fieldType` is Lombok `@NonNull`, so the SETTER raises; an empty object and an explicit `"fieldType":null` are both deserialized to null and then set, while an absent member never calls the setter and survives reading, to fail one tier later as A12 builds the model. All three rows move exactly as that account predicts and no other reading produces the split.

**An empty BODY is a fourth outcome again, and it is not a binding failure.** With `{}` written as the body, all thirteen bind; five then leave the model unbuildable because they construct from a member the empty body does not supply (`DateRangeType`, `DateFragmentType`, `EnumerationType`, `TypeDefType`, `CustomFieldType`), three build happily without a format (`DateType`, `DateTimeType`, `TimeType`), and `UnspecifiedType` binds, builds, and draws `MVK_UNSPECIFIED_TYPE_NO_CODEGEN` — the one row here that reaches a consistency verdict at all. A checker treating any of these as a reader refusal would report unreadability for a model A12 read perfectly well.

**A GROUP drops an undeclared member where a FIELD and a RULE refuse one** — measured while controlling the scope of the above, and a law about carriers rather than about `fieldType`. The identical unbindable fragment written onto a group is ignored and the model loads; onto a field or a rule it makes the source UNREADABLE. A member name that is nonsense on every carrier (`notAMemberA12Declares`, two spellings per carrier, so no single spelling can be the explanation) parts them exactly the same way, which is what separates "this member is read there" from "that carrier is strict". The denominator is three of the element kinds; the computation carrier is not measured, and the law claims nothing about it.

**A field with NO `fieldType` is not an untyped field — the model does not build (added 2026-09-13).** `Field.fieldType` is bound non-null with no default, so omitting the member leaves A12 reading the source and then failing to construct the model. Measured as a within-model pair on a field ADDED to the fixture for the purpose — same model, the member present against absent, nothing else varied — rather than by removing it from a field the fixture had already shaped. The distinction matters because the consequence is corpus-wide: any model whose fields omit the member is one A12 refuses to build.

**The five types an empty body defeats do NOT need the members a source read predicts (added 2026-09-13).** Supplying each type's `@NonNull` member is enough for `DateFragmentType` (`formatOfFragment`) and `CustomFieldType` (`name`), and `EnumerationType` builds from one value even though its `values` field carries a default and so should never have failed empty. Two rows part from the prediction outright: `DateRangeType` with only its `@NonNull` `format` is still refused — the `rangeSeparator` default in the kernel's own declaration does not survive this path — and a `TypeDefType` carrying `{"id": …}` is UNREADABLE. *Re-tiered 2026-09-15 ([KF420](#kf420)): that `DateRangeType` refusal is a CODELESS VERDICT and not a build failure, so of the five types an empty body "defeats", four are unbuildable and the fifth is judged and refused — one more row where the harness's collapse of the two codeless tiers read as one mechanism.* So the set of types an empty body defeats is a measured outcome and not a reading of which constructor argument is required; a checker deriving it from the `@NonNull` annotations would be wrong about three of the five.

**Corrected 2026-09-13:** that `TypeDefType` row was first read as "a dangling type reference refuses A12's reader", and it is wrong in both halves. The wire member is **`typeDefinitionId`**; `id` is only the Java field's name, so the probe was measuring an UNKNOWN member on a field body — which this carrier refuses whatever it spells, per the carrier-strictness row above. Re-measured with the real member (taken from a shipped model rather than from the class): a `typeDefinitionId` naming a DECLARED `content.typeDefinitions` entry is ADMITTED, and one naming nothing is **NOT BUILDABLE**, matching `EntityReferenceResolverVisitor.visitField`, which sets the unresolved reference to null and carries on rather than raising. An absent reference member is NOT BUILDABLE too. The lesson is the general one: a WIRE name is settled by a real document, never by the class the wire binds to.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldTypeBindingLawsTest`, measured on `/Order/CustomerName` — a field no declaration references, so a refusal cannot be attributed to an ordering reference as it could in [KF307](#kf307). The portable side is `consistency`'s `FieldTypeBindingTest`.

## §12 supplement — the condition lexer's ILLEGAL-CHARACTER class, derived from its terminals and measured (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf309"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §12, whose syntax material names `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` without saying what reaches it besides an unpaired quote.

**The class is derivable, which is what turns it from a survey into a law.** `Base_ConditionLexer.g4` declares no catch-all rule, so any character outside its terminals is a token-recognition failure. Outside a string literal the terminals admit exactly the `STR` fragment (`a-z A-Z _ Ä Ü Ö ä ü ö ß :`), `DIGIT`, the whitespace set, both quotes, and the punctuation the operator and bracket terminals spell (`+ - * / ^ > < = ! ( ) [ ] { } , . @ # $`). *Source:* `kernel-tool/kernel-core-parser/src/main/antlr4/…/Base_ConditionLexer.g4`, kernel `30.8.1`, read 2026-09-13.

**Measured against that reading, and it holds on every row.** `%`, `&`, `|`, `;`, `?`, `~`, a backslash, `é` and `€` each draw `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR`. The control is the half that separates a lexer failure from a parser one: `$`, `@` and `,` are terminals of their own and `ß` is in the `STR` fragment, so all four LEX and are refused a phase later with `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`. Every row puts one character in the same operand slot, so the two outcomes are told apart by A12's own codes rather than by anything the grid decides.

**An earlier probe read as a counterexample and was a positive control.** The note that "`@@@` lexes cleanly and fails a phase later" had been recorded as evidence that the character class was unmeasurable. It is the opposite: `@` is the `AT` terminal, so `@@@` lexing is exactly what the grammar predicts, and the probe agreed with the derivation nobody had done yet.

**Two characters exist ONLY inside a multi-character terminal, and they part from every intuition about "known punctuation".** `!` is spelled only in `'!='` and `#` only in `'#Zeile'`, so a lone one of either is illegal — measured, both drawing the lexer error. A checker admitting all punctuation the lexer "knows" is wrong about both; one refusing from a hand-listed alphabet happens to be right.

**Inside a string literal none of it applies.** `StringLiteral : '"' ( '""' | ~["] )* '"'` admits every character but a quote, and all eleven above are ADMITTED there — so a checker scanning raw text for a bad character refuses conditions A12 accepts.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ConditionCharacterLawsTest`. The portable side is `consistency`'s `ConditionLexicalityTest`, which reports the class with one deliberate exception: a lone `#` is left unreported, because `#Zeile`'s other language spellings are unknown there and refusing an unpaired `#` could reject text A12 accepts.

## §12 supplement — a PRESENT-but-BLANK DSL slot parses, and answers differently on each member (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf310"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §12, whose syntax material treats a slot as present or absent and never as present-and-empty.

**A blank slot is not an unset one: A12 hands it to the parser like any other text.** That much was already recorded for one member. What nobody had put side by side is that the four DSL-bearing members do NOT agree on the code, and two of the three answers were each measured in a test written for some other question:

| member | a blank draws |
|---|---|
| `errorCondition` | `MVK_CONDITION_MISSING` **and** `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` |
| `commonPrecondition` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `computationAlternatives[].precondition` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `computationAlternatives[].operation` | `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` |

**The `commonPrecondition` row is the one that completes the set, and it was predicted wrong.** It had never been measured, and the prediction — that a blank common precondition is simply unset and therefore ADMITTED — is false: a declared common precondition is a condition slot like any other and a blank one fails in the parser. Each row carries a FILLED control of the same shape, so the code is attributable to the blank rather than to the fixture built to carry it.

**Why this matters to a checker rather than being trivia.** A syntax layer reporting "a blank does not parse" under one code is right about one member and wrong about the rest, and the two that share `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` are a condition member and a *common* condition member, while the operation — the one member that is an expression rather than a condition — is the one that parts. So the split follows the member's GRAMMAR ROLE and not its carrier, which is not what the names suggest.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationAlternativeSlotLawsTest.aBlankSlotAnswersDifferentlyOnEachMemberOfThisCarrier` and `RuleConditionAndTargetSlotLawsTest`. The portable side is `consistency`'s `BlankDslSlotTest`.

## §12 supplement — with TWO syntax failures in one text, A12 reports the EARLIER one, whichever phase owns it (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf311"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §12, which gives each parse phase its code and says nothing about which phase speaks when two of them can.

[KF300](#kf300) established four parse codes, one per phase, each measured on a text carrying one failure. It left open which code a text carrying TWO draws, and an earlier reading of the rows — that the lexer wins unless a literal *swallows a delimiter* — described two shapes rather than a rule. **The rule is positional: the failure sitting earliest in the text is the one A12 names.**

| text | first failure | A12 says |
|---|---|---|
| `FieldFilled(Tier))` | the extra `)` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier) And "x` | the quote | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier)) And "x` | the extra `)` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `"x And FieldFilled(Tier))` | the quote | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier)) And %` | the extra `)` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `% And FieldFilled(Tier))` | the `%` | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled(Tier))"x` | the extra `)`, one character ahead | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `FieldFilled('Tier) ]` | the quote | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |
| `FieldFilled('Tier) And` | the quote | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |

**The rows are ordered PAIRS of the same two defects**, because order is the only variable that can move without changing what the defects are; a grid that varied the defects instead cannot tell position from phase. The last three rows are the ones that defeat the rival readings: a parse error BEHIND the lexical failure loses, so this is not a fixed "the parser outranks the lexer"; and both lexical classes are measured in both orders, so an unterminated literal and an illegal character are not assumed to share precedence merely because they share a code.

**`FieldFilled('Tier) And` is the row that separates first-wins from last-wins, and it is the only one that could.** ANTLR does not stop at a character it cannot take — it reports, skips the character, and lexes on — so that text raises the lexer's failure at the quote and then hands the parser `FieldFilled(Tier) And`, which runs out of input and raises a second failure; the control with the quote removed draws `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`. A12 reports the lexer. Every other row's failure is fatal to the token stream, so only this shape has two live candidates.

*Mechanism (hypothesis, consistent with every row and not separately proved):* ANTLR's lexer is demand-driven, producing a token only when the parser asks for one, so it cannot report at a position the parser has not reached, and the parser cannot reach a position the lexer has refused to hand it.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.SyntaxPhasePrecedenceLawsTest`. The portable side is `consistency`'s `SyntaxPhasePrecedenceTest`, which asserts the whole report's codes per row — the second mistake this closes was two families each reporting their own verdict for `FieldFilled('Tier) And`.

## §10 supplement — which member each constructing field type requires, derived from its BUILDER and necessary rather than sufficient (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf312"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §10, whose field-type material names the types and not what each one's body must carry.

[KF308](#kf308) measured that five of the thirteen types leave an unbuildable model when their body is `{}` and stopped there, so a body carrying a type's OPTIONAL members and not the one it builds from was outside every row. **The required member is derivable, and there is exactly one per type: the `@NonNull` constructor parameter the hand-written `…Builder` class does not pre-initialise.** Each of these classes takes its arguments through a Lombok `@Builder` on a private constructor and defaults the optional ones explicitly in the builder, with a comment saying why. *Source:* `kernel-md/kernel-md-a12internal/…/fieldtypes/`, kernel `30.8.1`, read 2026-09-13.

| type | required | body with an optional member only | body with the required member |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DateRangeType` | `format` | `{"rangeSeparator":"-"}` → REFUSED, codeless ([re-tiered 2026-09-15](#kf420)) | `{"format":"yyyy-MM-dd"}` → ADMITTED |
| `DateFragmentType` | `formatOfFragment` | `{"youngerThan1900Check":true}` → NOT BUILDABLE | `{"formatOfFragment":"dd.MM."}` → ADMITTED |
| `EnumerationType` | `values` | `{"alphabeticalSorting":true}` → NOT BUILDABLE | `{"values":[{"value":"A"}]}` → ADMITTED |
| `CustomFieldType` | `name` | `{"displayName":"Signature"}` → `CUSTOM_FIELD_TYPE_CODENAME_MISSING` | `{"name":"Signature"}` → ADMITTED |

**`EnumerationType` is the entry a source reading gets wrong, and the builder is what settles it.** Its `values` FIELD carries an initialiser (`= new EnumValues()`), so a reader skimming fields calls it defaulted; the initialiser is irrelevant, because the builder writes the field through the constructor and the builder class defaults `categories`, `errorMessage`, `alphabeticalSorting` and `annotations` — every other `@NonNull` parameter, and not that one. The measurement agrees with the builder, not with the fields.

**The member is NECESSARY and not sufficient, and two rows say so** — which is why a checker may report its ABSENCE and must stay silent on its presence:

- `DateRangeType` with `{"format":"dd.MM.yyyy"}` alone is REFUSED codeless ([re-tiered 2026-09-15](#kf420)) even though the builder defaults `rangeSeparator`. A12 allowlists the format-and-separator PAIR, the default separator is `/` (`FieldTypeConstants.A12_DATE_RANGE_SEPARATOR`), and (`dd.MM.yyyy`, `/`) is not among the eight admitted pairs ([TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md)). The discriminator is `{"format":"yyyy-MM-dd"}`, whose pair with `/` IS admitted and which is ADMITTED — without it the row would read as "a format alone is never enough for this type". **Amended 2026-09-13:** the pair is measured in its own right in [KF316](#kf316), which settles the tier and the omitted-separator reading, so this row is no longer the only thing a consumer can key on.
- `DateFragmentType` with `{"formatOfFragment":"dd.MM.","youngerThan1900Check":true}` draws `MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID` — a consistency verdict rather than a build failure, because the check needs a year and that format has none. Its discriminator is the identical pair of members with `dd.MM.yyyy`, which is ADMITTED.

**Corrected 2026-09-13** ([KF323](#kf323)): the `CustomFieldType` row is not a silent build refusal but a VERDICT, under a class carrying no `MVK_` prefix — it read as NOT BUILDABLE only because the harness lifted classes by that prefix. It is the one of the four that reaches a verdict, and the member is judged on its CONTENT there: `{"name":""}` and `{"name":"   "}` draw the same class as no `name` at all.

**The control is a type that requires nothing carrying the SAME optional member.** `DateType` and `DateFragmentType` both declare `youngerThan1900Check`, and `DateType` with only that member is ADMITTED — so the unbuildable rows are about the type constructing from something, not about a body with exactly one member being refused.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldTypeBodyMemberLawsTest`. The portable side is `consistency`'s `FieldTypeBindingTest.aConstructingTypeIsJudgedOnTheMemberItBuildsFrom`.

## §10 supplement — a TRAILING separator is part of the format string: `dd.MM.` is admitted where `dd.MM` is not (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf313"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §10's temporal-format material, which states the vocabulary by citing the derived artifact.

**The admitted temporal vocabulary is thirteen formats, not twelve, and the thirteenth is `dd.MM.` — the German short date without a year.** It is admitted on DATE, TIME and DATETIME alike and as a `formatOfFragment`, while `dd.MM` without the closing dot stays refused on all of them. So the separator axis [KF196](#kf196) established runs past the END of the string too, which no candidate the vocabulary generator produced could show: every generated candidate joined components and stopped.

**How it was found is the point, and it was not by probing.** It turned up as a fixture value while measuring which body member a `DateFragmentType` requires ([KF312](#kf312)) — a format someone had written into a test years' worth of probes had never put to the kernel. The generator now varies the trailing-separator axis (306 new candidates, 1223 in total), and of them exactly one is admitted: this one. A low-yield axis that nonetheless held a real member is the argument for generating an axis rather than sampling it.

**The consequence was four shipped surfaces advertising a legal declaration as illegal**, and the guard named them rather than a reader having to: three published JSON schema descriptions (`field add`, `field modify`, `typedef add`) and the diagnostic enricher's `MVK_INVALID_DATE_FORMAT` corrective, each quantifying the set as TWELVE and enumerating it. This is the fifth measured shortfall of this one domain — after `MM-dd` (2026-08-19), `yyyyMM` (2026-08-29), the compact trio the first derivation exposed, and the DATEFRAGMENT four-of-twelve (2026-09-05) — and the first the estate caught mechanically, because the denominator is derived and the claimants are registered.

**What it does NOT change.** The DATERANGE pair vocabulary stays at eight: no trailing-separator format is admitted with any separator. And `dd.MM.` is year-free, so `youngerThan1900Check` is refused on it with `MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID`, identically on the DATE and DATEFRAGMENT carriers — it joins `MM`, `MM-dd`, `MMdd`, `ddMM` and `HH:mm:ss` there rather than parting from them.

*Locked by:* the derived artifact itself ([TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md), regenerated) and its guard, plus the four vocabulary grids the guard holds to the admitted set — `rulekit.validate.laws.TemporalDeclarationConfigAdmissionLawsTest`, `TemporalAdditionalCheckCarrierLawsTest`, `TemporalEqualSetPairDenominatorLawsTest` (a fourth `{MONTH, DAY}` spelling, so ten equal-set pairs rather than seven), `adapter.laws.TemporalDeclaredFormatGateDiffTest` (the kernel differential) and `interpreter.TemporalDeclaredFormatFormalTest`.

## §6 supplement — the STORED members carrying the two date-config gates, and what an absent format means to them (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf314"></a>

> Fold: pending — supplies [KF251](#kf251)'s gates with their wire shape; folds into §6 with it.

[KF251](#kf251) established both `DateType` config gates by authoring models through the typed kit, which is the right oracle for the LAW and says nothing about the member names a reader of STORED JSON must look for. A checker cannot take those from the Java fields — doing exactly that with `TypeDefType.id` is what sent an earlier probe measuring an unknown member and reading the result as a dangling-reference law ([KF308](#kf308), corrected). Measured on stored bodies:

| stored body on a field | A12 says |
|---|---|
| `{"format":"MM","youngerThan1900Check":true}` | `MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID` |
| `{"format":"MM","youngerThan1900Check":false}` | ADMITTED |
| `{"format":"MM","datePrecision":"DAY_OPTIONAL"}` | `MVK_OPTIONAL_DATE_TYPE_INVALID` |
| `{"format":"MM","datePrecision":"FULL"}` | ADMITTED |
| `{"formatOfFragment":"MM","youngerThan1900Check":true}` (a `DateFragmentType`) | `MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID` |
| `{"format":"MM","rangeSeparator":"/","youngerThan1900Check":true}` (a `DateRangeType`) | ADMITTED — the carrier is exempt |
| `{"format":"MM","youngerThan1900":true}` — a nearly-right member name | UNREADABLE |

**The misspelling row is what makes the rest a measurement.** Without it every ADMITTED row is equally consistent with the member being ignored, and the whole grid would be measuring whether a name A12 never reads changes anything. The answer also extends [KF308](#kf308)'s carrier-strictness law to a new carrier: a **field type's BODY** refuses a member A12 does not declare, exactly as the field's own body does, so a misspelling cannot masquerade as the real member.

**An absent `format` is the declared DEFAULT and not "no format", on both gates.** `{"youngerThan1900Check":true}` and `{"datePrecision":"DAY_OPTIONAL"}` with no format member are both ADMITTED, because the builder fills `FieldTypeConstants.DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` — `yyyy-MM-dd`, which is year-bearing and a complete pure date, so it passes both. A checker reading the absent member as the default therefore gets A12's answer; reading it as nothing would produce findings A12 does not give.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.TemporalConfigWireShapeLawsTest`. The portable side is `consistency`'s `TEMPORAL_CONFIG` family and `TemporalConfigTest`.

## §13 supplement — the element-name alphabet is NOT one law: the FIELD carrier parts from the GROUP carrier on five of thirteen rows (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf315"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §13, whose declaration material states the group-name alphabet and says nothing about a field's.

[KF268](#kf268) established two gates on a GROUP's declared name: the path validator's alphabet, and a second gate reserving a leading underscore for `__meta` / `__attachment_meta*`. Run row for row on a FIELD, **five of thirteen rows differ, and one difference is in the direction a client-side refusal may never take.**

| name | as a GROUP | as a FIELD |
|---|---|---|
| `Slöts` (a non-ASCII letter) | ADMITTED | `MVK_PATH_INVALID` |
| `_Slots`, `__other` | `NAME_STARTS_WITH_UNDERSCORE_AND_WRONG_PATTERN` | **ADMITTED** |
| `1Slots` | `MVK_PATH_INVALID` | `MVK_PATH_INVALID` **and** `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_DIGIT_A12_DV` |
| `Slot:List` | `MVK_PATH_INVALID` | `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV` **instead** |
| 61 characters | refused, codeless | ADMITTED |

**Neither carrier is simply the stricter one**, which is what makes the transfer unsafe in both directions: the group refuses the leading underscore a field takes, and admits the non-ASCII letter a field refuses. The 60-character limit is the group's alone. The `_A12_DV` codes name the mechanism — a field's name answers to a second validator the group's name does not reach.

**On a field the CODE depends on the character, three ways**, which a checker naming A12's code has to reproduce rather than collapse: `.` and `:` draw `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV`; `/` draws `MVK_PATHS_INCONSISTENT`, because a name carrying the separator makes the element's own path disagree with the tree rather than being a bad name at all; `-`, space, `%`, `(`, `+`, `#`, `@`, `$`, `,`, `'` and `*` all draw `MVK_PATH_INVALID`. `_`, a digit in interior position, and both letter cases are the admitted controls.

**Why it was measured rather than assumed.** Applying a measured law to an unmeasured carrier needs no new branch, so nothing prompts the question — the recurring scope-transfer shape. Here the assumption would have made a checker refuse a field named `_Slots`, which A12 admits.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldNameAlphabetLawsTest`, row for row against `GroupNameAlphabetLawsTest`.

## §10 supplement — a DATERANGE's `(format, rangeSeparator)` pair is refused at the BUILD tier, and an omitted separator is the kernel's `/` (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf316"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §10, whose field-type material names `DateRangeType` without saying that its two members are allowlisted together.

[TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md) derives the eight admitted `(format, separator)` pairs, but it asks the kernel a boolean. A consumer that wants to SAY something about a refused pair needs the TIER as well, because a reader refusal, a build failure and an `MVK_*` code are three different claims about whether A12 examined the declaration at all. **It is the build tier: A12 reads the model, cannot construct the type, and issues no consistency code** — so a refused pair leaves a consumer with no verdict rather than a wrong one, exactly like an absent required member ([KF312](#kf312)).

**Neither half can be judged alone, measured in both directions on one carrier:**

| `format` | `rangeSeparator` | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `yyyy-MM-dd` | `/` | ADMITTED |
| `dd.MM.yyyy` | `-` | ADMITTED |
| `yyyy-MM-dd` | `-` | REFUSED, codeless |
| `dd.MM.yyyy` | `/` | REFUSED, codeless |

Every member of the two refused rows appears in an admitted row, so the allowlist reads the combination rather than either half. The two controls differ from their refused partner in exactly one member, which is what makes each refusal attributable.

**An omitted `rangeSeparator` is `/`, not "no separator"** — the kernel's `FieldTypeConstants.A12_DATE_RANGE_SEPARATOR`, pre-initialised by `DateRangeTypeBuilder` (source-read, kernel `30.8.1`). Only stored JSON can ask: the typed builder always writes one. Omission is ADMITTED on `yyyy-MM-dd` and REFUSED codeless on `dd.MM.yyyy`, which is the discriminating pair; an explicit `""` is a different declaration with admitted pairs of its own (`MM` takes it, `yyyy-MM-dd` does not), so a reader treating omission as the empty string gets both rows backwards.

**The range domain is not a projection of the field-format vocabulary, in both directions.** `yyyyMM` is an admitted field format and is refused on a range at every probed separator; `dd.MM` is refused as a field format and admitted on a range with `-`. Reusing the thirteen-member field vocabulary here would refuse a legal model and miss an illegal one.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DateRangePairAdmissionLawsTest`; the pair set itself is derived by `TemporalFormatVocabularyGuardTest` and published in [TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md).

## §8 supplement — the `supportedCharacters` restriction judges declared ENUM VALUES and nothing else, per distinct character per value (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf317"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §8's Enumeration account, whose declaration material does not mention the model-level character restriction.

[MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md)'s scope-boundary note established that `checkConsistency` re-runs the validation code generator, so `MVK_ENUM_VALUE_WITH_INVALID_CHARACTER` reaches an ordinary authoring gate: `supportedCharacters: ["A-Z"]` with an enum value `beta` draws four diagnostics. That settles REACHABILITY and leaves the two questions a consumer reproducing the gate has to answer — which declared strings it judges, and what a definition entry means.

**It judges enum VALUES and nothing else.** The identical refused spelling, under the identical restriction, in four other declared strings of the same model:

| the offending spelling sits in | verdict |
|---|---|
| an enum `values[].value` | 4 × `MVK_ENUM_VALUE_WITH_INVALID_CHARACTER` |
| an element NAME | ADMITTED |
| an error MESSAGE text | ADMITTED |
| an enum CATEGORY token | ADMITTED |
| a string field's HINT LIST | ADMITTED |

A consumer reading the restriction as "the model's text" would refuse four models A12 takes. The transfer needs no new branch, which is why it prompts no question.

**Amended 2026-09-13 — the hint-list row, and why source reading would have got it wrong.** `NoMetaModelChecks.checkEnumValues` runs the same `LegalCharTester` over `IStringType.getHintList(language)` as over an enumeration's values, so the arm reads as in scope; it is guarded by `type.isExtensibleEnum()`, and on kernel `30.8.1` **nothing sets that flag**. An anchored search of the checkout (excluding `build/` and delombok output) returns eleven mentions of `isExtensibleEnum`: ten calls and one declaration, the interface default on `IStringType` returning `false`; `md.model.a12internal.fieldtypes.StringType` carries a `hintList` but no `extensibleEnum` member and overrides nothing. So the arm is dead for a DM-JSON document model, the row measures ADMITTED, and a family widened onto the hint list by reading the source alone would refuse models A12 takes. The three non-value rows above are asserted on the whole-model VERDICT rather than on a count of this one code, which zero cannot distinguish from a refusal for another reason.

**Also asserted about the scope of that assertion:** the other four carriers are each measured, not transferred from one another. Display values are excluded by the kernel's own comment (`//no check for display values, they can have any characters`) and are not separately measured here.

**A definition is a LIST of independent entries, each a singleton or an inclusive range.** `["A-Z"]` admits both boundary characters; `["B-Y"]` refuses `A` and `Z`; `["A-Z", "b"]` takes `beta` from four offenders down to three, so the entries union rather than compose.

**The multiplicity is per DISTINCT character, scoped to the VALUE.** `aa` draws ONE diagnostic, not two — the repeat is folded — while the same two offenders spelled into two values (`ab`, `ba`) draw four. Neither row is inferable from the other, and a consumer keyed on occurrences or on model-wide distinctness disagrees with A12 on both.

**Amended 2026-09-13 — the scope is the value's SPELLING, not its position.** Declaring the SAME offending value twice (`ab`, `ab`) draws **two**, not four: A12 reports on the triple (field, value, character) and folds the repeat, which the `ab`/`ba` row above cannot say because its two values differ. A checker pairing per declared ENTRY over-counts exactly here, and this repository's did until the row was run.

**The restriction belongs to the EXPANDED model, not to the file that declares the enum.** A provider declaring no restriction of its own is clean when checked alone and draws the host's four diagnostics once mounted into a model that declares `A-Z`. So it is applied to mounted declarations as much as to local ones. The middle control is on the same instrument as the treatment — the same provider mounted into an UNRESTRICTED host draws none through `ModelLoader.loadAndCheck` — so the two-row form, which read the control through `BoundModel.ofJson`, is not moving the mount and the instrument together.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.SupportedCharactersDeclarationGateLawsTest` (the scope, the definition grammar, the multiplicity, and the two-model mount fixture); the reachability half stays with `CodegenErrorClassReachesConsistencyLawsTest`.

## §7 supplement — a declared string type's `pattern` and its own `errorMessage` require each other, and a message counts only where it REACHES a declared locale (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf318"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §7's string-declaration material, which covers the pattern and neither of the members that must accompany it.

[KF165](#kf165) settles WHICH declared patterns A12 admits; this settles what a pattern must be declared WITH. The two members look like independent slots and are one law with two directions, and a third code rides beside them. The fixture that measured KF165 already supplied a message with every pattern, on a comment asserting one was required — a claim no row of that grid could test, because none of them varied the message. These do.

| the string type declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| neither member — the control | ADMITTED |
| a `pattern` and an `errorMessage` for the declared locale | ADMITTED |
| a `pattern` and no `errorMessage` | `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_AND_PATTERN_INVALID` |
| an `errorMessage` and no `pattern` | `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_AND_NO_PATTERN` |

**A message "exists" only where it reaches a DECLARED locale with a non-blank text, and both directions read it that way.** Three weakenings, each leaving the member present, each measured on both arms: an empty `errorMessage` list, a blank `text`, and a text for a locale `header.locales` does not declare. All three refuse a pattern beside them with the pattern's own code, and all three are ADMITTED with no pattern — so one predicate serves both directions and a checker needs no branch for them. The undeclared-locale row is the one that separates *counted* from *collected*, and it corrected this repository's first prediction.

**The locale tier is a THIRD code and it belongs to the message alone.** Once some declared locale is answered and another is not, A12 reports `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_FOR_LANGUAGE_MISSING` — the same code a rule's own `errorMessage` draws — and it reports it whether or not the pattern that makes the member legal is there: a half-translated message with no pattern draws `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_FOR_LANGUAGE_MISSING` and `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_AND_NO_PATTERN` together. This is only visible on a two-locale header; on a one-locale model "every declared locale answered" and "some declared locale answered" are the same claim, which is the constant every row of the first grid holds fixed.

**Where A12's reader stops is not where the member's shape suggests.** A scalar at `errorMessage` BINDS — A12 collects no message from it and answers with the ordinary consistency code — while a non-object ENTRY inside the list refuses the source outright, so the model never loads and no verdict about it exists. That is the same boundary [KF290](#kf290) source-located on the rule carrier, measured here rather than carried across; the agreement is what lets one reader serve both carriers in this repository's checker.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.StringTypeMessageAndPatternLawsTest` (18 rows across the two grids); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.StringTypeMessageTest`.

## §7 supplement — a string type's own parameters: what `noValueValidation` excludes, and that `-1` is A12's "no bound" rather than an inverted one (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf319"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §7's string-declaration material, which covers the pattern and none of the parameters around it.

Five codes, one topic, measured as one grid because measuring a co-requirement's members separately produces a law that is false ([KF297](#kf297) already cost that lesson on the rounding pair).

| the string type declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| an ordinary type — the control | ADMITTED |
| `noValueValidation` alone | `MVK_STRING_TYPE_NO_VAL_AND_NO_LINE_BREAK` |
| `noValueValidation` with `lineBreaksPermitted` | ADMITTED |
| …and a `pattern` | `MVK_STRING_TYPE_PARAMS_INCONSISTENT` |
| …and a `minLength` | `MVK_STRING_TYPE_PARAMS_INCONSISTENT` |
| …and a `maxLength` | **ADMITTED** — the maximum is not one of the excluded parameters |
| …and a `hintList` | `MVK_NO_VAL_AND_HINT_LISTS` |
| `lineBreaksPermitted` with `maxLength: 1` | `MVK_LINE_BREAK_AND_MAX_LENGTH_1_INVALID` |
| `minLength: 5`, `maxLength: 3` | `MVK_MIN_LENGTH_BIGGER_MAX_LENGTH` |
| `minLength: 3`, `maxLength: 3` — the boundary | ADMITTED |

Each of the three excluded members is measured ADMITTED on its own, so every row above is attributed to the pair rather than to the member; `maxLength: 1` and `lineBreaksPermitted` with `maxLength: 2` are the two controls that separate the line-break conjunct from the length one.

**`-1` is A12's own encoding of "no bound", and reading it as a number makes a legal model unreadable.** `IFieldType.UNDEFINED` is `-1`, so a model may spell an unset length either by omitting the member or by writing the sentinel, and A12 admits `minLength: -1`, `maxLength: -1` and `minLength: 2, maxLength: -1` alike. This repository's `FieldTypeSpec.StringSpec` refused all three — `minLength must be ≥ 0` on the first two, and `minLength 2 > maxLength -1` on the third, an "inverted range" that is really a minimum with no maximum. Because `FieldTypeSpecReader` builds one of those records for every declared string field, the refusal fired on the READ path: a model A12 accepts could not be inspected through the kit. Same class as [KF216](#kf216), third occurrence, and again the sharper half was the read path rather than authoring.

**The sibling carrier agrees on the sentinel and DIVERGES on the inverted range.** `CustomFieldType` carries the same two member names and the same client-side refusals, so it was measured rather than inherited: `-1` is admitted there too, but `minLength: 5, maxLength: 3` leaves A12 unable to BUILD the model — no `MVK_*` code, no consistency verdict — where the string type reports `MVK_MIN_LENGTH_BIGGER_MAX_LENGTH`. A checker or a kit that carried the string type's row across would state a code A12 never emits on that carrier.

**The line-break flag's wire name is `lineBreaksPermitted`, taken from the serializer's Jackson mixin — `StringTypeImpl` spells its field `linebreaksPermitted`, one letter apart.** A row carrying the wrong spelling would measure nothing and read as a clean ADMITTED; the `noValueValidation` pair is the control that proves the flag arrives.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.StringTypeParameterLawsTest` (three grids); the read-path half by `modelkit.StringLengthSentinelReadTest`.

## §7 supplement — a number type's fractional-digit law is not `min > max`: an ABSENT member reads as 0 and a NEGATIVE maximum takes the pair out of the check (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf320"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §7's number-declaration material, which covers the scale but not the pair's defaulting.

| the number type declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| `maxFractionalDigits: 2` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `minFractionalDigits: 3`, `maxFractionalDigits: 2` | `MVK_FRACT_DIGITS_INVALID` |
| `minFractionalDigits: 2`, `maxFractionalDigits: 2` — the boundary | ADMITTED |
| **`minFractionalDigits: 2`, no maximum** | **`MVK_FRACT_DIGITS_INVALID`** |
| neither member | ADMITTED |
| `maxFractionalDigits: -1` | ADMITTED |
| `minFractionalDigits: -1`, `maxFractionalDigits: 2` | ADMITTED |
| `minFractionalDigits: 0`, `maxFractionalDigits: -1` | ADMITTED |
| **`minFractionalDigits: 1`, `maxFractionalDigits: -1`** | **ADMITTED** |
| `maxFractionalDigits: 14` | ADMITTED |
| `maxFractionalDigits: 15` | REFUSED, codeless — `"Only values smaller than or equal to 14 are allowed."` ([re-tiered 2026-09-15](#kf420): A12 builds the model and judges the member, naming no class) |
| `minFractionalDigits: 15`, `maxFractionalDigits: 15` | REFUSED, codeless |

**The last two bolded rows are the whole finding, and they pull in opposite directions.** A minimum with NO maximum is refused, so an absent maximum reads as `0` and the comparison runs; the same minimum beside an explicit `-1` is admitted, so a negative maximum takes the pair OUT of the comparison instead of being compared as a number. The observable law is therefore *`max >= 0` and `min > max`, with an absent member reading as 0* — and a checker comparing the members as declared is wrong on both rows, admitting one model A12 refuses and refusing one A12 takes. (Whether A12 normalizes the negative to an undefined marker or guards the rule is not observable through this code, so no mechanism is claimed.)

**The value range beside it is the ordinary law** — both bounds declared, equal admitted, inverted refused, a single bound admitted, a wholly negative range admitted — and it is stated separately because nothing about the digit pair predicts it.

**Two client-side refusals fell to this grid, one in each direction.** `FieldTypeSpec.NumberSpec` refused a negative digit count, which A12 admits, on the READ path as well as the authoring one; and it compared the pair only when both members were set, so `minFractionalDigits(2)` with no maximum was accepted and then refused by the kernel, because the emitter always writes `maxFractionalDigits`. The scale cap the same record enforces is confirmed rather than corrected: 14 builds, 15 does not, and the transitivity argument for refusing a minimum above 14 now has its second link measured.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.NumberTypeDigitLawsTest` (two grids, 19 rows); the record's own half by `modelkit.NumberDigitPairReadTest`; the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.NumberTypeDigitTest`.

## §8 supplement — an enumeration's value TOKEN is almost unchecked, and its label law is "started and not finished" (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf321"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §8's Enumeration account, which covers the values' runtime meaning and not their declaration.

**Almost nothing about a value TOKEN is A12's business at this tier**, which is the half that matters for a checker, because four `MVK_VALUE_*` codes read as though it were:

| the enumeration declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| two ordinary values — the control | ADMITTED |
| the same token twice | `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_DUPLICATE` |
| a single value | ADMITTED |
| an EMPTY token | ADMITTED |
| a token containing a space | ADMITTED |
| a 300-character token | ADMITTED |

`MVK_VALUE_INVALID`, `MVK_VALUE_TOO_LONG`, `MVK_VALUE_TOO_SHORT` and `MVK_VALUES_DUPLICATE` all fire for none of these; the duplicate is reported under the INTERNAL name instead. Reproducing any of the four would refuse a model A12 takes. (The tokens' ALPHABET is a separate gate that fires only under a `supportedCharacters` restriction — [KF317](#kf317).)

**The label law is neither "every value has a label" nor "every declared locale is answered".** Measured: *once ANY value carries an entry for ANY DECLARED locale, every value must carry a non-blank text for every declared locale.*

| the enumeration declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| no labels at all | ADMITTED |
| every value labelled for the declared locale | ADMITTED |
| only ONE value labelled | `MVK_COUNT_OF_VALUES_INVALID` |
| an EMPTY `label` array on one value | `MVK_COUNT_OF_VALUES_INVALID` |
| labels only for an UNDECLARED locale | **ADMITTED** |
| one value's text BLANK | `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_AND_DISPLAY_VALUES` |
| EVERY text blank | **`MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_AND_DISPLAY_VALUES`** |
| two labels for one locale on one value | ADMITTED |
| (bilingual) both locales answered | ADMITTED |
| (bilingual) only one locale answered | `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_AND_DISPLAY_VALUES` |
| (bilingual) one value bilingual, the other English only | `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_AND_DISPLAY_VALUES` |

**The two bolded rows are what pin the law, and neither follows from the other.** Labels written only for an undeclared locale are ADMITTED although no declared locale is answered — so a checker asking "is this locale answered" gets that row wrong. Labels present for the declared locale with every text blank are REFUSED although, again, no locale is answered — so a checker asking "is any label present" gets that one wrong. The entries' presence for a declared locale is what arms the law; the texts are what satisfy it. No mechanism is claimed for the split: both halves are stated as observed.

**The two codes are separated by WHOSE disagreement it is.** Values that disagree on carrying a label at all — an empty `label` array counts as carrying none — draw `MVK_COUNT_OF_VALUES_INVALID`, and A12 reports that INSTEAD of the locale code rather than beside it.

**modelkit's client-side refusal of a partially-labelled enumeration is CLEARED by this grid** rather than corrected: `DocumentModelDraft` throws when any value is labelled and any value lacks a label for a declared locale, which is exactly the pair of laws above, and it had only a comment for a basis.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumValueAndLabelLawsTest` (three grids, 20 rows); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.EnumValueLabelTest`.

## §13 supplement — a declared name's shape law is the CARRIER's, three ways: the code's spelling, whether a name code fires at all, and whether the name is judged (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf322"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §13's declaration account, next to [KF315](#kf315)'s alphabet pair.

[KF315](#kf315) measured which CHARACTERS a field and a group admit and left four questions open: the empty name, the SECOND code a digit-initial name draws, an `xml` prefix, and the rule carrier, which had no grid. Answering them on four carriers — a field, a group below the root, the root group, and a rule — shows the carrier moves the law in three independent ways, and no one of them predicts the others.

**The code's SPELLING splits field-vs-group.** A field answers with the `_A12_DV`-suffixed class, both group carriers with the unsuffixed one:

| the name | on a FIELD | on a NESTED group | on the ROOT group | on a RULE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| starts with `xml` | `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_XML_A12_DV` | `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_XML` | `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_XML` | ADMITTED |
| starts with `XML` or `Xml`, or IS `xml` | `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_XML_A12_DV` | `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_XML` | `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_XML` | — |
| starts with `xm` | ADMITTED | — | — | — |
| merely CONTAINS `xml` | ADMITTED | ADMITTED | — | — |
| starts with a digit | `MVK_PATH_INVALID`, `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_DIGIT_A12_DV` | `MVK_PATH_INVALID` | `MVK_NAME_STARTS_WITH_DIGIT` | REFUSED, codeless |
| is EMPTY or BLANK | NOT BUILDABLE | NOT BUILDABLE | RAISED (untyped) | NOT BUILDABLE |
| carries a dot | `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV` | `MVK_PATH_INVALID` | `MVK_PATH_INVALID` | REFUSED, codeless |

**Whether a name code fires at all splits root-vs-nested.** The digit row is the one to read: the root group draws the name class and no path class, the nested group draws the path class and no name class, and the field draws both. A checker that learned this row on one carrier names a class A12 does not emit on the other.

**A RULE's name is not judged.** A digit-initial or dotted rule name leaves A12 unable to build the model, so no consistency verdict exists and there is no class to reproduce; an `xml` prefix is simply admitted. A name family extended to rules by analogy with fields would refuse on a class that cannot fire there.

**And the leading-underscore gate is a law of groups BELOW the root.** [KF315](#kf315) measured `NAME_STARTS_WITH_UNDERSCORE_AND_WRONG_PATTERN` on one nested group, which was the constant its whole set held: the root group ADMITS `_Orders` and `__other`, a group two levels down refuses them like the one at depth two. The portable checker applied the nested measurement to every group and so refused a legal model — the one direction it may not take — until this grid was run. The alphabet rows transfer exactly (a hyphen, a space and a colon draw `MVK_PATH_INVALID` on both carriers, `/` draws `MVK_PATHS_INCONSISTENT`, a non-ASCII letter is admitted, and 61 characters is refused with no class), so which rows the carrier moves cannot be predicted from the ones it leaves alone.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DeclaredNameShapeLawsTest` (three grids, 33 rows).

## §13 supplement — A12's refusal classes are not all `MVK_`-prefixed, and a diagnostic ECHOES the author's own code back (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf323"></a>

> Fold: pending — a fact about A12's reporting vocabulary rather than about one construct, so it belongs wherever the notification shape is described.

Every coded notification ends with its class in brackets — `… [MVK_PATH_INVALID]`. **The class is not always spelled `MVK_*`**, and keying on that prefix silently drops the ones that are not:

| class | what draws it | where it was measured |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME_STARTS_WITH_UNDERSCORE_AND_WRONG_PATTERN` | a non-root group whose name begins with `_` | [KF315](#kf315), [KF322](#kf322) |
| `CUSTOM_FIELD_TYPE_CODENAME_MISSING` | a `CustomFieldType` with no `name` member | `FieldTypeBindingLawsTest`, `FieldTypeBodyMemberLawsTest` |
| `MIN_LENGTH_BIGGER_MAX_LENGTH` | an inverted length range on a `CustomFieldType` — the same law the string carrier reports as `MVK_MIN_LENGTH_BIGGER_MAX_LENGTH` | `StringTypeParameterLawsTest` |
| `RULE_HAS_NO_ERRORTEXT` | co-fires with `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` and with `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_FOR_LANGUAGE_MISSING` — **measured 2026-09-13**: exactly when the locale has NO TEXT AT ALL (an absent row, or an empty string), never when a text exists but is whitespace only, so it is a property of the declaration rather than of either message class | `MessageSlotRawShapeLawsTest`, `RuleVariantFilterLawsTest` |
| `INVALID_GROUP` | a message parameter naming an undeclared group | [KF315](#kf315) |

**The table above is a sample, not the denominator — derived 2026-09-13.** The kernel declares its diagnostic classes in nine `*ErrorType` / `*ErrorTypesEnum` enums (`git grep -l 'enum .*ErrorType' a12-kernel --include=*.java`, excluding `delombok`, `build` and test trees), holding **344 constants**, of which **65 carry no `MVK_` prefix**: 49 in `FehlertextErrorType` — the whole error-text parameter surface — 11 in `CSVTableErrorType` and 5 in `CharsetErrorType`. Twenty-four of those 65 are named anywhere in this estate. Nothing here claims all 65 are reachable from a stored model; the number is the vocabulary's size, which is the figure a reader of the five rows above would otherwise take from them.

**Five of the unprefixed classes have an `MVK_`-prefixed TWIN, so the tail does not identify a class either.** `NO_BASE_YEAR`, `INVALID_PARAMETER`, `INVALID_ROOT_GROUP`, `INVALID_ENTITY` and `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` each exist in both spellings, as different codes in different enums. That is the prefix lesson one layer deeper, and it is not hypothetical: the first pass at the count above used `git grep INVALID_ENTITY` and returned 75 files, nearly all of them `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`. A search for one of these five needs a real word boundary — `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` — and a lift that strips or ignores the prefix merges two laws.

Two consequences, both measured here rather than reasoned:

**A prefix-keyed reader reports a refusal A12 explained as one it could not explain.** Our own law harness lifted classes by scanning for `MVK_[A-Z0-9_]+`, so each row above fell through to "the Kernel could not BUILD the model" — a materially different claim, since it says A12 reached no verdict about the declaration when it had reached one. Eleven locked rows across seven law classes stated it, and the same misreading is available to any checker that keys on the prefix.

**Scanning the message TEXT reports the author's own input as A12's verdict.** A diagnostic echoes the offending code back into its prose, so a text scan lifts it: a computation suppressing `MVK_TOTALLY_BOGUS` — a class A12 does not have — was locked as drawing `MVK_TOTALLY_BOGUS`, when A12 answers `MVK_INVALID_SUPPRESSED_WARNING`. Read the terminal `[KEY]` off each notification instead; it keys on A12's format rather than on a family of names someone listed, so it cannot miss a class this way.

**Extended 2026-09-15 — a coded notification also says WHICH declaration it judged, and it says so by PATH.** Every one of the 98 keyed notifications A12 raised over the mutated committed estate (the population `adapter.laws.CheckerClassAgreementTest` compares) reads `<Kind> with path '<absolute path>': <prose> [KEY]`. All 98 spell the kind `Rule` and all 98 judge a rule, so the kind word's behaviour on other element kinds is NOT measured here — [KF160](#kf160)'s note that A12 calls a computation "Rule" too says what to expect and is a different measurement. So a notification is POSITIONABLE without any id resolution: the path is the same absolute spelling a reader's own element paths carry, which is what lets a clean-room checker's finding be compared to A12's at the declaration rather than only in class. Two things this measurement settles that a reading of the text would not: the prefix carries no element ID, so a comparison keyed on ids needs no id→path map because there is nothing to map; and A12 answered each of those 98 mutants with exactly ONE notification, so a class-only comparison against this population cannot see a second class at all and reads as stricter than it is.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.KernelLaws.verdictOf` and the rows above; the 2026-09-15 prefix extension by `adapter.laws.CheckerClassAgreementTest`, which refuses a keyed notification it cannot position rather than degrading to a class-only comparison; a mutant on the class lift is killed by `GroupNameAlphabetLawsTest` and `DeclaredNameShapeLawsTest`.

## §12 supplement — WHAT counts as a condition referencing its error field: an ancestor reaches it, a descendant does not, and a filter's mention does not count (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf324"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §12's rule-shape account, next to the error-target path arithmetic in [KF289](#kf289).

A rule's `errorEntityRelPath` must resolve AND its condition must name the target, else `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`. That gate was already locked on one row — a condition naming a sibling is refused — which says the gate exists and nothing about what satisfies it. A checker has to answer the second question for every condition it reads, and **every spelling it fails to recognise as a reference becomes a refusal of a model A12 admits**, so the reach was measured rather than assumed.

| the condition names… | target | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| the bare name — control | `../Carrier` | ADMITTED |
| an ABSOLUTE path to the same field | `../Carrier` | ADMITTED |
| the target in the second arm of an `Or` | `../Carrier` | ADMITTED |
| the target under a negated operator (`FieldNotFilled`) | `../Carrier` | ADMITTED |
| the target as a comparison operand (`[…] == "DHL"`) | `../Carrier` | ADMITTED |
| a STARRED path to the target | `../Parcels/Weight` | ADMITTED |
| the rule's own group via the `RuleGroup` self-reference | `../Carrier` | ADMITTED |
| **the self-reference BESIDE an operand that does not reach** | `../Carrier` | **ADMITTED** |
| **the self-reference alone, target two levels down** | `../Customs/Declaration` | **ADMITTED** |
| **the self-reference beside a non-reaching operand, target two levels down** | `../Customs/Declaration` | **ADMITTED** |
| a sibling field | `../Carrier` | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` |
| **the GROUP the target sits in** | `../Parcels/Weight` | **ADMITTED** |
| **a FIELD inside the target group** | `../Parcels` | **`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`** |
| **the target inside a `Having` filter only** | `../Parcels/Weight` | **`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`** |
| an operand that resolves to nothing | `../Carrier` | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` — this gate is PRE-EMPTED |

**The containment relation runs one way, and both directions are load-bearing.** Naming the group a target field sits in reaches it, so comparing the target's own path is too strict; naming a field inside a target group does not, so treating containment as symmetric is too loose. The law is *the reference is the target or an ancestor of it*.

**A `Having` filter's own reference does not satisfy the gate**, which is the row an implementation reading condition TEXT cannot act on: once the text is scanned, the names a filter contributed are indistinguishable from an operand's. Treating them as references is the direction that stays silent, so that is what the portable checker does — a disclosed under-report rather than a guessed refusal.

**The `RuleGroup` self-reference satisfies the gate OUTRIGHT** — whatever else the condition names, and however deep the target sits. The error field must lie under the rule's own group, so naming that group reaches every possible target. rulekit's builder already treated it so, citing the kernel; the rows above are this repository's own measurement of that claim rather than a citation of it.

**Corrected 2026-09-13 — this entry's one self-reference row carried the spelling ALONE, and that hid a live over-rejection.** This entry previously recorded that the portable checker "reaches the same silence by a different route: `RuleGroup` is a keyword there, so such a condition names no entity and the family has nothing to compare". That route agrees with A12 on every row a sole self-reference produces and disagrees the moment an ordinary operand stands beside it — the checker then has something to compare, nothing reaches, and it refuses a rule A12 admits. Two models in the reference corpus are exactly that shape (`GroupFilled(RuleGroup) And NoFieldFilled(FieldMappings*)` reporting on a sibling field) and the Kernel builds both. The three bolded rows above are the measurement on the other side of that axis, and the checker now asks the self-reference question separately from the reference list rather than inheriting an answer from it. **The confound is the one no control inside the set can catch**: the single row held an unnamed constant — the self-reference was the only thing its condition named — so two mechanisms predicted the same verdict everywhere the set could look. The corpus, not the grid, is what produced the discriminating row.

**An unresolvable operand pre-empts the gate**, so a condition naming nothing that resolves draws `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` alone. A checker reporting both would name a second fix for one mistake.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.ERROR_FIELD_REFERENCE`), which additionally stays silent whenever the target's own name appears in the condition text at all other than as a path prefix — so a gap in its reference extractor cannot become a refusal.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ErrorFieldReferenceReachLawsTest` (three grids, 19 rows); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.ErrorFieldReferenceTest`, and its agreement with the Kernel on real models is `adapter.laws.CheckerSilenceOnCleanModelsTest`.

## §1 supplement — WHEN two group-list operands are the same operand twice: identity is the resolved element, containment is by path step, and a starred operand is outside the gate (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf325"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §1's group-list quantifiers, next to the diagnostic identities in [KF185](#kf185).

[KF185](#kf185) measured that the duplicate and overlap gates are two classes rather than one, on four carriers, with every operand written in the same relative spelling. That says a duplicate is refused and says nothing about what counts as one — the half an implementation needs, because **every pair it wrongly calls a duplicate is a refusal of a model A12 admits**. Rule group `/Policy`, error field `../PolicyNumber` outside every repeatable group unless a row says otherwise.

| the operand list holds… | verdict |
|---|---|
| two distinct groups — control | ADMITTED |
| the same group twice, both relative — control | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` |
| **a relative path beside the ABSOLUTE spelling of the same group** | **`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`** |
| **two groups whose NAMES share a prefix (`Garage`, `GarageBay`)** | **ADMITTED** |
| an ancestor and its child | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` |
| an ancestor and its GRANDCHILD | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` |
| the descendant named FIRST | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` |
| **one repeatable group named twice, both STARRED (`NumberOfFilledGroups(Claims*, Claims*)`)** | **ADMITTED** |
| a starred operand beside its unstarred spelling (count carrier) | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` — the wildcard gate speaks first |
| both starred, on `AllGroupsFilled`, where stars are barred | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_G_ALLOWED` |
| an UNRESOLVABLE operand beside an exact duplicate | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` — this gate is PRE-EMPTED |
| **one FIELD named twice where groups belong** | **`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`** — before the operand-KIND gate |
| a ROOT group named twice | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` |
| **the same group once in EACH of two calls** | **ADMITTED** |
| an exact duplicate and an overlap in ONE call | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` — exact wins whatever the authored order |
| an overlap in one call and an exact duplicate in another | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` alone — A12 stops at the first |
| **a duplicate in an UNGRAMMATICAL condition** (`AllGroupsFilled(Garage, Garage))`) | **`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`** — the same text with a distinct second operand is `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| **a duplicate in an UNLEXABLE condition** (an unterminated quote later in the text) | **`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`** — the same text without the duplicate is `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` |

**Identity is the RESOLVED element and containment is by path STEP.** The two bolded rows at the top run against each other on purpose: comparing authored text misses the relative-beside-absolute pair, and comparing text prefixes refuses the `Garage`/`GarageBay` pair A12 admits. Neither row alone licenses the right implementation.

**A STARRED operand is outside the gate entirely** — `NumberOfFilledGroups(Claims*, Claims*)` names one repeatable group twice and is ADMITTED. This is the same skip the field-list carriers make ([MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`), now measured on the group list, and it is the row an implementation comparing every operand gets wrong.

**The gate reads ONE CALL's operand list.** A group named once in each of two calls is admitted, so no reading of a condition's flat set of names can decide this law — the argument list has to be recovered per call. That is why the portable checker parses the condition rather than scanning it for names.

**The duplicate gate runs before the operand-KIND gate**: `AllGroupsFilled(PolicyNumber, PolicyNumber)` over a FIELD draws the duplicate class, not `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`. So the law is about the operand list and not about groups.

**And it runs before BOTH SYNTAX PHASES**, which is the row a parse-based implementation has to know. The same text with a distinct second operand draws the parser's `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`, and the same text with an unterminated quote draws the lexer's `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` — so both are genuinely broken and the duplicate is what A12 chooses to report about them. The portable checker recovers operand lists by parsing and therefore stays SILENT there, a stated under-report: the author is told about the syntax defect by the families that own it, and reading an argument list out of text whose tokens are not the ones A12's lexer saw is the one thing worse than silence.

**Both gates hold on all six group-list carriers** — `AllGroupsFilled`, `NotAllGroupsFilled`, `GroupsNotCollectivelyFilled`, `AtLeastOneGroupFilled`, `NoGroupFilled`, `NumberOfFilledGroups`; KF185 exercised four of them, and the other two are measured here. **And the class is not locus-selected**, unlike the wildcard and arity classes beside it ([KF185](#kf185)): moving the error field INSIDE the repeatable group leaves both classes unchanged — measured on `AllGroupsFilled`, which is the carrier the locus grid showed switching classes for its wildcard gate, and not re-measured on the other five.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.GROUP_LIST_OPERANDS`), which reports EVERY violating call where A12 stops at the first. That is not a divergence: each reported call is a violation A12 reaches once the earlier one is fixed.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupListDuplicateReachLawsTest` (six grids, 26 rows); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.GroupListOperandsTest`.

## §1 supplement — WHEN a group-list carrier admits a ROOT operand: three refuse one outright, three admit it alone, and a wildcard exempts it from nothing (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf326"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §1's group-list quantifiers, next to [KF185](#kf185) and [KF325](#kf325).

[KF185](#kf185) established that the root classes are real and not the overlap class renamed — the measurement a single-root fixture cannot make. What an implementation needs beyond that is the shape of the PERMISSION. Own domain (an e-commerce storefront), three roots, one of them repeatable, so "is a root" and "is repeatable" are separable; rule group `/Storefront`, error field `../OrderRef` outside every repeatable group unless a row says otherwise.

| carrier | sole root | root beside another operand |
|---|---|---|
| `AllGroupsFilled` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` |
| `NotAllGroupsFilled` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` |
| `GroupsNotCollectivelyFilled` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` |
| `AtLeastOneGroupFilled` | **ADMITTED** | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_WITH_OTHER_PARAMETERS` |
| `NoGroupFilled` | **ADMITTED** | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_WITH_OTHER_PARAMETERS` |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups` | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDGN` fixed, **ADMITTED** starred | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_WITH_OTHER_PARAMETERS` |

The count's sole-root cell is not the root's doing: that carrier's own arity gate wants two fixed groups or one starred repeatable, so a sole FIXED operand draws the arity class whether or not it is a root. `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Batches*)` over a repeatable root is admitted, which is the permission's only reachable form there.

**A STARRED root is exempt from nothing** — `AllGroupsFilled(/Batches*, Billing)` draws `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` and `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Batches*, Billing)` draws `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_WITH_OTHER_PARAMETERS`. That is the asymmetry against the duplicate gate one finding over: there the wildcard takes an operand OUT of the comparison ([KF325](#kf325)), here it leaves it fully in.

**Position and multiplicity do not matter.** The root named second draws the same class as the root named first, two disjoint roots draw one class, and the rule's OWN root beside a disjoint root does too. An implementation reading only the first operand passes every row of the first table and fails all three of these.

**Three gates pre-empt the root classes, and one does not.** An operand that resolves to nothing draws `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` alone; a root beside its own descendant draws `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2`; an unstarred repeatable co-operand draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`. A FIELD where a group belongs does NOT pre-empt them — `AllGroupsFilled(/Warehouse, Billing/Payer)` is `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED`.

**And the root classes are NOT locus-selected**, unlike the wildcard and arity classes on the same carrier. Moving the error field inside the repeatable group leaves every root verdict unchanged — including the pre-empted one: `AllGroupsFilled(/Warehouse, Lines)` is `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` from outside and `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` from inside, so the root violation holds in both anchorings and only its REPORTING order moves. That is what lets a checker report the root class without any iteration analysis.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.GROUP_LIST_ROOT_OPERAND`), evaluated after both duplicate classes so their pre-emption is honoured.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupListRootOperandLawsTest` (four grids, 29 rows); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.GroupListOperandsTest`.

## §1 supplement — the group-list QUANTIFIERS admit a FIELD operand; only the count and the two scalars refuse one (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf327"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §1's group-list quantifiers, next to [KF326](#kf326).

`MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` is `erased` in the Java kits, and the reason recorded for the erasure was *"group predicates take groups only"*. **That reason is false for five of the eight carriers.** Own domain (a lending library), rule group `/Loan`, error field `../Barcode` outside every repeatable group.

| carrier | a FIELD operand beside a group |
|---|---|
| `AllGroupsFilled` | **ADMITTED** |
| `NotAllGroupsFilled` | **ADMITTED** |
| `GroupsNotCollectivelyFilled` | **ADMITTED** |
| `AtLeastOneGroupFilled` | **ADMITTED** |
| `NoGroupFilled` | **ADMITTED** |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups` | `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` |
| `GroupFilled` (scalar) | `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` |
| `GroupNotFilled` (scalar) | `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` |

The position does not matter — the field named second is admitted on the quantifiers too — and neither does the error field's locus: the same list is admitted with the error field inside the repeatable group.

**On the five quantifiers there is no kind gate at all, so the other gates answer a list holding a field.** The same field operand beside a different second operand draws `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` (unresolvable), `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` (the same field twice), `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` (a root), `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` (an unstarred repeatable), `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` (its own enclosing GROUP — so **A12's containment relation crosses the field/group boundary**) and `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID2` (as the sole operand). An unstarred field inside a repeatable group draws the wildcard class, and its starred spelling `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_G_ALLOWED` — neither is a kind verdict.

**On the three carriers that DO refuse a field, the kind gate runs after every other gate and ahead of exactly one.** Duplicate, overlap, unresolvable and root all pre-empt it; the arity class does not — `NumberOfFilledGroups(<field>)` as a sole operand draws `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` where a sole fixed GROUP draws `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDGN`.

**Consequence for the Java kits, stated rather than left implicit.** The typed surface's `GroupRef`/`FieldRef` split is STRICTER than A12 on the five quantifiers. It stays: the erasure is on the AUTHORING path only — no read path in `rulekit` or `core` reconstructs typed operands from a stored condition (searched `rulekit/src/main/java` and `core/src/main/java` for a condition parser: no matches), so a model carrying the shape stays readable and only becomes unauthorable through the builder. The [MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) row now carries the measurement as the erasure's basis instead of the false reason.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.GROUP_LIST_OPERAND_KIND`) on the three carriers only.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupListOperandKindLawsTest` (four grids, 26 rows); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.GroupListOperandsTest`.

## §10 supplement — a repetition wildcard on anything but a repeatable group is refused in every position, ahead of both the slot's wildcard gate and the entity gate, under a class fixed by WHAT it lands on (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf328"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §10's wildcard-path rules.

`MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` is pre-checked in the Java kits, and its basis was widened in 2026-08-12 from one carrier to two with the conclusion *"the star gate is carrier-independent after all"*. Carrier-independence is a scope-transfer claim and two carriers are two carriers, so the positions below were measured rather than inherited — a portable checker applies the law to EVERY starred reference it reads, and one position where A12 says something else turns that into a wrong class. Own domain (a hotel booking); every row is run twice, once over a FIXED group and once over a repeatable one.

| position | starred FIXED group | the same star on a REPEATABLE group |
|---|---|---|
| scalar `GroupFilled` | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |
| a quantifier's operand list | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_G_ALLOWED` |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups`'s operand | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | ADMITTED |
| a starred path PREFIX in a field list | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | ADMITTED |
| a starred prefix in a scalar field slot | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |
| an aggregate's operand | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | ADMITTED |
| a computation's OPERATION | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | ADMITTED |
| a computation's common PRECONDITION | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | — |

**The control column is what makes the claim falsifiable.** The same star on a repeatable group is answered three different ways depending on where it stands — two slot classes and outright admission — and on a non-repeatable one every position collapses to this single class. So the law is about what the star LANDS ON, and it pre-empts the slot's own wildcard gate rather than sharing the field with it.

**It outruns the entity gate too, which is the opposite order from every other pair measured this week.** `FieldFilled(Guest*/NoSuchField)` — a starred fixed group followed by a leaf that resolves to nothing — draws `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` and says nothing about the leaf.

**And it is a law about each SEGMENT, not about the reference.** A star on a FIELD, on the model ROOT, and on a FIXED group nested UNDER a legitimately starred repeatable one (`Nights*/Rate*/Amount`) all draw it, while the same reference with only the legitimate star (`Nights*/Rate/Amount`) is admitted. A rule reading the reference as a whole answers one of those two wrongly whichever way it is written.

**The member that decides it is `Group.repeatability`, an INTEGER whose default is 1 — there is no boolean `repeatable`.** Recorded here because the portable checker was written against the invented boolean for an hour and every one of its own tests passed: the fixtures beside it carried the same invented member, so implementation and evidence agreed with each other and not with A12. On a real model it would have refused every correctly starred group. `FixtureRepetitionMemberGuardTest` now derives the accepted spelling from the kits' own emitter and scans the checker's sources for any other.
