**Extended 2026-09-13 — the class is not one class. A star on a segment that is not a NAME draws a code of its own**, which the first pass here left unmeasured and the checker therefore left silent. Both were reachable in one grid:

| the star lands on… | anchoring | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| the rule-context entity (`RuleGroup*`) | any rule | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD_FOR_RULEGROUP` |
| …the same unstarred — control | any rule | ADMITTED |
| a LEADING up-step (`..*/Extras`) | a rule one level down | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD_REL` |
| a leading up-step with nothing after it (`..*`) | a rule one level down | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD_REL` |
| …the same step unstarred — control | a rule one level down | ADMITTED |
| a starred up-step (`..*/Extras`) | a ROOT-level rule | `MVK_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS` |
| …the same step unstarred — control | a ROOT-level rule | `MVK_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS` |
| a MID-PATH up-step (`Guest/..*/Extras`) | any rule | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| …the same mid-path step unstarred — control | any rule | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |

**Two of those rows are pre-emptions rather than wildcard verdicts, and their controls are what say so.** From a root-level rule the up-step leaves the model and the DEPTH class answers before any star is considered; a `..` outside the leading run is not valid A12 at all, starred or not, so the parser answers first. Only the nested anchoring reaches the wildcard gate, which is why a grid anchored where the rest of this entry is anchored could not have found the class — the root-level row looks like a measurement and reports on a different gate.

**A star on a leading up-step also PARSES.** `GroupFilled(..*)` is refused semantically, not syntactically, which is a fact about the grammar rather than about the gate: a reader treating `..` and `*` as a product accepts `..*/Extras` by accident (as division) and refuses `..*` outright, and is wrong both times.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.REPETITION_WILDCARD_TARGET`) under all three classes. It leaves alone: a starred segment whose own prefix does not resolve, a starred named turning point (`..Ancestor*`, unmeasured), and — a disclosed under-report — a reference that is nothing but starred up-steps, which its reference reader does not report as a reference at all.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.StarredNonRepeatableReachLawsTest` (four grids, 31 rows, two carriers); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.RepetitionWildcardTest`, and its agreement with the Kernel on real models is `adapter.laws.CheckerSilenceOnCleanModelsTest`.

## §11 supplement — a computation may not compute into a GROUP, and the rule slot that resolves identically ADMITS one (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf329"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside [KERNEL-SEMANTICS](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md) §11's computation account, next to the computed-field rules.

A rule's `errorEntityRelPath` and a computation's `computedFieldRelPath` are the same kind of member — a relative path to a declared element, read by the same reader, resolving the same way — so an implementation judges them alike unless something says not to. A12 says not to, in one direction only.

| the target resolves to… | as a computation's computed field | as a rule's error target |
|---|---|---|
| a sibling FIELD — control | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |
| a **FIXED group** | **NOT BUILDABLE** | **ADMITTED** |
| a **REPEATABLE group** | **NOT BUILDABLE** | **ADMITTED** |
| a field inside a fixed group | ADMITTED | — |
| nothing | NOT BUILDABLE | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING` ([KF289](#kf289)) |

**A12 has a key for this and never reaches it.** `MVK_GROUP_AS_CALCULATED_FIELD` is in the vocabulary, but the Kernel's BUILDER refuses a group-valued computed field before `checkConsistency` runs, so no consumer ever sees that key from this shape — the same tier, and for the same reason, as a computed field naming nothing. A checker reporting the `MVK_*` key here would claim a verdict A12 does not issue; the portable checker reports `CK_MODEL_NOT_BUILDABLE`, the code it owns for exactly this tier.

**The group KIND does not enter it**, which is the row worth having rather than assuming: fixed and repeatable are refused alike, so no repetition reasoning is involved and a checker needs none.

**The rule column is not extra coverage — it is the control that keeps the two slots apart.** Without it an implementation refusing a group in both slots looks correct and refuses a legal model on every rule that reports on a group; with only the rule column, the computation's law is invisible. Neither slot's row implies the other's, and the members are similar enough that nothing but a measurement separates them.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.COMPUTED_TARGET_KIND`). The shape exists only in stored DM-JSON: the kits' computed-field slot is a typed field handle, which is why `MVK_GROUP_AS_CALCULATED_FIELD` sits in the ledger's `erased` bucket.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputedFieldTargetKindLawsTest` (two grids, 8 rows); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.ComputedTargetKindTest`.

## §11 supplement — a computation may not compute into a group's INDEX field, and the sort field beside it may be computed freely (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf330"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure law on the computation's target slot, outside the evaluation scope.

**A12 has a key for this and reaches it**, unlike the group-valued target next door: computing into the field a repeatable group declares as its `indexFieldName` draws `MVK_ERROR_INDEX_AS_CALCULATED_FIELD` from `checkConsistency`, a verdict a consumer receives rather than a refusal to build. The law had never been put to the Kernel before — [MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) carried it as prose and no lock named the code.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| a computation writing into an ordinary sibling in the indexed group | ADMITTED |
| …into the group's `indexFieldName` field | **`MVK_ERROR_INDEX_AS_CALCULATED_FIELD`** |
| …into a field named by the group's `sortFields` | ADMITTED |
| …into the index field, declared OUTSIDE the repeatable group | **`MVK_ERROR_INDEX_AS_CALCULATED_FIELD`** |
| …into an ordinary field of that group, declared outside it | ADMITTED |
| a RULE reporting on the index field | ADMITTED |

**The SORT field is the row that makes this about the INDEX.** `indexFieldName` and `sortFields[].name` are both direct-child field references declared by the group, read by the same code and resolved the same way — our own checker reaches them through one shared helper — so "a field the group names" and "the field the group is identified by" are indistinguishable without this row. Only the second is refused.

**The law follows the TARGET, not the computation's own group.** A computation declared outside the repeatable group draws the same class, so an implementation may key on the resolved field alone. Measured rather than transferred from the inside-the-group row: the reuse would have needed no new branch, which is the tell the scope-transfer rule names.

**Its control needed a control.** The first outside-the-group row used a computation whose own operation sums `Fee` and wrote into `Fee`, so it drew `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` — a self-read, not the locus under test. A field the operation does not read is admitted, which is what makes the index row above about the index.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.COMPUTED_TARGET_INDEX_FIELD`).

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputedFieldTargetKindLawsTest` (three grids, 14 rows); the portable checker's mirror is `consistency.ComputedTargetKindTest`.

## §10 supplement — `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_INVALID` is the CONDITION-side index lookup, and it is reachable (source + measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf331"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure reference law reached from a condition's semantic index.

**The ledger described this code's locus wrongly, and the description is what made it look like unfinished work.** It read "a group's declared index field must exist in that group" — a shape [KF295](#kf295) measures **NOT BUILDABLE with no code at all**, so no consumer could ever have seen this key from it. The firing site is `CheckEntityUtils.getIndexField` (`kernel-core-parser`), whose message is *"For '%s' the used index field '%s' does not exist."* — reached when a CONDITION uses a semantic index over a group and that group's declared index field cannot be resolved as a field of it.

**That leaves exactly one shape where the two can meet, and it is the shape [KF295](#kf295) already isolated.** An `indexFieldName` that RESOLVES but lands outside its own group does not stop the build — it draws `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` as a verdict — so the model reaches the condition phase carrying an index declaration the lookup cannot use.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| a usable index field, with a semantic index over that group | ADMITTED |
| an index field resolving OUTSIDE its group, with a semantic index over that group | **`MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD`, `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_INVALID`** |
| the same unusable index field, with NO semantic index | `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` |

**The pair of controls is what makes the attribution, and each moves one variable.** The same condition over a usable index is admitted, so the class is not the semantic index's; the same unusable index without a semantic index draws only the declaration's own class, so the second class is not the declaration's. Both rows are the same model differing in one builder input.

**Not reported by the portable checker, deliberately.** It already names this defect through `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` on the declaration itself (`CheckFamily.GROUP_ORDERING_REFERENCES`), so a consumer of the checker already learns the model is refused and why. Emitting the second class would add a code without adding reach, and would require the checker to recognise semantic-index usage in condition text — a capability it has no other use for today.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupIndexAndSortReferenceLawsTest.whetherTheConditionSideIndexLookupIsReachable`.

## §10 supplement — the two MULTIPLE-index codes are CONDITION-side, one is reachable and the other has no stored spelling (source + measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf332"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-structure law reached from a condition's index resolution.

**Both were recorded as declaration laws and neither is.** They are thrown from `CheckEntityUtils.getIndexGroup`, which walks an entity's ancestor groups and is reached from `checkParallelIteration` — so the declaration alone never triggers them, and the framing mattered: it made them look like local structural families a Kernel-free checker could own.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| one indexed group on the path, with a semantic index over it | ADMITTED |
| an ANCESTOR group also declaring an index, same condition | **`MVK_MULTIPLE_INDEX_FIELDS`** |
| the same two indexed groups with NO semantic index | **ADMITTED** |
| `indexFieldNames: ["Sku","Count"]` beside the singular member, same condition | ADMITTED |

**Two indexed groups on one path are legal until a condition asks for the index**, which is the row that decides an implementation: a checker reporting this from the declarations alone would refuse a model A12 accepts. That is why it is not a local declaration family, and the reason is measured rather than argued from the call graph.

**`MVK_MULTIPLE_INDEX_FIELDS2` has no stored spelling that reaches it.** `IGroup.getIndexFieldNames()` is a `Set`, so the kernel's own model admits several names per group and the code guards exactly that; DM-JSON writes the singular `indexFieldName`, and a plural `indexFieldNames` member sitting beside it is not read — `getIndexGroup` still sees one name and the model is admitted. Since the surrounding rows prove `getIndexGroup` runs on this condition, the admission is the member being ignored rather than the check being skipped. Reachable only through a model built in memory, not through stored DM-JSON.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupIndexAndSortReferenceLawsTest.whatTheMultipleIndexCodesNeed`.

## §11 supplement — three predicates are prohibited in a computation's PRECONDITION, ordinary in a rule, and a grammar error in the operation beside it (source + measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf333"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a slot-scoped language restriction, not a property of the operators themselves.

**The denominator comes from the source, because naming a subset is the failure this estate keeps repeating.** `NormalisierteBerechnungsFormHelper` (kernel `30.8.1`) refuses exactly three language features in a normalized calculation condition, in an `if / else if / else if` chain, each reporting `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_LANGUAGE_FEATURE` with the offending terminal's own spelling interpolated: the legacy count-given op (`ANZAHL_ANGEGEBENE_USB`), an application condition (`APPLIKATIONS_BEDINGUNG`, spelled `CustomCondition`), then `WIEDERHOLUNG_NICHT_EINDEUTIG` (`RepetitionNotUnique`).

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| an ordinary precondition on the alternative — the control | ADMITTED |
| `CustomCondition` in the alternative's `precondition` | **`MVK_ERROR_INVALID_LANGUAGE_FEATURE`** |
| `RepetitionNotUnique` in the alternative's `precondition` | **`MVK_ERROR_INVALID_LANGUAGE_FEATURE`** |
| `CustomCondition` in the computation's `commonPrecondition` | **`MVK_ERROR_INVALID_LANGUAGE_FEATURE`** |
| `CustomCondition` in a RULE's `errorCondition` | ADMITTED |
| `RepetitionNotUnique` in a RULE's `errorCondition` | ADMITTED |
| `RepetitionNotUnique` in the alternative's `operation` | **`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`** |

**The restriction is on the SLOT, not on the operator.** Both predicates are ordinary in a rule condition, so a consumer that refused them wherever it met them would refuse a legal model. And the operation row says the slot distinction is sharper than "reported more often": the same text one member along draws A12's *grammar* vocabulary instead, because an operation is not a condition — so a reader that judged both string members of an alternative alike would answer with the wrong class, not merely too eagerly.

**Both precondition carriers reach it**, which follows from the mechanism rather than being assumed from one of them: the helper judges the NORMALIZED condition, into which the common precondition and the alternative's own guard are both folded, and each carrier is measured.

**Only two of the three are authorable from an `en_US` model.** The count-given op has no English spelling — it is a DE-only terminal with no catalog id — so the first arm of the chain is a stated boundary here, not a measurement, and nothing above claims anything about it.

Reported by the portable checker as `CheckFamily.COMPUTATION_PRECONDITION_FEATURES`, for the two English-spellable features only.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationPreconditionLanguageFeatureLawsTest`.

## §11 supplement — computations may not depend on each other in a CIRCLE, a precondition read builds that circle, and a one-node circle is a different code (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf334"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a whole-model graph law over the computation declarations.

**A12 sorts the calculated fields topologically before it generates anything** (`CodeGenCalcBuilder.getCalculatedFields`) and refuses a graph it cannot order, reporting `MVK_ERROR_CALC_CYCLE` with the cycle spelled out. The law reads only declarations — which field each computation writes, which fields its own members read — so it is decidable without a document.

| stored shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| an acyclic chain (`Weight ← Base`, `Volume ← Weight`) — the control | ADMITTED |
| two computations reading each other | **`MVK_ERROR_CALC_CYCLE`** |
| a three-step circle | **`MVK_ERROR_CALC_CYCLE`** |
| one computation reading its own target | **`MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD`** |
| the back edge carried by an alternative's `precondition`, not by an operation | **`MVK_ERROR_CALC_CYCLE`** |
| the back edge through a field no computation writes — the control | ADMITTED |
| a circle whose two ends sit in different groups (an aggregate over a repeatable group's field, and an absolute read back out of it) | **`MVK_ERROR_CALC_CYCLE`** |

**A PRECONDITION read is an edge.** The row matters because the two members look nothing alike — one is a condition, the other an operation, and a field read is spelled `FieldFilled(Volume)` in the first and `[Volume]` in the second — so an implementation reading only `operation` is the natural one to write, and it would admit a model A12 refuses.

**A one-node circle is NOT this code, which is the pre-emption an implementation cannot infer.** A computation reading its own target is a cycle of length one in any graph, and A12 answers it with `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` ([KF181](#kf181), [KF182](#kf182) for its projected variant). Reporting the cycle class there would name a verdict A12 never reached.

**The graph is over RESOLVED fields, not over declaration sites.** The cross-group row is measured rather than transferred from the same-group rows: it closes its circle through `Sum(Crates*/Cost)` in one direction and an absolute `[/Depot/Weight]` read in the other, and is refused exactly like two sibling reads — so keying on the resolved path alone is correct.

Reported by the portable checker as `CheckFamily.COMPUTATION_CYCLE`, which drops the self-loop for the reason above.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationDependencyCycleLawsTest`.

## §13 supplement — which CLASS each message-parameter shape draws, and that a computation's message is gated by its own members (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf335"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the implementation boundary of the parameter membership gate, not a new parameter form.

**[KF198](#kf198) and `RuleMessageParameterLawsTest` measure the parameter SURFACE; this measures what a reader of it may report.** Every shape below looks like a bad field reference, and only two of them are one — so a checker recognising the plain form and answering its class for everything else would over-reject, which is the one direction this project forbids.

| the message says, with a condition that reads `Reference` only | A12 |
|---|---|
| `$Reference$` — the control | ADMITTED |
| no parameter at all — the control | ADMITTED |
| `$Premium$`, a sibling the condition does not read | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `$Premium.value$`, the same field with a suffix | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `$NoSuchField$`, which resolves to nothing | **`INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `$Claims$`, a GROUP the condition does not read | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `$Claims/Payout$`, a pathed field the condition does not read | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `cost 5$$` — an escaped dollar, no parameter | ADMITTED |
| `cost 5$` — a lone dollar | **`WRONG_NUMBER_OF_DOLLARS`** |
| `see $Premium`, unterminated around a real unread field | **`WRONG_NUMBER_OF_DOLLARS`** |
| `$$Premium$ x`, an escaped dollar running into a name | **`WRONG_NUMBER_OF_DOLLARS`** |
| `$index$`, a field named after an uncataloged keyword | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `$Date$`, a field named after a CATALOGED operator | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `$'Date'$`, the same single-quoted | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `see $Premium$$Adjuster$`, two parameters sharing a dollar pair | **`INVALID_FIELD,INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `see $Prem$$ium$`, the pair inside what would be one name | **`INVALID_ENTITY,INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `see $Premium$ and $Adjuster`, a closed parameter before an unterminated one | **`WRONG_NUMBER_OF_DOLLARS`** |
| `$/Policy/Premium$`, an ABSOLUTE path | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `$../Premium$` from a rule in a ROOT group | **`ERROR_TEXT_PARAMETER_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS`** |

**Two of those are the rows an implementation would get wrong.** A name that resolves to NOTHING is `INVALID_ENTITY`, not the membership class — so answering every unknown parameter with `INVALID_FIELD` names a verdict A12 did not give. And a GROUP draws `INVALID_FIELD` too, not `INVALID_GROUP`: the membership gate does not care what kind it found, so keying the class on the resolved element's kind is wrong in the other direction.

**A parameter path is ordinary: absolute works, and `..` has its own class.** `ERROR_TEXT_PARAMETER_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS` is a second unprefixed class this family meets ([KF323](#kf323) counts the estate), and the row covers only a rule declared in a ROOT group — from there one `..` already leaves the outermost group, so nothing here says whether a legal `..` behaves like a condition's.

**No non-plain segment can name a real field, because A12 refuses the NAME.** `$'Claim Total'$` is the shape a quoting rule seems to invite, and the field cannot exist: adding `Claim Total` to a model draws `MVK_PATH_INVALID` for the whole model. So a reader narrowing itself to plain segments loses nothing measurable — which is also why no mutant can kill that narrowing, and why it is kept deliberately rather than as untested defence.

**An unterminated parameter refuses the text WHOLE.** The last row is the one that says so: the parameter A12 did close draws nothing at all, so a reader keeping what it collected before it lost the thread reports the membership class on a text A12 answered with the dollar count alone.

**`$$` is the escape only OUTSIDE a parameter — inside one, the first `$` closes it.** The two readings are not distinguishable on a single-class verdict, which is why the last two rows are there: A12 answers each with TWO classes, one per parameter, and the escape reading has only one name to judge. So `$Premium$$Adjuster$` is two parameters, both refused for membership, and a reader treating the pair as a literal dollar stays silent on a model A12 refuses twice.

**A parameter is NOT resolved against the condition lexer's terminals.** A field named after a keyword is an ordinary reference here, cataloged (`Date`) or not (`index`), bare or single-quoted — all draw the membership class. A checker holding the condition language's terminal table is tempted to exempt such names for safety; the exemption only hides real findings, and this repository shipped one until the mutant that removed it survived every row.

**A COMPUTATION's message is gated as well, by its own members.** This was the reverse of the first two readings taken of it, both of which came from a broken fixture:

| a computation into `Premium`, operation `1` | A12 |
|---|---|
| `$Premium$` — the computed target | ADMITTED |
| `$Adjuster$` — a field the computation never touches | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `$Bonus$` with operation `[Bonus] + 1` | ADMITTED |
| `$NoSuchField$` | **`INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| operation `[NoSuchField] + 1` — the vacuity control | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |

So the law belongs to the MESSAGE member rather than to the rule, and the membership set is whatever its own carrier reads: a rule's condition references, or a computation's target plus what its operation reads. A family skipping computations under-reports.

**The vacuity control is in the grid and not beside it, because it caught the measurement twice.** The first version injected the computation with a regex that matched nothing, so every row read ADMITTED off an unmodified model and the table said computations are ungated. The second had the computation's operation read its own target, so its "control" drew `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` — a different law. Neither is visible without a row that A12 must refuse.

**On a rule the error target is necessarily inside the membership set, so there is no second term to find.** Trying to build the pair that separates "the condition reads it" from "it is the error target" produces a different refusal instead — `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`, since A12 requires every rule's error field to appear among its condition's references ([KF35](#kf35), `ErrorFieldReferenceReachLawsTest`). The impossibility is the result.

Reported by the portable checker as `CheckFamily.MESSAGE_PARAMETER_REFERENCE`, for the plain parameter form only.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageParameterMembershipLawsTest`.

## §13 supplement — a message parameter's ADDRESS is answered in A12's own unprefixed vocabulary, outcome for outcome (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf336"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the error-text surface's diagnostic vocabulary, not an evaluation behaviour.

**[KF335](#kf335) measures whether a parameter may name an entity; this measures what A12 says when it cannot FIND one.** The same four resolution outcomes that draw `MVK_*` codes inside a condition draw unprefixed `FehlertextErrorType` members in a message — and the spellings do not follow one rule, so neither stripping the prefix nor reusing the condition arm produces this table.

| the address | inside a CONDITION | inside an error MESSAGE |
|---|---|---|
| resolves to nothing, below the declaring group | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` | **`INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| resolves to nothing, at ROOT-GROUP level | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP` | **`INVALID_ROOT_GROUP`** |
| a short name several fields carry | `MVK_FIELDNAME_NOT_UNIQUE` | **`ERROR_TEXT_FIELDNAME_NOT_UNIQUE`** |
| a `..` that climbs past the root group | `MVK_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS` | **`ERROR_TEXT_PARAMETER_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS`** |

Two of the four are the condition code's tail and two are not, and the two that are (`INVALID_ENTITY`, `INVALID_ROOT_GROUP`) are among the five classes [KF323](#kf323) names as sharing a tail with an `MVK_` code — so a search for either spelling needs `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` to tell the surfaces apart.

**The short-name fallback is LOCAL-FIRST and then model-wide, and only the second tier can be ambiguous.** This is what makes the uniqueness row reachable at all, and a fixture carrying only a duplicated name the declaring group OWNS cannot show it:

| the parameter, with the condition reading the same entity | A12 |
|---|---|
| a bare name the declaring group owns, carried in another group too | ADMITTED |
| the same bare name written from that OTHER group | ADMITTED |
| a bare name the declaring group does NOT own, unique in the model | ADMITTED |
| a bare name the declaring group does NOT own, carried by two groups | **`ERROR_TEXT_FIELDNAME_NOT_UNIQUE`** |
| the same, written as a path | ADMITTED |

The third row is the one that keeps the account honest: without it, the local hit explains every admission and a local-only rule fits the set exactly as well as the two-tier one. The fallback's second tier is gated on the model's `fieldRefByShortNameAllowed` — a checker whose fixture leaves it off measures the fallback as absent and reports the unresolvable class instead (caught here that way).

**A `..` step is ordinary; only the OVERSHOOT is refused.** From a rule in a root group one `..` already leaves the outermost group, so the refusal measured there says nothing about the step itself — from a rule one level down, `$../Premium$` is ADMITTED and judged for membership like any other address. A path ENDING in the step is an address too: `$..$` names the group it lands on and draws `INVALID_FIELD` there, so the step is not restricted to a prefix position.

**And `$BaseYear$` is none of these.** It is a terminal of the message grammar, ADMITTED where the model declares a base year and `NO_BASE_YEAR` where it does not ([KF198](#kf198)) — so a reader reporting unresolvable addresses must exclude the grammar's own terminals first, or it over-rejects on a parameter A12 admits. Every other terminal form carries a character no plain name admits and is refused earlier.

Reported by the portable checker as `ReferenceRole.MESSAGE_PARAMETER`, inside `CheckFamily.MESSAGE_PARAMETER_REFERENCE`.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageParameterShortNameLawsTest`.

## §13 supplement — an error message's control characters draw two classes, and the gates are ORDERED (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf337"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the error-text surface's character law, outside KERNEL-SEMANTICS's evaluation scope.

**The whole law is a character predicate, which makes this the cheapest check the error-text surface has** — and it splits in two, where a reader would expect one.

| the message text carries | A12 |
|---|---|
| printable text — the control | ADMITTED |
| a line feed, a carriage return, or a CRLF pair | **`INVALID_LINEBREAK`**, beside a CODELESS runtime diagnostic ("Only values without line breaks are allowed.") |
| a tab, NUL, BEL or DEL | **`INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| U+001F, the last C0 control | **`INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| U+0080 and U+009F, both ends of C1 | **`INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| U+0020, a plain space | ADMITTED |
| U+00A0, a non-breaking space | ADMITTED |
| **a line break AND a tab** | **`INVALID_LINEBREAK`** only |
| **a tab BEFORE a line break** | **`INVALID_LINEBREAK`** only |

**The last two rows are what an implementation turns on.** The gates run in ORDER rather than independently: the tab beside a line break draws nothing, so a reader reporting each kind it finds names a verdict A12 did not give — on exactly the text an author produces by pasting, which is the likeliest real input here. And the order is keyed on the KIND present, not on position: reversing the pair changes nothing, which is what separates "the line-break gate runs first" from "the first offending character decides". Both readings agree on every text where the break comes first, so a grid without the reversed row cannot tell them apart — measured here because a mutant swapping the two tests survived the row that had them in that order.

**The refused set is the ISO control blocks**, both ends measured — `U+0000`–`U+001F` and `U+007F`–`U+009F`, with the space and the non-breaking space outside them. A repertoire restriction is a *different* law: the charset refusal for a supplementary-plane code point carries no class at all ([KF279](#kf279)), so a family keying on the charset would answer a different question with the wrong code.

**A COMPUTATION's message meets the same two classes**, and without the codeless runtime diagnostic the rule rows carry beside them — that one belongs to the rule member rather than to the text. So the law is the message member's, as [KF335](#kf335) found for membership.

Reported by the portable checker as `CheckFamily.MESSAGE_TEXT_CHARACTERS`.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageTextControlCharacterLawsTest`.

## §13 supplement — a broken CONDITION withholds the message parameter's verdict entirely (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf338"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the error-text checker's dependence on a sibling member, not an evaluation behaviour.

**A12 does not judge a message parameter on a rule whose condition is unsound — it reports the condition's class and nothing about the message.** `FehlertextErrorType` even carries a class saying so (`INVALID_CONDITION`, "a text with a parameter can only be checked on rules with valid conditions"), and what is actually emitted is just the condition's own verdict:

| the rule | A12 |
|---|---|
| a valid condition, a parameter it does not read — the control | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |
| `FieldFilled(NoSuchField)`, the same parameter beside it | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** only |
| `FieldFilled(NoSuchField)`, a plain text — the control | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| `FieldFilled(`, the same parameter beside it | **`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`** only |
| a valid condition, a TAB in the text — the control | **`INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| `FieldFilled(NoSuchField)`, the same TAB in the text | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** only |
| a COMPUTATION with operation `[NoSuchField] + 1`, a TAB in the text | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** only |
| the same computation, a parameter it does not read | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** only |

The second row against the third is the measurement: the verdict is identical whether the message carries a parameter or not, so the parameter's class is WITHHELD rather than accompanied.

**It withholds the WHOLE error-text checker, not the parameter law.** The last pair is the sweep that says so: a control character in the text draws `INVALID_CHARACTERS` beside a valid condition and nothing at all beside a broken one — and that check needs nothing from the condition, so it could as easily have run regardless. So A12 declines to examine the message member at all, and every family reading that member answers to it.

**The gate is "this declaration's own DSL is sound", not anything about conditions.** The computation rows say so: that carrier has no condition, its broken member is an OPERATION, and both error-text verdicts give way to its class exactly as a rule's do. Naming the law after conditions would have been the carrier's accident.

**This is a cross-member dependency, which is the shape a family-per-member checker gets wrong by construction.** Each family reads its own member and reports what it finds, so one with a broken condition and a message beside it draws a parameter class A12 gave no sign of. The shape is not exotic: a half-typed condition is the ordinary state of a model being edited, and that is exactly when a checker is asked.

Reported by the portable checker as a WITHHOLDING — `CheckFamily.MESSAGE_PARAMETER_REFERENCE` and `CheckFamily.MESSAGE_TEXT_CHARACTERS` both fall silent for such a declaration, through one shared gate. Its stand-in for "does not parse" is an unbalanced delimiter, a necessary condition rather than a grammar, so balanced-but-refused text keeps its parameters judged — an under-report, which is the safe direction.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageParameterConditionDependencyLawsTest`.

## §13 supplement — a rule's error TARGET is examined first, and its failure ends the rule (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf339"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**[KF338](#kf338) found one withholding; this is the second, and it is wider.** A rule whose `errorEntityRelPath` does not resolve draws its two target codes and NOTHING else — not the condition's class, not either error-text class:

| the rule | A12 |
|---|---|
| both members sound — the control | ADMITTED |
| the error TARGET names nothing | **`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING,MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD`** |
| the CONDITION names nothing | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| **BOTH name nothing** | **`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING,MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD`** |
| the target names nothing, a control character in the text | the same pair |
| the target names nothing, a parameter the condition does not read | the same pair |
| a SOUND target, the same control character — the twin | **`INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| a SOUND target, the same parameter — the twin | **`INVALID_FIELD`** |

**The two twins are what make the withheld rows mean anything.** Without them, "the error-text class was withheld" and "this fixture never draws that class" are indistinguishable — those classes are measured elsewhere, on other fixtures, which is exactly the instrument a constant hides behind.

**Row four against rows two and three is the measurement.** Each member alone produces its own class; together they produce only the target's. So the target is examined first and its failure ends the rule, rather than the two members being judged independently and their classes unioned.

**An independent corroboration was already in the estate and had been read the other way.** [KF305](#kf305) measured a rule targeting a field a `variantFilter` removes and recorded `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING,MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD` with the comment "A12 answers with the error-target pair rather than the entity code" — the same law, on a different cause for the target's failure. The checker's MIRROR of that row nevertheless asserted the union of both codes and sat green, because nothing compares a mirror against the laws test it mirrors.

**How far past the DSL members the withholding reaches is NOT settled.** The discriminator tried for it — an illegal rule name, to see whether a non-member defect still reports — makes the model unbuildable and therefore moves two variables, so it is recorded here as a probe that could not decide rather than as a row. The portable checker takes the conservative reading and withholds every finding at such a declaration's path except those A12 gives about the target itself.

**A PATH does not identify a declaration, which bounds what a checker may do with this.** An element's path is its parent plus its NAME with no kind, so a rule and a field sharing a name in one group share a path — a model A12 refuses and a checker reports, so the shape is reachable. A withholding keyed on the path would delete the FIELD's findings, which A12 withheld nothing about, so a shared path is left alone.

Reported by the portable checker as a WITHHOLDING applied where the report is assembled, not inside any family: it is A12 declining to examine the declaration, and a family-local version would have to be repeated into every family added later.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleMemberVerdictWithholdingLawsTest`.

## §13 supplement — inside a condition, a name that does not resolve withholds the syntax classes beside it (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf340"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**Corrected 2026-09-13: this entry first read these rows as "reference resolution runs FIRST and wins over every syntax class", and that account is false.** Every row below puts the bad name FIRST in the text, so "resolution wins" and "the earlier defect in the text wins" predict all of them identically — the constant no control inside the set can catch. Reversing the pair brings the syntax class back, and the true account with its grid is [KF342](#kf342). The measurements here stand; only the mechanism was wrong.

**[KF339](#kf339) found A12 stopping between a rule's members; this is the same stop INSIDE one.** Each syntax class fires on its own and is withheld when the same text also carries a name that does not resolve *ahead of it*:

| the `errorCondition` | A12 |
|---|---|
| sound — the control | ADMITTED |
| `FieldFilled(NoSuchField)` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `FieldFilled(NoSuchField) And FieldFilled(AlsoMissing)` — two bad names | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`**, once |
| `FieldFilled(Reference) And` — a trailing operator alone | **`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT`** |
| `FieldFilled(NoSuchField) And` — the same, with a bad name | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `FieldFilled(Reference` — an unclosed delimiter alone | **`MVK_EXPECTED_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND`** |
| `FieldFilled(NoSuchField` — the same, with a bad name | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `… And And …` — an unexpected token alone | **`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`** |
| the same, with a bad name | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |

**Each withheld row sits directly under the row that fires it alone**, which is what makes "withheld" separable from "this text never draws that class".

**It is NOT "parse, then resolve".** `FieldFilled(NoSuchField` cannot be parsed — the delimiter is unclosed, and that alone draws `MVK_EXPECTED_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND` — yet with a bad name inside it the entity class still wins. So resolution is not running on a parse tree the syntax check already approved. (This row survives the correction above: resolution reaching an unparseable text is what makes text order, rather than a phase order, the surviving account.)

**Two bad names draw ONE class, not one per name.** A reader emitting a finding per reference says more than A12 did, though nothing A12 did not — a count divergence rather than a class one, and left as is because the per-reference finding is what tells an author which name to fix.

**This is the shape a family-per-defect-kind checker gets wrong on ordinary input.** ELEVEN families read the same condition text and each reports what it finds, so any condition carrying two defects — the normal state of one being written — draws classes A12 withheld. Nothing in the portable checker's suite had covered a text with two defects at once.

Reported by the portable checker as a WITHHOLDING applied where the report is assembled, listed as the condition-text codes to DROP rather than the codes to keep: a family added later that reads that text is then an under-report until its code is listed, where a keep-list would silently start dropping it.

**And it is per DECLARATION, not per text.** On a computation, a name that does not resolve in the PRECONDITION withholds the syntax class of the OPERATION beside it, and two bad names in the two members still draw one class — so the ordering spans a declaration's whole DSL rather than each text separately (`ComputationMemberVerdictLawsTest`).

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ConditionMultipleDefectLawsTest` and `…ComputationMemberVerdictLawsTest`.

## §13 supplement — a FIELD TYPE reports every defect it carries, which bounds the withholding class (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf341"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**[KF339](#kf339) and [KF340](#kf340) found A12 stopping at the first failure; this is the member where it does not.** The same question, asked of a field's type:

| `Reference`'s `StringType` | A12 |
|---|---|
| `{}` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `{"pattern":"a++"}` | **`MVK_PATTERN_INVALID,MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_AND_PATTERN_INVALID`** |
| `{"noValueValidation":true}` | **`MVK_STRING_TYPE_NO_VAL_AND_NO_LINE_BREAK`** |
| **both on one field** | **all three of the above, plus `MVK_STRING_TYPE_PARAMS_INCONSISTENT`** |

**So the stop is a property of particular members and must never be assumed from a neighbour.** Two members in this estate stop at their first failure and this one reports everything — measured in the same session, on the same kernel, hours apart. A checker generalising the withholding from a rule's members to a field's type would fall silent on input A12 answers in full.

**A FOURTH class appears that neither defect produces alone**: `noValueValidation` beside a `pattern` is its own refusal. This matters beyond the row, because **every other grid in this estate varies one defect at a time**, and a combination-only class is structurally unreachable that way — it is not that such rows were tried and found empty, it is that the shape was never built. The portable checker already emits this one, so nothing was missing here; what the row establishes is that the method has a blind spot, not that this instance cost anything.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldTypeMultipleDefectLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … FieldTypeMultipleDefectTest`.

## §13 supplement — inside a condition A12 reports the FIRST defect in the text, and two relational classes lose to all of them (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf342"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**[KF340](#kf340) said reference resolution runs first and wins. It does not — it wins when it comes first, and loses when it does not.** Every pair KF340 held put the bad name at the head of the text, so its account and this one made identical predictions on all of them; reversing the position separates them in one row. Each class below is measured three times — alone, with a bad name after it, and with the same bad name ahead of it:

| the defect beside `FieldFilled(NoSuchField)` | alone | bad name AFTER it | bad name BEFORE it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FieldFilled("Reference)` — an unclosed literal | `MVK_LEXER_STANDARD_ERROR` | — (the literal swallows it) | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `A And B Or C` — mixed connectives | `MVK_BRACKET_MISSING` | `MVK_BRACKET_MISSING` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `GroupFilled(/Policy/Archive)` — an empty group | `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` | `MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `AllGroupsFilled(X, X)` — one group twice | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `AllGroupsFilled(/Registry, X)` — a root group | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `GroupFilled(X/Notes)` — a field where a group belongs | `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` | `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `GroupFilled(X*)` — a star on a fixed group | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| `… And And …` — an unexpected token | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** (KF340) |

**The middle column is the whole finding.** KF340 had no middle column, and without it "resolution runs first" was untestable.

**Two classes are not in that competition at all — they lose wherever the bad name sits:**

| the relational class | alone | bad name AFTER it | ahead of an empty group |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` — the error target is not among the condition's references | fires | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** | **`MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY`** |
| `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_LANGUAGE_FEATURE` — an app condition in a computation's precondition | fires | **`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`** | **`MVK_GROUP_IS_EMPTY`** |

**The third column shows the bad name is not special.** Any other condition-text defect withholds these two, so the trigger is "something else spoke about this text", not "a name did not resolve". Both are relations over the condition's *resolved references* rather than a defect at an offset in it, which is a plausible reason they behave alike and is **not** measured — what is measured is that their position does not matter and the positioned classes' does.

**`MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` has no reversed row and cannot have one**: the class says the text ended early, so no second defect can sit after it.

Reported by the portable checker as two gates where the report is assembled. The first drops every condition-text code at a declaration with an unresolvable name and is deliberately **position-blind**, because a finding carries no offset into the text and threading one through eleven families is a larger change than it buys; the price is a SUBSTITUTION rather than an under-report — where the other defect comes first A12 names it and the checker names the bad name, one class either way and both true of the text. That cost is visible in `consistency.RepetitionWildcardTest`, which asserted BOTH classes on `FieldFilled(Guest*/NoSuchField)` until this entry: A12 stops at the star, and a class A12 did not draw is a divergence however true it is. The second gate drops the two relational codes wherever another family already reported on the same text, and reads the FINDINGS rather than the model, because the same unreferenced error target is reported on a sound condition and withheld on a defective one.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ConditionClassWithholdingLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … ConditionMultipleDefectTest`.

## §13 supplement — an error message LAYERS its checks: a character gate, then every parameter defect (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf343"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**The member beside the condition answers the multiple-defect question a third way.** [KF342](#kf342) found a condition reporting the first defect in its text; [KF341](#kf341) found a field type reporting all of them. A message does both, in two layers:

| the `errorMessage` text | A12 |
|---|---|
| `see it` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `see⇥it` — a tab | `MVK_INVALID_CHARACTERS` |
| `see $Adjuster$` — a parameter the condition does not read | `INVALID_FIELD` |
| `see $NoSuchField$` — a parameter that does not resolve | `INVALID_ENTITY` |
| `see $Adjuster` — unterminated | `WRONG_NUMBER_OF_DOLLARS` |
| a tab **before** an unread parameter | **`MVK_INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| an unread parameter **before** a tab | **`MVK_INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| a tab before / after an unresolvable parameter | **`MVK_INVALID_CHARACTERS`**, both |
| a tab before an unterminated parameter | **`MVK_INVALID_CHARACTERS`** |
| a LINE BREAK before an unterminated parameter | **`MVK_INVALID_LINEBREAK`** (added 2026-09-15) |
| `see $Adjuster$ and $NoSuchField$` | **`INVALID_FIELD`, `INVALID_ENTITY`** |
| the same two reversed | **`INVALID_ENTITY`, `INVALID_FIELD`** |

**BOTH ARMS of the character gate pre-empt the dollar count, measured rather than transferred** (2026-09-15). The tab row above settles the `MVK_INVALID_CHARACTERS` arm; the line-break row settles the other, and it was worth its own measurement because a checker placing the dollar gate behind "the character gate" is relying on the whole gate rather than its tab half. That ordering is what lets the portable checker report `WRONG_NUMBER_OF_DOLLARS` (`CheckFamily.MESSAGE_PARAMETER_SYNTAX`) by asking one already-shared predicate first.

**The character check is a GATE, not a competitor for first place.** It wins wherever the character sits, which is the row a position-blind reading and a first-defect reading both get right and only the reversed pair separates — the control [KF340](#kf340) did not have. Past it, both parameter defects are reported, ordered by where the parameter appears.

**The gate covers ONE MESSAGE, not the declaration.** A rule whose English text carries a tab and whose German text names an unread field draws both classes, in locale order. That is the opposite of the condition member, where a defect in one text withholds the class of another, so neither granularity may be carried to the other member.

**An INTERIOR line break draws a second, codeless refusal** — "Only values without line breaks are allowed" — beside `MVK_INVALID_LINEBREAK`. A leading or trailing break draws only the class, and so does a break with whitespace on one side and nothing beyond it, so the second check reads the TRIMMED value. A tab is the negative control: interior or trailing, it draws one refusal, so this is about line breaks rather than about where a control character sits.

Reported by the portable checker as a per-message gate inside the parameter family rather than at the report, which is the first gate here that is family-local — a finding carries its declaration's path and not its locale, so nothing assembled at the report could tell a sibling message's finding from this one's. The codeless whole-value refusal is not reported: it carries no class, and a checker inventing one would be naming a verdict A12 did not give.

**Extended 2026-09-15 — and the layers stop entirely where the CONDITION does not parse.** A rule whose condition A12 cannot reduce draws its parse class and nothing about its message, on six unparsable shapes (a trailing name, an unbalanced parenthesis, a bare name, an empty text, punctuation alone, an unknown operator) and with the message carrying a parameter, an escaped dollar, or no dollar. This was measured expecting the opposite: `RuleParser` re-parses the condition whenever any message text `contains("$")` and composes the unprefixed `INVALID_CONDITION` when that parse yields nothing, so the class looked reachable. **The absence is the load-bearing half**, because every message family in the portable checker skips a declaration whose DSL it could not read — this is what says that skip under-reports nothing. Recall limit: six authored shapes, not an enumeration, and the second parse runs under `ExpandMode.EXPAND` with a swallowing reporter, so "not reachable from these six" rather than unreachable.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageMultipleDefectLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … MessageMultipleDefectTest`. The unparsable-condition rows are `rulekit.validate.laws.MessageOnAnUnparsableConditionLawsTest`, which needs its own harness entry because [KernelLaws]'s message helper asserts an admitted condition as its precondition.

## §13 supplement — an enumeration's values report EVERY defect, and `MVK_CATEGORY_VALUE_DUPLICATE` is not what its name says (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf344"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**The third member put through the defect-pairing pass, and it answers like a field type rather than like a condition or a message.** Three checks read one `values` array — the tokens' identity, their alphabet, and the categories paired with them — and none withholds anything:

| the enum's `values` (alphabet restricted to `A-Z`) | A12 |
|---|---|
| `BASIC`, `PLUS` under a two-token category — the control | ADMITTED |
| `BASIC`, `BASIC` | `MVK_CATEGORY_VALUE_DUPLICATE`, `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_DUPLICATE`, + a codeless refusal |
| `BASIC`, `plus` | `MVK_ENUM_VALUE_WITH_INVALID_CHARACTER` ×4 — one per distinct offending CHARACTER |
| a category one token short | `MVK_MISSING_CATEGORY_VALUE` |
| `BASIC`, `BASIC`, `plus` | the union of rows 2 and 3 |
| `plus`, `BASIC`, `BASIC` — reversed | **the same string**, so the report's order is fixed by the CHECK, not by position |
| `BASIC`, `BASIC` under a short category | the union of rows 2 and 4 |

**`MVK_CATEGORY_VALUE_DUPLICATE` is drawn by a repeated INTERNAL value, not by a repeated category token.** Read off the name, a checker would be wrong in both directions — and both directions are measured:

| shape | A12 |
|---|---|
| `BASIC`, `BASIC` with **no** `categories` member | `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_DUPLICATE` + the codeless one, and **no** category class |
| `BASIC`, `PLUS` under a category whose own tokens are `STANDARD`, `STANDARD` | **ADMITTED** |

So the class means "this duplicate leaves the positional pairing ambiguous", and it is counted as the **cross product of duplicated values and categories** — 1×2 → two, 2×1 → two, and **2×2 → four**, which is the cell that separates a cross product from a maximum or a sum. It counts duplicated VALUES rather than extra occurrences: a token declared three times draws one.

Reported by the portable checker, which emitted the value class alone until this entry — an under-report of a class A12 draws on every enum that both repeats a value and declares a category.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumValueMultipleDefectLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … EnumValueMultipleDefectTest`.

## §13 supplement — a group's two ordering members both report, and the sort LIST has two verdicts of its own (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf345"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**The fifth member put through the defect-pairing pass.** [KF216](#kf216) and the type-gate grid beside it measure `indexFieldName` and `sortFields[].name` one at a time, and the latter's fixture deletes the index member before setting the sort one precisely so the two cannot fire together. That row:

| `/Order/Items` with `Sku` declared `noValueValidation` | A12 |
|---|---|
| both members on a plain field — the control | ADMITTED |
| an opaque `indexFieldName` alone | `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION` |
| an opaque sort field alone | `MVK_SORT_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION` |
| **both members on the opaque field** | **both classes** |

So neither member withholds the other, which makes this member the field type's shape rather than the condition's.

**The sort list carries two verdicts about ITSELF rather than about an entry, and both are once.**

| the `sortFields` list | A12 |
|---|---|
| one field named twice | `MVK_SORT_FIELD_DUPLICATE`, once |
| the same field named three times | the same, **once** |
| two fields each named twice | the same, **once** |
| two DIFFERENT opaque fields sorted | `MVK_SORT_FIELD_NO_VALUE_VALIDATION`, **once** |
| only the second of them opaque — the control | the same class, so the second entry IS judged |

The control is what makes the fourth row a stop rather than an unread entry. The duplicate and the type class ride together — the opaque field sorted twice draws both.

**An unresolvable ordering name is a different TIER and cannot be paired across.** It stops the model being built, in either member, and no member code survives beside it — so a grid putting an unresolvable name opposite a type defect would be varying buildability rather than the member.

Reported by the portable checker, which did not emit `MVK_SORT_FIELD_DUPLICATE` at all. Its per-entry type findings are deliberately kept where A12 gives one: that is the count divergence [KF340](#kf340) already settled, since a finding per entry names the field to fix and says nothing A12 did not.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupOrderingMultipleDefectLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … GroupOrderingMultipleDefectTest`.

## §7 supplement — the hint list's four value laws, three of them live, closed on the wrong carrier for two days (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf421"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside §7's string-declaration material, next to [KF319](#kf319)'s parameter grid.

`MVK_VALUES_DUPLICATE`, `MVK_VALUE_TOO_LONG`, `MVK_VALUE_TOO_SHORT` and `MVK_VALUE_INVALID` sat in [MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) as `n/a-structural`, each citing [KF321](#kf321) — which measured an ENUM value token: repeated, empty, spaced, 300 characters long, all ADMITTED. Every row of that measurement is right and none of them is about these four codes, whose own ledger prose already named the carrier: **a string type's `hintList`**. That member is stored DM-JSON (`"hintList":[{"locale":"en_US","values":["AB"]}]`) and nothing had asked it.

| the string type declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| a hint list and no other parameter — the control | ADMITTED |
| the same hint value twice in one locale's list | `MVK_VALUES_DUPLICATE` |
| a hint value longer than `maxLength` (and the same value AT it — the control) | `MVK_VALUE_TOO_LONG` / ADMITTED |
| a hint value shorter than `minLength` (and the same value AT it — the control) | `MVK_VALUE_TOO_SHORT` / ADMITTED |
| a hint value the type's own `pattern` refuses | **ADMITTED** |
| an EMPTY hint value, no bound declared | ADMITTED |

**Three live laws, and their multiplicities are part of them.** A length finding is per offending VALUE — two long values draw two — and a uniqueness finding is per duplicated VALUE rather than per list: the same value three times draws one, two distinct values each duplicated draw two, which one duplicated value could not have said. The list-level `MVK_NO_VAL_AND_HINT_LISTS` does not pre-empt them; A12 reports both.

**Only the locales the model DECLARES are examined**, in both laws — predicted the other way and measured, so a checker judging every entry present would refuse two models A12 takes. `-1` is A12's "no bound" here as everywhere else on this type.

**`MVK_VALUE_INVALID` keeps its disposition and gains a predicate.** `CheckConfiguration` registers `invalidValueInHintList` as `CheckHintList`, which resolves the SIBLING `pattern` of the `StringType` above the value and refuses a hint value the pattern does not match. That arm stays silent on a stored hint list under three attacked spellings — a lower-case value, an empty one the same pattern refuses, and one bad value among three good — so what is unreachable is now a specific readable check rather than an unknown one. **Why it is silent is NOT established**: the condition computes its pattern id by dropping two index levels from `…/StringType/HintLists/Values/value`, and whether the converted metamodel document puts the pattern where that lands is unmeasured. Stated as a hypothesis, not a mechanism.

Reported by the portable checker's `CheckFamily.HINT_LIST_VALUES`.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.HintListValueLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.HintListValueTest`.

## §13 supplement — A12 refuses in FOUR tiers, not three: a codeless VERDICT is not a build failure, and 18 recorded rows were on the wrong side (measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf420"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a reporting-tier taxonomy, outside KERNEL-SEMANTICS's evaluation scope.

**A12's refusals sort into four observable tiers, and the two codeless ones are different claims.** The reader refuses the bytes (nothing was examined); `checkConsistency` throws and the model is never built (nothing was judged); `checkConsistency` reports a notification carrying NO class key (the declaration WAS judged, and A12 names no class for it); or it reports one carrying an `MVK_*`/unprefixed key. The estate's laws harness collapsed the middle two into one verdict called `NOT BUILDABLE`, whose stated meaning was "A12 reached no verdict about this declaration" — the opposite of the truth for every row of the third tier.

**The discriminator was already published and is ours, not A12's.** `KernelModelPreparation` wraps a build failure as `"the kernel could not build this model: …"`, and `cli/…/schema/diagnostic.schema.json` already names that summary as what separates the two codeless tiers. `KernelLaws.REFUSED_CODELESS` now applies it.

**Eighteen recorded rows moved, across seven law classes, and each is a sentence A12 states about the declaration:**

| the declaration | A12's sentence |
|---|---|
| a `DateRangeType` whose `(format, rangeSeparator)` pair is not allowlisted — including a format alone, a separator alone, and an explicit `""` | `The date range format is invalid.` |
| a `maxFractionalDigits` of 15, or `maxIntegerDigits` past the budget | `Only values smaller than or equal to 14 are allowed.` |
| a group name of 61 characters | `Only values with up to 60 characters are allowed.` |
| a RULE name starting with a digit, or carrying a dot | (per-carrier prose) |
| an empty `errorCode` under an ONLY variant filter | (per-carrier prose) |

**What follows for a report, and it is the reason the distinction is worth a finding.** A codeless verdict is reportable: the refusal is real, it is about this declaration, and a consumer may state it — what it may not do is attribute one of A12's classes to it, which is why `RK_ENUM_TEXT_LINE_BREAK` exists ([KF418](#kf418)). A build failure is not reportable as a verdict at all. Collapsing them makes the first look like the second and turns eighteen measured facts into "A12 said nothing".

**A `NOT BUILDABLE` written in this estate before 2026-09-15 may be either tier.** Only the rows above were re-measured; the rest were not, so re-measure before citing one as evidence that A12 reached no verdict.

*Locked by:* the seven re-tiered classes — `DateRangePairAdmissionLawsTest`, `DeclaredNameShapeLawsTest`, `FieldTypeBindingLawsTest`, `FieldTypeBodyMemberLawsTest`, `GroupNameAlphabetLawsTest`, `NumberTypeDigitLawsTest`, `RuleVariantFilterLawsTest` — and `EnumValueForbiddenCharactersLawsTest`, whose grid found it.

## §8 supplement — the three "invalid value" enum classes are ONE predicate over four characters, and two of the four never reach it (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf418"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an authoring-gate account of three diagnostic classes, outside KERNEL-SEMANTICS's evaluation scope.

`MVK_INTERNAL_VALUE_INVALID`, `MVK_DISPLAY_VALUE_INVALID` and `MVK_CATEGORY_VALUE_INVALID` sat in [MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) as **unmeasured predicate** because [KF366](#kf366)'s sweep found markup and a control character both ADMITTED, so nothing authored had reached them. Their names invite "XML-safety"; that reading is wrong. `CheckConfiguration` registers `ungueltigerXMLWert`, `ungueltigerOberflaechenWert` and `ungueltigerKategorieWert` as three instances of ONE class, `CheckEnumOrCategoryValue`, whose whole body is `Strings.CS.containsAny(xmlValue, "\n", "\t", "\r", "|")`. So the carrier picks the class and the four characters are the entire predicate.

| the declared text carries… | internal value | display label | category token |
|---|---|---|---|
| a TAB | `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUE_INVALID` | `MVK_DISPLAY_VALUE_INVALID` | `MVK_CATEGORY_VALUE_INVALID` |
| a PIPE | the same | the same | the same |
| a NEWLINE or a CARRIAGE RETURN | refused CODELESS, on all three | | |
| a space, `<`, an escaped quote — the controls | ADMITTED | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |

**Half the predicate is dead, and the reason is a gate above it.** A line break draws `Field with path '/Policy/Tier': Only values without line breaks are allowed.` — a real verdict about the declaration, carrying no class key — so citing one of the three codes for a newline would name a class A12 does not use there.

Three further facts a family has to encode rather than infer, each measured: the unit of report is the TEXT, so a value carrying both a tab and a pipe draws one finding while two defective values draw two, and each carrier answers on its own account (a value and its own label each defective draw both classes); the line-break gate pre-empts the coded one **within one text only** — a sibling value's tab is still reported — and it is raised once for the FIELD however many of its texts carry one; and a label for a locale the model does NOT declare is ADMITTED however it is spelled, so a family judging every label text would refuse a model A12 takes.

**The category's own `name` is a different law.** A tab there is also refused codeless, and its sentence says why: *"A category name starts with a letter and may contain only letters, digits and the underscore"* — a name alphabet, not this predicate, so the character it was keyed on is incidental.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumValueForbiddenCharactersLawsTest`.

## §8 supplement — `MVK_NAME_INVALID_A12_DV` is a RESERVED final segment, which is why no character sweep could reach it (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf419"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an authoring-gate account of one diagnostic class, outside KERNEL-SEMANTICS's evaluation scope.

[KF367](#kf367)'s complete printable-ASCII sweep over field names draws OTHER classes for every illegal character, which left this code as an **unmeasured predicate**. Reading the gate settles it. `CheckFieldName` delegates to `NameValidationService.checkFieldNameNoMetaModelChecks`, which refuses on two arms: a name that does not match `[a-zA-Z0-9_:]+([.][a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*)*`, and — for a name that DOES match — a final dotted segment of `.value`, case-insensitively, in the English condition language. The first arm is what the sweep found pre-empted; the second is a name every alphabet gate admits, so no character sweep could ever have reached it.

| declared field name | classes |
|---|---|
| `Slot` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `value` — the reserved word with no dot before it | ADMITTED |
| `Slot.List` | `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV` |
| `Slot.value` · `Slot.VALUE` · `Slot.List.value` | `MVK_NAME_INVALID_A12_DV`, `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV` |
| `Slot.values` — one letter past it | `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV` |
| `Slot.value.List` — reserved in the MIDDLE | `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV` |

The pattern's dotted group is OPTIONAL, so an undotted name matches with the group unset and the reserved-word test is never asked — measured on the `value` row above, and the reason a checker keyed on the bare word would refuse a name A12 takes. A12 reports BOTH classes and this one FIRST (measured, same grid), so a report stopping at the dot names the half that is not the reason.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldNameReservedSuffixLawsTest`.

## §9 supplement — the error-field/iteration disagreement cannot arise in an A12 model, and the reason is the index the parser records (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf417"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a reachability account of one diagnostic class, not an evaluation behaviour.

`IterationChecker.checkVRefs` raises `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_AND_ITERATION_INVALID` when the error entity's own references record no `ITERATION` at index level 0 while some other reference does. Eight attempts across this estate failed to author it, the first seven by varying NESTED repeatable groups — level 0 is the OUTERMOST repeatable level, so those were varying the wrong thing. Varying the ROOT repetition instead, on a multi-form model, does not reach it either, and the eighth attempt is the one that says why.

`CheckIdNameRefImpl.setIndexOfCurrentLevel` records the index: `WILDCARD` when the reference carries a star, `ITERATION` when the level is repeatable and it does NOT. So the two states the check compares are "aggregate" and "per-row read", not "starred" and "unstarred" as the class's name suggests. Measured on `/Persons` (repeatable root) against `/Header` (fixed root), with the error field referenced in every row so the post-parse referenced-ness gate cannot answer first:

| the rule | verdict |
|---|---|
| fixed root reports, fixed root reads — the control | ADMITTED |
| fixed root reports, `AtLeastOneFieldFilled(/Persons*/Name)` | ADMITTED |
| fixed root reports, `FieldFilled(/Persons/Name)` — per-row | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| repeatable root reports, its own field read — the control | ADMITTED |
| repeatable root reports, the fixed root read | ADMITTED |

**The middle row is the whole account.** A per-row read is the only spelling that records `ITERATION`, and a per-row read of an extent the error field's own path does not enter is refused by the wildcard gate before the iteration check runs. Where such a read IS admitted, the error field shares the level and therefore records `ITERATION` too — so the disagreement has no A12 carrier. The class's other arm is the parallel-iteration one, which belongs to `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_*` and is dispositioned separately.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RootRepetitionIterationAgreementLawsTest`.

## §11 supplement — reading the computed field is CONTAINMENT, not equality, and two shapes are exempt (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf416"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs beside §11's computation account, next to [KF182](#kf182)'s projected-read split.

[KF181](#kf181) and [KF182](#kf182) settle which CLASS a self-read draws and what pre-empts it; both measured only reads of the computed field itself. The predicate is wider. `NormalisierteBerechnungsFormHelper.feldReferenziertOhneKontextAngegeben` asks `EntityUtils.isDescendantOrEqual(calculatedField, referencedEntity)` — the CALCULATED FIELD against the reference — so a reference to any **ancestor** of the computed field is a read of it.

Measured over one computation writing `/Routing/Legs/Distance` from the constant `1`, whose derived scale matches the target's declared zero so the gate [KF181](#kf181) puts ahead of this class cannot fire:

| the guard beside that operation | verdict |
|---|---|
| none, and a read of a SIBLING field — the controls | ADMITTED |
| `FieldFilled(Distance)` — the computed field itself | `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` |
| `GroupNotFilled(/Routing/Legs)` — its own GROUP | `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Routing/Legs*) > 0` | `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` |
| `GroupNotFilled(/Routing)` — the ROOT, an ancestor like any other | `MVK_ERROR_REFERENCE_TO_CALCULATED_FIELD` |
| `GroupFilled(/Routing/Legs)` | ADMITTED |
| `CurrentRepetition(/Routing/Legs) == 1` | ADMITTED |

**The last two are carved exemptions, not a rule about group predicates** — which is what the `GroupNotFilled` row establishes, since it names the same group. `GroupFilled` is the kernel's single-entity `AllGroupsFilled`, exempted in the walk as "context specified"; a `CurrentRepetition` operand is not traversed at all. A checker taking either half alone is wrong in one direction: keyed on equality it admits the group rows, keyed on containment alone it refuses the two A12 admits.

**The root row also settles which class answers there**, and it is not the one the operand families draw: the identical `GroupNotFilled(/Routing)` in an ordinary RULE is ADMITTED, so no parse-time gate speaks about a group predicate over a root group and `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` — an entity-LIST class — never competes.

**The law reaches a target with no scale unchanged**, which is the part a clean-room checker can carry without derived-scale inference: on the string `/Routing/PlannedLeg`, a self-read in the operation and a self-read in the precondition both draw the class, against an accepted peer-read control.

**The kernel's exemption tests arity, and that test is unreachable through this catalog's spelling** — worth recording because a checker would otherwise carry a branch nothing can exercise. The walk exempts `AllGroupsFilled` only at `entityIdList.size() == 1`, and our `GroupFilled` IS that single-entity spelling: a second operand draws `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID1` from a gate answering ahead of the calculation walk, and a second operand nested in the first draws `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2`. So no model reaching the walk carries a multi-entity form of the exempt predicate.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ComputationSelfReadScopeLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ComputationSelfReadTest`; reported by `CheckFamily.COMPUTATION_SELF_READ`.

## §11 supplement — the calculation gates judge a rule A12 SYNTHESIZES, which erases six of their classes for stored A12 models (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf415"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a reachability account of one module's diagnostic classes, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CalculationService.checkCalculationRule` reads an `IRule`, and for a stored A12 `Computation` that rule does not exist in the model: `ValidationModelConverter.createRuleFromComputation` builds a `RuleFromComputationImpl` whose condition text is assembled by `ComputationAlternativesJoiner.join()` (kernel `30.8.1`, source-read 2026-09-15). **Six of the module's classes test properties of that synthesis rather than of anything an author stored**, so they cannot fire through `checkConsistency` however the DM-JSON is written — and each one's basis is structural, not a claim about what a typed builder happens to expose.

| the class | what it tests | why no stored model reaches it |
|---|---|---|
| `MVK_CALC_INVALID_ACTION_TYPE` | `rule.getSeverityType() != ERROR` | the converter passes the literal `RuleSeverityType.ERROR`, and A12's `Computation` declares no severity member at all |
| `MVK_ERROR_WRONG_CALCULATED_FIELD` | computed field ≠ the rule's error field | both are `computation.getComputedField().getRelativePath()`, the same string resolved against the same parent |
| `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_FIELD_GATE` | the condition does not open `FieldFilled(<computed field>) And …` | that prefix is the joiner's own constant template |
| `MVK_ERROR_COMPARISON_WITH_OR` | a sub-computation joined by `Or` rather than `And` | every stored fragment — the common precondition, each alternative's precondition, each alternative — is wrapped in its own parentheses before joining, so no stored text can reach the operator that joins them |
| `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_COMPARISON` | the comparison is not an inequality or tolerance op | the operator comes from the joiner's five-way switch on the stored `toleranceRangeOp`, which throws on any other value |
| `MVK_ERROR_RESTRICTED_CALCULATION_RULE` | the rule restricts its iteration interval | the restriction is read off `IExtmpRule`, the H-model rule type; the synthesized rule is not one, so both intervals are always empty |

**The same `IExtmpRule` reading erases `MVK_ITERATION_RESTRICTION_IN_A12_MODEL`** one layer up, in `IterationChecker.checkIterationRestriction4A12Model`: an A12 `Rule` is not an `IExtmpRule` either, so the two Optionals it guards on are empty and the branch that raises the class is unreachable. The ledger had both of these on a typed-surface basis ("bounded iteration ranges are unrepresentable — rulekit renders only the unrestricted star"), which is the weaker claim: it says our builder cannot write the shape, where the measurement says the shape has no carrier in the A12 metamodel.

**`MVK_ERROR_INVALID_FIELDNAME` needed the carrier sweep rather than the synthesis argument**, because the name it tests IS an author's. It refuses a computed field whose `getFullName()` — the field's PATH — contains `.` or `:`, so any carrier on that path admitting one would reach it. All three refuse first, the root cell measured for this ([KF322](#kf322)): a field name draws `MVK_NAME_INVALID_DOT_COLON_A12_DV`, a nested group name `MVK_PATH_INVALID`, and a root group name `MVK_PATH_INVALID`.

**Corrected 2026-09-19 — both codes DO have a Java raiser, and this sentence asserted the opposite.** It read: *"Two of the module's codes have no JAVA raiser in kernel `30.8.1` — `MVK_RULE_GROUP_IS_EMPTY_OR_INVALID` and `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_VALID` carry message properties and an enum member and nothing calls them"*, which a walk of the checkout's 1821 non-generated `.java` files refutes on both: `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_VALID` is raised at `ParserService:517`, whose `throwError` overload two lines down does `throw new MVKParserError`, guarded by `!parser.isLenient()`; and `MVK_RULE_GROUP_IS_EMPTY_OR_INVALID` at `CheckRegelKontextEntityImpl:94`, which throws `createMVKParserError` when the rule group resolves to nothing. Neither is gated on `isHModel`. **The mechanism of the error is the one this file warns about elsewhere: a negative existential stated without its enumeration.** Every one of these codes *appears* in Java as an enum constant, so the distinguishing question is declaration versus use — and nobody had asked it, because the sentence generalized [KF354](#kf354)'s genuinely dormant label-only members to codes that merely resembled them. Measured 2026-09-19 over the seven rows resting on this claim: all seven are declared exactly once, and the USE counts are 1/0/0/0/1/0/2 — so four rows were right and three were not, the third being `MVK_ERROR_ITERATION_UNCHECKED` (`NormalisierteBerechnungsFormHelper:251`, `:463`, both behind `isHModel`). *Existence is all that is corrected here; reachability is not claimed, since two of the three raisers sit behind a condition.* **The Java axis now has the enumeration it lacked**, locked by `MvkLedgerTest.theJavaAxisRaisesNoneOfTheCodesTheLedgerCallsDormantThere` — a positive control on a real raiser, a file-count floor, and a declared-exactly-once check so a kernel rename reads as staleness rather than as absence. *Qualified 2026-09-15: the claim is about the Java estate and not about A12 as a whole, because the metamodel raises codes that appear in NO file of the checkout — `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUE_INVALID` is measured firing ([KF418](#kf418)) with a zero count everywhere. Both rows remain open on the metamodel axis; what is settled is that the calculation module's pre-flight guards nothing.* **Metamodel axis measured 2026-09-18, closing the escape hatch this qualification opened:** neither code — nor any of the seven ledger rows resting on this axis — is declared as an `errorCode` by any rule in this estate's metamodel corpus (all 59 JSON models of `a12-kernel-mm/documentModels`, carrying 105 distinct codes). The instrument's positive control is `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUE_INVALID` itself, this qualification's own witness, which IS carried there — so the sweep demonstrably sees a metamodel-axis raiser, and the absences are measurements rather than a blind read. *Recall limit: it measures the corpus this estate holds, so it cannot exclude a metamodel we do not have.* Locked by `MvkLedgerTest.theMetamodelAxisCarriesNoRuleForTheCodesTheLedgerLeavesUnmeasuredThere`, whose failure IS the re-open trigger.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupNameAlphabetLawsTest.theDotAndColonOnTheRootCarrier` for the carrier row; the remaining rows are source facts about a synthesis step and carry no authorable witness by construction, which is what the finding states.

## §13 supplement — which of the index terminal's five gates answers first (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf414"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class ordering fact about an error text's parameters, not an evaluation behaviour.
