`checkIndexFieldRef` applies five gates to `$index(Arg).value$`, in this order: the ARGUMENT must be the short name of an index field on the error entity's path (`INVALID_INDEX_FIELD`); the match must be unique (`INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_AMBIGUOUS`); the indexed group must not carry a composed index (`INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_COMPOSED_INDEX`, unreachable from stored DM-JSON, which writes a singular `indexFieldName`); the repeatability of the field must agree with the CONDITION's own references to it (`INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_REP`, `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_REP_ITER`, `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_NONREP_ENUM`); and only then must a suffix be present at all (`INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_PARAMETER`).

**The discriminating row is an unknown argument with NO suffix**, added to `validate.laws.RuleMessageIndexTerminalLawsTest` on 2026-09-15: it draws `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` and not `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_PARAMETER`, because the argument gate is first and the suffix gate never runs. Two of the five classes would otherwise be indistinguishable on shapes that violate both, and a checker reporting the missing-suffix class would name it on models where A12 answers the argument class instead.

**That ordering is what licenses reporting the first TWO gates.** *(Amended 2026-09-15: this read "the FIRST gate alone", and the ambiguity gate was then measured and reported.)* The portable checker reports `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` and `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_AMBIGUOUS` (`CheckFamily.ERROR_TEXT_INDEX_TERMINAL`, mirrored by `consistency.ErrorTextIndexTerminalTest`) and stays silent on the other three: each of them needs either the repeatability machinery computed from the condition's references or a shape stored DM-JSON cannot spell, and a class drawn after an unreproduced gate cannot be claimed to have been reached. The argument gate is first, so nothing pre-empts it; the ambiguity gate sits directly behind it, so reproducing the argument gate IS the whole precondition for reporting it — which is why the second gate costs no machinery the first did not already need.

**The ambiguity row, measured 2026-09-15 on its own fixture.** `/Policy` → `Claims` repeatable(20) index field `Ref` → `Items` repeatable(9) index field `Ref`, error entity inside `Items`: `$index(Ref).value$` draws `INVALID_INDEX_FIELD_AMBIGUOUS`, against the control of the same terminal with no parameter. It needs its own carrier because the ambiguity is a property of the whole path and would change every other row of the shared fixture — the unambiguous shape above is the control, and what moves between them is the second declaration of the name, nothing else.

**A non-repeatable indexed group still PASSES both gates.** Its index field is on the path and matches exactly once, so A12's answer comes from the repeatability gate — which is why silence there is the correct reading of a unique match rather than an omission.

## §13 supplement — the category suffix an error-text parameter may carry (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf413"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about an error text's parameters, not an evaluation behaviour.

A message parameter may project a field through an enum CATEGORY, written `$Field -> Band$`. `FullChecks_ErrorTextParameterParser` checks it in two steps: `checkAndGetCategoryName` answers `NO_CATEGORY` when the arrow carries no name, and `checkAccessToCategoryValue` then answers `FIELD_NO_ENUM` for a field that is not an enumeration and `INVALID_CATEGORY` for one whose type declares no such category. Measured on an own-domain catalogue desk whose condition reads every field but one (`validate.laws.ErrorTextCategorySuffixLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ErrorTextCategorySuffixTest`).

| the parameter | verdict |
|---|---|
| `$Reference$` — plain, no suffix | ADMITTED |
| `$Grade -> Band$` — a category the enumeration declares | ADMITTED |
| `$Grade -> NoSuch$` — a category it does not | `INVALID_CATEGORY` |
| `$Plain -> Band$` — an enumeration declaring NO categories at all | `INVALID_CATEGORY` |
| `$Amount -> Band$` — a number field | `FIELD_NO_ENUM` |
| `$Note -> Band$` — a text field | `FIELD_NO_ENUM` |
| `$Grade ->$` — the arrow with no name after it | `NO_CATEGORY` |
| `$Unread -> Band$` — a valid suffix on a field the condition never reads | `INVALID_FIELD` |

**An enumeration with NO categories draws the containment class, not one of its own.** "Declares no categories" and "declares other categories" feel like different failures and A12 answers both with `INVALID_CATEGORY` — the row a reader would most likely split.

**MEMBERSHIP runs first**, because `checkFieldRef` resolves the field against the condition to obtain the id it then hands to the category check. So the last row is `INVALID_FIELD` whatever the suffix says, and a family reporting a category class there would name a class A12 never reached.

## §13 supplement — the semantic index an error-text parameter may carry (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf412"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about an error text's parameters, not an evaluation behaviour.

A12 resolves an error-message parameter against the rule's own CONDITION, not against the model. `FullChecks_ErrorTextParameterParser.checkFieldReferencedInConditionAndGetFirstId` asks `refEntities.tryGetFor(fullName, semanticIndexSpec)`; finding nothing, it answers `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID` when a key was written and `INVALID_FIELD` when none was. Measured on an own-domain fulfilment desk whose condition reads `[Shipments/Weight For "T-1"]`, with the harness's own control that the condition is admitted (`validate.laws.ErrorTextSemanticIndexLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ErrorTextSemanticIndexTest`).

| the parameter | verdict |
|---|---|
| `$Reference$` — plain, the condition reads it | ADMITTED |
| `$Shipments/Weight For "T-1"$` — the condition's own pairing | ADMITTED |
| `$Shipments/Weight For "T-9"$` — a different literal key | `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID` |
| `$Shipments/Weight For LookupCode$` — a field key where the condition used a literal | `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID` |
| `$Shipments/Weight$` — the same field with NO key | `INVALID_FIELD` |
| `$Shipments/TrackingNo For "T-1"$` — the group's INDEX FIELD at the bound key | ADMITTED |
| `$Shipments/Carrier For "T-1"$` — a PLAIN sibling at the bound key | `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID` |
| `$Parcels/Volume For "P-1"$` — a group the condition never reads | `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID` |
| `$Total For "T-1"$` — a key on a field that does not repeat | `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID` |
| `$Shipments/Weight Fuer "T-1"$` — the German keyword in an `en_US` model | `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` |
| `$Shipments/Weight For Shipments/TrackingNo For "T-1"$` — a key that is itself keyed | `ILLEGAL_SEMANTIC_INDEX` |
| `$Parcels/Volume For Parcels/ParcelNo For "P-1"$` — the same, on a group the condition never reads | `ILLEGAL_SEMANTIC_INDEX` |

**The key binds a PAIR, not a repetition — and the last two rows of that pair are the whole finding.** A reader that takes the `TrackingNo` row alone concludes that a bound key makes the whole repetition readable and then admits `Carrier`, which A12 refuses; a reader that takes the `Carrier` row alone refuses `TrackingNo`, which A12 admits. What actually holds is narrower than either: the condition's own (field, key) pairings, PLUS the field that names the key itself. The rival mechanism was named and the discriminating case run before the clause was written.

**Matching is by key SPEC, so a literal and a field key never satisfy each other** even where they could denote the same value — `tryGetFor` keys on the written spec.

**A key that is itself keyed is refused BEFORE membership, which is what makes the last two rows a pair rather than a repetition.** `checkSemanticIndex` runs as the KEY sub-rule completes, so `ILLEGAL_SEMANTIC_INDEX` is answered without `checkFieldRef` ever consulting the condition — and the discriminating row is the second one, on `Parcels`, a group the condition never reads: it draws the chaining class and not `MVK_INDEX_FOR_ERROR_TEXT_INVALID`, which a membership-first reading would predict. That ordering is what lets the portable checker report the chaining class on any parameter carrying it, with no membership work at all (measured 2026-09-15).

**The error-text parameter keyword follows the MODEL's language, and the grammar file says otherwise.** `BaseErrorTextParameterLexer.g4` carries the terminal `FOR: 'Fuer'`, which reads as a German-only spelling; measured, an `en_US` model takes `For` and refuses `Fuer` with `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`. A source read of that lexer alone gets this backwards, which is the standing lesson about a grammar file being one layer of several — the first grid written here spelled every row `Fuer` and measured nine parse errors.

## §11 supplement — what an enum-valued computation may compute FROM (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf411"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about a computation's source, not an evaluation behaviour.

`NormalisierteBerechnungsFormHelper.checkBerechnungsFunktion` adds one gate an enumeration TARGET carries and no other kind does: the operation must be a string constant the target declares, a `FieldValue` read of an enumeration the target COVERS, or a `FirstFilledValue` over such reads — nothing else. The kernel's own note gives the reason: a computed value outside the domain has no display value to show.

| the source, assigned into a two-value enumeration | verdict |
|---|---|
| a declared value of the target | ADMITTED |
| an enumeration declaring exactly those values | ADMITTED |
| an enumeration declaring FEWER | ADMITTED |
| an enumeration declaring MORE | `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_ENUM_CALCULATION` |
| a category whose tokens the target covers | ADMITTED |
| a category whose tokens it does not | `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_ENUM_CALCULATION` |
| a TEXT field | `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_ENUM_CALCULATION` |
| `FirstFilledValue` over two covered enumerations | ADMITTED |
| `FirstFilledValue` where one is not covered | `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_ENUM_CALCULATION` |
| a concatenation of the target's own declared value | `MVK_ERROR_INVALID_ENUM_CALCULATION` |

**Coverage runs ONE way, and a CATEGORY substitutes its own tokens.** A narrower source is admitted and a wider one refused, so the law is subset containment rather than equality — and projecting the wide source through a category whose tokens the target covers rescues it, which is the one repair that does not touch either declaration's value list.

**The gate sits in the CALCULATION module and runs after the parse, so three shapes never reach it.** A computation is lowered to a comparison against its target, so the comparison walk answers first wherever it has a class: a constant outside the domain draws `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUM_COMPARISON`, a display-bearing source against an unlabelled target draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_ENUM_TO_STRING` ([KF407](#kf407)), and a NUMBER source draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_ENUM_OR_STRING`. The TEXT source is the discriminating case, and it is why this gate is not redundant with that walk: a plain text against a TEXTLESS enumeration is ADMITTED there, so only the calculation gate catches it.

**Every row is ADMITTED into a TEXT target**, which is the control that makes the table a law about the target's declared kind rather than about the operations.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.ENUM_COMPUTATION_SOURCE`), which stays silent on the three pre-empted shapes and on any operation it will not reduce to a read or a `FirstFilledValue` — a disclosed under-report rather than a guess at which class the walk would answer with.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumComputationSourceLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.EnumComputationSourceTest`.

## §9 supplement — an index field on the ROOT withholds the error-target iteration class (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf410"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class precedence law, not an evaluation behaviour.

[KF348](#kf348) locks the two classes `IterationChecker` draws when a rule reaches its error field only through a root-group reference, and [KF372](#kf372) the containment gate that outruns them. A third pre-emption was missed by both, and it is a DECLARATION rather than a condition shape.

| the model declares | the same condition draws |
|---|---|
| a repeatable root with NO index field | `MVK_ERROR_FIELDGROUP_ITERATION5_INVALID` |
| the same root carrying `indexFieldName` | `MVK_MULTIPLE_INDEX_FIELDS` |

The two models differ in that one member and nothing else. `MVK_MULTIPLE_INDEX_FIELDS` is thrown during the parse and `IterationChecker.checkIteration` runs after it, so the iteration class is never reached — the general rule [KF375](#kf375) already states, on a pair no grid had built.

**The portable checker reported BOTH until this measurement**, which is naming a class A12 did not draw on a model it correctly refuses. The cause was in the phase list rather than in the family: `POST_PARSE_CONDITION_CODES` was assembled by enumerating `ParserService.checkNormalRule`'s own `throwError` sites, and that method reaches two further checkers by a CALL — so only `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`, which the checker already reported, made the list. Sweeping both calls gives the complete post-parse set for this method: `IterationChecker.checkIteration` draws `MVK_ERROR_FIELDGROUP_ITERATION4_INVALID`, `MVK_ERROR_FIELDGROUP_ITERATION5_INVALID`, `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_AND_ITERATION_INVALID` and `MVK_ITERATION_RESTRICTION_IN_A12_MODEL` beside the referenced-ness class, and `checkSimpleIteration` draws `MVK_NEG_CONDITION_IN_ITERATION` (the H-model members of both are a separate enum). A phase list read off one syntactic form misses everything the method delegates.

**`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_AND_ITERATION_INVALID` is the class `checkVRefs` guards at level 0, and seven spellings failed to reach it.** Starring the root leaves the repeating group beneath it bare (`MVK_NO_WILDCARD`); the scalar group predicates refuse a star outright (`MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`); a group LIST predicate accepts the starred root and the level-1 sibling class answers anyway; and carrying the star all the way down is simply ADMITTED, on both models and into either group. That is an enumeration of attempts and NOT a proof of unreachability — the code stays kernel-delegated with its attempts recorded, rather than being claimed unauthorable.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RootLevelIterationPinningLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.RootLevelIterationPinningTest`.

## §9 supplement — the two gates `NumberOfValueInFields` runs after its string arm's type walk (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf409"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about an operator's operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

[KF379](#kf379) locks `NumberOfValueInFields`'s switch on the constant: four arms, four type classes. The STRING arm does not end at its type walk — `CheckAnzahlWertOpImpl` runs the walk, then `checkAllAreValueValidation`, then `CheckOpUtils.checkNoDateConstant`, and the last of those is the estate's ONLY caller of `MVK_NO_DATE_CONSTANT`.

**The last gate is about the CONSTANT and not about the fields.** `CheckKonstanteImpl` calls `DateUtils.isStringAValidDate` on every quoted literal and stores a DATE op-type where it matches, so an ordinary list of TEXT declarations is refused because of how the counted value happens to be spelled. An enumeration that DECLARES the date-shaped token is refused as well, its domain check having passed — which is the row that shows the gate never reads the list.

| the same literal `"01.02.2024"`, counted over | verdict |
|---|---|
| two text declarations | `MVK_NO_DATE_CONSTANT` |
| two DATE declarations | `MVK_NO_STRING_OR_ENUM` |
| a text declaration and one waiving value validation | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |
| enumerations that do not declare it | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION` |
| enumerations that DO declare it | `MVK_NO_DATE_CONSTANT` |

The type walk is the whole list's FIRST pass rather than a per-field interleaving, so it answers ahead of both later gates however the list is ordered. `Today` is a date constant by kind rather than by spelling and takes no arm of the switch at all: `MVK_INVALID_CONST`.

**Which spellings count as a date is decided by LENGTH before any pattern is tried**, and the near-misses are what bound the gate. `"01.02."` (the trailing dot is part of it), `"10:30:00"`, `"01.02.2024"` and `"01.02.2024T10:30:00"` are typed as dates; `"01.02"`, `"0102"`, `"2024-01-02"` and `"01.02.2024 10:30:00"` are the wrong length or the wrong shape, and `"32.01.2024"`, `"29.02.2023"` and `"29.02."` match their pattern and fail the non-lenient parse behind it — the year-less parse leaves the year at the epoch default, so that spelling is not year-agnostic. All seven stay strings and are counted, so a reader matching only the shape would refuse seven constants A12 admits.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.VALUE_IN_FIELDS_CONSTANT_KIND`), which reuses the literal reader `CheckFamily.DATE_ARGUMENT_SLOT` already needed for `MVK_INVALID_DATE_STRING` — the same `isStringAValidDate`, asked by two constructs for opposite reasons.

**Extended 2026-09-15 — the switch has a FIFTH outcome, and it is reachable.** `CheckAnzahlWertOpImpl.check` tests `Falsch`, `Wahr`, a string literal and a number in that order and throws `MVK_INVALID_CONST` after them. Read from the check method alone that arm looks unreachable, since "anything else" is where a parse failure lives; the GRAMMAR settles it instead — `commonKonstante` carries exactly six alternatives, and the two the switch never tests are the points in time. Measured: `NumberOfValueInFields(Today In …)` and `… (Now In …)` both draw `MVK_INVALID_CONST`, over a field list the number arm refuses with `MVK_NO_NUMBER` and another it admits outright, so the class is the constant's and not the list's. The typed builder writes no such call — its overloads take a number, a string or a boolean — so the shape arrives only as authored text, which is where a clean-room checker reading stored DM-JSON meets it. **And the arm's boundary is measured too, which is what keeps it from reading as an "anything else" rule:** a bare NAME in the constant slot draws `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`, identically whether the name is declared in the model or not — so the slot admits no identifier at all, and the fall-through is reachable only through the two point-in-time spellings the grammar names.

**The slot's admitted vocabulary, enumerated from the production rather than from the shapes to hand (measured 2026-09-15).** `konstante` is `commonKonstante` alone, and all nine spellings it can take are ADMITTED: an integer, a negative integer, a decimal, a negative decimal, a string, a string carrying A12's doubled `""` escape, the EMPTY string, `True` and `False`. Everything else is `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` — an operation in the slot, and, the row that makes the position rather than the token the law, **parentheses around a legal constant**. So the slot takes the bare production and nothing assembled from it, which is what lets a clean-room checker refuse the POSITION instead of only classifying the four typed arms.

**And the parse answers there ahead of every reference phase, whatever the spec would later be refused for (measured 2026-09-15).** A slot holding `Packing*/Fragile` — a path that RESOLVES and whose star is illegal because `Packing` does not repeat — is `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`, the same class as a bare name and as an undeclared one, so the wildcard check is never reached. That is what bounds a clean-room checker's stand-down in this slot: an unresolvable name is already withheld by the first-defect rule ([KF340](#kf340)), but a spec that resolves and cannot be ADDRESSED carries no unresolvable name, so a family that spoke there would draw its token class beside the wildcard class A12 never reaches — two classes where A12 draws one.


*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ValueInFieldsDateConstantLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ValueInFieldsDateConstantTest`; the 2026-09-15 fall-through extension by `rulekit.validate.laws.ValueInFieldsConstantKindLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ValueInFieldsConstantKindTest`.

## §6 supplement — what `ValueAsDate` demands of the field it resolves (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf408"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about an operator's operand, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldOpMitDatumSpecialImpl.check`, the checker for `ValueAsDate`, runs four gates over one operand and each of them throws, so the classes form a chain rather than a set: a group draws `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`, a repetition star `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`, a category access `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED`, and anything that is not a partially known date `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE_FOR_OP`. Every pairing that can be written at all was measured, the star against the category included.

**The kind gate draws ONE class for eleven different declarations.** `FieldUtils.isDatePartialKnown` asks two questions — the declaration is an `IDateType`, and its `partlyKnownDate()` is not `BEKANNT` — and the operator has no second class to tell them apart:

| the operand declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| a `DateType` with `datePrecision` DAY_OPTIONAL / MONTH_OPTIONAL / YEAR_OPTIONAL | ADMITTED |
| a `DateType` at the FULL default | `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE_FOR_OP` |
| `DateFragmentType`, `TimeType`, `DateTimeType` | `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE_FOR_OP` |
| `DateRangeType`, `StringType`, `NumberType`, `EnumerationType`, `BooleanType`, `ConfirmType`, `CustomFieldType` | `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE_FOR_OP` |

The three middle rows are the ones a reading of the operator's name gets wrong: A12's ADO layer gives time, datetime and fragment declarations the SAME `IDateType` interface a plain date carries, so all three clear the first question and fail on the precision. A checker keyed on the date interface would admit them.

**The group gate answers even on the ROOT group** — predicted `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` and refuted. That class belongs to the operators that ACCEPT a group and exclude the root one; a method with no group arm at all never reaches it. The one class that does outrun the whole chain from inside the reference reader is `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` on a name nothing declares, and `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` on an unstarred read into a repetition the reading rule does not sit inside — the same read from the row's OWN rule reaches the gates, which is what makes that a pre-emption rather than a property of the operand's spelling ([KF88](#kf88) and the locus law own the placement half).

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.VALUE_AS_DATE_OPERAND`), which reads `datePrecision` off the stored declaration and stays silent on a `TypeDefType` or `UnspecifiedType`, whose effective type it does not resolve.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ValueAsDateOperandGateLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ValueAsDateOperandGatesTest`.

## §8 supplement — when two declarations may be compared once their LABELS count (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf407"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about a comparison's operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`EnumComparabilityLawsTest` locks this law's core as ten single verdicts. Three facts a reproduction needs were not among them, and each is a discriminator a reading of `CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl` does not give.

**A label written for a locale the model does not DECLARE is invisible to the gate.** An enumeration labelled only in `fr_FR` inside an `en_US` model is TEXTLESS — it compares happily with an unlabelled one and draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_ENUM_TO_STRING` against a labelled one, exactly as a label-free declaration does. Combined with the value-label law ([KF321](#kf321)) — once any value answers a declared locale, every value owes every declared locale — this makes A12's own "shared display locales" INTERSECTION always the full declared set in a buildable model. The intersection is therefore unreachable as a narrowing, and a reader may walk the declared locales.

**A CATEGORY access on either side returns before the whole gate.** The identical conflicting pair is refused read plainly and admitted read as `[Tier -> Band]`, on both the enum/enum and the enum/text arm — so the projection is not a narrowing of the comparison but an exit from it.

**The text arm's gate is `isFeldWertOp`: it reads how the partner is WRITTEN, not what type it carries.** A labelled enumeration against `[Holder]` is refused and against `RangeAsString(Holder, 1, 3)` — the same field, the same string result — is admitted. A reader typing the partner would refuse the second.

The rest of the grid re-states the core on one carrier: identity labels are textless, a shared stored token carrying two texts and a shared display text standing for two tokens are both `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_ENUM_TO_ENUM`, and both equality spellings behave alike.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.ENUM_DISPLAY_COMPARABILITY`), whose silences are A12's own exits: a category access, an operand that is not one bare field, and a table-backed enumeration.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumDisplayComparabilityLawsTest` (with `EnumComparabilityLawsTest` for the core), mirrored by `consistency.EnumDisplayComparabilityTest`.

## §8 supplement — an ELEMENT's display label owes no locale at all (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf406"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-declaration law, not an evaluation behaviour.

[KF321](#kf321) measured the enumeration VALUE label's law: once any value answers a DECLARED locale, every value owes a non-blank text for every declared locale, while labels written solely for an undeclared locale are admitted. A field's and a group's label sit in the same `label` array one level up, and it is tempting to read that law as theirs. It is not.

| the element declares | verdict |
|---|---|
| a FIELD with no label — the control | ADMITTED |
| a FIELD label for the declared locale | ADMITTED |
| a FIELD label for an UNDECLARED locale only | ADMITTED |
| (bilingual) a FIELD label for only ONE declared locale | ADMITTED |
| a GROUP label for an UNDECLARED locale only | ADMITTED |
| (bilingual) a GROUP label for only ONE declared locale | ADMITTED |

**So the law belongs to the enumeration's values and to nothing beside them.** The value law is about the values AGREEING with one another — `MVK_COUNT_OF_VALUES_INVALID` when they disagree about carrying a label at all — and an element has no sibling to disagree with, which is why the analogy has no mechanism behind it.

Our own draft carried that analogy as a refusal until this measurement ([API-FINDINGS AF149](API-FINDINGS.md#af149)); it is removed, and the writer now emits exactly the locales an author supplied.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ElementLabelLocaleLawsTest`, with the kit's side in `modelkit.ElementLabelLocaleTest`.

## §7 supplement — what the two SUBSTRING operators demand of the field they cut (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf405"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`RangeAsString` and `RangeAsNumber` are checked by one method, `CheckFeldOpMitParamsImpl.check`, which chains six classes over the operand and the interval together.

| the gate, in the measured order | class |
|---|---|
| the operand names a group | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| it carries a repetition star | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |
| it reads a category | `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| the interval is not `1 <= start <= end` | `MVK_INVALID_INTERVAL` |
| the field is neither text nor a custom type | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE` |
| the field waives value validation | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |

**The interval answers ahead of both gates that read the declaration.** It is arithmetic on the written text and needs nothing from the model, while the operand is written first and so looks like the first thing judged — which is the half of the order a reader inverts. The three gates about the REFERENCE still come before it, so the interval is neither first nor last.

**The kind gate takes what `FieldUtils.isLikeString` takes: `IStringType` or `IPredefinedType`.** The kernel's own javadoc for this method lists "strings, predefined types or non-closed enumerations", and the third of those is not a kind — an extensible enum is a STRING declaration carrying suggestions, so it passes as the string it is, while a closed `EnumerationType` is refused. Both are measured, because reading that list as three kinds is what the wording invites and is the same trap [KF402](#kf402) recorded one code earlier.

**The gate reads the FIELD's declaration, never the operator's result kind.** `RangeAsNumber` produces a number and refuses a number field; the two operators are measured on one fixture so that they are one law rather than two that happen to agree.

**An unstarred read into a repetition pre-empts all six classes**, the interval included. `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` comes from the gate outside this method, so a model whose only other defect is the interval — which needs nothing from the model at all — still draws the iteration class.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.RANGE_OPERAND_GATES`), silent on the iterating operand for that reason, and on a declaration whose effective type it does not resolve. The kits pre-check the interval law on the typed surface (`dsl.operators.RangeOperandTest`); the checker reads it off stored DM-JSON, where nothing pre-checked it.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RangeOperandGateLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.RangeOperandGatesTest`.

## §9 supplement — the two semantic-index gates that read the KEY, and the class that is last rather than first (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf404"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's structure, not an evaluation behaviour.

[KF351](#kf351) measured every gate of the semantic index that needs no comparison of declared types, and left two: the key's type against the index field's, and a key read from inside the indexed group. Both are now measured, and measuring them corrected the chain's own tail.

| the gate, in the measured order | class |
|---|---|
| the key is not a field / carries a star | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NO_FIELD` / `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_WILDCARD` |
| the indexed reference is itself indexed | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_SEMANTIC_INDEX` |
| the indexed group declares no index field | `MVK_NO_INDEX_FIELD` |
| a constant key the index field refuses, the empty one included | `MVK_INDEX_VALUE_INVALID` |
| an entity key whose declared type the index field's does not admit | `MVK_INDEX_TYPE_INCONSISTENT` |
| an entity key read from inside the indexed group | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_CONTAINED_IN_INDEX` |
| an entity key waiving value validation | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |
| the key carries a category projection | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_CATEGORY` |
| a star at the indexed group's own level | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_AND_WILDCARD` |
| a star ABOVE the indexed group | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_BELOW_WILDCARD` |

**The star ABOVE the indexed group is LAST, and a source reading puts it first.** `CheckSemanticIndexImpl.doChecks` locates the indexed group before it examines the key at all, so `getIndexGroup` looks like the gate that raises it; it does not raise it. The class comes from a later pass over the finished index list (`CheckEntityUtils.checkIndicesForA12Model`), which only sees a semantic index below a wildcard once `checkAndSetIndex` has written the index into its level — so every other class of the chain, `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_AND_WILDCARD` included, answers ahead of it. Four rows pair that star with a different earlier class, because one row could not tell "last" from "later than this one".

**The type comparison is `IFieldType.matchBaseType`, and it is not symmetric.** A string-keyed group admits a custom (predefined) key and a custom-keyed one admits a string key, while an enumeration-keyed group admits nothing but an enumeration — so a reader comparing declared type names for equality refuses a key A12 admits, and one comparing "same kind of type" admits a key A12 refuses. Measured from both sides against a string index field and an enumeration one, over text, custom, enumeration, number, boolean, confirm, date, time and date-range keys.

**A12's model layer has ONE date interface**, so a time, date-time, date-fragment or date-range key is compared against a date index field by an `instanceof` that cannot separate them. Every temporal declaration therefore differs from text, number, enumeration, boolean and confirm — the direction measured here — and whether two temporal declarations differ from each other is a question this comparison cannot ask.

**The containment class is only reachable on an ANCHORED rule.** A key read from inside the indexed group makes the read iterate unless the rule is declared in that group, and the iteration gate renames every class of the chain to `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_INVALID_ITER` when it does ([KF351](#kf351)). What binds a level is the rule's own anchoring and nothing else: a key inside a DIFFERENT repetition still leaves the group, and A12 answers `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX` — the rule-level gate ahead of this whole chain — rather than any class here.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.SEMANTIC_INDEX_STRUCTURE`, which the two classes extend rather than adding a family: the residue sits in the same kernel method on the same carrier). It stays silent where the comparison is one this reader cannot settle — a type definition or an unspecified declaration on either side, and a non-empty constant key against an index field whose own value validation constrains anything.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.SemanticIndexKeyGateLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.SemanticIndexStructureTest`.

## §6 supplement — the two shapes that need a declared BASE YEAR, and the third that is disabled by it (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf403"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about a model-level declaration, not an evaluation behaviour.

Two unrelated kernel checkers ask the same one-line question of the model, and a third construct asks its opposite:

| the shape | what a declared base year does |
|---|---|
| the `BaseYear` constant (`CheckKonstanteReferenzjahrImpl`) | REQUIRED; without one, `MVK_NO_BASE_YEAR` |
| a `Date` construction with no year parameter (`CheckDatumKonstruktImpl.checkJahresParam`) | REQUIRED; without one, `MVK_MISSING_YEAR` |
| the year-agreement walk of the range-overlap operators ([KF401](#kf401)) | DISABLES it — the walk returns on `hasBaseYear` as its first statement |

**So the declaration is not one switch in one direction**, which is the reading a family would reach for: it enables two shapes and turns a third gate off. All three are measured with and without it.

**The constant is refused by its own checker wherever it stands.** `CheckKonstanteReferenzjahrImpl` hangs off the `konstanteReferenzjahr` grammar rule rather than off any operator, so the carrier does not matter — measured on a comparison, an extraction and a shift, because a single carrier could not be told apart from that carrier's own operand gate.

**The day and month parameters are checked BEFORE the year one.** `check` calls `checkDayParam`, `checkMonatParam`, then `checkJahresParam`, so a two-parameter construction whose day is also out of range answers `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`. The corollary is that a two-parameter `Date`'s written slots ARE judged by the ordinary slot gates ([KF373](#kf373)) — which the portable checker had been declining as an unjudged arity, a silence this measurement closed.

**The `Time` construction has no year to omit.** It admits any prefix of its three slots, so the same two-argument shape is admitted there — the discriminator against the tempting reading "a short construction needs a base year".

**Extended 2026-09-15 — the error MESSAGE is a third place, and it answers from a DIFFERENT vocabulary.** The same constant written as a message parameter draws the unprefixed `NO_BASE_YEAR`, not `MVK_NO_BASE_YEAR` — measured on both language spellings, the German one on a `de_DE`-condition model declaring no base year. So "the carrier does not matter" holds for the constant's admission and NOT for its class: a checker sharing one code across the condition and the message arms would name the wrong one on whichever arm it did not measure.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.BASE_YEAR_REQUIREMENT`, which looks for the constant's TOKEN rather than for a carrier that admits it, and reads the construction's earlier slots through the slot family's own walk). Silent on everything when the model declares a base year, which is the family's precondition. The kits only NAME `MVK_NO_BASE_YEAR`, in four javadocs that each state the requirement is the kernel's call; nothing there refuses.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.BaseYearRequirementLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.BaseYearRequirementTest`; the message carrier by `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleMessageParameterLanguageLawsTest` (both spellings, against the declaring model as its control), mirrored by `consistency.MessageParameterReferenceTest`.

## §8 supplement — one keyword spells two validity conditions, and the kind gate admits less than its code's name (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf402"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about two constructs' operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`Valid` and `Invalid` spell two different grammar rules, and the OPERAND SHAPE is what tells them apart: `Valid(Field, "Type")` is `predefinedTypeValidityCondition` and `Valid(Date(…))` is `dateValidityCondition`. Two checker classes that share nothing ask them.

| the arm | the gate, in order | class |
|---|---|---|
| `Valid(Field, "Type")` | the subject names a group | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| | it carries a repetition star | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |
| | it waives value validation | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |
| | it is neither text nor enumeration | `MVK_NO_STRING_OR_ENUM_OR_EXT_ENUM` |
| | the type name is empty | `MVK_NO_EMPTY` |
| `Valid(Date(…))` | no slot names an entity | `MVK_ONLY_CONSTANTS_USED` |

**The kind gate's admitted set is narrower than its code's name.** `FieldUtils.isStringEnumOrExtensibleEnum` is `isString || isEnum || isExtensibleEnum`, and `isExtensibleEnum` is `t instanceof IStringType && ((IStringType) t).isExtensibleEnum()` — a FLAG on a string declaration rather than a kind of its own. So the third disjunct adds nothing to the first, a `CustomFieldType` is refused, and no predefined-type declaration enters the gate at all. Measured member by member rather than read off the name.

**The type name is opaque at model-check time.** Predefined types are a runtime client SPI, not a model-time registry, so A12 stores whatever was written and admits a name nothing registers; only the EMPTY one is refused, and only after the subject has passed all four gates above it. Both orderings are measured — a wrong kind with an empty name draws the kind class, a waived value validation with an empty name draws the raw class — because a reader checking the cheap string first would name it on a model A12 refuses for its field.

**The date arm's test is `entitySpec() != null` PER SLOT**, so what it asks is not "does this construction mention a field". An EXTRACT operator is a different grammar alternative, and `Valid(Date(DayFromDate(X), "02", "2024"))` plainly reads a field and is still constants-only to A12 — measured, and the row a reader gets backwards.

**The construction's own slot gates answer before the date arm's question**, measured on `Valid(Date("32", "02", "2024"))`, which draws `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` rather than this arm's class although every slot is a constant.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.VALIDITY_CONDITION_OPERANDS`), which owns all five gates of the first arm — nothing else reads that carrier, so deferring the first three would leave a model A12 refuses with no finding at all — and reads the construction through the slot family's own walk rather than restating what a slot demands. Silent on a `TypeDefType` or `UnspecifiedType` subject, whose effective type this reader does not resolve, and on a subject shape it cannot reduce to one bare path.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ValidityConditionOperandLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ValidityConditionOperandsTest`.

## §6 supplement — the range-overlap operators ask two walks of their list, and only the second has a base-year escape (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf401"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one operand list, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckEntityListenUtils.checkDateRangeWithoutSpecificInterpretationOfYear` and `checkDateRangeConsistentRegardingYear` are called back to back by both range-overlap constructs, so `DateRangesOverlap`'s plain list and `AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps`' subject-plus-values list are judged by the same two walks:

| the walk | the gate | class |
|---|---|---|
| per expanded field, in order | it is not a date-range declaration | `MVK_NO_DATE_RANGE` |
| | its `interpretationOfYear` is `FROM` or `TO` | `MVK_INVALID_DATE_RANGE_FORMAT` |
| then over the whole list | the references disagree about carrying a year | `MVK_DATE_WITH_AND_WITHOUT_YEAR` |

**The per-field walk completes before the agreement walk starts**, measured in both pairings: a list that is both wrong in kind and inconsistent about the year answers with the kind class, and one carrying a year-interpreting range beside a year mismatch answers with the format class.

**A model-level BASE YEAR disables the agreement walk and nothing else.** `checkDateRangeConsistentRegardingYear` returns on `hasBaseYear` as its first statement; the format walk has no such guard, so a `FROM`-interpreting range is refused with or without one. That pair of rows is the discriminator, and a reader taking "a base year makes year questions moot" from the first would admit a model A12 refuses.

**The agreement walk takes each REFERENCE's distinct FORMATS and only then asks which carry a year.** `map(getFormatOfDate).distinct().map(s -> s.contains("y"))`, then `res.size() > 1` refuses. So a reference expanding to two differently-spelled dated formats fails it although both carry a year — measured on a group of ranges declared `dd.MM.yyyy` and `yyyy-MM-dd`, where a group whose members share one format is admitted. The operator's own law would take both lists; the second is refused on the spelling.

**That spelling refusal stops at the REFERENCE boundary, and the walk asks the two carriers genuinely different questions (measured 2026-09-21).** `distinct()` runs inside one reference's expansion and is applied to format STRINGS, which is what makes `res.size() > 1` a count of spellings; the cross-reference test beside it is `flag.equals(res.get(0))`, a comparison of year-bearing BOOLEANS, so a spelling difference between two references is invisible to it. The discriminating pair is within one model and moves only the reference count: the same two range declarations (`dd.MM.yyyy` and `yyyy-MM-dd`) are refused as `DateRangesOverlap(Renewals)` — one group reference — and **ADMITTED** as `DateRangesOverlap(Renewals/RenewalOne, Renewals/RenewalTwo)`. So the general form of this row — "two differently-spelled dated formats are refused" — is false, and the qualifier "a reference expanding to" is the whole claim. Measured because our 2026-09-21 handback quoted the row without it and a12-kernel-lean declined the general reading on exactly that ground; their `05:328` year clause is correct for the cross-reference case.

**What comes BEFORE the two walks differs between the carriers, and neither may borrow the other's answer.** The plain list asks its own group gate first (`MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`, ahead of the arity gate — measured on a lone group, which fails both and draws the group class), and takes a starred field without asking, that arm calling no wildcard gate at all. The value list instead demands exactly one plain field as its subject and a matching base type from its values, so a wrong KIND on either side is `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` and never reaches the range walk. Two fields that AGREE do reach it, which is what keeps that pre-emption from reading as "this carrier cannot report the kind class".

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.DATE_RANGE_OPERAND_LIST`, keyed on the RANGE LIST rather than on either carrier's method, since the two walks are one shared helper). Silent where a pre-gate of another family answers, on a `DateRangeType` declaring no format, and on a repeated entity, whose duplicate class A12 draws first.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DateRangeOperandListLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.DateRangeOperandListTest`.

## §6 supplement — every date operator shares ONE argument slot, whose kind gate takes all four temporal declarations and whose constant gate takes four shapes (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf400"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about a shared operand slot, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckDatumAngabeImpl.check` is the checker for the grammar's `datumAngabe`, which the difference, shift and extraction operators all hand their operands to, so the gates below are the same bytes on every one of them. It branches on which of the slot's forms was written, and each form asks a different question:

| the form | the gate | class |
|---|---|---|
| a field spec | a category access | `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| | it names a group | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| | it carries a repetition star | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |
| | its declaration is not a date | `MVK_NO_DATE` |
| a string literal | it is none of the four accepted shapes | `MVK_INVALID_DATE_STRING` |
| a nested extraction | the extraction does not itself yield a date | `MVK_INVALID_DATE_FOR_OP` |

**The kind gate takes ALL FOUR temporal declarations.** `FieldUtils.isDate` tests `IDateType`, which covers time, stamp and fragment as well as date — a name that settles nothing, so each member is measured. A `TimeType` and a `DateFragmentType` pass this gate and are refused one layer up by the carrier's own format gate as `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`; the `DateRangeType` is the only temporal declaration the slot itself refuses, as `MVK_NO_DATE`. Those four rows are what separate the two layers, and a reader that folded them would name this class on a model A12 refuses with the other.

**The constant gate accepts FOUR shapes, not the two the kernel's own javadoc names.** `DateUtils.isStringAValidDate` switches on the string's LENGTH and then matches exactly one pattern:

| length | shape | example |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | `dd.MM.` — with a TRAILING DOT | `01.02.` |
| 8 | `HH:mm:ss` | `10:30:00` |
| 10 | `dd.MM.yyyy` | `01.02.2024` |
| 19 | `dd.MM.yyyy'T'HH:mm:ss` | `01.02.2024T10:30:00` |

Because the length picks the pattern and nothing else does, a 19-character stamp spelled with a SPACE instead of the `T` reaches the date-time pattern and fails it, one character from the row above; and the year-less shape without its trailing dot is not a shorter date but a length no case handles. The parse behind the pattern is non-lenient, so `32.01.2024` and `29.02.2023` match their pattern and are still refused by the calendar.

**The year-less constant is NOT year-agnostic.** `29.02.` is refused, because `SimpleDateFormat` fills the missing year with the epoch's — 1970, not a leap year. Measured rather than reasoned: the opposite was the intuitive prediction and was wrong.

**The slot accepts the year-less spelling; the MIXTURE is refused one layer up.** `"01.02."` against a dated field draws `MVK_DATE_WITH_AND_WITHOUT_YEAR`, and against another year-less constant is admitted — the same layering as the temporal-kind rows, and the pair that shows it.

**The nested form has its own gate**: an extraction standing in a date slot must itself yield a date, which the seven component extractors (`YearFromDate`, `HoursFromTime`, …) do not — they yield a number, and draw `MVK_INVALID_DATE_FOR_OP`. `DateFromDateTime` and `TimeFromDateTime` are admitted.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.DATE_ARGUMENT_SLOT`, keyed on the SLOT rather than the operator, so a new date operator needs one map entry rather than a table of its own). Silent on the two classes A12 draws one layer up, which no family owns; on a category access, whose operand the shared reducer declines before any family sees the call — an under-report with no owner; on a `TypeDefType` or `UnspecifiedType` declaration, whose effective type this reader does not resolve; and on a slot whose repetition stars do not match its repeating levels, where a wildcard-validity class answers ahead of everything here.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DateArgumentSlotLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.DateArgumentSlotTest`.

## §9 supplement — `NumberOfDifferentValues` types its list from the LEADING field, and the leader NO arm claims has a class of its own (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf399"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one operation's operand list, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldListenAnzahlOpImpl.check`'s third case reads `CheckEntityListenUtils.firstType` — the operand type of the first EXPANDED field — and branches on it, so the same list is admitted under one leader and refused under another, and which code it draws is decided before any member is looked at:

| the leader | what the rest of the list must be | otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| text, custom or enumeration | one of those three | `MVK_STRING_ENUM_AND_NON_STRING_ENUM` |
| …and then, over the whole list | not waiving value validation | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |
| a number | a number | `MVK_NUMBER_AND_NON_NUMBER` |
| temporal | the component-set comparison ([KF193](#kf193)) | `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE`, … |
| Boolean, Confirm or DateRange | — | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_CMP_DATE_ALLOWED` |

**The else branch has a class of its OWN rather than falling into the numeric arm**, which is the row a reader assembling the arms from the codes' names would miss — "not string, not number, not date" reads like the numeric arm's territory and is not. All three unclaimed leaders are measured separately.

**The string arm FOLDS custom and enumeration in with text**, where the extrema of the neighbouring method refuse both — `isLikeString || isEnum` against `isNumber`. So the same list is legal under `NumberOfDifferentValues` and refused under `MaxValue`, with no change to the model.

**The leader is the first EXPANDED field, not the first operand**, so a GROUP leader is typed by its own first member — measured on a group of numbers leading a text list, which draws the numeric arm's class.

**The value-validation gate runs over the WHOLE list after the kind walk**, not interleaved with it: a kind defect later in the list than a waiving field still answers first.

**`checkNoCategories` is the FIRST statement of the method** and outruns even the duplicate walk, which every other gate of this construct sits behind — measured on a list carrying a category access and a duplicate together, which draws `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED`.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.FIELD_LIST_OPERATION_OPERANDS`, which carries this operator beside the four of `CheckFeldListenOpImpl` — the two methods never share a carrier, so neither family can name the other's class), silent on a temporal leader (`TEMPORAL_AGGREGATE_OPERANDS` owns it), on a `TypeDefType` or `UnspecifiedType` leader, and — an under-report with no owner at all — on the category gate, whose operand the shared reducer declines.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DistinctValueOperandKindLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.FieldListOperationOperandsTest`.


## §8 supplement — the SCALAR value list judges its subject completely first, and a CUSTOM declaration rides with text on both gates that group them (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf398"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's operand gates, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldUndWerteListenBedingungImpl.check` judges the SUBJECT field completely before looking at the list, and the list is then two different questions depending on which of its two spellings it takes:

| the gate, in order | class |
|---|---|
| the subject is a group | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| the subject carries a repetition star | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |
| the subject is neither text, custom, enumeration nor number | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` |
| the subject waives value validation | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |
| `[field]` entries: one named twice, the subject included | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` |
| `[field]` entries: one of another base type | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| `[field]` entries: one waiving value validation | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |
| a written-out list whose KIND is not the subject's | `MVK_INVALID_TYPES_FOR_COMPARISON` |
| a written-out value outside a plain enumeration's domain | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION` |
| …outside the CATEGORY's classifications | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION_CATEGORY` |

**The subject gates run on BOTH list spellings**, which is what makes the two one construct rather than two: a boolean subject draws `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` whether the list is `"x"` or `[Other]`.

**A CUSTOM declaration rides with text on both gates that group declarations, and its name says otherwise on each.** `isLikeString` admits `IPredefinedType` beside `IStringType`, so a custom subject passes a gate spelled `…STRING_ENUM_NUMBER…`; and `matchBaseType` gives the two the same base type, so a custom `[field]` entry matches a STRING subject where an enumeration entry does not. Both cells measured rather than transferred — the second is the one that would be got wrong in both directions by a reader expecting the gate's own name.

**The kind gate is asked before the domain one**, so a NUMBER list under a categorized enumeration draws `MVK_INVALID_TYPES_FOR_COMPARISON` and never reaches the category at all.

**…and a `->` CATEGORY access SWAPS the domain rather than widening it**, the same asymmetry [KF397](#kf397) measured on the quantifier carrier, here on the scalar one and with the scalar's own class.

**The seven refused subject kinds are measured one by one rather than transferred from each other.** A12 asks three POSITIVE predicates, so what the gate refuses is their complement — and a complement is exactly what a checker may not infer: the grid puts Boolean, Confirm, Date, Time, DateTime, DateFragment and DateRange to the kernel separately.

**The duplicate walk takes the SUBJECT together with the entries**, so naming the subject inside its own list is `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` rather than a self-comparison A12 admits.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.SCALAR_VALUE_LIST_GATES`, renamed from `ENUM_CONSTANT_DOMAIN` when the rest of the method's gates landed beside the one it had), silent on a `TypeDefType` or `UnspecifiedType` subject, on an enumeration declaring a `tableName`, and on a subject whose repetition stars do not match its repeating levels, where a wildcard-validity class answers ahead of every gate here.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ScalarValueListGateLawsTest` and `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumConstantDomainLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ScalarValueListGatesTest`.


## §8 supplement — the value-list condition judges its FIELD list before the list it is compared with, and one of its four operators is a different construct (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf397"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's two operand lists, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldListeUndWerteListenBedingungImpl.check` walks one shape for all four operators and branches on the operator token TWICE — once on the field list and once on the value list:

| the gate, in order | class |
|---|---|
| the FIELD list's entries do not all share a base type | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| `AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps`: the field list is not exactly one plain field | `MVK_INVALID_PARAMETER_FOR_DATE_RANGE_COMPARISON` |
| the other three: an entry is neither text, enumeration nor number | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` |
| `AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps` against a WRITTEN-OUT list | `MVK_NO_CONST` |
| a written-out list against a NUMBER field list | `MVK_INVALID_TYPES_FOR_COMPARISON` |
| a written-out value outside the enumeration's domain | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION_OR_CATEGORY` |
| an ENTITY value list of another base type | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` |

**The FIELD list is judged before the value list's type is looked at**, and that ORDER is the finding rather than any single row: a date-range field list against a text one is `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED`, the field list's own kind class, while a text field list against a date-range one is the disagreement class. A reader merging the two lists into one same-type walk gets the first of those wrong — [KF380](#kf380)'s portable family did, and its own grid could not see it because every row it held had a listable field list.

**The same-type gate runs for all FOUR operators**, ahead of the branch on the operator token, so a mixed field list under `AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps` is the disagreement class and its own shape class is never reached.

**Its shape gate reads the REFERENCE list, not the expansion.** A group holding exactly one date-range field is refused, even though every other operator in this construct expands a group to its fields — the two readings of "exactly one" separated by one row.

**The enum domain is the UNION over the whole field list**, so a written-out constant that only the SECOND listed enumeration declares is admitted; a reader checking each field separately would refuse a model A12 takes.

**…and a `->` CATEGORY access SWAPS that entry's contribution rather than widening it.** One enumeration read through its category contributes the category's tokens and stops contributing its own values, so `BandedTier -> Band In "BASIC"` is refused where `BandedTier In "BASIC"` is admitted. Held on one declaration with only the access varying.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.VALUE_LIST_CONDITION_GATES`, renamed from `VALUE_LIST_QUANTIFIER_OPERAND_KIND` when the two branches landed), silent on a repeated entity (the duplicate walk answers first), on the `noValueValidation` gate between the field gates and the value list, on the date-range arm's two year-consistency classes, and on an enumeration declaring a `tableName`, which A12 exempts from the domain check.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ValueListConditionOperandLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ValueListConditionGatesTest`.

## §5 supplement — `+` is not an arithmetic operator: it asks its own question, and refuses an enumeration that carries LABELS (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf396"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's operand types, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckOperationImpl.checkAndSetTypes` switches on the operator's grammar context. Four of the five arms call `CheckOpUtils.checkOpIsANumberInCalc` on both operands; `+` calls it on neither.

| the expression | A12 |
|---|---|
| `*`, `/`, `-` or `^` over anything but a number | `MVK_NO_NUMBER_FOR_CALC` |
| `+` over two numbers, or over two string-LIKE sides | admitted |
| `+` over a mixed pair | `MVK_NO_STRING_OR_NUMBER_FOR_ADD` |
| `+` over an enumeration carrying display LABELS | the same class |

**A CUSTOM declaration is string-LIKE and a date is neither**, which `OperationResultTypeMap.getOpTypeForField` makes explicit: it sorts `IStringType` and `IPredefinedType` into one STRING base type and gives a date, a range, a boolean and a confirm their own, so all four fail both of `+`'s arms. Measured over all seven declared kinds on each of the four numeric operators.

**The display-label refusal is the row a source read alone would miss the shape of.** Two enumerations declaring the same two tokens differ only in whether their values carry a `label`, and the labelled one is refused beside a plain text — under the KIND class, not a class of its own. A12 exempts a category access at that branch, which is the only way to concatenate such an enumeration.

**The kind walk PRE-EMPTS both arity gates inside one operation context.** A string in a two-division chain is `MVK_NO_NUMBER_FOR_CALC` alone and the same chain with a number there is `MVK_TOO_MANY_DIV_FOR_CALC`; the same pair holds for a nested power. That is what makes the five classes ONE portable family rather than two: a checker asking the questions independently would name a second class on a model A12 answers once ([KF378](#kf378) measured the arity half's own ordering).

**`^` asks the kind question BEFORE the exponent's scale**, so a non-numeric exponent draws the kind class and never `MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP` — the order inside `checkAndSetPowerType`, measured rather than read.

**An inner operation's RESULT type is what the outer operator judges**, which is the only way the two classes meet on one expression: a concatenation subtracted from is the number class, and a product added to a text is the addition class.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.ARITHMETIC_OPERATION_GATES`), silent on a written-out text, a call, a comma-separated argument list, a category access, and a typedef or unspecified declaration.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ArithmeticOperandKindLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.ArithmeticOperationGatesTest`.

## §11 supplement — the four single-field value operators share ONE head and then demand four different things, two of them the opposite of their names (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf395"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's operand, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldOpImpl.check` gates the operand as a field without a repetition star and then switches on the operator token. The four arms share nothing after that switch:

| the operator | what it demands | otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `AbsValue` | no category, a Number declaration | `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED`, `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| `FieldValueAsString` | no category, a **Number** declaration | `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED`, `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| `Length` | no category, a string-LIKE declaration | `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED`, `MVK_NO_STRING` |
| `FieldValueAsNumber` | a declaration A12 can convert; **no category gate at all** | `MVK_NO_CONVERT_IN_NUMBER` |
| all four, first | one field, no star | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`, `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |

**`FieldValueAsString` demands a NUMBER**, which inverts the reading its name invites — it stringifies a numeric value, so a string operand is `MVK_NO_NUMBER`. Read as "any field's value, as a string" it is wrong on every non-numeric declaration, and the mistake is invisible until the model is checked. Measured against all four declared classes.

**`FieldValueAsNumber` is the one arm with no category gate**, and the kernel source carries a standing note at the switch asking each new arm to decide that for itself — so this is a deliberate asymmetry rather than an omission. The row that separates the two possible readings is a category whose tokens differ in kind from the enumeration's own values: it reads the CATEGORY's, not the enumeration's.

**Its string arm reads the DECLARATION and never a stored value** — a bounded `maxLength` of at most 15 AND exactly the pattern `[0-9]+`. A five-character string with no pattern is refused, and so is a `[0-9]+` string with no length bound; whatever a document happens to hold is never consulted. Its enumeration arm reads the declared values, each of which must parse inside the same 15-digit budget.

**`MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` never arrives ALONE through this operator, and both links were ATTACKED rather than read.** It fires on a `noValueValidation` string and runs after the conversion gate, whose pattern demand that declaration excludes: declare both and A12 answers `MVK_STRING_TYPE_PARAMS_INCONSISTENT, MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`; drop the pattern to make the declaration legal and `MVK_NO_CONVERT_IN_NUMBER` answers first. Measuring each link separately would not have established the chain, which is why both are in the grid.

**`MVK_INVALID_TABLE_ENUM` is unreachable for a different reason entirely** — an enumeration carrying a `tableName` makes the document model UNREADABLE, so no consistency check runs at all (§8).

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.FIELD_VALUE_OPERATOR_OPERANDS`), narrower than A12 on the enumeration arm by design: it refuses a declared value only where a character outside the numeric alphabet makes it certain, leaving a spelling the kernel's own parser rejects for its grammar to A12.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldValueOperatorOperandLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.FieldValueOperatorOperandsTest`.

## §11 supplement — a CUSTOM declaration is text-like on every gate that admits a string and a number on none (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf394"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about how one declared type is sorted, not an evaluation behaviour.

A12's `FieldUtils` puts `IPredefinedType` beside `IStringType` under `isLikeString` and leaves it out of `isNumber`, and the five gates that ask the question each ask it in their own method. Measured on one custom declaration across all five:

| the carrier | the condition | A12 |
|---|---|---|
| the rounding field spelling | `RoundUpValue(Serial, 2)` | `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| the rounding operation spelling | `RoundUp([Serial], 2)` | `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| a field list that is added up | `Sum(Serial, Quantity)` | `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| a field list that is ordered | `MaxValue(Serial, Quantity)` | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` |
| the amount a date is shifted by | `AddDays(PlacedOn, [Serial])` | `MVK_NON_NUMERIC` |
| the text arm of a value list | `NumberOfValueInFields("X" In Serial, …)` | **admitted** |
| the same arm over a number — the control | `NumberOfValueInFields("X" In Quantity, …)` | `MVK_NO_STRING_OR_ENUM` |

Two more rows sit in [KF395](#kf395)'s grid on the same declaration: `Length` admits it and `AbsValue` refuses it, which is the same split one gate earlier.

**The grid exists because of the defect it caught, and the defect is a spelling.** The portable checker matched the token `CustomType` in four of its type sets, while the discriminator A12 STORES is `CustomFieldType` — so every one of those sets was blind to a custom declaration and nothing could see it: a set that matches nothing simply never matches, each family's mirror stayed green against the checker's own output, and no laws grid had ever put a custom field to the kernel. Three of the four were silences; the fourth was the forbidden direction, `ValueInFieldsConstantKind`'s text arm listing the custom type among the declarations it ADMITS, so the dead token turned an admission into an over-rejection.

**The class is now guarded rather than remembered.** `CheckerFieldTypeTokenGuardTest` reads the legal spellings off the checker's own `DECLARED_FIELD_TYPES` — the table mirroring A12's deserializer switch — and scans every checker source for a capitalized `…Type` literal that is not one of them. Both denominators are derived, so a new family's type set enters the scan without anyone declaring it.

Reported by the portable checker on all five numeric carriers; the text arm's admission is a silence it now correctly keeps.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.CustomFieldTypeOperandLawsTest` and `CheckerFieldTypeTokenGuardTest`.

## §11 supplement — the six rounding operators are TWO constructs sharing one digits gate, asked last (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf393"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's operand shapes, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckRundenOpImpl` and `CheckRundenOperOpImpl` differ in what their operand may BE, and end at the same `CheckOpUtils.isSpecificationForRounding`:

| the spelling | the operand | the gates it meets, in order |
|---|---|---|
| `RoundUpValue`, `RoundDownValue`, `RoundAccountingValue` | an entity spec | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`, `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`, `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED`, `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| `RoundUp`, `RoundDown`, `RoundAccounting` | an operation | `MVK_NO_CONST`, `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| both, last | the digit count | `MVK_INVALID_DIGIT_FOR_ROUNDING` |

**The digit domain is `0..14` inclusive**, the raise dated `A12K-3691` in the kernel source, and it holds identically across all six operators — measured on the full cross product rather than on one spelling.

**Neither operand refusal set is derivable from the other.** The bare spelling refuses a CONSTANT, a shape the field spelling cannot express; the field spelling refuses a group, a wildcard and a category, none of which is an operation. A consumer treating the six as one operator is wrong on both halves.

**The digits gate is asked LAST on both constructs**, so an out-of-range count is invisible behind an operand the construct already refuses — `RoundUpValue(ATextField, 99)` is `MVK_NO_NUMBER` and `RoundUp(5, 99)` is `MVK_NO_CONST`. That fixes the gate's POSITION rather than only its class, and it is what the portable family's walk order reproduces.

**The comparand is a confound here too, on the SCALE axis.** A rounded result's scale is the digits argument, so comparing it to a field with a scale of its own draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` from the number-comparison gate and no rounding gate is reached at all — which masked every admitted cell of the first grid run. Every row is compared against a literal instead ([KF249](#kf249) is the same confound on the kind axis).

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.ROUNDING_OPERANDS`), with two disclosed under-reports: a category operand, which reduces to no entity spec, and a digits argument written as anything but plain digits, whose grammar-level treatment is not measured.

**A SIGNED digits argument is a grammar refusal, not a digits-gate one (measured 2026-09-22).** `RoundUpValue(UnitPrice, -1)` and `RoundUp([UnitPrice], -1)` are both `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`, while `15` on either is `MVK_INVALID_DIGIT_FOR_ROUNDING` and `0` is admitted: the slot is an unsigned integer token, so the two ends of `0..14` are two different classes. `AbsValue`, the one `…Value` spelling without a digits slot, draws the same class for ANY digits argument — `AbsValue(UnitPrice, 2)` and even `AbsValue(UnitPrice, 0)` — against an admitted `AbsValue(UnitPrice)`. This answers the kernel half of the second disclosure above for a sign; other non-digit spellings stay unmeasured, and whether the portable checker reports these is not settled here. *Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RoundingPlacesOverflowLawsTest`, which also pins rulekit's refusals citing each class.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RoundingOperandLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.RoundingOperandsTest`.

## §6 supplement — date arithmetic asks FOUR questions of its operand, and the ORDER is what makes two of the classes reachable (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf392"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's operand types, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckDatumAddOpImpl.check` runs one fixed sequence over the date it shifts, then types the amount:

| # | the question | class |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | is the date fully known? | `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE` |
| 2 | does its format spell the component this operator adds? | `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` |
| 3 | does its format spell any calendar component at all? | `MVK_INVALID_TIME` |
| 4 | is it a stamp under `AddMonths` or `AddYears`? | `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` |
| 5 | is the amount a number? | `MVK_NON_NUMERIC` |

**`MVK_INVALID_TIME` is reachable only through the three CLOCK operators**, and that is the finding — reading gate 3 on its own gets it backwards. The gate sits BEHIND the component gate, so under `AddDays`/`AddMonths`/`AddYears` any format that reaches it already carries a calendar component; only `AddHours`/`AddMinutes`/`AddSeconds` over a pure `TimeType` arrive with none. Measured over all six operators against six declared temporal shapes: a clock under `AddDays` draws gate 2's class, not gate 3's.

**Gate 4 is not a component question**, which is what its own row is for: `AddMonths` and `AddYears` refuse a `DateTimeType` whose format spells exactly what they add, the kernel source citing `A12K-620` — the behaviour over a stamp was never settled. `AddDays` and the three clock operators accept the same field, and that pair is the discriminator against reading the refusal as a missing component.

**A model-level BASE YEAR disables gate 2 for `AddYears` alone**, the same supplementation the aggregates' component comparison applies ([KF193](#kf193)).

**The amount is typed LAST**, so a model with both operands wrong reports the date one — the control that fixes gate 5's position rather than only its class.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.DATE_ARITHMETIC_OPERANDS`), which judges the amount only where it is a bare field reference: A12 types it as a whole OPERATION, so a computed amount is left alone.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DateArithmeticOperandLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.DateArithmeticOperandsTest`.

## §9 supplement — the field-LIST operations share one list and one arity gate, then each asks a different KIND question (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf391"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one construct's operand kinds, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldListenOpImpl.check` is a switch on the OPERATOR token run over a list two shared gates have already accepted, so the class a model draws is decided by the caller rather than by the list:

| the operator | what it demands of every expanded field | class |
|---|---|---|
| `FirstFilledValue` | not a Confirm declaration (`checkNoBoolY`) | `MVK_NO_BOOLY_ALLOWED` |
| `FirstFilledValue`, behind it | one operation RESULT type across the list | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| `Sum`, `SumOfProducts` | a Number declaration | `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |
| `MaxValue`, `MinValue`, behind a non-temporal LEADER | a Number declaration | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` |
| `MaxValue`, `MinValue`, behind a temporal LEADER | the component-set walk of [KF389](#kf389) | three classes |

**`MVK_NO_BOOLY_ALLOWED` names a kind it does not name.** `checkNoBoolY` tests `FieldUtils.isYes`, which is `IYesType` alone, and `IYesNoType` is a SIBLING interface rather than a subtype — so a BOOLEAN declaration clears the gate entirely and only a CONFIRM one is refused. Measured over all twelve declared kinds in both positions: one confirm anywhere in the list refuses it whatever else is there, a boolean list is admitted, and a boolean beside a text field is refused by the type-matching gate behind it instead. Reading the code as "no boolean kinds" is wrong in exactly that cell, and it is the cell a consumer reaches for first.

**The type-matching gate compares the OPERATION RESULT type, not the declared base type, and inside the temporal family that means the declared FORMAT.** The arm calls `checkAllFieldsMatchingOperationType`, which maps every expanded field through `OperationResultTypeMap.getOpTypeForField` and matches it against the FIRST field's mapping (`OperationResultType.matches` — `equals`, then `hasSameKnownFormatStringIfExists`). That mapping folds ENUM into STRING, so String, Enumeration, Custom and a string-based typedef mix freely; it sends every `IDateType` — date, clock, stamp and fragment alike — to ONE `DATETIME` result base type *carrying `getFormat()`*, so the kind is not consulted there and the format decides; and it gives `IDateRangeType` a result base type of its own, so a range is refused beside a date carrying the range's own declared format.

**Corrected 2026-09-21: this paragraph read "reads the operand BASE type … every other pair of distinct kinds is refused — including two temporal kinds".** Both halves were wrong and both were already contradicted inside this repository. The gate is not `checkSameBaseType`: that method's `IDateType.matchBaseType` admits *any* `IDateType` pair and reads no format at all, so it cannot produce the refusals measured here — `CheckFeldListenOpImpl`'s `ERSTER_ANGEGEBENER_WERT` arm asks the result-type gate instead. And the temporal claim was a **confounded fixture**: every temporal field in `FieldListOperandKindLawsTest` carries a format bound 1:1 to its kind, so its "DATE then TIME" row moves both variables and cannot say which was read. [KF206](#kf206) had already established that the format vocabulary is kind-independent, which is what makes the discriminating declarations authorable, and both the operator catalog's `FirstFilledValue` constraint line and `FirstFilledValueFamilyLawsTest` had carried the format-keyed law since 2026-08-19. Flagged by a12-kernel-lean (`SPEC-2026-09-21-02`) against our own §9 question; re-measured here rather than adopted on their report, and the range cell that moves the KIND alone was added to the owning lock in the same pass, because the published family claim did not rest on one.

**`Sum` has no leader slot and no escape arm**, which is what separates it from the extrema: a date operand is `MVK_NO_NUMBER` there and `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE`-or-admitted at `MaxValue`, over the same two fields.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.FIELD_LIST_OPERATION_OPERANDS`), which transcribes the caller table and leaves `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` and `SumOfProducts`' own six gates to other families.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldListOperandKindLawsTest` (the confirm and `Sum` arms) and `rulekit.validate.laws.ExtremumOperandKindGridLawsTest` (the extrema's numeric arm), mirrored by `consistency.FieldListOperationOperandsTest`. The result-type gate's own keying is `rulekit.validate.laws.FirstFilledValueFamilyLawsTest`'s — cite that class for it, never this entry's grid, whose temporal rows are confounded by construction.

## §9 supplement — `FieldValuesNotUnique`'s kind gate admits the CLOCK and STAMP kinds, and its date test is the SPELLING (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf390"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one operator's operand kinds, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldListenBedingungImpl`'s `FELD_WERTE_NICHT_EINDEUTIG` arm runs four gates in a fixed order, and the grid measures all four so the second one's position is fixed rather than assumed:

| # | gate | class |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `checkIsMoreThanOneFieldOrIsAGroup` | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN` |
| 2 | `checkOnlyStringEnumNumberOrDateWithSameFormat` | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_DATE_ALLOWED` |
| 3 | `checkSameBaseType` | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| 4 | `checkAllAreValueValidation` | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` |
