**Gate 2's admitted KIND set cannot be read off its class name, and four shapes turn on it.** "String, enum, number or date" reads as a closed list, but `FieldUtils.isDate` accepts the clock and stamp kinds too: a `TimeType`, a `DateTimeType` and a `DateFragmentType` beside a text field all CLEAR this gate and are refused by gate 3 instead — as is an `EnumerationType`, which clears it as string-like. A `DateRangeType` is the only measured refusal. Naming gate 2's class on any of the other four would be the wrong class on a correct rejection.

**Gate 2's date test is the declared format STRING, and it spans KINDS.** `yyyy-MM-dd` beside `dd.MM.yyyy` is refused although the two are one component set — the contrast that separates this gate from the aggregates' component-set gate ([KF193](#kf193)) — and a `DateType` spelled `yyyy-MM-dd` beside a `DateTimeType` spelled `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss` draws this class rather than gate 3's, the kind gate running first.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.FIELD_VALUES_NOT_UNIQUE_OPERAND_KIND`), whose refusal set is an allow-list of what was measured rather than the complement of the admitted one.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldValuesNotUniqueKindGateLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.FieldValuesNotUniqueOperandKindTest`.

## §6 supplement — a date operand list's three gates are ONE walk, so two defects answer by POSITION (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf389"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about aggregate operand types, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckEntityListenUtils.checkOpTypesAreComparableDatetimeType` walks a date-typed operand list ONCE and asks three questions of each operand in turn, in this order: is its base type DATETIME (`MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE`), is its date fully known (`MVK_PARTIAL_DATE_NOT_ALLOWED`), and do its declared components match the FIRST operand's (`MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE`). [KF260](#kf260) and [KF193](#kf193) measured the second and third; the first was recorded as pre-checked by the typed builders and so had never been measured on a STORED model, where nothing prevents the shape.

**A later operand of any plainly non-temporal kind draws `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE`** — measured on a text and on a number operand, across all three carriers that type their list from its leading field (`MaxValue`, `MinValue`, `NumberOfDifferentValues`).

**The LEADING operand is a different question, and the row that shows it is the control.** It decides which arm types the list at all, so a non-temporal leader never reaches this gate: `MaxValue` and `MinValue` answer `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE`, and `NumberOfDifferentValues` answers `MVK_STRING_ENUM_AND_NON_STRING_ENUM` — three carriers, two classes, neither of them this one.

**Two defects in one list answer by OPERAND POSITION, not by a precedence among the classes.** `MaxValue(FiledOn, Adjuster, CoverFrom)` is `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` and `MaxValue(FiledOn, CoverFrom, Adjuster)` is `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` — the same two defects, swapped, each answered by whichever operand comes first. A fixed class precedence would give both rows one code, so this pair is what makes the three questions one walk rather than three passes.

**The boundary: two carriers take a different arm entirely.** `FieldValuesNotUnique` and `FirstFilledValue` route through `matchBaseType` / `checkAllFieldsMatchingOperationType`, which compares each operand against its PREDECESSOR under a single class — both answer `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` on the same list, so this file's class is not "any date list".

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.TEMPORAL_AGGREGATE_OPERANDS`), which refuses only on a declared type it is CERTAIN is non-temporal: a `DateTimeType` declaring no format takes its default and is still a date, so absence of a format is never read as absence of a date.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DateAggregateBaseTypeGateLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.TemporalAggregateOperandsTest`.

## §9 supplement — an entity list's DUPLICATE and ROOT-GROUP gates are the CALLER's, not the list's (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf388"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about which gate answers an entity list, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckEntityListenUtils.getRefList` refuses a repeated entity while it BUILDS the reference list, and its callers then ask a root-group gate — or do not. Both are shared utilities, so the operator never decides the LAW; it decides only whether the law is asked. That makes the caller table the thing to measure, and the grid therefore moves the operator and holds the list fixed. [KF325](#kf325) and [KF326](#kf326) measured this on the GROUP-LIST carrier; this widens it onto the field and value lists their own boundaries named as out of scope.

| the list | class | on which carriers |
|---|---|---|
| an unstarred entity named twice | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` | all 28 that build a list |
| an entity under another of the same list | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` | all 28 |
| a lone ROOT group | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` | 22 |
| …a root group beside another parameter | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_WITH_OTHER_PARAMETERS` | `AtLeastOneGroupFilled`, `NoGroupFilled`, `NumberOfFilledGroups` |
| a lone root group, under `NumberOfFilledGroups` | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDGN` | its own arity gate answers |
| a lone root group, under `GroupFilled`/`GroupNotFilled` | ADMITTED | they ask no root-group gate at all |
| a lone root group, under `AtLeastOneGroupFilled`/`NoGroupFilled` | ADMITTED | their gate speaks only above arity 1 |

**Duplicates precede everything.** Measured on lists that break two laws at once: `(/Order, /Order)` is the duplicate class rather than the root-group one, and `(Quantity, Quantity, Quantity)` under a one-entity operator is the duplicate class rather than the arity one — because `getRefList` asks while it builds, and every other gate is asked of the list it returns.

**The ROOT GROUP beside any other entity of its own model is a NESTED DUPLICATE, never a root-group reference.** Every entity of a model is under its root group, so `(/Order, Shipping)` satisfies `isEntityIndirectlyReferenced` and the earlier gate answers — on all 28 carriers. The consequence is that `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_WITH_OTHER_PARAMETERS` looks dead from any one-root fixture, and it is not: a model with a SECOND root group is the only shape on which a list can hold a root group beside something not under it, and there `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Order, /Payment)`, `AtLeastOneGroupFilled(/Order, /Payment)` and `NoGroupFilled(/Order, /Payment)` all draw it while `AllGroupsFilled(/Order, /Payment)` and `AllFieldsFilled(/Order, /Payment)` draw the plain class. The class was measured rather than declared unreachable, which is the row a one-root grid could not have produced.

**Corrected 2026-09-21: the carrier column above read "`NumberOfFilledGroups` alone", and the correction is a DENOMINATOR fix rather than a new measurement.** The second-root grid held that one carrier against two plain-class controls, so the two other carriers that ask the same gate were never in it — and the class-level operator list this finding's grids iterate does not name them either, which is why nothing looked missing. [KF326](#kf326) had measured both a day earlier, the source-verified caller split in [KF11](#kf11)'s rootGroup-bar paragraph had carried them since 2026-07-12, and `GroupListRootOperandLawsTest.whichClassARootBesideAnotherOperandDraws` had been green on them the whole time; this entry contradicted all three. Re-measured here on THIS fixture — both draw `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_WITH_OTHER_PARAMETERS` — and locked by the two rows now in `whetherTheMoreThanOneParameterRootGroupGateIsReachable`. **The shipped portable checker was never wrong**: `GroupListOperands.kt`'s `SOLE_ROOT_CARRIERS` has carried all three since the family landed, so no consumer under-reported. Found by a12-kernel-lean reading our law test against our finding (`SPEC-2026-09-21-01`) — a defect no guard of ours could catch, two live statements of one fact having disagreed without either being wrong about its own fixture.

**A STARRED read is exempt from the direct test and not from the nested one.** `checkDuplicatesInDirectRefs` skips a reference carrying a wildcard on an A12 model — two starred reads of one repetition are two different rows rather than one entity twice — so `(Lines*/Amount, Lines*/Amount)` reaches each operator's own gate instead, which is how the exemption is visible: `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID1` on the one-entity operators, `MVK_INCOMPLETE_INPUT` on the aggregates, ADMITTED on the field quantifiers. `checkDuplicatesInIndirectRefs` skips nothing.

**Two mechanisms behind the split, both read from source and each confirmed by its measured row.** `GroupFilled`/`GroupNotFilled` take the `KONTEXT_ANGEGEBEN` arm of `CheckKontextListenBedingungImpl`, which asks only `checkOnlyGroups`; the `ALLE_KONTEXTE_ANGEGEBEN` arm beside it does ask the gate, which is why operators whose names suggest the same family split. And three carriers — `AtLeastOneGroupFilled`, `NoGroupFilled`, `NumberOfFilledGroups` — ask `checkNoRootGroupWhenMoreThanOneParameter` rather than `checkNotRootGroupReferenced`, a different method with a different class and an arity precondition, which is what makes their sole-root cell admit rather than exempt them from a gate.

**The one caller that asks no root-group gate and still asks both duplicate gates** is `RepetitionNotUnique`: `CheckWiederholungBedingungImpl` calls `getRefList` and goes straight to its own key-list gates, so `RepetitionNotUnique(Shipping, Shipping/Carrier)` is `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` — ahead of the `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` that a lone group draws there ([KF355](#kf355)), which is what fixes the order between the two sets.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.ENTITY_LIST_PRE_GATES`) on the carriers the group-list families do not own.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.EntityListPreGateLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.EntityListPreGatesTest`.

## §1 supplement — the PATTERN arm's first question is about SHAPE, and its four classes are strictly ordered (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf387"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about comparison operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkPatternOp` returns before every type-agreement arm and asks four questions of its own. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.PatternComparisonOperandLawsTest` (15 rows), mirrored by `consistency.PatternComparisonOperandsTest`.

| the question | class |
|---|---|
| is the left side a plain FIELD READ? | `MVK_INVALID_PARAMETER_FOR_PATTERN_COMPARISON` |
| is each side a TEXT declaration or a written-out text? | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_PATTERN_COMPARISON` |
| is the right side WRITTEN OUT? | `MVK_MISSING_CONST_IN_PATTERN_COMP` |
| is that written-out value a pattern the admission gate takes? | `MVK_INVALID_PATTERN` |

**The first question is about SHAPE, not type, and the row that shows it is a written-out value on the left**: `"x" PatternMatched [GiftNote]` is refused for the left side being an expression rather than for what it spells, and a call on the left is refused before its result type is asked at all. A reading that started from types would name the second class on both.

**The constancy question is asked AFTER both type questions.** A number declaration on the right draws the type class; a TEXT declaration on the right draws the constant one. The pair is what fixes the order, since a reading that asked about constancy first would give one class to both.

**An EMPTY pattern is admitted.** It compiles and it spells no blacklisted adjacency, so the last question takes it — measured, because an empty regex reads as the obvious refusal.

**The whole arm yields to the constant gate**: two written-out values are `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_CONST` ([KF382](#kf382)), asked ahead of it.

**The pattern gate here is the same admission gate a DECLARED pattern meets, under a different code** — `MVK_INVALID_PATTERN` on a condition, `MVK_PATTERN_INVALID` on a declaration, the same two words swapped ([KF165](#kf165)). Both refuse `a++` and the escaped `a\*+`, the gate reading SOURCE TEXT rather than the expression it spells.

## §1 supplement — the DATE arm compares three format QUESTIONS, not formats, and claims every partner of another kind (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf386"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about comparison operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkDateType` and `checkDateRangeType` run back to back, ahead of the text, enumeration and number arms. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.TemporalComparisonAgreementLawsTest` (23 rows), mirrored by `consistency.TemporalComparisonAgreementTest`.

| the question | class |
|---|---|
| is a date's partner a date, agreeing about year, calendar-ness and — under equality — clock-ness? | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` |
| is a date range's partner a date range of the same components? | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE_RANGE` |

**The date arm never compares the format STRINGS, only three questions about their components.** `dd.MM.yyyy` against `yyyy-MM` is ADMITTED though the precisions differ, because both carry a year and both carry a calendar component — A12's own comment calls this the weaker condition and wonders whether it is intended. The clock question is asked of `==` / `!=` alone: a date against a date-and-time is refused under equality and admitted under ordering, measured in both as the control that attributes the refusal to the operator.

**A date's partner of ANOTHER KIND lands on the date arm**, whichever arm would otherwise own it — a number, a text and a date range each draw `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` rather than that partner's own class, measured in both operand orders. A DATE FRAGMENT is a date carrier here too: matching components admitted, differing ones refused.

**The date-range arm demands EXACT component agreement and ignores both the format string and the separator.** Two ranges spelled `dd.MM.yyyy`/`-` and `yyyy-MM-dd`/`/` are ADMITTED; `dd.MM.yyyy` against `MM` is refused. A12 passes `false` for the base year in this arm alone, where the date arm supplements.

**The range arm's own ORDERING refusal is UNREACHABLE.** A date range is not orderable, so `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` answers first ([KF382](#kf382)) — measured, not read: the branch is written and cannot fire.

**And the walk is reached by six operators only.** The tolerance arm RETURNS once it has refused, so a date inside a tolerance comparison draws `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_TOLERANCE_OP` and nothing else; under ORDERING the walk is reached only once both sides clear the orderability gate, which is why a date ordered against a number is `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` and a date ordered against a text is `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON`. The tolerance row was found by a co-firing checker family rather than by reading, and is the reason the operator set is stated rather than assumed.

## §11 supplement — equality between two numbers compares DECLARED SCALES, and only a written-out one may be rescaled (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf385"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about comparison operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkNumberComparison` is the last arm of the comparison walk and carries two classes. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.NumberComparisonScaleGateLawsTest` (26 rows), mirrored by `consistency.NumberComparisonScaleGateTest`.

| the question | class |
|---|---|
| do `==` / `!=` join two numbers of the same fractional-digit count? | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` |
| is a number's partner number-like at all? | `MVK_INCONSISTENT_TYPES_COMPARED` |

**A differing pair is admitted exactly when the SMALLER-scale side is the written-out one.** `[UnitPrice] == 1` with `UnitPrice` at scale 2 is ADMITTED; `[Quantity] == 1.00` with `Quantity` at scale 0 is refused, and so is `1.00 == [Quantity]`. Both rows pair a declaration with a literal of a different scale and they answer oppositely, which is what separates "a literal has no scale" (it has one — what it spells) from "a literal is the operand A12 will rescale" (it is, and only upward). The existing locks reach this through EXPRESSIONS, where a multiplicative constant carries the same capability (`NumberLawsTest`, `PowerDerivedScaleWaiverLawsTest`); on a bare pair the literal is the whole of it.

**A `NumberType` body that OMITS `maxFractionalDigits` declares scale zero**, measured rather than defaulted: refused against a scale-2 declaration and against `1.00`, admitted against `1`.

**The gate is asked of equality alone**, and the tolerance arm returns before reaching it — two declarations of differing scale are ADMITTED under `<` and under `DiffersWithToleranceRange1`, each measured as the control that attributes the refusal to the operator.

**The scale gate is the one comparison class a COMPUTATION may switch off for itself**, through `errorCodesToSuppress`, which A12 renders into an inline `@SuppressWarning` pragma its parser honours. Measured with the unsuppressed computation as the control; no other carrier can suppress, and no other class is suppressible.

**`MVK_INCONSISTENT_TYPES_COMPARED` is reachable on a comparison only through a written-out BOOLEAN constant.** Every non-number DECLARATION is answered by an earlier arm — a date by `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`, a boolean by [KF383](#kf383)'s yes/no arm, text and enumerations by [KF384](#kf384) — so `True` and `False` are what survives to it, measured against a boolean declaration on the same shape, which draws the other class.

## §1 supplement — a comparison's text/enumeration arm asks a KIND question and a DOMAIN one, and they never meet (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf384"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about comparison operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkStringOrEnumType` is called TWICE, once per side, after the date, date-range and boolean arms of [KF383](#kf383). Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.StringEnumComparisonAgreementLawsTest` (23 rows), mirrored by `consistency.StringEnumComparisonAgreementTest`.

| the question | class |
|---|---|
| is a text or enumeration side's partner a NUMBER? | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_ENUM_OR_STRING` |
| is a written-out value opposite an enumeration one of its declared values? | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUM_COMPARISON` |
| does a DISPLAY-BEARING enumeration meet a text field or a textless enumeration? | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_ENUM_TO_STRING` |
| do two display-bearing enumerations map a value differently in a shared locale? | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_ENUM_TO_ENUM` |

**The first two questions never contend with the last two**, which is what makes them separable rather than merely distinct. The kind question fires only where the partner is a NUMBER, and the display questions are reachable only where both sides are text-or-enum — disjoint by construction. And a written-out value opposite an enumeration takes `checkEnumValue` and returns, so the display branch beside it is the `else` arm and is never entered on that shape. Both halves measured against a display-bearing enumeration, which is the carrier that would have collapsed them if they did contend.

**Because the walk runs once PER SIDE, the text side raises the kind class wherever it sits.** `[Quantity] == "a"` is refused exactly as `[GiftNote] == 1` is: the forward call sees NUMBER on the left and says nothing, the backward call sees the text and answers. A reading that asked only about the left operand would admit half of these.

**The domain question reads the STORED values and never the DISPLAY ones.** An enumeration declaring `BASIC` with the label `Basic plan` refuses `"Basic plan"` and admits `"BASIC"` — the discriminating row, because a labelled enumeration is exactly where the two readings diverge.

**The arms ahead of it answer first, each measured rather than assumed**: a date partner is `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`, a boolean one `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YESNO`, an ordering operator `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON`, and two written-out values `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_CONST`. A text or enumeration side cannot survive the ordering gate at all, so equality is this arm's whole reachable population.

## §1 supplement — the two boolean KINDS answer with different classes, and the confirm arm narrows again under EQUALITY (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf383"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about comparison operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkYesAndYesNoOperations` runs after the operator gates of [KF382](#kf382) and asks a different question: whether a side that is one of A12's two boolean kinds has a partner it can mean anything against. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.BooleanComparisonAgreementLawsTest` (27 rows), mirrored by `consistency.BooleanComparisonAgreementTest`.

| the declaration | what it stands against | otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `ConfirmType` | `True`; another confirm under `!=` ALONE | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YES` |
| `BooleanType` | `True`, `False`, another boolean, under either operator | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YESNO` |

**The EQUALITY OPERATOR is a second axis inside the confirm arm, and [KF270](#kf270) held it fixed.** That entry measured the confirm arm under `==` alone and read it as refusing every field on the right; `[TermsAccepted] != [NewsletterOptIn]` is ADMITTED, and so is a confirm against itself under `!=`. The source says why — `isTypeAYes(rt1) && isTypeAYes(rt2) && eq.ne == null` is its own throw, separate from the comparability test — and two controls separate the readings the rows could otherwise carry: `!=` does **not** lift the arm (a confirm against a boolean, a text constant or `False` is refused under `!=` exactly as under `==`), and two DISTINCT confirms under `==` are refused like the self-comparison, so the pairing is what `==` refuses rather than the identity.

**The confirm arm is asked FIRST**, so a confirm compared with a boolean is `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_YES` and not the boolean class — measured, because the two predicates alone read just as naturally in the other order.

**The class is invariant under operand order and under the partner's kind.** Both spellings of every refused pair were measured, and the partner was varied across text, number, date and enumeration declarations as well as text constants and `Today`: the declaration's own kind picks the class and nothing about the partner moves it.

**The operator gates answer ahead of this walk on every spelling a measurement reaches** — a confirm under `<` is `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON`, two written-out constants are `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_CONST` — so the reachable population of these two classes is equality alone.

**The two VALUE-equality branches of the same method are unreachable through a consistency check**, for the mechanism [KF379](#kf379) records: A12's model conversion substitutes the literals `true`/`false` for whatever either declaration spelled, so two declarations never disagree about their representation and the mismatch branches are never taken.

## §1 supplement — a comparison's first three questions are about its OPERATOR, and are answered before any type agreement (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf382"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about comparison operands, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.check` is A12's largest single check method — thirteen classes reachable from stored DM-JSON — and it opens with three questions that have nothing to do with whether the two sides agree. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ComparisonOperatorOperandLawsTest` (16 rows), mirrored by `consistency.ComparisonOperatorOperandsTest`.

| the question | class |
|---|---|
| are BOTH sides constants? | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_CONST` |
| does a TOLERANCE operator have a number on both sides? | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_TOLERANCE_OP` |
| does an ORDERING operator have a number or a date on both sides? | `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON` |

**The constant question is asked first, and the grid moves the OPERATOR to show it.** `1 > 2` is refused as two constants, not as an ordering comparison — so a reading that asked about the operator first would name the wrong class on it. The exemption is DATETIME: two constants are admitted when exactly one of them is `Today`/`Now`, which is why a checker must leave those comparisons alone rather than refuse them.

**The tolerance and ordering arms RETURN once satisfied**, so a comparison that clears them is never asked the agreement questions at all — measured as admitted rows (`[Quantity] DiffersWithToleranceRange1 5`, `[PlacedOn] <= [ShippedOn]`) rather than assumed.

**Ordering admits dates and nothing else beyond numbers.** Two text fields under `<` are refused; the same two under `==` are admitted, which is the control that attributes the refusal to the operator rather than to the declarations.

**A field reference inside a comparison must be BRACKETED** — `[Quantity] == 1`, not `Quantity == 1`, which is `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`. The same trap as an operation's operands, and it silently turns a type measurement into a grammar one.

**Extended 2026-09-14: `True` and `False` are written-out values to all three gates, like any literal.** The original grid used number and string literals only, which left the one constant family an author actually writes beside a boolean field unmeasured. `True == False` and `True == 1` are `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_CONST`; `[Quantity] > True` is `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON`; `[Quantity] DiffersWithToleranceRange1 True` is `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_TOLERANCE_OP`. A12 spells these two as bare NAMES rather than as literals, so a reader that recognised only literals left them outside every gate. Under `==` the same pairing clears all three and reaches the type-agreement walk instead, as `MVK_INCONSISTENT_TYPES_COMPARED`.

## §9 supplement — six arity gates, one per operator, and two classes that differ only in an underscore (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf381"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about operand arity, not an evaluation behaviour.

Every entity-list operator calls exactly one arity gate from `CheckEntityListenUtils`, chosen by a switch in its construct class. The gates are not variations on one predicate, and reading them as "at least two" would refuse models A12 admits. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.EntityListArityLawsTest` (23 rows), mirrored by `consistency.EntityListArityTest`.

| the law | refuses | class | operators |
|---|---|---|---|
| exactly one entity | any other count | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID1` | `FieldFilled`, `FieldNotFilled`, `GroupFilled`, `GroupNotFilled` |
| exactly two entities | any other count | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID_2` | `SumOfProducts` |
| more than one FIELD, or a group | a lone unstarred field | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN` | `AllFieldsFilled`, `NotAllFieldsFilled`, `FieldsNotCollectivelyFilled`, `NotExactlyOneFieldFilled`, `MoreThanOneFieldFilled`, `FieldValuesNotUnique`, `MinValue`, `MaxValue`, `Sum`, `FirstFilledValue`, `NumberOfFilledFields`, `NumberOfDifferentValues`, `NumberOfValueInFields` |
| the same | a lone unstarred field | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDFN` | `DateRangesOverlap` |
| more than one ENTITY | a lone unstarred entity of any kind | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID2` | `AllGroupsFilled`, `NotAllGroupsFilled`, `GroupsNotCollectivelyFilled` |
| the same | a lone unstarred entity of any kind | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDGN` | `NumberOfFilledGroups` |

**The two predicates differ in what a lone entity has to BE, and that is the row a rule of thumb gets wrong.** `checkIsMoreThanOneEntity` refuses only when the lone entity is a FIELD, so `AllFieldsFilled(Packing)` — one group — is ADMITTED; `isMoreThanOneParameter` refuses a lone entity whatever its kind, so `AllGroupsFilled(Packing)` is not.

**A wildcard satisfies the second predicate and is irrelevant to the first.** `NumberOfFilledGroups(Lines*)` is admitted where `NumberOfFilledGroups(Packing)` is not. The starred group row is measured on `NumberOfFilledGroups` rather than on `AllGroupsFilled`, because that operator family runs a wildcard gate straight after its arity one and answers `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_G_ALLOWED` first — itself a measured row.

**`MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID2` and `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID_2` are different laws on different operators** and differ only in an underscore, so each is measured on its own carrier rather than inferred from the other.

**Three operators ask about KIND before they ask about count**, measured on lists whose count is separately wrong so the rows cannot be explained by the arity gate having passed: `SumOfProducts` and `DateRangesOverlap` answer a group list with `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`, and `NumberOfFilledGroups` answers a field with `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED`.

**An operand crossing an UNSTARRED repetition never reaches its operator's arity gate**, the reference reader refusing it while the list is built: `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` where the error field sits outside that group, `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED` where it sits inside. `Sum(Lines/Amount)` is therefore not a one-entity arity question at all, which matters because it looks exactly like one.

**`AtLeastOneFieldFilled`, `NoFieldFilled`, `AtLeastOneGroupFilled` and `NoGroupFilled` call no arity gate at all** — their arms of the same switches return immediately.

## §8 supplement — a value-list quantifier asks its field list two questions in a fixed order, and the value list a third (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf380"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about operand typing, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckFeldListeUndWerteListenBedingungImpl.check` walks the FIELD list twice before it ever looks at the values: first that every expanded field shares a base type, then that each is a text, enumeration or number declaration. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ValueListQuantifierOperandKindLawsTest` (11 rows), mirrored by `consistency.ValueListQuantifierOperandKindTest`.

| what fails | class |
|---|---|
| the expanded fields do not all share a base type | `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| one of them is neither text, enumeration nor number | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` |
| a LITERAL value list stands opposite a NUMBER field list | `MVK_INVALID_TYPES_FOR_COMPARISON` |

**The order is what makes a grid necessary rather than a column.** Two Date declarations agree on base type and fail the second question; a Date beside a text one fails the first. Both measured, because a reading that keys on "the list carries a Date" would name whichever class it happened to meet.

**The VALUE list is judged against the FIRST field's type, not against itself.** `matchBaseType` seeds the expected type from the field list and then walks the values, so an entity value list of another kind draws the same `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` the field list would — measured, with an entity value list of the matching kind as the control.

**A repeated entity pre-empts all three, and the duplicate walk spans BOTH lists**: a field named again among the values is `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` exactly as a field named twice among the fields is. Measured.

**These shapes are unauthorable through the typed surface**, which is why they are `erased` in the ledger and still worth a checker: the typed quantifiers are kind-typed (`StringRef`, `EnumRef`, `GroupListRef` overloads), so a mixed-kind list cannot be built at all and the shapes reach a checker only as stored DM-JSON. The grid keeps one row on the typed path so the admitted control does not rest on hand-written text.

**`AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps` shares the construct and skips this walk**, taking an arm of its own that asks about DateRange formats instead — the reason a family reporting these classes must exclude it by name rather than by operand shape.

## §9 supplement — `NumberOfValueInFields` is a switch on its CONSTANT: four arms, four classes, and two the checker cannot reach (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf379"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about one operator's operand typing, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckAnzahlWertOpImpl.check` is one method whose body branches on the constant standing to the LEFT of the `In`, and each branch sends the same field list down a different type gate. So which class a list draws is decided by the constant, not by the fields: the same list is admitted under one constant and refused under another. Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ValueInFieldsConstantKindLawsTest` (22 rows), mirrored by `consistency.ValueInFieldsConstantKindTest`.

| the constant | declarations it admits | otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `True` | Boolean, Confirm | `MVK_NO_TYPE_YES_OR_YESNO` |
| `False` | Boolean | `MVK_NO_TYPEYESNO` |
| a string | String, Custom, Enumeration — and the constant must be a MEMBER of an Enumeration it meets | `MVK_NO_STRING_OR_ENUM`, `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION` |
| a number | Number | `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |

**The two boolean arms are not mirror images**, which [KF113](#kf113) already recorded from the other side and this grid completes: a Confirm declaration carries a yes-representation and no no-representation, so `False` has nothing to compare and refuses it while `True` admits it. Measured on Date and Enumeration carriers as well as text and number ones, because an arm's refusal is about the declaration's KIND rather than about any one neighbouring type.

**A GROUP operand is expanded to every field beneath it, nested groups included.** The discriminating row is a group declaring one Boolean directly and one text field inside a subgroup: an expansion stopping at the group's own members would admit it under `False`, and A12 refuses it.

**Four gates run before the switch, and each answers with a class of its own** — measured, and the reason a portable checker must stay silent on those shapes rather than name a type class: a repeated entity is `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`, a group listed beside a field it contains is `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2`, a lone unstarred FIELD is `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN`, and a root group is `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED`. The last is the one exception to "measured": in a single-root model the reference reader refuses the root group's own name with `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` before the operator is reached at all, so that gate is a source read on this carrier.

**Two of the method's classes cannot be reached through a consistency check at all.** `MVK_DIFFERENT_YES_VALUE` and `MVK_DIFFERENT_NO_VALUE` compare the two declarations' stored true (or false) representation, spelled in DM-JSON as `notInDCustomTrueValue`/`notInDCustomFalseValue`. Splicing two different representations onto two Boolean declarations is ADMITTED, match and mismatch alike — measured. No control can show the splice arrived, also measured: the model reader ignores an unknown property, so a deliberately misspelled key behaves identically to the correct one. The mechanism is therefore source-verified rather than settled by the table — `DocumentModelServiceUtils.convert(model, variant, problemReporter)` passes `considerNotInD = false`, and on that setting `TypeConverter.convertBoolean`/`convertConfirm` substitute the literals `true` and `false` for whatever the declaration wrote, leaving the two compared representations always equal.

## §11 supplement — an arithmetic expression's arity gates, and why the verdict follows the TEXT rather than the gate order (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf378"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about operation shape, not an evaluation behaviour.

`CheckOperationImpl.check` runs three gates over every operation context, in this source order: the type walk (which carries the exponent's own demand), then at most ONE division per multiplicative chain, then no power directly under a power. None of the refused shapes is authorable through the typed builders — `DslRenderer` braces a left power child and a left division under division — so all of them reach a checker only as stored DM-JSON.

| the expression | verdict |
|---|---|
| `RoundDown([BaseFee] * 2, 2)` — the control | admitted |
| `[BaseFee] ^ 2` | admitted |
| `[BaseFee] ^ 2.5` | `MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP` |
| `[BaseFee] ^ [BaseFee]`, the field declaring scale 2 | `MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP` |
| `[BaseFee] ^ 2 ^ 2` | `MVK_TOO_MANY_POW_FOR_CALC` |
| `{[BaseFee] ^ 2} ^ 2` | admitted |
| `[BaseFee] ^ 2 ^ 2.5` | `MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP` |
| `[BaseFee] / 2 / 4` | `MVK_TOO_MANY_DIV_FOR_CALC` |
| `[BaseFee] / 2 + [BaseFee] / 4` | admitted |
| `[BaseFee] / {[BaseFee] / 4}` | admitted |
| `[BaseFee] / 2 * 4` | admitted |

**The verdict follows the TEXT, not the source order of the gates.** An expression violating both arity gates draws whichever violation is written first — `[BaseFee] ^ 2 ^ 2 + [BaseFee] / 2 / 4` reports the power class and the same pair with the divisions first reports the division class. `check` runs per operation CONTEXT as the expression is parsed, so the gate order inside one call decides nothing between two subexpressions. One text order alone reads as "the power gate wins", which is why both were measured.

**Inside ONE context the order does hold**: the type walk runs first, so `[BaseFee] ^ 2 ^ 2.5` reports the exponent's own defect rather than the nesting it also has.

**The exponent is judged by its DECLARED scale**, not by the values it could take, so a field an author will only ever fill with whole numbers is refused. Source-read and NOT measured: `checkNoFractionalDigitsInExponent` refuses a null scale as well as a positive one, so a number field declaring no `maxFractionalDigits` should be refused too — the estate's fixtures cannot author one, and the portable checker stays silent there rather than acting on the reading.

**The brace rule is a compatibility decision, not a semantic one**, and the kernel says so in its own comment: the nested division `a / {b / c}` *could* be recognised as two divisions and is admitted because the previous parser admitted it. Reading the class names alone would predict the opposite.

**Measuring any of this needs the scale gate held constant.** A power or a division leaves the operation's scale undeterminable, and `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES` then answers every row — so each row wraps its operation in `RoundDown(…, 2)` into a scale-2 target. Without that the grid measures the computed field's declaration instead of the operator's arity.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.CalculationOperatorArityLawsTest`; mirrored by `consistency … CalculationOperatorArityTest`.

## §9 supplement — one error class, three throw sites, two phases: `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED` is decided in the filter walk, never by the gate that names it (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf377"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class phase law, not an evaluation behaviour.

`ParserService.checkNormalRule` collects every filter condition and refuses one that uses a semantic index. Reading that branch alone puts the class in the post-parse phase ([KF375](#kf375)) — and every shape measured for it is decided two layers earlier, by `CheckEntitySpecImpl.checkIndicesInFilterCondition`, whose per-level walk throws the SAME class the moment a filter reference's level carries `SEMANTIC_INDEX`. A third site, `CheckEntityUtils.checkNoSemanticIndex`, serves the operand slots that forbid the notation.

**The control that separates the phases** (insurance model, `Coverages` and `Endorsements` keyed alike): a filtered operand riding a parallel-iterated level draws `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_FOR_FILTERED_ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED` — a whole-rule gate checked two branches BEFORE the semantic-index one. Put an index in that same filter and the verdict becomes `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED`. A post-parse reading predicts the filtered-entity class; the parse-time throw is what actually answers.

**So a code is not owned by the phase that happens to name it.** A second site of the same class can sit in the other phase and win every race, which is invisible to a reader who greps the class once and stops at the first hit. The check is cheap — grep the class across the parser and read each site's method.

**The rest of the set was then swept both ways, and this is the only split one (2026-09-14).** For each of the seven other classes `checkNormalRule` and `IterationChecker` draw, every throw site outside the enum declarations lies in that same phase; for each of the twenty-six classes this estate treats as positioned, no site lies in `ParserService`, `IterationChecker`, `IterationNotValidVisitor` or `core/calc`. Command: `git grep -n "<CODE>" -- '*.java' ':!*/build/*' ':!*delombok*'` over the kernel checkout, reading every hit; 33 classes, 33 read.

**What the filter walk asks, level by level, per reference in authored order:**

| the level carries | class |
|---|---|
| iteration of a level the filtered entity does not sit under | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` |
| iteration below a wildcard the same reference set | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| a semantic index | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| *(after every reference)* no level any reference iterates is one the operand stars | `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD` |

**The index and iteration branches are REFERENCE-positional, measured in both text orders.** An index replaces `ITERATION` at the level it addresses, so a reference carrying one is never asked the scope question; a body with an off-path read and an indexed read draws whichever the text writes first. One order alone cannot tell that from "the index always wins".

**The group the index addresses is not a variable**, and neither is the key: an index over the filtered group, over an unrelated group, and one whose key is read from the filtered group all draw the class. The gate visits the filter's parse tree and asks only whether some level carries an index at all.

**The index's OWN spec gates run earlier still** — while the spec is parsed — so an index whose key names a group draws `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NO_FIELD` and never reaches the filter walk. That also **bounds a clause this estate held**: the iteration class `checkIterationAndErrorField` renames into ([KF351](#kf351)) is drawn against the RULE's error target, and inside a filter the anchoring is the filtered entity — two measured shapes there are answered by the key-kind gate and by the filter branch, by neither an iteration class.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.SemanticIndexInFilterLawsTest`; mirrored by `consistency … SemanticIndexInFilterTest`.

## §9 supplement — a parallel iteration marks the rule's OWN keyed group too, which is what a `Having` filter is then refused on (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf376"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class law about which operands a whole-rule gate looks at, not an evaluation behaviour.

`ParserService.checkNormalRule`'s second gate asks `AnalyseService.hasParallelIteratedFilterConditionId`, which walks the built condition for ONE entity id carrying both a filter condition and the parallel-iteration marker, and refuses the rule with `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_FOR_FILTERED_ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED`. The natural reading — the filtered operand reads a parallel-iterated group — is measurably too narrow.

**The marker is set by TWO passes, and the second is the one nobody predicts.** `setSeparatePathIndexes` marks, on each reference, the lowest level it iterates OFF the error field's path; that is the joint iteration itself, and finding one is the precondition for the second pass. `setIndexesForParallelIteration` then marks, on EVERY reference, each unstarred repeatable level that is an ancestor-or-equal of the error field **and declares an index field** — the rule's own group included.

**The discriminating pair, within one model** (`Lines` and `Picks` keyed alike, rule anchored in `Lines`):

| condition | verdict |
|---|---|
| a filter on an operand under `Picks` | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_FOR_FILTERED_ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| the same operand with NO filter — the control | admitted |
| a filter on an operand under the rule's own `Lines` | admitted |
| the same, plus an unrelated unstarred read of `Picks` | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_FOR_FILTERED_ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| the parallel level declaring no index field | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`, during the parse |

Rows three and four carry byte-identical filtered operands and differ only in a conjunct that names neither of them, so "the filtered operand reads a parallel group" admits row four and is false.

**A star marks the level it sits on and nothing above it.** An aggregate over `Picks` with a star on a group BENEATH it still iterates `Picks` jointly — measured through the uniqueness gate, which refuses that condition. A reader treating "the reference carries a star" as "the reference does not iterate" therefore misses the whole shape; ours did, and stayed silent on it until this row.

**Gate order inside the phase:** `checkForParallelIteration` runs first, so a condition carrying a `RepetitionNotUnique` as well draws `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED`. Both are post-parse ([KF375](#kf375)), so neither hides behind a positioned class and only the measurement settles it.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.FilteredEntityParallelIterationLawsTest`; mirrored by `consistency … FilteredEntityIterationTest`.

## §9 supplement — a whole-rule gate runs only on a COMPLETED parse, so a parse-time class erases it (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf375"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law across A12's two checking phases, not an evaluation behaviour.

A12 checks a condition in two phases and the estate had only ever measured inside one of them. The per-construct `Check…Impl` classes run DURING the parse and raise by throwing; a second, smaller set runs after it, on the built condition, because what they ask cannot be seen from one construct. `CheckWiederholungBedingungImpl.checkForParallelIteration` is the worked example and states its own precondition: *"This is checked after parsing because for groups on the error field path parallel iteration can be detected only in the context of the whole condition. Preconditions: Has to be called after parsing is complete."*

**So a parse-time class does not merely outrank a whole-rule one — it removes the input the whole-rule one needs.** The throw ends the parse, no condition is built, and nothing calls the second phase at all. That is a stronger claim than the first-defect rule ([KF342](#kf342)) and decides cases the first-defect rule cannot, a whole-rule gate having no position in the text to be compared against.

**The discriminating control, within one model** (`RepetitionNotUniqueFromScopeLawsTest`, two index-keyed parallel groups): a `RepetitionNotUnique` whose key list straddles both branches reports `MVK_NOT_IN_SAME_PATH` and nothing else, while the same model with a CLEAN key list beside a parallel read reports `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED`. The gate is live on this shape; it disappears only behind the parse-time throw.

**The phase's own membership, read off `checkNormalRule`'s body in source order** (kernel `30.8.1`), because a reproduction that holds one member is the same defect one size smaller:

| what it asks | class |
|---|---|
| `RepetitionNotUnique` beside a parallel iteration | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| a filter condition on a parallel-iterated entity | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_FOR_FILTERED_ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| a filter condition that parallel-iterates | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED` again |
| a filter condition using a semantic index | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| two `RepetitionNotUnique` (or two row-uniqueness) calls in one condition | `MVK_INVALID_COMBINATION_OF_REPETITON_NOT_UNIQUE` |
| a raw-type `Length` whose constant is out of domain | `MVK_INVALID_LENGTH_OF_RAW_TYPE` |
| `IterationNotValidVisitor.testParallelIteration` | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_INVALID` |

`IterationChecker.checkIteration` and `checkSimpleIteration` run after those and draw their own classes, `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` included — which is why that class, measured separately as losing to every condition-text defect, turns out to be the same law rather than a neighbouring one.

**Read that table as PHASE MEMBERSHIP, never as the class a model draws — two of its rows are known not to be reached, and quoting one as a verdict cost an outbound claim (noted 2026-09-21).** It says what `checkNormalRule` asks, in the order it asks; what a model actually draws is decided by whichever parse-time gate speaks first, and for both filter rows one does. Row 4 is superseded by [KF377](#kf377): every measured shape draws that class from `checkIndicesInFilterCondition`, two layers earlier. Row 3 is superseded by [KF353](#kf353): a filter whose own body reads the parallel group draws `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION`, a filter body not being allowed to iterate at all, so the second `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED` site has no measured shape that reaches it. Our 2026-09-21 handback quoted row 3 as the verdict for a parallel iteration inside a filter; the peer disputed it with the *filtered-entity* class, which belongs to a third shape again (an operand riding a parallel-iterated outer level), and the measured answer was in this estate the whole time.

**The second member was measured the same way, on the same model**: a `RepetitionNotUnique` with a containment defect beside a SECOND `RepetitionNotUnique` reports `MVK_NOT_IN_SAME_PATH` alone, while two CLEAN calls on that model report `MVK_INVALID_COMBINATION_OF_REPETITON_NOT_UNIQUE`. Two gates of the phase, one pre-emption — so it is the phase and not a property of either gate.

**What it means for a reproduction**: a checker that reports both classes over-reports, and the fix is one rule over the whole finding list rather than per family — a post-parse class is dropped wherever a positioned class already speaks for the same rule. A second-phase gate is recognizable in kernel source by taking a built `ICondition` rather than a parser context.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueFromScopeLawsTest`; mirrored by `consistency … RepetitionKeyContainmentTest`.

## §9 supplement — a `Having` filter's body is walked LEVEL by level, and the two gates it answers are one method's two branches (source-verified, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf374"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the mechanism behind §9's two filter codes, which the section states as separate rules.

`CheckEntitySpecImpl.checkIndicesInFilterCondition` is one loop. It collects every entity spec in the filter body, walks each one's index vector level by level, and asks two things of every repeatable level the spec rides unmarked: is the FILTERED entity underneath that level, and is that level one the operand stars. The first question throws immediately; the second only sets a flag, and the flag is read once after every reference has been walked.

| the walk reaches | class |
|---|---|
| a ridden level the filtered entity does not sit under | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` |
| the end, with no ridden level the operand stars | `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD` |

**That structure is the whole of the conjunct asymmetry [KF-§9](#kf242)'s grid measured behaviourally.** The scope gate is an occurrence check read after the loop, so any in-scope reference anywhere clears it; the iteration gate throws inside the loop, so nothing later can rescue it — the enclosing rule's own iteration of the level included, which is the row that surprises and is exactly what the source predicts, since the walk never consults the rule's environment at all.

**A level is ridden by ENDING at it as much as by passing through it**, which the index vector makes plain and a path-prefix reading would miss: `CurrentRepetition(Legs)` resolves to the group and carries the marker at its own level. Measured on both carriers — a field beneath the group and the group itself draw the same code in the same position.

**The `$`-marked reference is not walked at all**, and that is a skip rather than a pass: the extractor returns early on `ctx.outer != null`, so a marked reference contributes no ridden level, cannot clear the scope gate, and cannot trip the iteration one. Where its outer environment has no coordinate for the level, the reference reader has already answered `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` and none of this runs.

**One more gate runs after this walk, and it is the LAST of the filter's five** (added 2026-09-15). `checkFilterCondition` calls `checkNoDisallowedConstructsInFilterCondition` once the index walk returns, and its listener refuses exactly three constructs, each by its own terminal: a NESTED filter, `CustomCondition` (`ApplikationsBedingung`) and `RepetitionNotUnique` (`WiederholungNichtEindeutig`). Source-read, and the count matters — the MVK ledger had described the kit's three pre-checks as a representable subset of a larger delegated set, and there is no larger set.

**Because it runs last, the construct class is reachable only from a filter that is otherwise legal**, which is the part a checker needs and a single-construct measurement cannot show. Measured on the two shapes that violate two gates at once: a star inside the body draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` and an outer-only body draws `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD`, neither co-firing with the construct class; and a construct beside an in-scope conjunct still draws the construct class, so the conjunct only feeds the gate before it. A body naming a forbidden construct and NOTHING else never reaches this gate at all, the scope gate answering first — which is why the sibling conjunct in the reporting row is load-bearing rather than decorative.

**One `CustomCondition` body, moved one step in either direction, draws all three classes** — which is the sharpest statement of the ordering and the grid a checker should be held against. Beside an in-scope reference it is the construct class; alone it is `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD`, the scope gate answering first because the construct names no level; beside a STARRED reference it is `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`. The text naming the forbidden construct never moves, so nothing about the construct itself decides the verdict.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.HavingFilterIterationGateLawsTest`, `…HavingFilterGrammarAndScopeLawsTest`, `…FilteredOperandGateOrderLawsTest` and `…AggregateSlotLawsTest`; mirrored by `consistency … FilterBodyGatesTest`.

## §6 supplement — a `Date`/`Time` construction is judged SLOT by slot, and the slot's arm picks the class (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf373"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a per-slot admission law for the two construction operators.

`CheckBaseDateConstructionImpl` with its two subclasses is one construct: each slot takes a quoted CONSTANT, a date/time EXTRACT operator, or an ENTITY, and each arm has its own gate. A12 walks the slots left to right and answers at the first defective one, whichever arm that slot happens to carry — measured in both orders, so "the constant gate runs before the operator gate" is excluded.

**The constant arm**, all digits with no sign, inside a half-open range, and at the complete-year slot a width of exactly four:

| slot | admits | the year slot alone also demands |
|---|---|---|
| `Date` day | 1–31 | — |
| `Date` month | 1–12 | — |
| `Date` year | 1800–2199 | exactly four digits |
| `Time` hour | 0–23 | — |
| `Time` minute / second | 0–59 | — |

A leading zero is optional (`Date("1","2","2024")` is admitted), so the day and month slots have no width demand at all; the year slot's is what makes `"24"` a refusal where `"1"` is not.

**The extract-operator arm splits TWO ways, and the discriminating case is `QuarterFromDate`.** An operator of the construction's own family in the wrong slot draws `MVK_INVALID_DATE_OR_TIME_EXTRACT_OP`; every other operator draws `MVK_DATE_OR_TIME_EXTRACT_OP_NOT_ALLOWED`. The obvious reading — "the other family's operator is not allowed, one's own is merely misplaced" — predicts the wrong-slot class for `QuarterFromDate`, which is a date operator; measured, it draws the not-allowed class, because the kernel's switch lists the three operators its own slots expect by NAME rather than asking which family an operator belongs to.

**Both `Date` arities either side of three are other laws'.** Two components is the year-less shape, admitted only when the model declares a base year (`MVK_MISSING_YEAR`); four is the split-year H-model shape, whose own class is erased in A12 models.

**The entity arm asks a different question of the same slot, and its numbers are not the constant arm's.** A field component satisfies a slot by its stored `maxLength` *or* by its declared `maxValue`, either alone; at the complete-year slot the accepted maxima run 1000–9999, where a constant year must lie in 1800–2199. So a reader carrying one maximum per slot refuses `maxValue: 9999` — a declaration A12 admits, measured. Its own two gates are ordered rather than alternative: a `StringType` whose pattern is not one of the six spellings A12 recognises draws `MVK_NO_DIGIT_PATTERN` before any width is compared, so a component of exactly the right width still draws the pattern class. Only three declared types reach a positive answer — a scale-free non-negative number, a digit-patterned string of the slot's width, and, at the complete year alone, a `DateType` declared exactly `yyyy`.

**The REFERENCE READER answers before the slot gate, so a component that is also a cross-repetition read never reaches it (measured 2026-09-14).** A field component reached by crossing a repetition the rule's own group does not sit in draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` whatever its declaration says, and the slot class is not drawn at all. Two controls hold the rest fixed: the same read with the component declared CORRECTLY still draws the reference class, so that class does not depend on the declaration; and the same wrong declaration read from INSIDE the repeating group does draw the slot class, so the slot gate is live on the fixture. This is the same layer order [KF369](#kf369) measured for the group predicates, on a construction operand — and for a Kernel-free checker it is the difference between one finding and two, `OPERAND_REPETITION_SCOPE` owning that class.

**The sign gate has TWO satisfiers, and the second one has no minimum to read (measured 2026-09-14).** `positivesOnly` passes it with no `minValue` at all: the same field declaring the flag and a right width is ADMITTED, while the field with neither the flag nor a minimum is refused. The rival account — "the gate is exactly a declared non-negative minimum" — was consistent with every row that measured this arm, because none of them declared the flag, and it predicts a refusal on the discriminating case. Source: `CheckBaseDateConstructionImpl.positivesOnly()` is `checkNonNegativeMinValuePresent(…) || !hasSign()`, and A12's `positivesOnly` is the core `hasSign()` inverted; the kernel's own comment beside it says the data modeller cannot set that member, which is what made the second satisfier look unreachable — it is declarable in DM-JSON and reaches the gate.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.DateConstructionSlotLawsTest` (constant and operator arms) and `…TemporalComponentDeclarationLawsTest` (the entity arm, the sign gate's second satisfier included); mirrored by `consistency … DateConstructionSlotsTest`.

## §9 supplement — the root-only iteration classes need the target INSIDE the declaring group, the fourth constant of the set that measured them (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf372"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a gate-order result completing [KF348](#kf348)'s account of the same two classes.

[KF348](#kf348) named three conditions for `MVK_ERROR_FIELDGROUP_ITERATION4_INVALID` / `…ITERATION5_INVALID`, two of which had been constants of the set. A fourth was still constant and nobody had asked: **every row declared the rule in the error field's OWN group.** Move the rule to the parallel group, change nothing else, and both classes disappear — `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP` answers instead, on the own-group read and on the parallel read alike.

**Source-verified, and the discriminating case is measured**: the mechanism is layer order rather than precedence inside one check — the containment gate is the first statement of `CheckEntityUtils.checkIterationAndErrorField` and throws during the PARSE, while both iteration classes come from `IterationChecker`, which runs over the finished reference set afterwards. A precedence-inside-one-check rival predicts the parallel class on the row whose read IS parallel, since that is the arm precedence would leave standing; measured, that row draws the containment class like the other two. So no condition reaches either class with the target outside the declaring group.

**The control had to change fixture, and that is a finding of its own.** On a repeatable ROOT every reference iterates at level 0, so `GroupFilled(/Shipment)` alone already draws the containment class — there is no non-iterating reference in such a model, and the intended control read as "placement alone refuses", which is exactly the misreading [KF212](#kf212) corrects. Re-run on a fixture differing in the root's repeatability alone, the same rule is ADMITTED.

**Why it mattered:** the shape reaches a Kernel-free checker only through stored DM-JSON — `Rule.build()` refuses the pair up front ([KF212](#kf212), measured OVER-REJECTING) — and that is precisely the input such a checker reads. `ERROR_TARGET_ITERATION` named the parallel class there until this was measured.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RootOnlyErrorTargetIterationLawsTest.aTargetOUTSIDETheDeclaringGroupIsAnsweredFirstByTheContainmentGate`; mirrored by `consistency … ErrorTargetIterationTest`.

## §11 supplement — the operand-scope walk is PER LEVEL, and the level reached outranks the order of the gates inside it (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf371"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an operand-admission law plus a walk-order result; it completes §11's scope account rather than restating it.

**One construct, one method, one chain.** `CheckEntityUtils.checkIndicesForA12Model` walks every level of every reference a rule or computation makes and asks, for each level it ITERATES, whether the target's coordinates address that repetition. [KF295](#kf295) and [KF332](#kf332) read pieces of this chain from the semantic-index side; this is the whole of it from the operand side, and it is what turns eight separately-recorded ledger rows into one family.

| the iterated level, relative to the target's group | class |
|---|---|
| sits below a level the SAME reference stars | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| sits strictly below the target's group | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| is the target's group, or an ancestor of it | ADMITTED |
| is PARALLEL and declares no index field | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| is PARALLEL, and two groups on its OWN chain declare one | `MVK_MULTIPLE_INDEX_FIELDS` |
| is PARALLEL, and nothing on the TARGET's chain declares one | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NO_INDEX` |
| is PARALLEL, and the two index fields differ in NAME | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX` |
| is PARALLEL, same name, different base TYPE | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX_TYPE` |
| is PARALLEL, same name and base type | ADMITTED — a legal parallel iteration |

**The result the chain alone gets wrong: the WALK outranks the gates.** Reading `checkParallelIteration` gives the order above, in which the operand's own index chain resolves before the target's — so a doubly-keyed operand should draw `MVK_MULTIPLE_INDEX_FIELDS` whatever the target looks like. It does not. The same operand (`/Fulfilment/Credits/Lines/LineAmount`, keyed under a keyed parent) draws `MVK_MULTIPLE_INDEX_FIELDS` into a keyed target and **`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NO_INDEX`** into an unkeyed one, because the OUTER level is refused first and the inner level is never asked. The two rows differ in the TARGET and in nothing else, which is what identifies the walk rather than the gate as what decides it — predicted wrong here before it was measured.

**The index demand falls on BOTH ends, and the target end had never been measured.** [KF347](#kf347)-era rows and `RuleOperandScopeLawsTest` varied the OPERAND's declaration against a keyed target; with the target in a group that declares no index and the operand keyed, A12 answers `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NO_INDEX` — the mirror row of `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX`, and the reason the family reads two chains rather than one.

**Every level is asked on its own declaration, not once per reference.** An operand crossing an admitted keyed parallel level and then an UNKEYED one below it is refused at the lower level with that level's own class (`MVK_NO_WILDCARD`) — so "the reference is parallel" is not a property of the reference.

**A star collapses its own level and nothing beneath it.** `Sum(Shipments*/Parcels/ParcelWeight)` is `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` on `Parcels`; starring both levels is admitted. This closes the residue `ErrorFieldReference`'s own note left open — a reference starring an outer level while crossing an inner repeatable group unstarred.

**Which class the SIBLING cells draw was re-measured on one fixture rather than carried.** `RuleOperandScopeLawsTest` (motor claims), `ComputationOperandScopeLawsTest` (the same model, computation carrier) and `ParallelIterationGateLawsTest` (depot) each pinned some of them, and a checker implementing this chain reads ONE model — so a table mixing cells from three fixtures cannot say whether a verdict belongs to the chain or to a fixture. All four re-measure unchanged, the type row included, whose two index fields here differ in declared type and in nothing else.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.ParallelIterationRouteLawsTest` (this chain) beside `…RuleOperandScopeLawsTest` and `…ComputationOperandScopeLawsTest` (the carrier pair); mirrored by `consistency … OperandRepetitionScopeTest`.

## §9 supplement — `SumOfProducts`' four operand laws are ONE gate chain, and the order is what a reproduction gets wrong (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf370"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an operand-admission law plus a gate-order result.

**One operator, one `switch` arm, six gates in source order.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.SumOfProductsLawsTest`; the source counterpart is `CheckFeldListenOpImpl.check`'s `SUMME_VON_PRODUKTEN` branch.

| the operand pair | A12 |
|---|---|
| two parallel lists over one owning group — the control | ADMITTED |
| one operand only, or three | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID_2` |
| the same starless field twice | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` |
| a GROUP beside a field inside it | `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2` |
| a repeatable level left unstarred | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| the fields' OWNING groups differ | `MVK_DIFFERENT_GROUPS` |
| an operand carrying a `Having` filter | `MVK_WILDCARD_AT_LOWEST_LEVEL_REQUIRED` |
| an operand starring two levels | `MVK_WILDCARD_ONLY_AT_LOWEST_LEVEL_ALLOWED` |
| neither operand has a repeatable level, and they share an owning group | `MVK_REPEATABLE_LEVEL_REQUIRED` |
| a pair every row above admits, with a non-Number field in either position | `MVK_NO_NUMBER` |

**The arity code is `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID_2`, not `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID2`** — two distinct members of one enum, and this operator's `checkParamSizeIs2` draws the underscored one. Recorded because a checker quoting the sibling would name a code the model never drew.

**Two gates answer ahead of the ones the operator's own branch calls.** The duplicate gate takes both duplicate rows, so a GROUP operand never reaches `checkOnlyFields` and the kind class is unreachable on that pair; and it is STAR-SENSITIVE — the identical pair `Lines*/Qty, Lines*/Qty` is admitted while `Total, Total` is a duplicate.

**The second class is not the shape its name suggests, and this is the row that matters most.** `MVK_WILDCARD_AT_LOWEST_LEVEL_REQUIRED` reads as "a star above the lowest level", and that shape never reaches it: the reference reader answers a missing or misplaced star with `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` first. What does reach it is a FILTER — `isWildcardRestricted` returns `hasFilterCondition()` for every level, so a filtered operand fails at its lowest level. Measured on both sides of the pair, and measured against a multi-star operand, where the filter wins because the loop reaches the lowest level first.

**The owning-group gate outranks every wildcard gate below it**, so a filtered operand whose owning group also differs draws `MVK_DIFFERENT_GROUPS`, and so does a pair with no repeatable level at all when the two groups differ — the cell that corrected this file's own earlier reading of `MVK_REPEATABLE_LEVEL_REQUIRED`.

**The number question comes last** (*extended 2026-09-22*). On a text-bearing pair that also breaks a structural gate, the kernel reports that gate alone, for each of the five structural classes above. Each such pair was measured beside a number-only twin of the same structure, and the twin drew the same class. rulekit had asked the kind first, so a text list with a structural defect was refused as a kind error. Its check now runs last and cites no code, because one gate that outranks it (a repeatable ancestor left unstarred, `Lines/Parts*/Code, Lines/Parts*/Count` → `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`) depends on a repeatability that the operand does not carry.

Reported by the portable checker under `CheckFamily.SUM_OF_PRODUCTS_OPERANDS`, which speaks only where each operand resolves to a FIELD inside the declaring group and stars exactly the repeatable levels between them — the condition that keeps the reference reader's three classes out of its way.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.SumOfProductsLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … SumOfProductsOperandsTest`.

## §9 supplement — the SEVEN group conditions split THREE ways over a repetition wildcard, and the star-required gate outruns all of them (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf369"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — an operand-admission law plus a gate-order result.

**One `switch` decides the whole family, and it has three arms rather than two.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupQuantifierWildcardLawsTest`; the arms are `CheckKontextListenBedingungImpl.check`'s three token groups, and the grid is what turns that source read into a measurement.

| the operator | a starred REPEATABLE operand | a non-repeatable operand — the control |
|---|---|---|
| `GroupFilled`, `GroupNotFilled` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` | ADMITTED |
| `AllGroupsFilled`, `GroupsNotCollectivelyFilled`, `NotAllGroupsFilled` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_G_ALLOWED` | ADMITTED |
| **`AtLeastOneGroupFilled`, `NoGroupFilled`** | **ADMITTED** | ADMITTED |
| `NumberOfFilledGroups` | ADMITTED | ADMITTED (two operands; a lone one draws `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDGN`) |

**The third arm is the whole point.** Those two are spelled like the three above them and take the same operand list, so a checker assembled from what the operators are CALLED over-rejects two of seven — the one direction this project forbids. Reported by `CheckFamily.GROUP_CONDITION_WILDCARD`.

**And the control could not be the same group unstarred, because there is no such spelling.** A repeatable group named from a non-repeating rule context draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` from the reference reader — in every one of the seven, including the two with no wildcard gate and including the shape whose arity gate would otherwise answer. So in the three refusing operators a repeatable group is refused starred and refused unstarred: it cannot be used there at all, which is a stronger statement than the wildcard law alone.

**What the refusing arm counts as a wildcard is the REFERENCE, not the operand's kind** — the row a reader of the kernel's own predicate would get backwards. `EntityRef.hasWildCardsInGroup` exempts a field's own repetition index, so a field one level below the starred group looks admitted; measured, `AllGroupsFilled(Lines*/Sku, Shipping)` is refused exactly like the bare group. Two starred levels and a single starred operand are refused too — the arity gate reads a star as standing for a list (`isMoreThanOneParameter`), so a one-operand starred call draws the wildcard class and not `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALID2`.

**The two arms order differently against the ROOT gate, which is why a family may not treat them alike.** `checkNotRootGroupReferenced` runs before the list arm's wildcard gate and after nothing in the scalar arm, so a starred ROOT group draws `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` in the first and `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` in the second. Unstarred, a repeatable root draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` in both — the star-required gate outruns the root gate as it outruns every operator gate.

**Inside a `Having` filter the operator's own gate still answers**, and the discriminating row is what settles it: `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_G_ALLOWED` is a class no filter gate can produce, so a quantifier nested in a filter is not answered by the filter's wildcard gate. The scalar arm's row alone could not have shown that — the filter gate draws the scalar class too ([KF97](#kf97)). The classes are also unchanged from a rule anchored INSIDE the repeatable group, measured rather than transferred.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupQuantifierWildcardLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … GroupConditionWildcardTest`.

## §8 supplement — an enumeration's LABEL TEXTS must differ within one language, and the rest of the per-language block is unreachable (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf368"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a declaration-admission law plus a reachability result.

**The last of the enumeration's fifteen structural laws, and one more of them is live.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumValueAndLabelLawsTest`.

| the labels | A12 |
|---|---|
| distinct texts — the control | ADMITTED |
| two values sharing one text in `en_US` | `MVK_DISPLAY_VALUES_DUPLICATE` |
| the same text for one value in `en_US` and another in `de_DE` | ADMITTED |

**The scope is ONE LANGUAGE, which is the row a checker would get wrong.** A12 writes one per-language block per declared locale and asks each block's `displayValue` list to be unique, so a family comparing the texts across the declaration would refuse the third row. Reported by `CheckFamily.ENUM_VALUE_LABELS`, and only where the label set is otherwise complete — a short or half-blank set draws its own class first and whether A12 adds this one there is unmeasured.

**Everything else in the per-language block is unreachable, and one mechanism accounts for most of it.** `FieldDataCollector` builds those blocks by walking the DECLARED locale set and takes each block's language from it, so the language is never absent (`MVK_LANGUAGE_MISSING`, `MVK_LANGUAGE_FOR_VALUES_MISSING`), never repeated (`MVK_LANGUAGES_DUPLICATE`, `MVK_VALUE_LANGUAGES_DUPLICATE`) and never undeclared (`MVK_LANGUAGE_INVALID`, `MVK_VALUE_LANGUAGE_INVALID`). `addErrorMessageIntern` sharpens the first of those: it writes the language and the text together or writes neither, so the co-requirement `MVK_LANGUAGE_MISSING` tests can never be half-satisfied.

**Two more fall to a dead ARM rather than to a member.** `MVK_DISPLAY_VALUES_MISSING` and `MVK_DISPLAY_VALUE_TOO_LONG` are laws of an extensible enumeration, an arm entered only for an `IStringType` whose `isExtensibleEnum()` is true — a default the md-side `StringTypeImpl` never overrides, DM-JSON having no such type.

**And `MVK_VALUES_FOR_LANGUAGE_MISSING` is the one settled by an existing grid rather than by the collector**: the shape it names — labels for one of two declared locales — draws `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_AND_DISPLAY_VALUES` alone, and that grid reports every class A12 gives.

## §13 supplement — A12 reserves ONE whole name, and the sweep that closed sixteen structural rows around it (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf367"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a declaration-admission law plus a reachability sweep.

**`Id` is the one name A12 refuses outright, and only as a ROOT group's.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupNameAlphabetLawsTest`.

| the root group is named | A12 |
|---|---|
| `Bin` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `Id`, `ID`, `id`, `iD` | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_NAME_INVALID` |
| `Identity`, `BinId` | ADMITTED |
| a NESTED group or a FIELD called `Id` | ADMITTED |

The match is the WHOLE name and case-insensitive, and it is the root carrier's law alone — every other name law in the estate is about an alphabet. Reported by the portable checker under `CheckFamily.ELEMENT_NAME_ALPHABET`.

**The MODEL HEADER's own laws, measured because two published claims disagreed with the collector** (`ModelHeaderSlotLawsTest`):

| the header | A12 |
|---|---|
| the built fixture — the control | ADMITTED |
| no `modelConfig` at all | ADMITTED |
| no `id`, no `modelType` | ADMITTED |
| no `modelVersion` | NOT BUILDABLE |
| no `locales` | NOT BUILDABLE |
| the same locale declared twice | NOT BUILDABLE |
| a model written by hand | NOT BUILDABLE |

**One header member is load-bearing and it is not the one a reader expects.** A model builds with no `id` and no `modelType`; it does not build without `modelVersion`, and the refusal carries no class. That corrects [KF362](#kf362)'s collateral note, which attributed a hand-written model's failure to `MVK_MAX_DIGITS_MISSING` and `MVK_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_MISSING` — both of which name members `DataCollectorUtils` fills from a constant and the codegen parameter, so neither can ever be missing. A repeated locale is likewise a classless build refusal, which takes `MVK_SUPP_LANGUAGES_DUPLICATE` with it.

**And the sweep behind those rows is the transferable part: the COLLECTOR decides reachability.** Every `n/a-structural` code comes from a rule in A12's metamodel document model, and exactly two files build that document from a stored model — `CodeGenValidationDataCollector` and `FieldDataCollector`. Reading the collector line for the member a rule tests answers the reachability question before any fixture is written: a member written unconditionally kills every `FieldNotFilled` law over it, one never written kills every `FieldFilled` gate. Applied across the residue it closed, in one pass:

| the block | why no stored model reaches it |
|---|---|
| the four `*_H_DV` name laws, and `MVK_ROW_TOO_BIG` | all gated on `ModelProperties/oldWorld`, which `addIsOldWorld` writes only for an H model |
| `MVK_MAX_DIGITS_MISSING`, `MVK_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_MISSING` | written from `IProjectSpecificSettings.MAXDIGITS_IN_NUMBERS` and the codegen parameter — constants, always present |
| `MVK_NAME_MISSING` (five carriers), `MVK_TYPE_MISSING` | the collector writes a name and a type for every element it emits |
| `MVK_FORMAT_MISSING`, `MVK_FORMAT_DATE_RANGE_MISSING` | `addDateType` and `addDateRangeType` write the format unconditionally, the builder having filled a default |
| `MVK_DATE_RANGE_FORMAT_INVALID_CODEGEN` | its trigger values carry a `…vonReferenzjahr` suffix the collector never writes: it composes `format + separator + format` and puts the year interpretation in a member of its own |
| `MVK_ROW_INVALID` | `maxRows` is a field's row count, and an A12 document model's field has no row dimension |
