**Two of the sweep's rows were UNMEASURED rather than unreachable, and the distinction is what made one recoverable.** `MVK_NAME_INVALID_A12_DV` and `MVK_NAME_INVALID_H_DV` are metamodel CUSTOM CONDITIONS over a field name (`ungueltigerFeldName`, `ungueltigerFeldNameHDV`), and the complete printable-ASCII sweep in `FieldNameAlphabetLawsTest` draws other classes for every character. *The A12 one is now measured ([KF419](#kf419), 2026-09-15): its live arm is a RESERVED final dotted segment, a name every alphabet gate admits — which is exactly why a character sweep could not reach it, and why the sweep's own rows stand unchanged.* The H-model one keeps this disposition.

## §8 supplement — the Enumeration's declaration laws: one live class, a table axis the reader refuses, and two custom conditions nothing reaches (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf366"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — declaration-admission laws plus a reachability result.

**[MVK-LEDGER] carries fifteen Enumeration shape laws as `n/a-structural`, and one of them is a class a stored model draws.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumDeclarationShapeLawsTest`.

| the declared `EnumerationType` | A12 |
|---|---|
| two values — the control | ADMITTED |
| an EMPTY `values` list, or none | NOT BUILDABLE |
| `sValue` naming a declared value | ADMITTED |
| `sValue` naming no declared value | `MVK_S_VALUE_INVALID` |
| a BLANK `sValue` | ADMITTED |
| a `tableName`, with or without a `columnName` | UNREADABLE |
| two categories sharing a name | NOT BUILDABLE |
| a repeated value with a category declared | `MVK_CATEGORY_VALUE_DUPLICATE` + `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_DUPLICATE` |
| the same repeat with no category | `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUES_DUPLICATE` |
| a repeated category TOKEN over distinct values | ADMITTED |
| a category one token short | `MVK_MISSING_CATEGORY_VALUE` |
| a value or token carrying `<`, or a control character | ADMITTED |

**`MVK_S_VALUE_INVALID` is the kernel basis modelkit's one documented over-strictness never had.** `EnumSpec` refuses a special value outside the declared domain and API-FINDINGS 96 records that as deliberate; the row above is A12 agreeing. A BLANK member is read as unset, so the law is not asked there — the boundary that keeps a checker from refusing a model A12 admits.

**The whole TABLE axis is refused one tier further out than expected.** A12's stored `EnumerationType` declares `values`, `categories`, `errorMessage`, `alphabeticalSorting` and `sValue`; writing a `tableName` beside them makes the source UNREADABLE rather than being ignored. So the five "not allowed beside a table" laws, the table/column co-requirement and the four dependent-column laws have no stored shape at all — ten codes closed on one measured row plus a member list.

**Two of the fifteen stayed UNMEASURED rather than unreachable**, and the distinction is what made them recoverable: `MVK_INTERNAL_VALUE_INVALID` and `MVK_CATEGORY_VALUE_INVALID` are metamodel CUSTOM CONDITIONS (`ungueltigerXMLWert`, `ungueltigerKategorieWert`), and neither markup nor a control character reaches either, so nothing reproduced them — a checker guessing a predicate it has not seen fire would refuse values A12 takes. *Both are now measured ([KF418](#kf418), 2026-09-15): the predicate is a tab, a pipe, or a line break, which is why markup was the wrong probe, and the two rows above stay exactly as measured.*

**And `MVK_CATEGORY_NAME_DUPLICATE` and `MVK_MISSING_VALUE_FOR_CATEGORY` fail on the COLLECTOR's shape rather than on the law.** The categories arrive as a `Map` keyed by name, so a repeated name is a conversion failure and never a verdict; and the collector writes the enum's values and the category's tokens into one repeating group, so that group's count is the larger of the two and can never fall short of the value count.

## §13 supplement — a group's repetition cap depends on the CARRIER, and the three laws beside it are unreachable (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf365"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a declaration-admission law plus a reachability result.

**[MVK-LEDGER] carries four group-declaration laws as `n/a-structural`; one is live and three have no stored spelling.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupIndexAndSortReferenceLawsTest`.

| the group's declaration | A12 |
|---|---|
| the fixture untouched — the control | ADMITTED |
| a ROOT group declaring no `repeatability` | ADMITTED |
| a NESTED group declaring none | ADMITTED |
| a root group at 999 999 999 | ADMITTED |
| a root group at 1 000 000 000 | `MVK_MAX_TOO_BIG` |
| a nested group at 1 000 000 000 | ADMITTED |
| a nested group at 1 999 999 999 | ADMITTED |
| a nested group at 2 000 000 000 | `MVK_MAX_TOO_BIG` |
| a nested group at 2 147 483 647 | `MVK_MAX_TOO_BIG` |
| a nested group at 2 147 483 648 | UNREADABLE |
| `indexFieldName` holding two names | UNREADABLE |
| a plural `indexFieldNames` repeating one name | ADMITTED |

**The two caps are an order of magnitude apart, and A12 states them as two rules rather than one.** A checker holding a single bound would refuse a legal nested group or miss an illegal root one — the carrier axis is the whole result, so both were walked rather than one measured and the other assumed.

**Past a signed 32-bit count A12 stops READING**, `Group.repeatability` being an `int`, so the model reaches no verdict at all. Both cells of that boundary are measured, because it is the constant a checker must encode if it is not to name a class A12 never issued.

**`MVK_MAX_MISSING` cannot fire on a stored model**: `CodeGenValidationDataCollector.addRootGroup` and `addGroup` both write `maxRepetitions` unconditionally, from `EntityUtils.getMaxLfdNr`/`getMax` — the count A12 derived, never the member it read. An omitted `repeatability` is a group that repeats once.

**Nor can either INDEX-cardinality law**, and both spellings a stored model could reach for were attacked: A12's `Group` holds a single `indexField` reference and `IGroup.getIndexFieldNames()` answers with a `Set`, so an array under the singular member is refused by the reader and a plural member is ignored. `MVK_INDEX_FIELD_DUPLICATE` needs a repeat inside that set and `MVK_TOO_MANY_INDEX_FIELDS` needs two members of it; neither has a stored shape. (`kernel-core-calc` asserts the same cardinality in its own code.)

## §13 supplement — the number type's digit budget is 15, and five of its seven metamodel laws reach a stored model (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf364"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — declaration-admission laws plus a reachability result.

**[MVK-LEDGER] carries seven number-type laws as `n/a-structural` beside the two already measured, and they split five-to-two.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.NumberTypeDigitLawsTest`.

| the declared `NumberType` | A12 |
|---|---|
| an ordinary scale — the control | ADMITTED |
| both fractional members `-1` | `MVK_FRACT_DIGITS_MISSING` |
| only the maximum `-1` | ADMITTED |
| `trait:"amount"` with no `maxIntegerDigits` | ADMITTED |
| the same amount with `maxIntegerDigits` | ADMITTED |
| `trait:"amount"` with no fractional part either | ADMITTED |
| `trait:"percent"` with no `maxIntegerDigits` | ADMITTED |

**`-1` is the suppression sentinel, and it is what makes "missing" expressible at all.** `FieldDataCollector.addNumberType` writes `fractionalDigits` and `maxFractionalDigits` into the metamodel document only when the member is not `-1`, so an ABSENT member arrives as the primitive default 0 and counts as declared. `MVK_FRACT_DIGITS_MISSING` therefore needs BOTH members explicitly `-1` — which is why `{}` is admitted and the pair `-1,-1` is not.

**`MVK_AMOUNT_INT_PART_MISSING` is unreachable, and its two links were attacked separately.** The arm is reached — `extractFieldTypeName` returns `GeldBetragMitCent`/`GeldBetragOhneCent` for exactly `isNumberTraitAmount()`, split on whether a fractional part is declared — but on that arm the member the law demands is never absent: `TypeConverter.convertNumber` fills the integer-place count with `15 - maxFractionalDigits` whenever an amount declares none, and the collector writes it whenever it is present.

| the same field against the budget | A12 |
|---|---|
| `maxLength` 15, 16 | ADMITTED |
| `maxLength` 17 | `MVK_MAX_LENGTH_TOO_BIG` |
| `minLength` 17 | `MVK_MIN_LENGTH_TOO_BIG` |
| `maxLength` 16 with `positivesOnly` | `MVK_MAX_LENGTH_TOO_BIG` |
| `maxLength` 17 beside `maxFractionalDigits: 2` | ADMITTED |
| `maxLength` 18 beside `maxFractionalDigits: 2` | `MVK_MAX_LENGTH_TOO_BIG` |
| `maxLength` 4 beside `minFractionalDigits: 3` | `MVK_MAX_LENGTH_TOO_SMALL` |
| `maxLength` 5 beside the same | ADMITTED |
| `minLength` 8 with `maxLength` 4 | `MVK_MIN_LENGTH_BIGGER_MAX_LENGTH` |
| `maxIntegerDigits: 14` with `minFractionalDigits: 2` | `MVK_ARITY_TOO_BIG` |
| `maxIntegerDigits: 15` alone | ADMITTED |
| `maxIntegerDigits: 16` or 20 | REFUSED, codeless ([re-tiered 2026-09-15](#kf420)) |

**The budget is 15 and the length threshold is `15 + a sign + a fractional part`** — derived from the rows rather than assumed, by walking 16 across the sign and across a declared scale. The sign is `!positivesOnly` (`TypeConverter` writes `hasSign`), so an ordinary number gets 16 and a signless one 15.

**A SUPPRESSED fractional member costs nothing in that threshold**: with both at `-1`, `maxLength` 17 is refused, so the branch taken is the metamodel's `== 0` one against a member the collector never wrote. A checker reading `-1` as "some fractional part" would allow 17 and under-report.

**`MVK_ARITY_TOO_BIG` is reachable only from within the budget.** An integer-place count above 15 is refused at the BUILD tier with no code at all, so the law needs a count of at most 15 that a fractional part then pushes past it. The amount arm reaches it through the derived count: a minimum scale above the maximum leaves the count buildable and the sum over budget, drawing `MVK_ARITY_TOO_BIG` beside `MVK_FRACT_DIGITS_INVALID`; suppressing the maximum instead derives 16 and is refused at the build tier.

**`MVK_MIN_LENGTH_BIGGER_MAX_LENGTH` is measured on this carrier because it was measured on the other one.** A12's metamodel states the law twice, once under the string type and once under the number types, and a class measured on one carrier is not a class measured on the other — [KF319](#kf319) had only the string one.

## §13 supplement — a name may repeat freely across parents; only the within-parent and root-group collisions are refused (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf363"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a reachability result plus an admission law.

**[MVK-LEDGER] carries three MODEL-WIDE name laws as `n/a-structural`** — group names unique, root-group names unique, field name+group pairs unique model-wide. Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.ModelWideNameUniquenessLawsTest`.

| the collision | A12 |
|---|---|
| the fixture untouched — the control | ADMITTED |
| a second ROOT group with a distinct name | ADMITTED |
| a second root group with the SAME name | NOT BUILDABLE, no code |
| two subgroups of the SAME parent sharing a name | NOT BUILDABLE, no code |
| two subgroups of DIFFERENT parents sharing a name | ADMITTED |
| two fields of different groups sharing a name | ADMITTED |

**A name is scoped to its parent, and the two "model-wide" laws are not laws of a stored model.** `Insured` under one root group and `Insured` under another are both admitted, as are two fields of different groups sharing a name — so a checker that widened the within-parent law to the model would refuse two shapes A12 takes. None of the three codes is reachable: the two collisions A12 does refuse are build refusals carrying no class at all.

**Both refused shapes are already covered**, so this block closes with no new family: the within-parent case is `CheckFamily.ELEMENT_NAME_UNIQUENESS`, and the duplicate ROOT-group name is reported as `CK_MODEL_NOT_BUILDABLE` — verified against the checker rather than assumed from the family's wording, which speaks of a group's children and root groups are not one.

**A mislabelled row nearly made this grid wrong.** The "different parents" case was first written as an insertion into the SAME parent's element list, which measured NOT BUILDABLE and would have read as a model-wide law being real. The label said different parents; the patch said otherwise. Read the patch, not the label.

## §13 supplement — none of the four YES/NO declaration laws is reachable from a stored A12 model (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf362"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a reachability result.

**[MVK-LEDGER] carries four yes/no laws as `n/a-structural`** — the yes and no representations must each be declared, must differ, and must form a sanctioned pair. A12's DM-JSON `BooleanType` carries them as `notInDCustomTrueValue` / `notInDCustomFalseValue`. Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.BooleanCustomValueLawsTest`.

| the `BooleanType` body | A12 |
|---|---|
| neither custom value — the control | ADMITTED |
| both, and distinct | ADMITTED |
| both, and IDENTICAL | ADMITTED |
| only the TRUE value | ADMITTED |
| only the FALSE value | ADMITTED |
| both, and BLANK | ADMITTED |
| the same patch with an unknown `fieldType.type` — the POSITIVE CONTROL | UNREADABLE |

**Every row is admitted, which is why the control is the load-bearing one.** A patch that silently failed to land produces exactly this table, so the grid says nothing without a row proving the mechanism reaches A12. It does, and one tier earlier than a build failure: an unknown type name is refused by the deserializer.

**The mechanism, consistent with the rows.** `TypeConverter.convertBoolean` reads each member through `orElse("true")` / `orElse("false")`, so an absent one is indistinguishable from the default downstream and "missing" never reaches a check. The pair laws do not fire on a stored model either. *(Why the pair laws are silent is a HYPOTHESIS — presumably the `considerNotInD` gate — and nothing rests on it: the rows are the finding.)*

**Two collateral facts worth carrying.** A hand-written model is NOT a substitute for a draft here: every row of a hand-written grid read NOT BUILDABLE for unrelated reasons — measured, on the first attempt. *(Corrected 2026-09-14, [KF367](#kf367): the reason given here was the header's own laws, `MVK_MAX_DIGITS_MISSING` and `MVK_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_MISSING`, and it is wrong in both halves — both codes name members A12's collector fills from constants and neither is reachable at all. What refuses a hand-written model is a single missing `header.modelVersion`, with no class; `id` and `modelType` may both be left out. So hand-writing a fixture is fine as long as it carries that member — `ModelHeaderSlotLawsTest`.)* And modelkit's `BooleanSpec` is an empty record, so neither member is authorable through the typed surface at all.

## §13 supplement — a sort list needs a REPEATABLE carrier, and the four PRIORITY laws beside it cannot be expressed in DM-JSON (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf361"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a declaration-admission law plus a reachability result.

**[MVK-LEDGER] carries five sort laws as `n/a-structural`, and they do not share a fate.** Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.GroupIndexAndSortReferenceLawsTest`.

| the group's `sortFields` | A12 |
|---|---|
| a non-empty list on a REPEATABLE group — the control | ADMITTED |
| a non-empty list on a NON-repeatable group | `MVK_INVALID_SORTINFO` |
| an EMPTY list on a non-repeatable group | ADMITTED |

**The member's PRESENCE is not the gate, its CONTENT is** — the empty row is what separates "this group declares sorting" from "this group cannot be sorted", and a checker keyed on the key would refuse every non-repeatable group that merely carries it.

**The other four are unreachable by SHAPE, not by policy.** `MVK_SORT_PRIO_DUPLICATE`, `MVK_INVALID_SORT_PRIO`, `MVK_SORT_PRIO_VALUE_MISSING` and `MVK_SORT_INFO_MISSING` are all about a PRIORITY, and A12's DM-JSON `Group.SortField` (`kernel-md-a12internal`) declares exactly two members, `field` and `order`. The position an `ISortField` reports is derived from the list INDEX by `GroupWrapper.SortFieldWrapper`, so a stored model has no priority to duplicate, to overrun, or to leave a hole in, and no third member to fill or omit.

**That is what the `n/a-structural` bucket actually contains**, and it is worth stating once: those codes come from rules in A12's own METAMODEL document models, which validate a model-under-edit represented as an A12 document. Whether a given one also constrains a stored DM-JSON model is a per-code reachability question — the first one examined here splits four ways unreachable and one way live, so the bucket is a queue of questions rather than a queue of families.

## §8 supplement — a string CONSTANT against an Enumeration draws FOUR different classes, one per carrier (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf360"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**Two kernel methods own this law and they do not agree on a class.** `CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkEnumValue` answers a comparison; `CheckEntityListenUtils.checkEnumType` answers a value list, splitting again on whether the reference is categorized; and the multi-member quantifiers answer with a fourth. Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.EnumConstantDomainLawsTest`.

| the constant's carrier | A12 |
|---|---|
| `[Tier] == "BASIC"` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `[Tier] == "NOPE"` | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUM_COMPARISON` |
| `[Tier -> Band] == "NOPE"` | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUM_COMPARISON` |
| `FieldValueIncludedInValueList(Tier, …, "NOPE")` | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION` |
| `FieldValueNotIncludedInValueList(Tier, "NOPE")` | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION` |
| `FieldValueIncludedInValueList(Tier -> Band, …, "NOPE")` | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION_CATEGORY` |
| the three multi-member quantifiers, `(Tier, Segment In "NOPE")` | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUMERATION_OR_CATEGORY` |
| `FieldValueIncludedInValueList(Reference, "anything")`, a STRING field | ADMITTED |
| `FieldValueIncludedInValueList(Premium, "anything")`, a NUMBER field | `MVK_INVALID_TYPES_FOR_COMPARISON` |

**The category splits the value list and NOT the comparison**, which no reading of either method predicts on its own and is the row a one-carrier family would have got wrong: both categorized and plain comparisons draw the same class, while the value list draws two.

**A STRING field's list is admitted whatever it carries** — `isLikeString` is a `continue` in A12's loop, so there is no domain to be outside of. A family reading only "a literal must be a declared value" refuses every string value list in an estate.

**The NUMBER row was PREDICTED WRONG from that same loop**, which falls through to `MVK_NO_STRING_OR_ENUM`: a comparison gate answers ahead of it, so the loop's kind class is not reachable by this shape. That is the second source-order prediction refuted here in one day ([KF358](#kf358) is the first).

**The portable family (`CheckFamily.SCALAR_VALUE_LIST_GATES`, then named `ENUM_CONSTANT_DOMAIN`) takes the two SCALAR value lists and stops there**, and that carrier boundary still holds: the comparison and the quantifiers answer with two OTHER classes, so widening by analogy would name the scalars' class on them. **Two of the three under-reports its KDoc stated are closed** ([KF397](#kf397) gave the quantifiers their own family, [KF398](#kf398) gave this one the CATEGORIZED operand, which the category reader reduces); the comparison carrier remains another method's.

## §8 supplement — the gate chain over a `->` CATEGORY reference, and the three classes around it (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf359"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**`CheckEntityUtils.checkCategory` runs two gates**: the referenced entity must be an Enumeration, then the name behind the arrow must be one it DECLARES. Neither class had a measurement in this estate. Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.CategoryReferenceGateOrderLawsTest`.

| the arrow's operands | A12 |
|---|---|
| `[Tier -> Band]`, a declared category — the control | ADMITTED |
| `[Tier -> NoSuchBand]` | `MVK_CATEGORY_UNKOWN` |
| `[Reference -> Band]`, a STRING field | `MVK_NO_ENUMERATION` |
| `[Insured -> Band]`, a GROUP | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| `[NoSuchField -> Band]` | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| `[Tier -> Band] == "NOPE"`, a declared category and an undeclared CLASSIFICATION | `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUM_COMPARISON` |

**Six rows, six distinct classes, and the last two are the ones worth carrying.** Resolution and the operand's kind both answer ahead of this chain, so the two category classes are reachable only where the reference is otherwise sound. And the category's own VALUE domain is a THIRD law with a third class: naming a declared category and then comparing it to a classification the category does not carry is `MVK_INVALID_STRING_CONSTANT_FOR_ENUM_COMPARISON`, about the comparison's constant rather than about the arrow.

**The portable family (`CheckFamily.CATEGORY_REFERENCE`) is silent on a `TypeDefType` field, and the reference corpus is why.** A field typed by reference to a type definition may BE an Enumeration declaring the category — preparation keeps type definitions' ids alone, so the checker cannot tell. A first version reported `MVK_NO_ENUMERATION` on `[format->containsYear]` in a model A12 builds, caught by `adapter.laws.CheckerSilenceOnCleanModelsTest` before the family landed. The silence is the documented under-report; the coverage gap it rides on was already declared in `Check.kt`.

## §9 supplement — the complete gate chain over a `Having` filter's OWN operand, whose measured order is NOT its source order (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf358"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**`CheckEntitySpecImpl.checkFilterCondition` carries the whole chain in one method**: the filtered operand must be a field (`checkIsField`), then must carry a wildcard (`checkHasWildCards`), then no semantic index, and only then is the filter BODY judged — the body being [KF97](#kf97)'s subject. Locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.FilteredOperandGateOrderLawsTest`.

| the filtered operand | A12 |
|---|---|
| a starred field — the control | ADMITTED |
| an UNSTARRED field | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| a starred GROUP | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| a GROUP with no star either | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| a starred field carrying a SEMANTIC INDEX | `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED` |
| the same with no star | `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED` |
| a GROUP carrying a semantic index — BOTH defects | `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED` |
| a disallowed construct in the filter BODY | `MVK_DISALLOWED_CONSTRUCT_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` |

**The code's own name is misleading, and that is the first load-bearing row.** `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED` is NOT what a plainly unstarred filtered field draws — A12's iteration gate outruns this chain and answers `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`. The class is also reachable where the operand carries a semantic index, which the last two rows show holds with a `*` present in the text: the index spelling consumes the wildcard, so `hasWildCards()` is false despite the star.

*Corrected 2026-09-15 ([KF424](#kf424)): the first sentence's measurement stands and its reach did not. Every row of this grid sits on a rule whose error field is outside every repetition, so "the iteration gate outruns this chain" was true of the whole SET rather than of the unstarred operand — on a rule that iterates, and on an operand that crosses no repetition at all, that gate is satisfied and a plainly unstarred filtered field does draw `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED`. The semantic index is therefore one of two routes to the class, not the only one; "only" above is amended to "also".*

**The order is measured, and the measurement contradicts the source order — the second load-bearing row.** Reading the method predicts that an operand which is both a group and indexed draws the kind class, `checkIsField` being written first. A12 answers `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED`. A checker built by transcribing the chain in its written order names the wrong class there, which is why the portable family tests the index before the kind (`CheckFamily.FILTERED_OPERAND_KIND`). *(Why the index moves the verdict is a HYPOTHESIS — presumably the indexed ref is no longer the group — and nothing here rests on it: the rows are what the family encodes.)*

**The star is not a variable on either defect**, which is what the two paired rows establish: a group operand answers the same starred or not, and an indexed operand likewise. So a family keyed on the wildcard would be wrong in both directions.

## §9 supplement — which FIELD predicates refuse a GROUP operand: the two scalars, and only where the starring is already right (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf357"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**A12's `CheckEntityUtils` carries the pair `checkIsField` / `checkIsGroup`, and only the second had ever been measured here** ([KF327](#kf327), the `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` direction). This is the first: `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`, locked by `rulekit.validate.laws.FieldOperandKindLawsTest`.

**Two carriers refuse a group; eight expand it.** `FieldFilled` and `FieldNotFilled` take one entity and have nothing to expand it to. Every field-LIST carrier — `AllFieldsFilled`, `NoFieldFilled`, `AtLeastOneFieldFilled`, `NotAllFieldsFilled`, `FieldsNotCollectivelyFilled`, `NotExactlyOneFieldFilled`, `MoreThanOneFieldFilled`, `NumberOfFilledFields` — ADMITS a group operand and quantifies over its fields (`EntityUtils.expandToFieldList`). A family assembled from what the operators are CALLED would refuse those eight, which is [KF327](#kf327)'s trap arriving from the other side: there the name would have refused five.

**Three gates outrun the kind gate, so the class is only reachable where the path is otherwise well formed.**

| the operand, on `FieldFilled` | A12 |
|---|---|
| a field — the control | ADMITTED |
| a group that neither repeats nor is the root | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| a repeatable group read WITHOUT a star | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| a star on a group that does not repeat | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` |
| the ROOT group | `MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED` |
| a correctly STARRED repeatable group | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| a nested group below a correctly starred level | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |

**The two wildcard rows are the discriminating pair, and they point opposite ways.** A star is neither necessary nor sufficient: adding one to a repeatable group moves the verdict from the wildcard class to the kind class, and adding one to a group that does not repeat moves it from the kind class to the other wildcard class. So a checker cannot treat the star as noise in either direction — the portable family tests that the operand's star COUNT equals the number of repeating levels on its path, and stays silent otherwise (`CheckFamily.FIELD_OPERAND_KIND`).

## §14 supplement — a path is resolved SEGMENT BY SEGMENT, and the root-group class turns on WHICH segment missed (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf356"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**A12 walks a path left to right and runs three gates per segment — resolution, the H-model `.*` suffix, then the wildcard's landing site** (`CheckIdNameRefImpl.checkIdNameRef`). So the first defective segment answers, and within a segment resolution answers before the other two.

| the path | A12 |
|---|---|
| `Sum(Claims*/Amount) > 0` — the control | ADMITTED |
| `/NoSuchRoot/Amount` | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP` |
| `/NoSuchRoot` alone | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP` |
| `/Claims*/Amount` — a DECLARED group read at root level | `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP` |
| `/Policy/NoSuchField` — the root resolves | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| `Claims*/NoSuchField` | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| `Claims.*/Amount` | `MVK_POINT_IN_A12_MODEL` |
| `NoSuchGroup.*/Amount` | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` — resolution first |
| `NoSuchGroup*/Amount` | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` — resolution first |
| `Insured*/InsuredName` — a star on a non-repeatable group | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` |
| `Insured*/NoSuchField` | `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` — the earlier segment answers |
| `../../../Reference` | `MVK_TOO_MANY_PARENT_GROUPS` |

**`MVK_POINT_IN_A12_MODEL` had never been drawn in this estate.** Its ledger row calls it erased because the typed renderer never emits `.*` — true of the renderer, and not of a raw condition string, which `rule check` and `modify --condition` both accept.

**The row that mattered was `/NoSuchRoot/Amount`, and it exposed a live wrong-class defect in the portable checker.** Every earlier measurement of the root-group class used a path of exactly one segment, so "the path is one segment long" and "the ROOT segment is what failed" were one thing across all of them — and the checker had implemented the first, counting separators in the whole candidate. It named `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` where A12 names `MVK_INVALID_ROOT_GROUP`, on every absolute path whose missing root carries a child. Two of its own mirrors asserted that wrong class, neither of them ever put to the Kernel; the message-parameter surface had the separating row (`RuleMessageGroupParameterLawsTest`) and the shared helper got it wrong there too.

Locked: `validate.laws.ReferenceSegmentGateOrderLawsTest`. **Fixed in the portable checker on 2026-09-14** — `Reference.Undeclared` now carries whether the root segment resolved, because only the resolver knows which roots a model declares.

## §9 supplement — `RepetitionNotUnique`'s COMPLETE gate order, and the two branches that never both run (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf355"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**Eleven classes guard one construct, and until now the estate had measured them one containment assertion at a time across four files.** A containment claim cannot say which gate answers when two are violated, which is the only question that matters to a client-side checker deciding whether it may speak.

**The KEY LIST is checked first, in this order**, every gate over the whole list: a CATEGORY projection `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED` · a GROUP `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` · a WILDCARD `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` · a SEMANTIC INDEX `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED` · a field without value validation `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`. **Every one of them reports ahead of every scope and placement gate** — measured on three shapes that break a key rule and a later rule at once.

**Then exactly ONE of two branches runs, chosen by whether `@From` is present**, and that is the structural claim worth keeping:

| with `@From` | without |
|---|---|
| scope is a FIELD → `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` | keys on PARALLEL paths → `MVK_NOT_IN_SAME_PATH` |
| scope does not repeat → `MVK_GROUP_NOT_REPEATABLE` | a key outside the RULE GROUP → `MVK_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP` |
| a key outside the scope → `MVK_NOT_IN_GROUP` | no repeatable group between key and rule group → `MVK_REPEATABLE_GROUP_MISSING` |

Keys on parallel paths draw `MVK_NOT_IN_SAME_PATH` with no scope and `MVK_NOT_IN_GROUP` with one: the shared-path check is not run at all in the `@From` branch, rather than being outranked.

**Amended 2026-09-14, the shared-path check's own mechanism** (`CheckEntityListenUtils.checkAllRepeatableGroupsOnSamePath`, source-verified), which a reproduction needs and a containment reading gets wrong: it accumulates rather than compares pairwise. It walks the keys in authored order, skips any key with no repeatable group of its own, and keeps the LONGEST path seen so far — `getLongestSharedPath` returns the longer of two when one is a prefix of the other and `null` otherwise. So the key REPORTED is the first one that cannot extend the chain, not the pair that disagrees. Both this gate and `checkAllEntitiesInRuleGroup` compare parent paths carrying a trailing slash, which is what keeps `/Depot/Crate/` from reading as inside `/Depot/Crates/`.

**The carrier fact that had to be discovered before any placement row could be measured.** A key in a second repeatable group is read by a rule whose error field sits in the first, so unless the two groups are INDEX-KEYED on the same field the read iterates past the target and `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` answers first — on every placement row at once. That is [KF350](#kf350)'s gate again, and it is what [KF349](#kf349) recorded narrowly for `MVK_NOT_IN_GROUP`: the requirement is the carrier's, not that class's.

Locked: `validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueGateOrderLawsTest`. `MVK_CATEGORY_NOT_ALLOWED` and `MVK_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP` had no measurement anywhere in this estate before it.

## §14 supplement — four `MVK_*` members are message LABELS and can never be a verdict, and one command enumerates them (source-verified, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf354"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a property of A12's diagnostic vocabulary, not an evaluation behaviour.

**A12's checkers share helpers that take the CALLER's operation name as a parameter, and a caller supplies it by asking the message bundle for its own code's bare text.** `CheckEntityUtils.checkIsValueValidation(ref, opName, ctx)` is the worked example: it raises `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` with `opName` interpolated, and seven callers reach it. A code used that way is never thrown, so no model can draw it — and a ledger row describing it as a law names a real constraint under a code that cannot carry it.

**The enumeration is complete and derivable, which is what makes this a class rather than an anecdote.** `grep -rn 'getBareErrorMessage(' --include='*.java' kernel-tool` returns every label site; four of them name a `ParserErrorTypesEnum` member, and each of those members has **exactly one** occurrence in the kernel outside its own enum declaration — that label site.

| code | its one site | what A12 reports instead |
|---|---|---|
| `MVK_FIELD_REF_OP` | `CheckFeldWertOpImpl` | the code the shared check raises, with this text as the operation name |
| `MVK_CATEGORY_REF_OP` | `CheckEntitySpecImpl.checkCategory` | likewise, through `checkIsField` |
| `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_REF_OP` | `CheckSemanticIndexImpl` | `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE` ([KF351](#kf351)) |
| `MVK_CONDITION` | `MVKDefaultErrorStrategy` | one of the four parse-phase codes (`RuleConditionSyntaxLawsTest`) |

**Two of the four were found one at a time, months apart, each time as a surprise.** `MVK_FIELD_REF_OP` was corrected on 2026-06-10 by a `Check*Impl` cross-validation and `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_REF_OP` on 2026-09-14 by a grid whose prediction it refuted; both corrections describe the same mechanism without naming it, which is why the remaining two were still carried as laws. The `_REF_OP` suffix is the visible half of the pattern and `MVK_CONDITION` shows it is not the whole of it — the mechanism is the bare-message call, not the name.

Locked: no test can lock a negative of this shape, and none is claimed. The basis is the enumeration above, re-derivable in one command against the pinned checkout; `validate.laws.RuleConditionSyntaxLawsTest` independently measures that `MVK_CONDITION` is not what a malformed condition draws.

## §9 supplement — the four whole-RULE gates over a PARALLEL iteration, and the type half nobody had varied (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf353"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**Two index-keyed repeatable groups iterate jointly with no construct to say so, and A12 then runs four whole-rule gates over the finished parse tree in a fixed order** (`ParserService.checkNormalRule`). Three of their classes had no measurement anywhere in this estate.

| the condition | A12 |
|---|---|
| a parallel iteration alone (`FieldsNotCollectivelyFilled` over both groups) | ADMITTED |
| a pure NEGATIVE over both groups | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_INVALID` ([KF123](#kf123)) |
| `RepetitionNotUnique` beside a cross-group read | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| both at once | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED` — the uniqueness gate runs first |
| a `Having` filter on an operand whose OUTER level is parallel-iterated | `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_FOR_FILTERED_ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| a filter whose own BODY reads the parallel group | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` |

**The filtered-entity class needs a repetition INSIDE a parallel-iterated group, which is why it had never been drawn here.** A star puts a WILDCARD at its own level, so the parallel-iterated level has to be an outer one — a flat two-group fixture cannot express it, and an unstarred filter operand is refused by the aggregate's own arity gate (`MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED`) long before any parallel-iteration gate is reached. Both of those were measured on the way.

**`MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_NOT_ALLOWED`'s second firing site is not reached by a filter that parallel-iterates**, because a filter body may not ITERATE at all and that broader class answers first. One shape is not an unreachability proof and none is claimed.

**The load-bearing correction: the index fields' TYPE is not a detail of the joint iteration, it selects a different class.** Every row above and every earlier row in this estate pairs two STRING keys, so "same name" and "same name and type" were one thing across the whole set. With the two `LineRef` fields declared STRING and NUMBER, the same condition draws **`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX_TYPE`** — ahead of the uniqueness gate, not instead of the iteration. A client-side check keying on the index field's NAME alone would therefore name the parallel class where A12 names this one: a wrong class on a correct rejection, which is what any family reading this area has to avoid.

Locked: `validate.laws.ParallelIterationGateLawsTest`. **Reported by the portable checker since 2026-09-14** (`PARALLEL_ITERATION_UNIQUENESS`), which pairs two repeatable groups only when their index fields share a NAME and a declared TYPE and neither read is starred — the intersection of what is measured rather than A12's own `matchBaseType`, so it under-reports rather than guessing.

## §9 supplement — one `RepetitionNotUnique` per condition, counted as CALLS over the whole tree (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf352"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**A condition carrying two `RepetitionNotUnique` calls draws `MVK_INVALID_COMBINATION_OF_REPETITON_NOT_UNIQUE`, and one call with a COMPOSITE key does not.** The law is about the operator's multiplicity, never the key's — which matters because merging the keys into one call is the fix the rejection asks for, so a client-side check reading key count would refuse the corrective.

| the condition carries | A12 |
|---|---|
| one call | ADMITTED |
| one call, composite key `(Items/Sku, Items/Count)` | ADMITTED |
| one call beside an ordinary conjunct | ADMITTED |
| two calls over different keys | `MVK_INVALID_COMBINATION_OF_REPETITON_NOT_UNIQUE` |
| two calls in opposite arms of an `Or` | `MVK_INVALID_COMBINATION_OF_REPETITON_NOT_UNIQUE` |
| the same call twice | `MVK_INVALID_COMBINATION_OF_REPETITON_NOT_UNIQUE` |

**The `Or` row is the one worth keeping.** No evaluation of that condition reaches both calls, so a per-branch reading fits every other row and is false: A12 runs this over the finished parse tree, in `ParserService.checkNormalRule`, after the condition has parsed.

**It is a whole-RULE gate, so every construct's own gate reports ahead of it** — measured on two conditions that each carry two calls AND break a rule of one call: a `@From` scope naming a group that does not repeat draws `MVK_GROUP_NOT_REPEATABLE`, and a key naming a group draws `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`. That places the gate in the order rather than merely establishing it exists.

**And a second call inside a `Having` filter is not a second call at all**: the construct is refused in that position outright, `MVK_DISALLOWED_CONSTRUCT_IN_FILTER_CONDITION`, so removing the filter's call leaves one legal call behind. The row exists because the portable checker's call scanner does descend into a filter body, and counting naively named this class on a model A12 answers with another.

Locked: `validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueCombinationLawsTest`. **Reported by the portable checker since 2026-09-14** (`REPETITION_NOT_UNIQUE_COMBINATION`), which counts calls outside filters and reports even where a construct gate would pre-empt it in A12 — both defects are real and A12 simply stops at the first.

## §9 supplement — the SEMANTIC INDEX's nine classes, in the order they answer, and the two that are never reported (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf351"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**`[Field For key]` carries nine rejection classes and they form one chain, so which one answers is a fact about ORDER rather than about any single gate.** Five of them had no measurement anywhere in this estate before this grid, and every ledger row describing them was written from the code's NAME. Two of those readings were wrong, in the direction that hands an author a fix for a gate they did not trip.

| the index is malformed by | A12 reports |
|---|---|
| a key naming a NON-REPEATABLE group | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NO_FIELD` |
| a key carrying a wildcard | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_WILDCARD` |
| a key carrying its own semantic index | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_SEMANTIC_INDEX` |
| a key whose type does not match the index field's | `MVK_INDEX_TYPE_INCONSISTENT` |
| a key field declared without value validation | **`MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`** — not `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_REF_OP` |
| a key carrying a CATEGORY projection, types otherwise matching | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_CATEGORY` |
| an indexed group declaring no index field | `MVK_NO_INDEX_FIELD` |
| an empty literal key | `MVK_INDEX_VALUE_INVALID` |

**`MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_REF_OP` is never a verdict — it is the operation NAME interpolated into someone else's message.** The value-validation gate is A12's shared `checkIsValueValidation`, which takes the caller's label as a parameter and raises `MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`; the semantic-index caller passes its own code's bare text as that label. A ledger row reading "a semantic index's referenced field must have value validation enabled" therefore names a real law under a code no model can ever draw.

**An ITERATING key pre-empts the whole chain, and A12 renames the class instead of adding one.** A key that reads a repeatable group unstarred — the group itself, a field inside one, or a NON-repeatable group inside one (measured 2026-09-14, the row that separates "the gate reads the key's KIND" from "the gate reads what the READ does": that key is a group and could have drawn the key-kind class) — draws `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_INVALID_ITER`, and the discriminator is that the SAME condition with the same read outside any index draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`. It is one gate with two spellings: A12's `checkIterationAndErrorField` asks `isSemanticIndex(errorCtx)` and picks the class from the answer, which is also why `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_CONTAINED_IN_INDEX` ([KF205](#kf205)) needs the rule anchored so the iteration is legal before it can be reached at all.

**The three wildcard classes are one law read at three positions, and only a grid separates them.** Where the star sits relative to the indexed group chooses the class outright: at the indexed group's own level `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_AND_WILDCARD`, at any level above it `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_BELOW_WILDCARD`, inside the key `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_WILDCARD`. `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_BELOW_WILDCARD` had never been drawn here, and a first enumeration concluded it had no raiser at all — a `grep --include` whose globs the shell ate, returning the confident zero this record warns about. It is live, from a second site (`CheckEntityUtils.checkIndicesForA12Model`) rather than from the index checker.

**Extended 2026-09-23: "the indexed group" is the INDEX GROUP, and a star BELOW it is admitted.** The group the star is measured against is the nearest one on the entity's own chain that declares an index field (`CheckEntityUtils.getIndexGroup`), not the group or field the index is written on. So `Packages/Parcels* For "P1"`, indexed on `Packages`, is legal, and it is the index that binds the unstarred `Packages` level: without it, `NoGroupFilled(Packages/Parcels*)` is `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`. With no index group on the chain, the class is `MVK_NO_INDEX_FIELD` whether or not a star is present. This was measured as a 4×2 grid (below, at, above, no index group), with a group operand and a field operand, on `FirstFilledValue` and on `NoGroupFilled`. The class does not change with the carrier or the operand kind. rulekit had refused every star beside an index with `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_AND_WILDCARD`, so the admitted shape could not be authored, and the adapter could not read it back. *(Locked: `validate.laws.SemanticIndexWildcardPlacementLawsTest`.)*

**The key-kind gate reports ahead of every gate below it**, measured on two shapes that violate it and a later one at once: a group key in a group declaring no index field, and a group key whose indexed path is starred. Both draw `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NO_FIELD`.

**Extended 2026-09-14 with the ORDER AMONG the structural gates**, which the single-defect rows above cannot settle and which a reproduction turns on, because the pairs an author writes violate two at once:

| the index carries | A12 |
|---|---|
| a starred KEY where the indexed group declares no index field | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_WILDCARD` |
| a starred KEY beside a star at the indexed group's level | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_WILDCARD` |
| a star at the indexed group's level, that group declaring no index field | `MVK_NO_INDEX_FIELD` |
| an EMPTY key where the indexed group declares no index field | `MVK_NO_INDEX_FIELD` |
| an EMPTY key beside a star at the indexed group's level | `MVK_INDEX_VALUE_INVALID` |
| a CATEGORY key beside a star at the indexed group's level | `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_WITH_CATEGORY` |

So the chain descends: the key's own star, then the missing index field, then the empty key, then the category, and the star on the indexed path answers only when nothing above it does.

Locked: `validate.laws.SemanticIndexStructureLawsTest`. **The key-kind gate is reported by the portable checker since 2026-09-14** (`SEMANTIC_INDEX_KEY`), on the one shape it can decide without knowing the rule's anchoring: a key naming a group with nothing repeating on its path. **Six more of the chain are reported since the same day** by `CheckFamily.SEMANTIC_INDEX_STRUCTURE` (`consistency … SemanticIndexStructureTest`) — every class above except the two that compare declared TYPES or locations, `MVK_INDEX_TYPE_INCONSISTENT` and `MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_CONTAINED_IN_INDEX`. It reports at most one class per condition text and stops at the first index it cannot read through, which is what the iterating-key pre-emption above demands of any reproduction.

## §9 supplement — an UNSTARRED repetition read decides the class a flat error target draws, and referencedness does not enter it (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf350"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**A12 reports `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` on a rule whose condition reads a repeatable group UNSTARRED while its error target sits outside that repetition — whether or not the condition also names the target.** A STAR over the same list collapses it to one value, no iteration remains, and the error-field gate answers instead. So the two gates are independent and the iteration one reports first.

| the condition reads | flat target UNREFERENCED | flat target REFERENCED |
|---|---|---|
| `FieldFilled(Parcels/Weight)` — unstarred | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| `Sum(Parcels*/Weight) > 0` — starred | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` | **ADMITTED** |
| `FieldFilled(Customs/Declaration)` — nothing repeating | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` | ADMITTED (the grid above) |

**Found by a DIFFERENTIAL, and no grid in the estate could have found it.** `adapter.laws.CheckerSilenceOnMutatedModelsTest`'s sibling probe repointed each committed model's first rule at a newly added, unreferenced field; seven models answered `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` where the portable checker's reference family named its own class. Every row of `ErrorFieldReferenceReachLawsTest` had held the condition flat, so "the target is unreferenced" and "nothing iterates" were one thing across all of them — the constant no control inside a set can catch, and here the set was the whole file.

**The first transfer from those seven models was WRONG and is worth recording as the trap.** Reproducing them as "the condition reads a repetition" on our own carrier drew `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`, not the wildcard class: the seven models all read their repetition UNSTARRED, and the reproduction used a starred aggregate. A differential names a shape, never a mechanism.

Locked: `validate.laws.ErrorFieldReferenceReachLawsTest.aRepetitionReadPreEmptsTheUnreferencedTargetClass`. **Reported correctly by the portable checker since 2026-09-14** — `ERROR_FIELD_REFERENCE` now stays silent on an unstarred read past the target (`consistency.ErrorFieldReferenceTest.anUnstarredRepetitionReadPreEmptsTheClass`), which was a live wrong-class defect until the differential found it.


## §9 supplement — `MVK_NOT_IN_GROUP` needs the two groups to be INDEX-KEYED, which is why its reachability looked fixture-sensitive (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf349"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class reachability law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**[MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) records this class's reachability as fixture-sensitive with the reason unmeasured. The reason is joint iteration.** A `RepetitionNotUnique` key outside its `@From` scope is a containment violation, but A12 only *asks* about containment once the operands iterate together. Two repeatable groups that share an index field iterate JOINTLY; two that do not are an unpaired repetition, and A12 refuses at the wildcard gate first. So the same violation draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` on an index-free model and `MVK_NOT_IN_GROUP` on an index-keyed one — measured on one shape built both ways:

| the shape | index-free | index-keyed |
|---|---|---|
| key in a group PARALLEL to the `@From` scope | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NOT_IN_GROUP` |

**A rival mechanism was measured and refuted first, and it is the one the prior evidence suggested.** The single cell that had ever drawn this class put the rule INSIDE the key's own repeatable group, so "the rule's position decides it" fits that cell exactly. Reproducing that position on an index-free model still draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`, so position is not the variable — the prior fixture was index-keyed for unrelated reasons, and nothing recorded that this was load-bearing.

**What the scope admits, on the index-free carrier** (every violation there therefore reported as `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`, the gate in front of containment rather than a containment verdict): a key sitting directly in the scope is admitted, and so is a key in a DESCENDANT of it — confirming on a second carrier the boundary row that `@From`'s contribution covers the group and its subtree. A key ABOVE the scope, and a second key outside it, are both violations.

**`@From` must name a GROUP before it must name a REPEATABLE one, and the ordering is what a checker needs** *(extended 2026-09-14)*. Naming the rule's own non-repeatable root draws `MVK_GROUP_NOT_REPEATABLE` and no containment class at all — already held (§9, subscription carrier; pre-checked by `RepetitionNotUniqueCondition.from`), so that row confirms it on a second carrier rather than finding it. The two rows measured for the checker are the ones that fix what may be reported from:

| the scope names | class |
|---|---|
| a non-repeatable group that is **not** the root | `MVK_GROUP_NOT_REPEATABLE` — the repeatability class had only ever been measured on a root scope, so reporting it from `isRepeatable` alone was a transfer to an unrun carrier |
| a **FIELD** | `MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED` — the KIND gate runs first. Predicted `MVK_GROUP_NOT_REPEATABLE` and refuted: "not a repeatable group" is true of every field, so a family testing repeatability alone would have handed the author a fix for a different gate |

**The mechanism transfers to `MVK_NOT_IN_SAME_PATH`, measured rather than assumed.** The ledger carried the identical "fixture-sensitive, reason unmeasured" note for that class — two `RepetitionNotUnique` keys in parallel repeatable groups, no `@From` involved. It is a different class from a different check, so the transfer was predicted and then built on the same model both ways: index-free draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`, index-keyed draws `MVK_NOT_IN_SAME_PATH`. One mechanism therefore closes both of the ledger's unexplained-reachability notes.

Locked: `validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueFromScopeLawsTest`. **The containment classes stay unreported by the portable checker** — their reachability turns on parallel iteration, which no family models. **The scope's own demand is reported since 2026-09-14** as `REPETITION_SCOPE_GROUP` (`consistency.RepetitionScopeGroupTest`), which the condition reader had to be taught first: `CallOperand` now carries the clause-reduced `base` and `clauses` beside the deliberately narrow `path`, so a family can see a scope at all.

## §9 supplement — the root-only error-target iteration classes need THREE conditions, two of which were constants (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf348"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**A12 has to know WHICH repetition a violation attaches to, and it refuses when the condition has not said.** A rule whose condition reaches its error field only from ABOVE its own group, while also reading a repeating field, draws one of two classes — `MVK_ERROR_FIELDGROUP_ITERATION4_INVALID` when the read is in the error field's OWN group, `MVK_ERROR_FIELDGROUP_ITERATION5_INVALID` when it is under a repeatable group parallel to it. With both present the parallel class wins, measured in BOTH text orders because one order cannot tell that from "the later read wins" ([KF340](#kf340) shipped exactly that confusion two days earlier).

**PINNING is a conjunction, and neither half alone gives it**: a reference pins when it reaches the error field AND sits at or below the rule's own group. The root group reaches the target on every row and pins nothing; a sibling field sits below the rule's group and reaches nothing. Naming the rule's own group, or the error field itself, admits the rule however much else the condition reads.

**Three conditions carry the law and TWO of them were constant across the first grid**, which is the part worth carrying forward — each was found by the checker refusing a model A12 admits, not by reading the grid again:

| condition | how it was constant | the cell that exposed it |
|---|---|---|
| a reference must REACH the error field | every row carried `GroupFilled(/Shipment)` | a condition naming a SIBLING field instead draws `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` alone — that family's territory, not this one |
| the error field's group must REPEAT | both grids put the error field in a repeatable group | a flat model — nothing repeating anywhere — is ADMITTED, so there is no repetition to be unable to choose between |
| the reaching reference must sit ABOVE the rule's group | — (this one was varied deliberately) | the rule's OWN group is admitted, so "reached via the ROOT" is not what matters |

**The root's own repeatability is NOT the variable.** It was repeatable throughout the first grid, so "the reaching reference is the root" and "the reaching reference is itself an unpinned repetition" were indistinguishable; re-measured on a non-repeatable root, both classes fire exactly as before.

Locked: `validate.laws.RootOnlyErrorTargetIterationLawsTest`, across three carriers (repeatable root, fixed root, flat). Reported by the portable checker as `CheckFamily.ERROR_TARGET_ITERATION`; four mutants planted on its three conditions and its class selection, all killed.

## §9 supplement — what pre-empts `MVK_REPEATABLE_GROUP_MISSING` is a key OUTSIDE the rule group, and its carrier picks the class (measured, 2026-09-14) <a id="kf347"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a diagnostic-class selection law, not an evaluation behaviour.

**The law A12 enforces is a boundary, not a property of the key.** `RepetitionNotUnique` asks whether a repeating element takes the same key twice, so every key needs a repeatable group strictly BETWEEN the rule's own group and itself. Three structurally different shapes collapse onto the one class — a sole key in a non-repeatable group, a second key beside a good one, and the rule group sitting AT the repeated group rather than above it (both key spellings). [KF295](#kf295)'s row and the kernel's own corrective for the code both state the boundary; what had never been measured is what happens when it is violated *and* something else is wrong too.

**An OUTSIDE key pre-empts the class, and which class replaces it depends on the outsider's carrier.** Two readings fitted every row that existed — "a second key of any carrier pre-empts" and "only a key outside the rule group does" — and they disagree at exactly one cell, which is why it was built rather than inferred. Measured on one cart model, varying the rule group's position against the second key's carrier and holding the error field on the repeated group's own field (`rulekit.validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueKeyPathLawsTest`, kernel 30.8.1):

| rule group | second key's carrier | A12 |
|---|---|---|
| above the repeated group | none (sole key) | ADMITTED |
| above | the same repeated group | ADMITTED |
| above | a non-repeatable group, inside the rule group | `MVK_REPEATABLE_GROUP_MISSING` |
| above | a parallel REPEATABLE group, inside the rule group | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| AT the repeated group | none (sole key) | `MVK_REPEATABLE_GROUP_MISSING` |
| AT | the same repeated group | `MVK_REPEATABLE_GROUP_MISSING` |
| AT | a non-repeatable group, OUTSIDE the rule group | `MVK_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP` |
| AT | a parallel repeatable group, OUTSIDE the rule group | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |

**`MVK_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP` is the discriminating cell and had no evidence anywhere in the estate before it.** It is what makes the second reading the right one: being a second key is not what pre-empts, being outside the rule group is — and the outsider's own carrier then decides between the two replacement classes. A checker built from the collapse alone reports `MVK_REPEATABLE_GROUP_MISSING` on both outside rows, where A12 draws neither.

**DEPTH does not enter it, and one of the two depth rows is the one a naive implementation passes.** A repeatable group two levels above the key suppresses the class exactly as a direct parent does, and a non-repeatable group at any depth draws it — so the test is "a repeatable group anywhere on the path between", never "the key's own parent is repeatable". The two-level row exists because the one-level row cannot tell those apart: it was added after a mutant reading only the parent survived the grid.

**The multiplicity is ONE finding per call.** Two keys each lacking a repetition draw a single class, so it is a verdict on the call rather than on a key.

Locked: `validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueKeyPathLawsTest` (23 rows, the twelve pre-existing ones re-run unchanged after the fixture gained its depth carriers, which is what makes them evidence the extension is inert). Reported by the portable checker as `CheckFamily.REPETITION_KEY_PLACEMENT`, which stays silent on every pre-empted row.

## §13 supplement — a rule reports every SLOT defect, and `RULE_HAS_NO_ERRORTEXT`'s split is enumerated (measured, 2026-09-13) <a id="kf346"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — the checker's examination order, not an evaluation behaviour.

**The sixth and last member of the defect-pairing pass.** A rule's own slots are separate members with no order between them, so the only question is whether one withholds another — and none does:

| the rule's slots | A12 |
|---|---|
| all sound — the control | ADMITTED |
| a reserved `vk_vk` name | `MVK_RULE_NAME_INVALID` |
| a blank `errorCode` | `MVK_ERROR_CODE_MISSING` |
| no `errorMessage` | `MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` + `RULE_HAS_NO_ERRORTEXT` |
| any pair of those | both classes |
| all three | **all four classes** |

**`severity` is not in that grid, because an unknown spelling is a TIER and not a class.** It makes the source UNREADABLE, and takes every other slot's verdict with it — so a row pairing it with another defect would be varying buildability rather than the member.

**The `RULE_HAS_NO_ERRORTEXT` split is now enumerated, and it has exactly one exception.** [KF323](#kf323) had measured two shapes, one on each side, and left the rule unknown. Every shape that leaves a declared locale uncovered draws BOTH classes — no `errorMessage` member, an empty array, an empty text, a text only for an undeclared locale, an empty message locale code, a filled entry replaced by a blank one — **except** a text that is whitespace rather than empty, which draws the prefixed class alone.

**The exception is over the DECLARED LOCALES, not over the texts present**, which only a two-locale model can show:

| two declared locales | A12 |
|---|---|
| one empty text, one whitespace | both classes |
| **both texts whitespace** | **`MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING` alone** |
| one whitespace, the other locale ABSENT | both classes |

So "every collected text is whitespace" fits every single-locale row and is false on the last one. Measured on the computation carrier too, because the class is spelled `RULE_HAS_NO_ERRORTEXT` and reads as a rule's: a computation behaves identically.

**And a model with no usable declared locale draws neither class**: an empty `header.locales`, a code A12's reader refuses, and the empty code all leave it unbuildable or unreadable, so no verdict about the message exists at all.

Reported by the portable checker, which emitted the prefixed class alone on the stated ground that the split was unmeasured — an under-report on every shape but one.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.RuleSlotMultipleDefectLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency … DeclarationSlotTest`.

## §8 supplement — the table-enum condition family: one gate every model reaches, closed as unreachable on an inverted reading (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf422"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a reachability correction plus the gate order behind it.

[MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) carried six codes of `ValueNotConsistent` on one sentence — table-backed enums are not DM-JSON-serializable, so the construct is un-buildable, [KF366](#kf366) — and the sentence is right about five of them and **inverted on the sixth**. `CheckFieldAndValueListConditionImpl.check` asks `checkField` first, and that call ends in `CheckEntityUtils.checkEnumWithTableReference`, which raises `MVK_TABLE_ENUM_EXPECTED` when the subject is **not** a table enum. The absence of a table enum is therefore not what makes that code unreachable; it is exactly what fires it.

| the subject of `ValueNotConsistent(<subject> To <values>)` | verdict |
|---|---|
| an ordinary enumeration field | `MVK_TABLE_ENUM_EXPECTED` |
| a string field, a number field | `MVK_TABLE_ENUM_EXPECTED` |
| a group | `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` |
| a repetition-list selector | `MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED` |
| a path naming nothing declared | `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` |
| an ordinary enum with two value-list members, or with a FIELD member | `MVK_TABLE_ENUM_EXPECTED` |
| another operator on the same subject — the control | ADMITTED |

**The last two rows are what make this a gate and not a kind law.** The arity gate (`MVK_DEPENDENT_COLUMN_SIZE_MISMATCH`) and the member-kind gate (`MVK_ONLY_ENUMS_ALLOWED`) are both written *after* `checkField` returns, so neither a wrong member count nor a non-enum member is visible: the table-enum demand answers first in both. The subject's own kind never matters either — a string, a number and an enumeration draw one class.

**The five behind it stay closed, and for a reason the sixth never had.** `MVK_DEPENDENT_COLUMN_SIZE_MISMATCH` and `MVK_ONLY_ENUMS_ALLOWED` sit below `checkField`; `MVK_STRING_VALUE_NOT_IN_COLUMN` and `MVK_ENUM_VALUES_NOT_IN_COLUMN` sit inside `enumType.getTable().ifPresent(…)` below that — so all four need the stored table enum [KF366](#kf366) measured A12's own READER refusing. `MVK_INVALID_TABLE_ENUM` is the mirror image. *Corrected 2026-09-19: this sentence went on to claim it "carries a second, independent reason: its sole raiser is `CheckEntityUtils.checkNoTableEnum`, which no site in the 30.8.1 checkout calls" — and `CheckFeldOpImpl:105` calls it, in the live `FELD_WERT_ALS_ZAHL` switch case, so the raiser is reached whenever a condition applies field-value-as-number to a field. The second reason is withdrawn; [KF366](#kf366)'s serializability argument still closes the row on its own.* **The correction matters most for what it says about this entry's own closing paragraph.** That paragraph names the defect class — a search grouped six codes and one member was read for all six — and this sentence then committed a fresh instance of it one clause later: a call-site absence asserted over a 1821-file checkout without the enumeration that a negative existential needs. Diagnosing a class does not inoculate the diagnosis, and the grep that refutes it is the same one the paragraph recommends.

**The defect class is the one the oracle table names: a search grouped six codes and one member was read for all six.** Every row said "same §8 fact", and five of them were right — the sixth is the one whose predicate runs the other way, and no amount of re-reading the five would have shown it. Reading the FIRING SITE per code, rather than the ledger's own grouping, is what separated them.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.TABLE_ENUM_OPERAND`), which emits all three reachable classes in the kernel's own order.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.TableEnumConditionLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.TableEnumOperandTest`.

## §10 supplement — the four-parameter split-year `Date` is not an H-model shape, and one of its laws is live in A12 (source-verified + measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf423"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a reachability correction plus the slot law it exposes.

[MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md) carried `MVK_EXTRACT_OP_NOT_ALLOWED_4_DATE_CONSTRUCT_WITH_4_PARAMS` as "the four-parameter (split-year) date construction is an H-model shape — legacy-only". The grammar carries no such restriction: `datumKonstrukt: 'Datum' '(' dp1 ',' dp2 (',' dp3 (',' dp4)? )? ')'` is un-predicated, and `CheckDatumKonstruktImpl.checkYearFormat(century, shortYear)` routes a `datumExtractOp` in either year slot to `handleDatumExtractOpAtYearParam` with no `isHModel()` gate anywhere on the path.

| the `Date` construction, on an `en_US` model | A12 |
|---|---|
| `Date("01", "02", "20", "24")` — century and short year as constants | ADMITTED |
| `Date("01", "02", YearFromDate(TravelDate), "24")` | `MVK_EXTRACT_OP_NOT_ALLOWED_4_DATE_CONSTRUCT_WITH_4_PARAMS` |
| `Date("01", "02", "20", YearFromDate(TravelDate))` | the same |
| `Date("01", "02", YearFromDate(TravelDate))` — the same op in the THREE-parameter year slot | **ADMITTED** |
| `Date("01", "02", "17", "24")` — a century outside 18..22 | `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` |

**The third and fourth rows are the pair that makes this a SPLIT-YEAR law rather than a year-slot one.** The identical operator in the identical position of the three-parameter form is admitted, so what forbids it is the presence of the fourth parameter, not the operator and not the year.

**The last row was predicted as the constant class and is not.** An out-of-range century draws the comparison's format class instead, so the split-year pair's own constant bounds are not what answers — which is why the portable checker reports only the extract law of that pair and leaves its constant and entity arms alone.

**The defect class is the third of its kind in one day, and they share a shape: an unmeasured "legacy-only" basis.** [KF282](#kf282) corrected one by moving the condition LANGUAGE; [KF422](#kf422) corrected one whose predicate ran the opposite way; this one needed only the grammar production read for a predicate that is not there. A disposition whose whole basis is the word "legacy" has not been measured, and the cheapest test is to look for the gate that is supposed to make it legacy.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.DATE_CONSTRUCTION_SLOTS`, whose KDoc had carried the same wrong claim).

## §11 supplement — which class an unstarred aggregate operand draws is decided by whether the RULE iterates (measured, 2026-09-15) <a id="kf424"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — it corrects a published silence whose stated basis was a constant of the grid that measured it.

[KF358](#kf358) recorded that a plainly unstarred field operand under a `Having` filter is `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` and never `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED`, "A12's iteration gate outruns this chain". The measurement was right and the claim was too wide: every row of that grid sat on a rule whose error field is outside every repetition, so "does not iterate" was a constant of the set rather than one of its variables. Moving it splits the row in two.

| the operand, on an aggregate | rule does NOT iterate | rule ITERATES |
|---|---|---|
| unstarred, with a `Having` filter | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED` |
| unstarred, no filter | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN` |
| starred, with a filter — the control | ADMITTED | ADMITTED |

All four cells REJECT, so the axis chooses which gate answers rather than whether one does. Off an iteration the unstarred read crosses a repetition the rule does not sit in and the reference gate answers for both columns; on an iterating rule that gate is satisfied — the read is a legal per-row one — and what remains is the aggregate having a single value to aggregate, reported by the filter's star demand where there is a filter and by the operator's arity gate where there is not.

**The filter's class is not the iterating column's own.** A NON-repeating operand with a filter draws `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED` off an iteration too — there being no repetition for the reference gate to object to first — which is what keeps the account above a reading rather than a restatement of the table. It also means a filtered lone field never reaches its operator's arity gate at all, on any carrier.

**A third iteration carrier exists and a containment test cannot see it.** A level the target iterates JOINTLY with — parallel, both ends keyed on an index field of the same name and type — satisfies the iteration gate exactly as a contained one does, and the unstarred filtered operand there draws `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED`. Measured on its own fixture rather than transferred, with a sibling keyed on another name as the control (`MVK_ERROR_FIELD_INVALID_INDEX`).

**How the defect was found is the reusable part.** The differential lane had the checker silent on seven rejected mutants, all `MVK_WILDCARDS_REQUIRED`; reproducing the shape on the shared order fixture produced `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` instead, and that disagreement — not a source read — is what exposed the unnamed constant. A silence pinned BY CLASS is what made the seven visible as one shape; the count they replaced said only that a gap existed.

**The OUTER MARKER silenced the same walk for the same reason, one step further out.** `$` binds the enclosing iteration for a filter BODY's references, so a condition carrying one carries it there — and the scope family read its presence as a reason to skip the whole text, discarding the rule's own unstarred reads along with it. Reading the condition with its filter bodies removed settles both: the body goes to the family that owns it, the marker goes with the body, and what surrounds them is judged normally. Two mirror rows that had DISCLOSED this under-report in their own comments gained the class.

**The last class needed TWO facts, and having only the first made the report worse.** Removing the same filter leaves from `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED`'s iteration pre-emption is correct on its own and still wrong in the report: A12 answers a filtered PARALLEL operand with `MVK_PARALLEL_ITERATION_FOR_FILTERED_ENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED` ahead of the not-referenced gate, so the family named a wrong class beside a right one until it yielded to that gate. The order was already kernel-locked — a laws row measuring exactly this pair, on a rule whose error field is unreferenced — and nobody had connected it to the silence it explained. A correction that is right in isolation can still be a regression, and only the second fact says which.

**What it adds up to: the checker names an A12 class for every one of the 116 rejected mutants, at the declaration A12 named it about.** The differential's pinned silence went 16 → 9 → 7 → 3 → 0 in one sitting, and no new family was written to do it — every class was one the checker already stated somewhere, reached by a shape an existing family did not read.

**Then the lane's POPULATION was widened at the same axis, and that is the more transferable half.** Its mutation that repoints a rule's error field only ever pointed OUT of a repetition, so every mutant it had ever produced sat on a non-iterating rule — the very carrier this finding is about was unreachable by construction, which is why both of the day's near-over-reports were caught by family mirrors instead. A kind that repoints INTO a repetition took the population from 98 to 116 and immediately found two more silences, each a PARALLEL level the target iterates jointly with, invisible to a containment test. **A pinned silence is only as good as the shapes its population can build**, and widening the population is cheaper than widening any family.

**The same fact one layer down was a defect in a SHARED reader, and no mutant pointed at it.** `addressedTargetOf` — the gate nine families ask before judging an operand — asked whether the DECLARING group sits in each repetition the reference crosses, where A12 asks whether the TARGET's coordinates address it. The two agree on every rule whose error field sits beside it and part company on exactly the iterating rules above, so all nine families were yielding on operands A12 admits. Fixing the one helper closed the differential's remaining `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN` silences as a side effect: the lane's pinned silence went 16 → 9 → **7 of 98** in one sitting, and the second step was bought by a helper none of the pinned classes named.

**THREE readers were keyed on the declaring group, and the third needed its own row because no grid had built the carrier.** Every carrier that had measured the filter's iteration gate declares its rule in the error field's own group, which makes "the DECLARING group's iteration addresses the level" and "the TARGET's coordinates address it" the same sentence — so the question was never posed. Posing it settles it outright: a rule declared at the root but reporting one level down inside a repetition iterates it, and an operand that crosses that level unstarred goes from `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` to ADMITTED with its filter then judged on its own merits, the error field being the only thing that moved.

| the rule, operand starring only the inner level | A12 |
|---|---|
| declared at the root, reporting at the root | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| declared at the root, reporting INSIDE the repetition, in-scope filter | ADMITTED |
| the same, filter leaf off the operand's path | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` |

The third row is what makes the second a measurement rather than a coincidence: the operand is reached, so the filter's own gate is what answers.

**The class is swept, not merely fixed three times.** `grep -rn 'iteratedLevels(' consistency/src/commonMain` returns five sites and all five were read: its own definition, the three corrected here, and two that ask a DIFFERENT question correctly — `SemanticIndexKey` already compares against the target's group, and `FilterBodyGates`' body walk compares against the FILTERED entity, which is right because a filter body's references are judged against it rather than against the rule's target.

Reported by the portable checker (`CheckFamily.FILTERED_OPERAND_KIND`, which now asks the iteration walk instead of the star; `OPERAND_REPETITION_SCOPE` gained the filtered operand's base, `ENTITY_LIST_ARITY` yields on any filtered operand, `ERROR_FIELD_REFERENCE` exempts a jointly iterated level, and the shared `addressedTargetOf` and `FILTER_BODY_GATES` key on the declaration's iteration).

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.AggregateSlotLawsTest` and `…HavingFilterIterationGateLawsTest`, mirrored by `consistency.AggregateOperandIterationTest` and `consistency.FilterBodyGatesTest`.

## §12 supplement — `checkConsistency` runs the CODEGEN tier's checks, so `NoMetaModelCheckErrorType` is consistency-reachable (measured + source-read, 2026-09-16) <a id="kf425"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — it corrects a scope boundary that excluded 26 classes from a coverage denominator.

[MVK-LEDGER](MVK-LEDGER.md)'s scope note puts `NoMetaModelCheckErrorType` (`kernel-tool/kernel-core-codegen`) outside the ledger, and the natural reading of a type in a *codegen* module is that its 26 classes arise when code is generated rather than when a model is checked. They do not. An unparseable `modelConfig.timeZone` draws `MVK_INVALID_TIME_ZONE` from `checkConsistency` itself, with the same model at `Europe/Berlin` admitted as the within-model control.

**One reachable class settles the whole tier, which is why this is one row rather than 26.** `NoMetaModelChecks` exposes exactly one public entry point — `check()`, constructed over `CodeGenData` — and raises all 26 classes from private methods beneath it (source-read, kernel `30.8.1`). So the question was never per class; it was whether that single door opens on the consistency path, and it does. `check()` also runs its checks in two batches with an early return between them, the name/package/language/character-set/dynamic-enum/time-zone batch gating the enum-table, index-field and sort-field batch — source-read, and *not* asserted here as a pre-emption law, since no model was built to defeat the other reading.

The tier's reachability was in fact already pinned once, indirectly: `GroupIndexAndSortReferenceLawsTest` expects `MVK_INVALID_INDEX_FIELD` — also a `NoMetaModelCheckErrorType` member — from the real Kernel, with a no-semantic-index control. Nobody had read that row as a statement about the tier, which is how a 26-class denominator stayed excluded while one of its members was already locked.

**Consequence for the portable checker**, tracked in [the coverage-residue record](archived/PORTABLE-CONSISTENCY-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md#coverage-residue): 7 of the 26 are reported by `:consistency`, so the remaining 19 are each a candidate route to a false pass. Measured on the witness above — A12 reports `MVK_INVALID_TIME_ZONE`, the portable engine returns INCONCLUSIVE with zero findings. That is honest under the current contract, which cannot emit VALID at all; it is exactly the row that would become a false VALID if that bar were lifted before these 19 are dispositioned.

*Locked by:* `rulekit.validate.laws.CodegenTierReachedByCheckConsistencyLawsTest`.
