## §8 supplement — the value-list quantifier's kind gate is one class over seven kinds, SHAPE-BLIND, with NUMBER inside the admitted set (measured 2026-09-22) <a id="kf453"></a>

> Fold: pending — belongs in §8 beside the scalar value-list gates ([KF109](#kf109)).

**Why §8 when the operator's other findings are §9.** [KF187](#kf187), [KF258](#kf258) and [KF278](#kf278) name the same operator and sit in §9 because their subject is the entity-list SHAPE — group operands, starred references, arity — which is repetition's business. This entry's subject is which field KINDS the slot admits, which is [KF109](#kf109)'s question one carrier over. The `§` is a section-class hint rather than an address, so one operator legitimately appears under both; a reader arriving from the operator index should expect that rather than read it as a misfile.

The carrier throughout is the quantifier `AtLeastOneFieldValueIncludedInValueList`; its scalar twin `FieldValueIncludedInValueList` appears only in the asymmetry row at the end.

**The whole table below holds at a BOUND level only** — a non-repeatable group, or a repeatable one that is starred. See the scope-gate amendment at the end of this entry before implementing it; a checker that applies the table unqualified reports this gate's class where the kernel reports `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`.

Each kind measured in **three slot shapes** — a homogeneous group, the same two fields listed out, and a sole field of that kind — against one String literal list:

| slot kind | all three shapes |
|---|---|
| STRING — the control | admitted |
| DATE · TIME · DATETIME · DATEFRAGMENT · DATERANGE · BOOLEAN · CONFIRM | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` |
| NUMBER, against those same String literals | `MVK_INVALID_TYPES_FOR_COMPARISON` |
| NUMBER, against a number FIELD · ENUM, against its own member | admitted |
| CUSTOM, against String literals | admitted |

**Amended 2026-09-22 (same day): the ADMITTED set has four members, not the three the diagnostic names.** A CUSTOM field is admitted in all three shapes although `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` lists only String, Enumeration and Number. *(Mechanism, source-read at the PARSER layer and corrected the same day: the gate expands the operand and applies `FieldUtils.isStringEnumOrNumber` per expanded field — `CheckEntityListenUtils.java:614-616` — and that is `isEnum(f) || isLikeString(f) || isNumber(f)`, where `isLikeString(f)` is `t instanceof IStringType || t instanceof IPredefinedType`, `FieldUtils.java:188-191,284-286`. So CUSTOM enters through `isLikeString`'s SECOND DISJUNCT, as a predefined type. It does not "share the string's base type", which this entry first said: that phrasing belongs to a different site, the base-type map the `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED` gate reads. Both facts are true and fusing them named neither file nor layer.)* The refused denominator above is therefore the complement of FOUR kinds over `ValueKind`'s eleven authorable members, which is what makes it a closed statement rather than a list of seven. The first cut of this entry measured ten of the eleven and inferred completeness from the code's name; CUSTOM was the unmeasured one, and the scalar carrier's own row ([KF109](#kf109), `ScalarValueListGateLawsTest`) had already recorded the same admission. **Our kit is over-strict here:** its kind-typed literal overloads take a String or an Enum slot, so a CUSTOM slot has no typed spelling although the kernel admits it — unlike the seven refused kinds, where the erasure and the kernel agree.

The gate does not read the slot's shape: a group is expanded and its expansion judged, so all three spellings of one kind draw the identical class. **NUMBER is the separator, not an eighth refusal** — every refused row pairs a slot against String literals, so "the slot disagrees with the literals" predicts the whole refused half equally well; the Number rows clear this gate against those same literals and are refused one gate later, which no account keyed on disagreement can produce. The four temporal kinds and DATERANGE are each measured rather than transferred from DATE: the gate reads three POSITIVE predicates, so its refused half is a complement. Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-22-03`.

**A carrier asymmetry found while building the positive control.** The QUANTIFIER's value list admits no number literal at all — after `In`, a bare `1` is read as a PATH (`MVK_INVALID_ENTITY`) and `1.00` does not survive the parser (`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`) — while the SCALAR twin takes `FieldValueIncludedInValueList(Assessed, 1, 2)` in the same model. Invisible from either carrier alone, and the reason the admitted Number control has to be field-valued.

**Amended 2026-09-22 (cold review of this entry's own slice): a SCOPE gate outranks the kind gate, so the table above is a claim about a BOUND level and says nothing about an unbound one.** `Visits` and `Dates` are the same shape — two DATE fields spelled `yyyy-MM-dd` — and differ in exactly one builder call:

| slot | verdict |
|---|---|
| `AtLeastOneFieldValueIncludedInValueList(Visits In "x","y")` — repeatable, unstarred | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| the same two fields listed out, unstarred | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| a sole field of it, unstarred | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| `AtLeastOneFieldValueIncludedInValueList(Visits* In "x","y")` — starred | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` |
| `AtLeastOneFieldValueIncludedInValueList(Dates In "x","y")` — non-repeatable, the control | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_ALLOWED` |

Shape-blindness survives — all three spellings agree at each scope — but it is now measured at BOTH scopes rather than one. Starring binds the level, the scope gate falls silent, and the kind gate answers; unstarred, the kind gate is never reached and no kind is refused for its kind.

**Why the first cut could not see it, which is the transferable part.** All twelve groups in the fixture were non-repeatable and the entry never named that, so `repeatable` was a constant across every row — the account fitted all of them and was false outside the set. This is [KF242](#kf242)'s shape a second time, and the remedy both entries point at is the same: a within-model 2×2 that varies one builder call, which cannot borrow a constant the way two separate carriers can. The unqualified row had already been carried into a12-kernel-lean's `spec/06 §B.3` and was corrected there on the same day. Sharpest detail for anyone reading this as a retrieval problem rather than a knowledge one: `ConstantGateImmediacyLawsTest`, written in the same session, already identifies `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` as a gate asked earlier.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.ValueListSlotShapeBlindnessLawsTest`; the scalar carrier's own field-slot denominator stays with `ScalarValueListGateLawsTest`.)*

> Fold: pending — belongs in §12's full-vs-partial account.

Two rules identical in guard, error field, group, comparison operator and threshold, differing only in the operand left of `> 1`, on a two-row `/Src/Rows`:

| coverage | `CurrentRepetition(/Src/Rows) > 1` | `[Level] > 1` |
|---|---|---|
| full validation | fires, second row | fires, both rows |
| the error field, every row | fires, second row — as full | silent |

A relevant set cannot drive `CurrentRepetition(G)` to UNKNOWN, because it answers from the iterated row rather than from a cell. **The error-field gate is independent of this and still runs first, per row** — a coverage naming only the other field skips the coordinate-reading rule too, although the coordinate needed no coverage at all — so the correct reading is "not masked", never "always evaluated". ## §8 supplement — the built-in custom-field-type error keys are a CLOSED set of 14, and the two date types split the key while sharing one message member (kernel SOURCE, 2026-09-22) <a id="kf455"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends the custom-extensibility surface; folds into §8 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

**The denominator is the class, not a survey.** `CustomFieldTypeErrorKeys` (`kernel-core-customfieldtype-impl`, `…impl.internal.error`) is `public final` and holds nothing but `public static final String` constants, so reading it out *is* the complete set rather than a sample of one. At our pin (30.8.1) it holds **exactly 14**, enumerated here so a later reader can check the claim instead of trusting it:

| key constant | wire value | note |
|---|---|---|
| `UNGUELTIGE_ID_NUMMER` | `ungueltigeIDNummer` | |
| `TEST_ID_NUMMER` | `testIDNummer` | `@Deprecated(since = "30.6.0", forRemoval = true)` — the `A12K-3589` removal surface |
| `UNGUELTIGE_STNR` | `ungueltigeSteuernummer` | |
| `UNGUELTIGES_EWAZ` | `ungueltigesEinheitswertAktenzeichen` | |
| `UNGUELTIGE_BUFANR` | `ungueltigeBundesfinanzamtsnummer` | |
| `UNGUELTIGES_LAENDERKUERZEL` | `ungueltigesLaenderkuerzel` | |
| `UNGUELTIGE_IBAN` | `ungueltigeIBAN` | |
| `UNGUELTIGE_BIC` | `ungueltigeBIC` | |
| `UNGUELTIGES_DATUM_MMJJ` | `ungueltigesDatumMMJJ` | |
| `UNGUELTIGES_DATUM_TTMMJJ` | `ungueltigesDatumTTMMJJ` | |
| `UNGUELTIGE_BUSTNR` | `ungueltigeBundessteuernummer` | |
| `UNGUELTIGER_BICINTERNATIONAL` | `ungueltigerBICinternational` | |
| `UNGUELTIGE_IBANINTERNATIONAL` | `ungueltigeIBANinternational` | |
| `UNGUELTIGES_STRAFAZ` | `ungueltigesStrafAktenzeichen` | |

So **13 live keys plus one deprecated**, and the deprecated one is the only member whose disappearance is already scheduled — worth stating separately, because "14" and "13" are both true answers to different questions and a bare count invites the wrong one.

**The two date types split the KEY and share the MESSAGE member, so only the key separates them in every locale.** `DatumMMJJVerifier` and `DatumTTMMJJVerifier` both extend the abstract `DatumVerifier`, and each supplies its own `getErrorKey()` (`UNGUELTIGES_DATUM_MMJJ` / `UNGUELTIGES_DATUM_TTMMJJ`). But `DatumVerifier.checkDatum` returns a single member for every failure path, `CustomFieldTypeErrorEnum.DATUM_UNGUELTIG`, and the format only reaches the rendered message by **literal substitution** — `errorMsg.replace("<dateFormat>", getFormatFuerFehlermeldung())` — rather than through a parameter slot. A consumer that keys on the error KEY can therefore tell the two apart; one that keys on the message member cannot.

**Corrected 2026-09-22 — the "cannot tell them apart from the text" half was wrong, and locale-conditionally so.** a12-kernel-lean challenged it the day it was written; re-reading the five shipped catalogs of `kernel-core-customfieldtype-impl` at our pin confirms them, so the correction rests on our own read of `internal/custom_field_types/error_messages*.properties` rather than on their report. The substitution exists precisely so the message names the format, and the two subtypes return **different** names — `DatumMMJJVerifier` `"MM.JJ"`, `DatumTTMMJJVerifier` `"TT.MM.JJ"` — so wherever the token is present the two render **differently**. Whether it is present is the catalog's business and is not uniform: `error_messages_en` and `error_messages_nl` carry `<dateFormat>` (English: `Invalid date: The date must be in the format <dateFormat>.`); the no-locale `error_messages.properties` carries the key WITHOUT the token (`Kein Fehler definiert!`); and `error_messages_de` / `error_messages_fr` omit `DATUM_UNGUELTIG` entirely, resolving to that default by ordinary `ResourceBundle` parent fallback. So the text distinguishes them under two of the five and not under three, and **neither unconditional reading is safe — the surfaced code is the only locale-independent axis.** The original clause is the register CLAUDE.md's oracle table calls *scope transfer*: the mechanism (one shared member, substitution not parameterization) was read correctly and its consequence was asserted on a carrier — the catalog — that was never opened.

**Basis, stated so it is not read as stronger than it is.** This is a SOURCE read of the consult-only `../a12-kernel` checkout at our pin — the class inventory above and the single `validate`/`checkDatum` pair — and it is **not** locked by a test here: `CustomFieldTypeErrorKeys` sits in an `internal` package of `kernel-core-customfieldtype-impl`, and only `kernel-core-customfieldtype-api` is on our classpath, so a reflective denominator lock would mean taking a dependency on kernel internals. The completeness claim needs no runtime (a closed final class is settled by reading it); the substitution mechanism is a local source read and has **not** been confirmed to manifest through the full validation path, which per DOC-DISCIPLINE keeps that half a source-read claim rather than a measured one.

*(a12-kernel-lean's report that the German and international IBAN validators carry disjoint keys, and that the international one lacks a country-code key, is THEIR measurement and is deliberately not restated as ours — the key table above is what we read.)*

## §3 supplement — the kernel READS an over-capacity document and refuses to WRITE it, so the same excess is two ordinary messages on one path and a raise on the other (probe differential, both strategies, 2026-09-22) <a id="kf456"></a>

> Fold: pending — sharpens §3's structural over-repetition error with its write-side counterpart; folds into §3 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

**The asymmetry, measured on one document.** A document carrying four `Order/Legs` rows against a declared maximum of three deserializes without complaint, validates, and reports the excess as two ordinary `ERROR`/`VALUE_ERROR` messages — `zuGrosseKontextnummer@Order/Legs[4]/Distance` and `zuGrosseZeile@Order/Legs[4]`. Serializing it back out does not: `IDocumentComputationResult.applyTo`'s copy raises `DocumentSerializationException: Following errors were found:\nMax repetition exceeded: Order/Legs[0] (got 4 but max repetition is 3)`. So the **read** path treats over-capacity as a reportable document defect and the **write** path treats it as an unrepresentable one, and a caller meets whichever the entry point it chose happens to use.

**The two paths do not even address it the same way.** The validator names the offending ROW (`Legs[4]`) and the field read inside it; the serializer names the LIST (`Legs[0]`) and the count it found. One condition, two vocabularies — so a consumer joining the message channel to a serialization failure on an address will not match them, and the `[0]` is a list address rather than a row that is over the limit.

**Both kernel strategies agree**, so this is a kernel property and not a codegen split: `kernel-groovy-dynamic` and `kernel-java-static` produce the identical messages on the read side and the identical raise on the write side (`enginesAgree` is true on both runs).

*Locked by:* `adapter.laws.KernelProbeOverCapacityFaultTest.anOverCapacityDocumentValidatesButItsAppliedCopyCannotBeSerialized`, which pins both codes with their addresses and the raise text verbatim, on both strategies. Reached through `computeResults`, whose applied-document channel is the only observable that exercises the write path.

**Why it was measured.** a12-kernel-lean reported the symptom on 2026-09-22 against `2304a6849` — their measurement, re-run here rather than cited. It also exposed a defect on our side rather than the kernel's: the probe used to let the `computeResults` raise discard the validation messages the same row returns without it, breaking the guarantee `observe` advertises. Fixed in the same change; the contract and its enforcement locus are [KERNEL-PROBE-SPEC](KERNEL-PROBE-SPEC.md) §3.

**A SECOND CARRIER, independently measured — their report, not a pin of ours (2026-09-22).** a12-kernel-lean holds the same asymmetry at their own `src-applied-document-over-limit-unobservable`, measured on a `Rows` group under `max 3` rather than our `Order/Legs`, with an at-capacity control in the same request and the same result on both strategies. Two genuinely different carriers is what a scope-transfer claim needs, and neither of us took it from the other. They classify it as an **observability boundary rather than a behavioural clause** — it says what a serializer-based route cannot observe, not what the engine decides — which is why it is not a rule in their `spec/` and why no letter was sent for it.

They also reproduced the ADDRESS disagreement above on their carrier: their retained fault chain spells `Rows[0]` on both strategies while the same document's over-limit findings index the fourth row.

**The `[0]` means the LIST, and that needed its own case, because both carriers shared a constant.** Our row and theirs each put the excess at exactly one row past the maximum, at the end of the list — so across two independent carriers "the serializer names index 0" and "it names the first offending row, which happened to render as 0" stayed indistinguishable. A document over capacity by **two** separates them, and it does: five rows against `max 3` gives `Max repetition exceeded: Order/Legs[0] (got 5 but max repetition is 3)` — the index is fixed at `[0]` while only the count tracks the excess. So the serializer's address carries no information about which row offends, which is the sharper form of the mismatch above. Locked by `…KernelProbeOverCapacityFaultTest.theSerializerNamesTheListRatherThanAnyOffendingRow`.

## §6 supplement — `Min`/`Max`'s bracketed spelling takes the extrema's full kind grid, and `Abs` answers one code for all of it (probe, 2026-09-22) <a id="kf457"></a>

> Fold: pending — carries [KF263](#kf263)'s declared-kind grid, measured on the field-list `MinValue`/`MaxValue`, to the bracketed operand-list spelling; folds with KF263 beside [KF226](#kf226).

**What was already held, and what this adds.** [KF249](#kf249) locked the position law — the FIRST operand fixes the class, and the code names that class rather than the offender's — on all four extrema, bracketed `Min([…])`/`Max([…])` included, but on the NUMBER/DATE pair only. [KF263](#kf263) completed the grid on the field-list spelling alone. This entry measures the rest of it on the bracketed spelling, which is the one rulekit's `OpListMath` refuses client-side: TIME and DATE_TIME against each other and against DATE, the non-sortable kinds in both positions, a homogeneous DATE_RANGE pair, and DATE_FRAGMENT on both sides of the component-set line. Every cell agrees with KF263's table, so the two spellings are one gate — measured now, where before it was an assumption. The grid is measured on `Min`, and ten of its cells again on `Max`, which answers each identically:

| the FIRST operand is… | and the disagreeing one is… | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| NUMBER, DATE, TIME or DATE_TIME | the same kind (homogeneous) | ADMITTED |
| temporal (DATE · TIME · DATE_TIME) | temporal, with another component set | `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` |
| temporal | non-temporal (NUMBER · STRING · …) | `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` |
| non-temporal (NUMBER · STRING · BOOLEAN · ENUMERATION · DATE_RANGE) | anything at all, temporal included — and a DATE_RANGE even beside another | `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` |

The component set is the axis, not the kind, exactly as KF263's 2×2 has it: a DATE_FRAGMENT `yyyy-MM-dd` beside a plain DATE is ADMITTED in both positions, and a DATE_FRAGMENT `yyyy-MM` is `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` in both.

**`Abs`, the one-operand sibling, does not split — the position law seen from the other side.** With a single operand there is no head to compare anything against, so every kind it turns away draws one code, `MVK_NO_NUMBER`: STRING, BOOLEAN, ENUMERATION and all three temporal kinds, measured on the same carrier with NUMBER as the admitted control. It is the expression form of the demand [KF395](#kf395) measured on the field-valued `AbsValue`.

**The first version of this entry, and of rulekit's gate, cited `MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE` for a NUMBER head beside a temporal operand — the cell KF249 had measured as `MVK_NOT_SORTABLE` on this very operator seventeen days earlier, and which our catalog's `Min` corrective states.** The grid was built from a fresh probe without first searching our own findings or the catalog for the operator, and every temporal row in it led with the temporal operand, so "the first operand decides" and "either operand decides" were indistinguishable inside it. A cold review caught it. The prior art was not narrower than the question, which is the usual way a record misleads; it was exact, and it was never opened.

**Three fixture traps, each presenting as kernel behaviour.** The project fixture's `Date` is a `StringType`, so "a date field" measured §10's keyword quoting (`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`). A DATE_TIME format needs its quoted `'T'` — `dd.MM.yyyy HH:mm:ss` is refused at declaration and leaves two codeless field errors on every row, which then read as ADMITTED. And `dateField(…).format("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss")` declares a `DateType`, so the first "DATE_TIME" control was a second DATE control; `dateTimeField` exists and was missed by a grep, `[a-z]+Field\(`, that cannot match its capital letter — an absence reported from a pattern that could never match. When a grid's fixture is broken its rows do not fail, they go quiet.

**Lock:** `rulekit.validate.laws.OpListMathKindGateLawsTest` pins the kernel grid and the `Abs` row, and pins rulekit's refusal codes against them in both directions. The catalog's `Min`, `Max` and `Abs` entries carry the three codes as correctives, each CI-executed to its code with a kernel-accepted repair. It also pins where rulekit under-reports, which is safe and is written down because the opposite direction would not be: `OpListMath` compares declared KINDS where the kernel compares COMPONENT SETS, so the gate goes quiet on every cell where the two disagree. Two are measured — a `DateType` carrying a datetime format beside a plain DATE, and a `yyyy-MM` fragment beside a date, which `OpListMath.resultKind` folds to DATE — and the kernel refuses both `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE`. The same fold is correct for a fragment with the date's own components, which both sides admit. The typed accessors narrow the first cell, since `BoundModel.dateTime(path)` checks the format shape, so it is the generic `field(path)` and the read path that reach it.
